- [parameter] **Context**: Subagents=Own context window; results return to the caller; Agent teams=Own context window; fully independent — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#compare-with-subagents
- [parameter] **Communication**: Subagents=Return a result to the caller. Subagents that Claude named when it spawned them can also [message each other](/docs/en/sub-agents#what-loads-at-startup); Agent teams=Teammates message each other directly — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#compare-with-subagents
- [parameter] **Coordination**: Subagents=Main agent manages all work; Agent teams=Self-coordination through messages, plus a shared task list for [agents that have the Task tools](/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#compare-with-subagents
- [parameter] **Best for**: Subagents=Focused tasks where only the result matters; Agent teams=Complex work requiring discussion and collaboration — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#compare-with-subagents
- [parameter] **Token cost**: Subagents=Lower: results summarized back to main context; Agent teams=Higher: each teammate is a separate Claude instance — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#compare-with-subagents
- [parameter] **Team lead**: The main Claude Code session that spawns teammates and coordinates work — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#architecture
- [parameter] **Teammates**: Separate Claude Code instances that each work on assigned tasks — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#architecture
- [parameter] **Task list**: Shared list of work items that teammates claim and complete — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#architecture
- [parameter] **Mailbox**: Messaging system for communication between agents — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#architecture
- [definition] Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions — Coordinate multiple Claude Code instances working together as a team, with shared tasks, inter-agent messaging, and centralized management. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#orchestrate-teams-of-claude-code-sessions
- [definition] When to use agent teams — Agent teams are most effective for tasks where parallel exploration adds real value. See [use case examples](#use-case-examples) for full scenarios. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [definition] Compare with subagents — Both agent teams and [subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents) let you parallelize work, but they operate differently. For separate sessions that pass messages to each other without a team, see [cross-session messaging](/docs/en/cross-session-messaging). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#compare-with-subagents
- [definition] Enable agent teams — Agent teams are disabled by default. Enable them by setting the `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS` environment variable to `1`, either in your shell environment or through [settings.json](/docs/en/settings): — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#enable-agent-teams
- [definition] Start your first agent team — After enabling agent teams, describe the task and the teammates you want in natural language. Claude spawns them and coordinates work based on your prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [definition] Control your agent team — Tell the lead what you want in natural language. It handles team coordination, task assignment, and delegation based on your instructions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#control-your-agent-team
- [definition] Specify teammates and models — Claude decides the number of teammates to spawn based on your task, or you can specify exactly what you want: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#specify-teammates-and-models
- [definition] Have teammates plan before implementing — For complex or risky tasks, you can have teammates plan before implementing. A teammate that Claude spawns while the lead is in [plan mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#analyze-before-you-edit-with-plan-mode) works in read-only plan mode until its plan is ready. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#have-teammates-plan-before-implementing
- [definition] Talk to teammates directly — Each teammate is a full, independent Claude Code session. You can message any teammate directly to give additional instructions, ask follow-up questions, or redirect their approach. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#talk-to-teammates-directly
- [definition] Assign and claim tasks — The shared task list coordinates work across the team. The lead creates tasks and teammates work through them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#assign-and-claim-tasks
- [definition] Shut down teammates — To gracefully end a teammate's session, refer to it by name. For example, with a teammate named researcher: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#shut-down-teammates
- [definition] Enforce quality gates with hooks — Use [hooks](/docs/en/hooks) to enforce rules when teammates finish work or tasks are created or completed: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#enforce-quality-gates-with-hooks
- [definition] How agent teams work — This section covers the architecture and mechanics behind agent teams. If you want to start using them, see [Control your agent team](#control-your-agent-team) above. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#how-agent-teams-work
- [definition] How Claude starts agent teams — To start a team, ask Claude for teammates. Claude launches a teammate when it calls the [Agent tool](/docs/en/tools-reference) with a [`name`](/docs/en/sub-agents#subagent-names) while agent teams are enabled, and Claude Code doesn't ask you to confirm. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#how-claude-starts-agent-teams
- [definition] Use subagent definitions for teammates — When spawning a teammate, you can reference a [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) type from any [subagent scope](/docs/en/sub-agents#choose-the-subagent-scope): project, user, plugin, or CLI-defined. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-subagent-definitions-for-teammates
- [definition] Permissions — Teammates start with the lead's permission settings. If the lead runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, all teammates do too. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#permissions
- [definition] Context and communication — Each teammate has its own context window. When spawned, a teammate loads the same project context as a regular session: CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, and skills. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#context-and-communication
- [definition] Token usage — Agent teams use significantly more tokens than a single session. Each teammate has its own context window, and token usage scales with the number of active teammates. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#token-usage
- [definition] Use case examples — These examples show how agent teams handle tasks where parallel exploration adds value. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-case-examples
- [definition] Run a parallel code review — A single reviewer tends to gravitate toward one type of issue at a time. Splitting review criteria into independent domains means security, performance, and test coverage all get thorough attention simultaneously. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#run-a-parallel-code-review
- [definition] Investigate with competing hypotheses — When the root cause is unclear, a single agent tends to find one plausible explanation and stop looking. The prompt fights this by making teammates explicitly adversarial: each one's job is not only to investigate its own theory but to challenge the others'. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#investigate-with-competing-hypotheses
- [definition] Give teammates enough context — Teammates load project context automatically, including CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, and skills, but they don't inherit the lead's conversation history. See [Context and communication](#context-and-communication) for details. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#give-teammates-enough-context
- [definition] Choose an appropriate team size — There's no hard limit on the number of teammates, but practical constraints apply: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#choose-an-appropriate-team-size
- [definition] Wait for teammates to finish — Sometimes the lead starts implementing tasks itself instead of waiting for teammates. If you notice this: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#wait-for-teammates-to-finish
- [definition] Start with research and review — If you're new to agent teams, start with tasks that have clear boundaries and don't require writing code: reviewing a PR, researching a library, or investigating a bug. These tasks show the value of parallel exploration without the coordination challenges that come with parallel implementation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-with-research-and-review
- [definition] Avoid file conflicts — Two teammates editing the same file leads to overwrites. Break the work so each teammate owns a different set of files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#avoid-file-conflicts
- [definition] Monitor and steer — Check in on teammates' progress, redirect approaches that aren't working, and synthesize findings as they come in. Letting a team run unattended for too long increases the risk of wasted effort. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#monitor-and-steer
- [definition] Teammates not appearing — If teammates aren't appearing after you ask Claude to spawn them: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#teammates-not-appearing
- [definition] Claude spawns teammates instead of subagents — While agent teams are enabled, a subagent that Claude names in the lead's session launches as a teammate. Claude [can name subagents on its own](#how-claude-starts-agent-teams), so this can happen during delegation you never framed as team work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#claude-spawns-teammates-instead-of-subagents
- [definition] Too many permission prompts — Teammate permission requests bubble up to the lead, which can create friction. Pre-approve common operations in your [permission settings](/docs/en/permissions) before spawning teammates to reduce interruptions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#too-many-permission-prompts
- [definition] Agents stopping early — Teammates may stop after encountering errors instead of recovering. Check their output by selecting the teammate in the agent panel and pressing Enter in in-process mode, or by clicking the pane in split mode, then either: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#agents-stopping-early
- [definition] Orphaned tmux sessions — If a tmux session persists after the Claude Code session ends, it may not have been fully cleaned up. List sessions and end the one created by the team: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#orphaned-tmux-sessions
- [definition] Limitations — Agent teams are experimental. Current limitations to be aware of: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#limitations
- [definition] Next steps — Explore related approaches for parallel work and delegation: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#next-steps
- [concept] Agent teams are designed for tasks where parallel exploration adds real value. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [fact] Agent teams add coordination overhead and use significantly more tokens than a single session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [idea] For sequential tasks, same-file edits, or work with many dependencies, a single session or subagents are more effective. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [concept] Agent teams allow teammates to share findings, challenge each other, and coordinate on their own. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [fact] Subagents operate as quick, focused workers that report back without the same level of peer interaction. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [concept] Agent teams are most effective when teammates can operate independently. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [fact] For separate sessions that pass messages to each other without a team, see cross-session messaging. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [idea] Use agent teams for research and review where multiple teammates investigate different aspects simultaneously. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [idea] Use agent teams for new modules or features so teammates can each own a separate piece without stepping on each other. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [idea] Use agent teams for debugging with competing hypotheses to test different theories in parallel and converge faster. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [idea] Use agent teams for cross-layer coordination where changes span frontend, backend, and tests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#when-to-use-agent-teams
- [fact] Agent teams are disabled by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#enable-agent-teams
- [actionable] Enable agent teams by setting the CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS environment variable to 1. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#enable-agent-teams

- [fact] In non-interactive mode with the -p flag, including Agent SDK sessions, Claude does not spawn teammates even if agent teams are enabled. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#enable-agent-teams
- [concept] Enabling agent teams changes ordinary delegation behavior so that named subagents form teams automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#enable-agent-teams
- [concept] Agent teams allow users to describe tasks and teammates in natural language, after which Claude spawns them and coordinates work based on the prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [concept] Claude populates a shared task list in a session with Task tools, spawns teammates for each perspective, and synthesizes findings when finished. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [problem] Claude may use subagents instead of creating a team; since they appear in the same panel, the panel alone does not confirm a team formed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [actionable] If Claude spawns subagents instead of an agent team, ask again and explicitly request an agent team. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [concept] The lead's terminal lists teammates in the agent panel below the prompt input for selection and interaction. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [actionable] Use up and down arrows to select a teammate in the agent panel. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team

- [fact] As of v2.1.199, an idle teammate's row stays in the panel while any teammate or subagent is still working. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [fact] In v2.1.181 through v2.1.198, an idle row hid 30 seconds after its own turn ended, even while other teammates were still working. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [fact] Idle rows are not hidden on versions before v2.1.181. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [concept] When more than three teammates are idle at once, the rows beyond the first three collapse into a single row counting the collapsed teammates. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [actionable] Select a collapsed row and press Enter to expand it, or press Esc to collapse them again. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [fact] Working teammates, failed teammates, and the teammate you are viewing always keep their own rows regardless of count. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team
- [idea] To have each teammate in its own split pane, refer to the section on choosing a display mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#start-your-first-agent-team

- [fact] A single reviewer tends to gravitate toward one type of issue at a time. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-case-examples
- [actionable] Assign each teammate a distinct lens in the prompt so they do not overlap. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-case-examples
- [concept] The lead synthesizes findings across all reviewers after they finish their individual work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-case-examples
- [problem] Sequential investigation suffers from anchoring, where subsequent investigation becomes biased toward the first explored theory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-case-examples
- [idea] Make teammates explicitly adversarial to fight the tendency of a single agent to stop looking after finding one plausible explanation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-case-examples

- [fact] With multiple independent investigators actively trying to disprove each other, the surviving theory is much more likely to be the actual root cause. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#use-case-examples

- [parameter] Working: Icon shows as=Animated; What it means=Claude is actively running tools or generating a response — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] Needs input: Icon shows as=Yellow; What it means=Claude is waiting on something only you can provide: an answer to a question, a permission decision, or another prompt only you can answer, such as a [sandbox](/docs/en/sandboxing) prompt to allow a network host or an MCP server's [request for input](/docs/en/mcp#respond-to-mcp-elicitation-requests). A command that needs an attached terminal, such… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] Idle: Icon shows as=Dimmed; What it means=The session has nothing to do and is ready for your next prompt — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] Completed: Icon shows as=Green; What it means=The task finished successfully — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] Failed: Icon shows as=Red; What it means=The task ended with an error — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] Stopped: Icon shows as=Grey; What it means=You stopped the session with `Ctrl+X` or `claude stop`, [its process was ended from outside Claude Code](#the-supervisor-process), or [it ended while the background service was off](#sessions-show-as-failed-after-shutdown) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] `✻` or animated `✽`: The session process is alive and replies immediately — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] `∙`: The process has exited. You can still peek at the row, and when you reply or attach, Claude restarts from where it left off — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] `✢`: A [`/loop`](/docs/en/scheduled-tasks) session sleeping between iterations. The row shows its run count and a countdown — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [parameter] Yellow: Waiting on checks or review, or checks failed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#pull-request-status
- [parameter] Green: Checks passed and no review is blocking — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#pull-request-status
- [parameter] Purple: Merged — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#pull-request-status
- [parameter] Grey: Draft or closed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#pull-request-status
- [parameter] `a:<name>`: Sessions running the named agent — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#filter-sessions
- [parameter] `s:<state>`: Sessions in the given state, such as `s:working`. Also accepts `s:blocked` for everything waiting on you — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#filter-sessions
- [parameter] `#<number>` or a pull or merge request URL: The session working on that pull request or merge request — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#filter-sessions

- [parameter] `Tab`: On an empty input, browse all subagents. Otherwise apply the highlighted suggestion — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts

- [parameter] `Ctrl+J`: Insert a newline in the dispatch input — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts
- [parameter] `Ctrl+X`: Stop the session; press again within two seconds to delete it — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts
- [parameter] `Shift+↑` / `Shift+↓`: Reorder the selected session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts
- [parameter] `Esc`: Close the peek panel, clear the input, or exit. When you opened agent view by backgrounding your session with `←`, the final `Esc` returns to that conversation instead of exiting. With [vim editor mode](/docs/en/interactive-mode#vim-editor-mode) on, pressing `Esc` in the input switches from INSERT to NORMAL mode and keeps your text, as in the main prompt — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts
- [parameter] `Ctrl+C`: Clear the input; press twice to exit — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts
- [parameter] `?`: Show all shortcuts — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts
- [parameter] `<agent-name> <prompt>`: If the first word matches a custom [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) name, that subagent runs as the session's main agent with the configuration from its frontmatter — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-agent-view
- [parameter] `@<agent-name>`: Mention a custom subagent anywhere in the prompt to run it as the main agent — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-agent-view
- [parameter] `@<repo>`: Mention a repository to run the session there. See [Dispatch to a specific directory](#dispatch-to-a-specific-directory) for which repositories are listed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-agent-view
- [parameter] `/<command>`: Suggest [skills](/docs/en/skills) and [commands](/docs/en/commands) to dispatch as the prompt — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-agent-view
- [parameter] `! <command>`: Run a shell command as a background job instead of starting a Claude session. The job appears as a row you can attach to, watch, and detach from — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-agent-view

- [definition] Manage multiple agents with agent view — Dispatch and manage many Claude Code sessions from one screen. Agent view shows what every session is doing and which ones need your input. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#manage-multiple-agents-with-agent-view
- [definition] Quick start — This walkthrough covers the core agent view loop: dispatch a task, watch its row update as Claude works, peek to check on it and reply, and attach for the full conversation. The session you dispatch keeps running after you close agent view, so you can leave and come back to it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#quick-start
- [definition] Dispatch a session — Type a prompt describing a task and press `Enter`. A new background session starts on that task and appears as a row showing whether it's working, waiting on you, or done. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#quick-start
- [definition] Peek and reply — Select a row with the arrow keys and press `Space` to open the peek panel. It shows the session's most recent output, or the question it's waiting on, rather than the full transcript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#peek-and-reply
- [definition] Attach and detach — Press `Enter` or `→` on a row to attach when you want the full conversation. The session takes over the terminal as a full interactive Claude Code session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#peek-and-reply
- [definition] Bring an existing session in — This step needs a running session. If you followed the earlier steps you don't have one open in this terminal, so open a regular `claude` session in another terminal and send it a message first. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#peek-and-reply
- [definition] Monitor sessions with agent view — Run `claude agents` to open agent view. It takes over the full terminal and lists every session grouped by state, with pinned sessions and the ones that need you at the top. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#monitor-sessions-with-agent-view
- [definition] Read session state — Each row starts with an icon whose color and animation show the session's state: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#read-session-state
- [definition] Row summaries — The one-line summary in each row is generated by a [Haiku-class model](/docs/en/model-config) so the row can tell you what the session is doing, what it needs, or what it produced without opening the transcript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#row-summaries
- [definition] Pull request status — When a session [opens a pull request](#how-file-edits-are-isolated), Claude Code adds a label at the right edge of the row, linked to the pull request: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#pull-request-status
- [definition] Peek and reply — Press `Space` on a selected row to open the peek panel. It opens with the sentence the row truncates at the terminal edge, and which sentence that is depends on the session's state: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#peek-and-reply
- [definition] Attach to a session — Press `Enter` or `→` on a selected row to attach. Agent view is replaced by the full interactive session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#attach-to-a-session
- [definition] Organize the list — Agent view groups sessions so the ones that need input are at the top, with `Ready for review` and `Needs input` above `Working` and `Completed`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#organize-the-list
- [definition] Filter sessions — Type in the dispatch input to filter instead of dispatching: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#filter-sessions
- [definition] Keyboard shortcuts — Press `?` in agent view to see every shortcut in context. The table below summarizes them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#keyboard-shortcuts
- [definition] Dispatch new agents — You can dispatch new background sessions from agent view, send or copy an existing interactive session to the background, or start one directly from the shell. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#dispatch-new-agents
- [definition] From agent view — Type a prompt in the input at the bottom of agent view and press `Enter` to start a new background session. The session is named automatically from the prompt; rename it later with `Ctrl+R`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-agent-view
- [definition] From inside a session — Two commands move work from the session you're in to the background: `/background` sends the current conversation there and frees your terminal, and `/fork` sends a copy while you keep working where you are. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-inside-a-session
- [definition] From your shell — Pass `--bg` or its long form `--background` to start a session that goes straight to the background: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#from-your-shell
- [definition] How file edits are isolated — Every background session, whether started from agent view, `/bg`, or `claude --bg`, starts in your working directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated
- [definition] Set the model — The model name shown in the agent view header is the dispatch default. New sessions you start from the input use this model, which comes from the [`model` setting](/docs/en/settings-reference#model) in your user settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#set-the-model
- [definition] Permission mode, model, and effort — A background session takes its settings, provider, permission mode, model, and effort from where and how you dispatched it. The subsections below cover each source, and what persists when the supervisor restarts the session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#permission-mode-model-and-effort
- [definition] Settings, plugins, and MCP servers — Agent view accepts the same configuration flags as `claude` for loading settings, plugins, MCP servers, and additional directories. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#settings-plugins-and-mcp-servers
- [definition] Manage sessions from the shell — Every background session has a short ID you can use from the shell. The ID is printed when you start a session with `claude --bg`, and each session's ID is its directory name under `~/.claude/jobs/`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell
- [definition] List sessions as JSON — `claude agents --json` prints active sessions as a JSON array and exits: every live session, plus background sessions that are still working or blocked even when their process has exited. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#list-sessions-as-json
- [definition] How background sessions are hosted — Claude Code treats every session listed in agent view as a background session, whether or not you're currently attached to it. By contrast, a session started by running `claude` directly is tied to that terminal and ends when it closes, unless you [send it to the background](#from-inside-a-session). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted
- [definition] The supervisor process — Background sessions are hosted by a per-user supervisor process, separate from your terminal and from agent view. The supervisor starts automatically the first time you background a session or open agent view, and you don't manage it directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process
- [definition] Where state is stored — Session state is stored under your Claude Code config directory. If you set [`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`](/docs/en/env-vars), the supervisor uses that directory instead of `~/.claude` and runs as a separate instance with its own sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#where-state-is-stored
- [definition] Turn off agent view — To turn off background agents and agent view entirely, set the `disableAgentView` [setting](/docs/en/settings) to `true` or set the `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW` environment variable. Administrators can enforce this through [managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#turn-off-agent-view
- [definition] `claude agents` lists subagents instead of opening agent view — If `claude agents` prints a count followed by your configured subagents and then exits, agent view is unavailable in your environment. Run `claude update` to install the latest version. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#claude-agents-lists-subagents-instead-of-opening-agent-view
- [definition] Agent view opens with no sessions — Before you dispatch your first session, agent view shows the empty section headers with a description under each, plus a one-line explanation above the input, in place of the session list. Type a prompt in the input at the bottom and press `Enter` to dispatch your first session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#agent-view-opens-with-no-sessions
- [definition] Backgrounding shows a `Background this session?` dialog — If you press `←` to background the current session and Claude Code shows a `Background this session?` dialog, the session has in-flight work that backgrounding would stop, restart, or leave running unattended, and Claude Code asks before it does any of those: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#backgrounding-shows-a-background-this-session-dialog
- [definition] Prompt rejected as too short — The dispatch input expects a task description, not a conversational opener. A prompt shorter than four characters is rejected with a `Too short` hint so a stray keystroke doesn't start a session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#prompt-rejected-as-too-short
- [definition] Sessions show as failed or stopped after shutdown — Shutting down or restarting your machine stops running background sessions. A session that was waiting on your input stays under `Needs input` when you come back. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#sessions-show-as-failed-or-stopped-after-shutdown
- [definition] Opening a session says the conversation is already open — Two processes can't write to the same transcript. When a stopped session's saved conversation is already open in another live Claude Code process, Claude Code refuses to start the session's own process. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#opening-a-session-says-the-conversation-is-already-open
- [definition] Opening a session says it has no saved transcript — A stopped session that was [backgrounded from another conversation](#from-inside-a-session) and stopped before its first response finished has nothing to resume: until that first response finishes, the conversation still lives only in the session it was backgrounded from. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#opening-a-session-says-it-has-no-saved-transcript
- [definition] The terminal host died or the session stopped responding — The [supervisor](#the-supervisor-process) runs each background session's terminal in its own host process. When that process dies or stops responding, Claude Code shows the reason and offers a restart; in both cases the conversation is saved and the restart resumes it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#the-terminal-host-died-or-the-session-stopped-responding
- [definition] A session fails before starting with a `possibly low memory` note — When a background session's process exits before it finishes starting and the host is low on memory, the row's status names the exit and adds `possibly low memory — free some up and retry`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#a-session-fails-before-starting-with-a-possibly-low-memory-note
- [definition] Agent view says the background service did not respond — If attaching, peeking, or `claude logs` reports that the background service did not respond, the supervisor process has likely stalled. Stop it and let the next `claude agents` start a fresh one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#agent-view-says-the-background-service-did-not-respond
- [definition] Dispatch fails with `Could not resolve authentication method` — If a background dispatch fails with `Could not resolve authentication method` while interactive sessions authenticate normally, the worker that received the dispatch didn't pick up credentials. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#dispatch-fails-with-could-not-resolve-authentication-method
- [definition] Background sessions can't read Desktop, Documents, or Downloads on macOS — On macOS, the background session host runs as its own process and requests access to protected folders separately from your terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#background-sessions-cant-read-desktop-documents-or-downloads-on-macos
- [definition] Background sessions can't reach local-network hosts on macOS — On macOS 15 and later, the system blocks a process from reaching devices on your local network until you grant Local Network permission, so a command targeting a LAN address can fail with `connect: no route to host` in a background session even though it works in a foreground terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#background-sessions-cant-reach-local-network-hosts-on-macos
- [definition] A session is slow to respond after attaching — Once a session has finished and sat unattached for about an hour, the supervisor stops its process to free resources. Attaching starts a fresh process from where it left off and switches to the session immediately while the process restarts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#a-session-is-slow-to-respond-after-attaching
- [definition] `.claude/worktrees/` is filling up — Deleting a session in agent view removes the worktree Claude created for it, but [some deletes keep the worktree or leave its directory on disk](#what-deleting-a-session-removes), so leftover directories can accumulate. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#claudeworktrees-is-filling-up
- [definition] Limitations — Agent view is in research preview with the following limitations: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#limitations
- [definition] Related resources — For other ways to run Claude in parallel, and for passing findings between the sessions you run, see: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#related-resources
- [definition] Version history — Agent view has evolved quickly during research preview. If you are on an older Claude Code version, some behavior on this page may differ; in particular, `claude agents` rejects flags it doesn't yet support with an `unknown option` error. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#version-history

- [problem] A session backgrounded with `←` or `/background` that you manually end (e.g., with `kill`) is marked stopped instead of restarted. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted

- [concept] Background work started at the top level by a session is handed off to the next process upon stop or restart. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted
- [problem] Work whose state lives only inside the process itself, such as shell commands started by a subagent or running monitors, stops with the process and is not handed off. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted

- [fact] If a restarted session misreads its transcript as empty, the file is renamed with an `.orphaned-` suffix instead of deleted. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted

- [problem] If the supervisor runs an older Claude Code version than the session's process, the session keeps running the newer version until the supervisor updates. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted

- [fact] Each background session has the `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` environment variable set to its `~/.claude/jobs/<id>` directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted

- [problem] Sessions that have finished and sat unattached for about an hour may become slow to respond because the supervisor stops their process to free resources. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#troubleshooting
- [idea] Pin a session with Ctrl+T to prevent it from being stopped while waiting, ensuring it remains responsive. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#troubleshooting
- [concept] Attaching to a stopped session starts a fresh process from where it left off and switches to the session immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#troubleshooting
- [fact] While a session starts, Claude Code displays the tail of the transcript with markdown, highlighted code blocks, and tool calls as dimmed rows above a dimmed prompt area. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#troubleshooting
- [problem] Deleting a session in agent view does not always remove the worktree or its directory on disk, causing leftover directories to accumulate. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#troubleshooting
- [actionable] List leftover git worktree entries by running `git worktree list` in the project directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#troubleshooting
- [actionable] Remove specific leftover worktrees by running `git worktree remove <path>` for each entry found. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#troubleshooting

- [concept] Cross-session messaging allows sessions to pass findings to each other. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#related-resources
- [fact] Agent teams coordinate multiple sessions that message each other. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#related-resources
- [concept] Claude Code on the web enables running sessions in a managed cloud environment instead of locally. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#related-resources

## Run agents in parallel
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents>

- [parameter] [Subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents): What it gives you=Delegated workers inside one session that do a side task in their own context and return a summary; Use it when=A side task would flood your main conversation with search results, logs, or file contents you won't reference again — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#run-agents-in-parallel
- [parameter] [Agent view](/docs/en/agent-view): What it gives you=One screen to dispatch and monitor sessions running in the background, opened with `claude agents`. Research preview; Use it when=You have several independent tasks and want to hand them off, check status at a glance, and step in only when one needs you — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#run-agents-in-parallel
- [parameter] [Agent teams](/docs/en/agent-teams): What it gives you=Multiple coordinated sessions with a shared task list and inter-agent messaging, managed by a lead. Experimental and disabled by default; Use it when=You want Claude to split a project into pieces, assign them, and keep the workers in sync — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#run-agents-in-parallel
- [parameter] [Dynamic workflows](/docs/en/workflows): What it gives you=A script that runs many subagents and cross-checks their results, for work too big to coordinate one turn at a time or that needs more than a single pass; Use it when=A job outgrows a handful of subagents, or you want findings verified against each other: a codebase-wide audit, a 500-file migration, cross-checked research, or a plan… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#run-agents-in-parallel
- [definition] Run agents in parallel — Compare the ways Claude Code can take on multiple tasks at once: subagents, agent view, agent teams, and dynamic workflows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#run-agents-in-parallel
- [definition] Choose an approach — The right approach depends on who coordinates the work, whether the workers need to communicate, and whether they edit the same files: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#choose-an-approach
- [definition] Check on running work — The command for checking on running work depends on which approach you used: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#check-on-running-work
- [definition] Learn more — Each guide below covers setup and configuration for one approach: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents#learn-more
- [concept] Subagents, agent view, agent teams, and dynamic workflows are four distinct approaches to parallelizing work with Claude sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] Claude delegates and collects results inside one conversation using subagents. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] Agent view allows users to hand off independent tasks and check back later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] Agent teams involve Claude planning, assigning, and supervising a group of workers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] Dynamic workflows use a script to hold the plan instead of relying on Claude's turn-by-turn judgment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] Workers in an agent team message each other directly and share a task list when they have the Task tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [problem] Agent teams do not isolate teammates in worktrees, requiring users to partition work so each teammate owns different files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] Worktrees give each session a separate git checkout to prevent parallel sessions from editing the same files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] Agent view moves each dispatched session into its own worktree automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] Cross-session messaging lets Claude list and message other Claude Code sessions on the same or different machines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] The `/batch` skill splits one large change into 5 to 30 worktree-isolated subagents that each open a pull request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] A background bash command runs one shell command without blocking the conversation but does not spawn an agent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] A forked subagent inherits the full conversation context instead of starting fresh. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [actionable] Start a forked subagent with the `/subtask` command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] To copy the whole session into a new background session that runs alongside it, use the `/fork` command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [problem] With agent view turned off, the forked-subagent command is `/fork` instead and `/subtask` isn't available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [concept] A routine runs a session on a schedule in the cloud rather than in parallel on your machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] As of v2.1.198, the `/agents` command no longer opens a panel but prints a notice pointing to subagent file locations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [actionable] Use `claude agents` to open agent view and see every session, its state, and which ones need input. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [actionable] Use `/tasks` to list items running in the background of the current session, check on them, attach to them, or stop them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [actionable] Use `/workflows` to list running and completed dynamic workflow runs, their phases, and agent completion counts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents
- [fact] Running several sessions or subagents at once multiplies token usage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents

- [fact] The same mapping defined in `modelOverrides` applies when passing the Anthropic model ID directly through `--model` or `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` environment variables. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#set-up-manually

- [fact] Valid values for ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX are us, eu, apac, jp, au, and global. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [fact] The environment variable requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [actionable] Set ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX to global when your account has global. profiles enabled but Claude Code derives a geography-specific prefix from your AWS region. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [concept] The preferred prefix is a preference, not a guarantee, and its application depends on whether profile availability can be checked in the account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [fact] When profile discovery is available, Claude Code resolves models by first checking for a profile with the preferred prefix. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [fact] If no profile exists with the preferred prefix, Claude Code checks for any matching profile for that model. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [fact] If no matching profile exists at all, Claude Code uses the built-in model ID with the preferred prefix without checking availability. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [problem] When profile discovery is unavailable, if the account lacks inference profiles with the specified prefix, requests fail with a 400 error. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [fact] Claude Code does not rewrite Amazon Bedrock inference profile IDs or ARNs configured by the user. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [fact] In AWS GovCloud regions, Claude Code always uses us-gov. as the prefix regardless of configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [problem] Setting ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX to an invalid value causes Claude Code to fall back to the region-derived preferred prefix. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes
- [actionable] Create an IAM policy with the required permissions for Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#iam-configuration
- [concept] The `bedrock:GetInferenceProfile` permission allows Claude Code to resolve an application inference profile ARN to its backing foundation model to select the correct request shape. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#iam-configuration
- [problem] If the token is missing the `bedrock:GetInferenceProfile` permission, requests still succeed but incur an extra round-trip as Claude Code retries once with an alternate shape. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#iam-configuration
- [idea] Granting the `bedrock:GetInferenceProfile` permission avoids the retry overhead, which is particularly relevant for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` deployments where token policies are typically narrower. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#iam-configuration
- [fact] For more restrictive permissions, you can limit the IAM policy Resource to specific inference profile ARNs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#iam-configuration
- [concept] Claude Code automatically recovers from missing `bedrock:GetInferenceProfile` permissions by retrying once with an alternate request shape. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#iam-configuration
- [fact] The permission is most often required for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` deployments where the token's policy is typically narrower than a full IAM role. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#iam-configuration
- [concept] Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 support the 1M token context window on Amazon Bedrock. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#1m-token-context-window
- [fact] Sonnet 5 always runs with the 1M window on both the Invoke API and the Mantle endpoint, with no [1m] variant to select. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#1m-token-context-window
- [actionable] To enable the extended context window for models other than Sonnet 5 on the Invoke API, append [1m] to the model ID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#1m-token-context-window
- [fact] The setup wizard offers a 1M context option when it pins models. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#1m-token-context-window
- [actionable] To enable the 1M context window for a manually pinned model, append [1m] to the model ID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#1m-token-context-window
- [fact] Amazon Bedrock documentation is available at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#additional-resources
- [fact] Pricing information for Amazon Bedrock can be found at https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#additional-resources
- [concept] Amazon Bedrock inference profiles are supported and documented separately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#additional-resources
- [fact] Documentation regarding Amazon Bedrock token burndown and quotas is available at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-token-burndown.html. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#additional-resources
- [actionable] Users can follow the Quick Setup Guide for Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock available at https://builder.aws.com/content/2tXkZKrZzlrlu0KfH8gST5Dkppq/claude-code-on-amazon-bedrock-quick-setup-guide. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#additional-resources
- [idea] The AWS Solutions Library provides a monitoring implementation guide for Claude Code with Amazon Bedrock at https://github.com/aws-solutions-library-samples/guidance-for-claude-code-with-amazon-bedrock/blob/main/assets/docs/MONITORING.md. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#additional-resources

- [parameter] No backend: An artifact is a static page. It can't store data submitted through a form or authenticate viewers itself. Start there for project conventions and behavioral rules. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#where-the-classifier-reads-configuration
- [definition] Define trusted infrastructure — For most organizations, `autoMode.environment` is the only field you need to set. It tells the classifier which repos, buckets, and domains are trusted: the classifier uses it to decide what "external" means, so any destination not listed is a potential exfiltration target. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [definition] Generate environment entries with `/auto-mode-setup` — Run `/auto-mode-setup` to have Claude Code draft `autoMode.environment` entries, and sometimes [rule entries](#override-the-block-and-allow-rules) too, from your project and your recent sessions in it. If you accept the draft, Claude Code writes it to `~/.claude/settings.json`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#generate-environment-entries-with-auto-mode-setup
- [definition] What `/auto-mode-setup` reads — If `~/.claude/settings.json` already holds `autoMode` entries, Claude Code starts by asking whether to add to your environment list or replace it, and keeps the rules you wrote either way. Claude Code then asks how you use this project and offers two optional scans before it scans anything. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#what-auto-mode-setup-reads
- [definition] Review and save the draft — Claude Code scans in the background, then shows you the draft. You accept or discard it as a whole, so edit `~/.claude/settings.json` afterwards to adjust single entries. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#review-and-save-the-draft
- [definition] Turn off `/auto-mode-setup` — Once auto mode has blocked several actions and you still have no `autoMode.environment` entries, Claude Code shows a dialog titled "Teach auto mode about your environment?" at the end of a turn and offers to run `/auto-mode-setup` for you. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#turn-off-auto-mode-setup
- [definition] Override the block and allow rules — Three additional fields let you replace the classifier's built-in rule lists: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#override-the-block-and-allow-rules
- [definition] Edit rules from `/permissions` — To view and edit classifier rules without opening a settings file, run [`/permissions`](/docs/en/permissions#manage-permissions) and select the **Auto mode** tab. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [definition] Route all shell commands through the classifier — By default, narrow Bash and PowerShell allow rules such as `Bash(npm test)` stay in effect in auto mode, and Claude Code resolves them before the classifier runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#route-all-shell-commands-through-the-classifier
- [definition] Inspect the defaults and your effective config — The `claude auto-mode` subcommands help you inspect, validate, and reset your configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#inspect-the-defaults-and-your-effective-config
- [definition] Review denials — To review and retry actions the auto mode classifier denied, open `/permissions` and select the **Recently denied** tab, where Claude Code records each denial. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#review-denials
- [definition] Fix a denial with an allow rule, an environment entry, or a retry — To see what the classifier blocked, find the tool call in the conversation. If the call appears shortened or folded into a summary line such as `Ran 3 shell commands`, press `Ctrl+O` to open the [transcript viewer](/docs/en/interactive-mode#transcript-viewer), which expands it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#fix-a-denial-with-an-allow-rule-an-environment-entry-or-a-retry
- [definition] Fix repeated denials — Repeated denials for the same destination usually mean the classifier is missing context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#fix-repeated-denials
- [concept] Auto mode lets Claude Code run without routine permission prompts by routing tool calls through a classifier that blocks irreversible, destructive, or external actions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [fact] Deny and explicit ask rules are evaluated before the classifier and still block or prompt regardless of auto mode settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [concept] The `autoMode` settings block tells the classifier which repos, buckets, and domains your organization trusts to stop blocking routine internal operations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [fact] Auto mode is available to all users on every provider, including the Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and signed-in Claude apps gateway sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [fact] In versions v2.1.158 through v2.1.206, auto mode on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and Claude apps gateway sessions required setting `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [fact] The requirement for `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1` was removed in version v2.1.207. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [fact] By default, the classifier trusts only the working directory and the current repo's configured remotes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [problem] Actions like pushing to a company's source-control org or writing to a team cloud bucket are blocked by default until added to `autoMode.environment`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [actionable] Use the `permissions.ask` setting to add a human checkpoint for pushes and pull requests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [concept] Rules can be set across CLAUDE.md, user settings, and managed settings to determine where the classifier reads configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config

- [actionable] Generate environment entries using the `/auto-mode-setup` command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [concept] You can override the default block and allow rules when they do not fit your specific pipeline requirements. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config

- [concept] The page serves as a configuration reference for how sessions end up in auto mode and what the classifier blocks by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config
- [concept] Auto mode allows pushes to any branch of the repository you're working in, including the default branch, and pull request creation by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#common-boundaries
- [fact] A non-default branch whose name marks it as a deploy or publication target, such as `production`, `release`, or `gh-pages`, is judged on its own terms rather than covered by the default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#common-boundaries
- [fact] Pushes to deploy targets are checked for content, blocking force pushes, secrets entering the commit, or changes that would send secrets outside the repository when CI runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#common-boundaries
- [fact] Before version v2.1.211, the classifier allowed pushes only to your working branch, branches Claude created, and routine pushes to the default branch. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#common-boundaries
- [actionable] To require a human checkpoint before every push or pull request, add permission rules using `permissions.ask` in your settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#common-boundaries
- [concept] Content-scoped ask rules are evaluated before the classifier and always force a permission prompt, even in auto mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#common-boundaries
- [idea] Add explicit ask rules to your settings to define specific boundaries while keeping auto mode on for everything else. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#common-boundaries
- [concept] The `autoMode.environment` field tells the classifier which repos, buckets, and domains are trusted to decide what 'external' means. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure

- [fact] Versions before v2.1.195 print only the first five trust slots. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [concept] Context slots describe your organization, stack, and security posture so the classifier reads other rules in your context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] A repository is assumed private unless its remote host and name indicate otherwise or a visibility check shows it is public. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [problem] The classifier reads messages and commands but not their output, so evidence like `gh repo view` output does not reach it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] Transcript-evidence checks for repository visibility require Claude Code v2.1.200 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] Public paste and gist services are treated as outside the trust boundary until you name one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [concept] Trust slots name what the classifier treats as inside your boundary, including Trusted repo, Source control, and Trusted internal domains. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] The repo and source-control entries default to the working repository and its configured remotes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [problem] A private repository is an acceptable destination for confidential material but never clears secrets or personal data into it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] Content ported, repointed, or first read from outside the working repository is treated as not that repository's own work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] Repository visibility scoping requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [concept] Sensitivity slots name what the protective rules treat as high-risk, such as Sensitive data locations & audiences. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] Sensitive remote targets default to a heuristic treating any host or namespace with `prod` or `production` as sensitive. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [problem] Before v2.1.211, context slots included a Default / protected branches entry that treated `main` and `master` as protected. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] In v2.1.211, the protected-branch default was removed so pushes to any branch are allowed by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [actionable] Include the literal string `$defaults` in the array to splice default entries alongside your custom entries. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [actionable] Run `claude auto-mode config` after saving settings to confirm effective rules include your entries. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [concept] Entries are prose, not regex or tool patterns; the classifier reads them as natural-language rules. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] The Internal package registry, Sensitive data locations & audiences, Sensitive remote targets, and Protected IaC scopes entries require Claude Code v2.1.195 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [fact] In versions v2.1.195 through v2.1.197, the Sensitive data locations entry was named PII / regulated-data locations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure
- [idea] Start with the defaults and add your source control org and key internal services to resolve common false positives. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#define-trusted-infrastructure

- [fact] The Auto mode tab requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later to function. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [fact] The Auto mode tab appears only when auto mode is available to the current session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [concept] The tab displays allow, soft_deny, hard_deny, and environment entries from all classifier scopes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [fact] Entries sourced from managed settings or the --settings flag are displayed as read-only in the tab. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [actionable] Changes made in the tab are automatically saved to ~/.claude/settings.json. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [concept] Adding the first rule to a section automatically inserts "$defaults" to maintain built-in rules. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [actionable] Users can add, edit, or delete rules within the allow, soft_deny, and hard_deny sections. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [concept] Built-in rules for a section are toggled by adding or removing "$defaults" from that section's list. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [problem] A section must contain at least one user-defined rule before its built-in rules can be turned off. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [actionable] Users can edit environment entries as a single document in their editor. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [fact] If no environment entries exist, the system prompts to replace the built-in environment before opening the editor. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions
- [actionable] Including the "$defaults" line in the editor preserves the built-in environment entries upon saving. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config#edit-rules-from-permissions

- [definition] Give Claude a way to verify its work — Give Claude a check it can run: tests, a build, a screenshot to compare. It's the difference between a session you watch and one you walk away from. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#give-claude-a-way-to-verify-its-work
- [definition] Explore first, then plan, then code — Separate research and planning from implementation to avoid solving the wrong problem. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#explore-first-then-plan-then-code
- [definition] Explore — Enter plan mode by pressing `Shift+Tab` until the status bar shows `⏸ plan mode on`, or start the session with `claude --permission-mode plan`. Claude reads files and answers questions without making changes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#explore-first-then-plan-then-code
- [definition] Plan — Ask Claude to create a detailed implementation plan. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#explore-first-then-plan-then-code
- [definition] Implement — Switch out of plan mode by approving the plan or pressing `Shift+Tab`, then let Claude code, verifying against its plan. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#explore-first-then-plan-then-code
- [definition] Commit — Ask Claude to commit with a descriptive message and create a PR. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#explore-first-then-plan-then-code
- [definition] Provide specific context in your prompts — The more precise your instructions, the fewer corrections you'll need. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#provide-specific-context-in-your-prompts
- [definition] Provide rich content — Use `@` to reference files, paste screenshots/images, or pipe data directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#provide-rich-content
- [definition] Configure your environment — A few setup steps make Claude Code significantly more effective across all your sessions. For a full overview of extension features and when to use each one, see [Extend Claude Code](/docs/en/features-overview). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#configure-your-environment
- [definition] Write an effective CLAUDE.md — Run `/init` to generate a starter CLAUDE.md file based on your current project structure, then refine over time. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#write-an-effective-claudemd
- [definition] Configure permissions — To get fewer prompts without giving up control, pre-approve the tools you trust with `/permissions` and let sandboxed commands run without asking with `/sandbox`. Switch to Manual mode when you want to approve edits and commands yourself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#configure-permissions
- [definition] Use CLI tools — Tell Claude Code to use CLI tools like `gh`, `aws`, `gcloud`, and `sentry-cli` when interacting with external services. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#use-cli-tools
- [definition] Connect MCP servers — Run `claude mcp add` with a server name and URL or command to connect external tools like Notion, Figma, or your database. - [definition] Set up hooks — Use hooks for actions that must happen every time with zero exceptions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#set-up-hooks

- [definition] Rewind with checkpoints — Every prompt you send creates a checkpoint. You can restore conversation, code, or both to any previous checkpoint. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#rewind-with-checkpoints

- [definition] Generate a task list — Have Claude write the list of files that need migrating to a file, so the loop in the next step can read it, with a prompt like `list all 2,000 Python files that need migrating and save the list to files.txt` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#fan-out-across-files

- [actionable] Run the bundled `/code-review` skill to review the current diff for bugs in a fresh subagent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#automate-and-scale
- [problem] Reviewers prompted to find gaps will usually report some even when work is sound, potentially leading to over-engineering. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#automate-and-scale
- [idea] Instruct reviewers to flag only gaps affecting correctness or stated requirements to avoid chasing optional findings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#automate-and-scale
- [problem] The kitchen sink session occurs when you switch between unrelated tasks without clearing context, leaving irrelevant information. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [actionable] Use the /clear command between unrelated tasks to reset the context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [problem] Correcting over and over pollutes the context with failed approaches when Claude repeatedly makes mistakes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [actionable] After two failed corrections, use /clear and write a better initial prompt incorporating what you learned. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [problem] An over-specified CLAUDE.md that is too long causes Claude to ignore half of it as important rules get lost in the noise. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [actionable] Ruthlessly prune your CLAUDE.md by deleting instructions if Claude already performs the task correctly or converting them to hooks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [problem] The trust-then-verify gap happens when Claude produces a plausible-looking implementation that fails to handle edge cases. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [actionable] Always provide verification such as tests, scripts, or screenshots before shipping code generated by Claude. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [problem] The infinite exploration pattern occurs when you ask Claude to investigate without scoping it, causing it to read hundreds of files and fill the context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [actionable] Scope investigations narrowly or use subagents to prevent exploration from consuming your main context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#avoid-common-failure-patterns
- [concept] The patterns in the guide are starting points that work well generally but may not be optimal for every situation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#develop-your-intuition
- [idea] Let context accumulate when you are deep in a complex problem and the history is valuable. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#develop-your-intuition
- [idea] Skip planning and let Claude figure it out when the task is exploratory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#develop-your-intuition
- [idea] Use a vague prompt when you want to see how Claude interprets the problem before constraining it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#develop-your-intuition
- [concept] Developing intuition involves noticing what works, such as prompt structure, context provided, or mode used, when Claude produces great output. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#develop-your-intuition
- [actionable] When Claude struggles, ask why the context was too noisy, the prompt too vague, or the task too big for one pass. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices#develop-your-intuition
