- [parameter] `channelsEnabled`: Purpose=Master switch. Must be `true` for any channel to deliver messages. Blocks all channels including the development flag when off. See [Enable channels for your organization](#enable-channels-for-your-organization).; When not configured=claude.ai Team and Enterprise: channels blocked. Console: channels allowed unless your organization deploys managed settings, in which… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [parameter] `allowedChannelPlugins`: Purpose=Which plugins can register once channels are enabled. Replaces the Anthropic-maintained list when set.; When not configured=Anthropic default list applies — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [parameter] [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web): What it does=Runs tasks in a fresh cloud sandbox, cloned from GitHub; Good for=Delegating self-contained async work you check on later — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#how-channels-compare
- [parameter] [Claude in Slack](/docs/en/slack): What it does=Spawns a web session from an `@Claude` mention in a channel or thread; Good for=Starting tasks directly from team conversation context — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#how-channels-compare
- [parameter] Standard [MCP server](/docs/en/mcp): What it does=Claude queries it during a task; nothing is pushed to the session; Good for=Giving Claude on-demand access to read or query a system — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#how-channels-compare
- [parameter] [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control): What it does=You drive your local session from claude.ai or the Claude mobile app; Good for=Steering an in-progress session while away from your desk — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#how-channels-compare
- [definition] Push events into a running session with channels — Use channels to push messages, alerts, and webhooks into your Claude Code session from an MCP server. Forward CI results, chat messages, and monitoring events so Claude can react while you're away. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#push-events-into-a-running-session-with-channels
- [definition] Supported channels — Each supported channel is a plugin that requires [Bun](https://bun.sh). For a hands-on demo of the plugin flow before connecting a real platform, try the [fakechat quickstart](#quickstart). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Create a Telegram bot — Open [BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) in Telegram and send `/newbot`. Give it a display name and a unique username ending in `bot`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Configure your token — Run the configure command with the token from BotFather: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Restart with channels enabled — Exit Claude Code and restart with the channel flag. This starts the Telegram plugin, which begins polling for messages from your bot: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Pair your account — Open Telegram and send any message to your bot. The bot replies with a pairing code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Create a Discord bot — Go to the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications), click **New Application**, and name it. In the **Bot** section, create a username, then click **Reset Token** and copy the token. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Enable Message Content Intent — In your bot's settings, scroll to **Privileged Gateway Intents** and enable **Message Content Intent**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Invite the bot to your server — Go to **OAuth2 > URL Generator**. Select the `bot` scope and enable these permissions: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Configure your token — Run the configure command with the bot token you copied: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Restart with channels enabled — Exit Claude Code and restart with the channel flag. This connects the Discord plugin so your bot can receive and respond to messages: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Pair your account — DM your bot on Discord. The bot replies with a pairing code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Grant Full Disk Access — The Messages database at `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` is protected by macOS. The first time the server reads it, macOS prompts for access: click **Allow**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Restart with channels enabled — Exit Claude Code and restart with the channel flag: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Text yourself — Open Messages on any device signed into your Apple ID and send a message to yourself. It reaches Claude immediately: self-chat bypasses access control with no setup. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Allow other senders — By default, only your own messages pass through. To let another contact reach Claude, add their handle: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [definition] Quickstart — Fakechat is an officially supported demo channel that runs a chat UI on localhost, with nothing to authenticate and no external service to configure. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#quickstart
- [definition] Install the fakechat channel plugin — Start a Claude Code session and run the install command: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#quickstart
- [definition] Restart with the channel enabled — Exit Claude Code, then restart with `--channels` and pass the fakechat plugin you installed: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#quickstart
- [definition] Push a message in — Open the fakechat UI at [http://localhost:8787](http://localhost:8787) and type a message: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#quickstart
- [definition] Security — Every approved channel plugin maintains a sender allowlist: only IDs you've added can push messages, and everyone else is silently dropped. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [definition] Enterprise controls — Admins control availability through two [managed settings](/docs/en/settings) that users cannot override. The default depends on how you authenticate: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [definition] Enable channels for your organization — Enable channels for your organization from [**claude.ai → Admin settings → Claude Code → Channels**](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code), which requires the Owner role, or by setting `channelsEnabled` to `true` in managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enable-channels-for-your-organization
- [definition] Restrict which channel plugins can run — By default, any plugin on the Anthropic-maintained allowlist can register as a channel. Admins on Team and Enterprise plans can replace that allowlist with their own by setting `allowedChannelPlugins` in managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#restrict-which-channel-plugins-can-run
- [definition] Research preview — Channels are a research preview feature. Availability is rolling out gradually, and the `--channels` flag syntax and protocol contract may change based on feedback. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [definition] How channels compare — Several Claude Code features connect to systems outside the terminal, each suited to a different kind of work: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#how-channels-compare
- [definition] Next steps — Once you have a channel running, explore these related features: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#next-steps
- [concept] Channels are MCP servers that push messages, alerts, and webhooks into a running Claude Code session to enable reactions while the user is away. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [fact] Channels are currently in research preview and require Anthropic authentication via claude.ai or a Console API key. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [problem] Channels are not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [fact] Team and Enterprise organizations must explicitly enable channels through enterprise controls. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [concept] Channels can be two-way, allowing Claude to read an event and reply back through the same channel like a chat bridge. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [problem] Events only arrive while the session is open, requiring a background process or persistent terminal for always-on setups. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [idea] Use channels to forward CI results, chat messages, and monitoring events so Claude can react autonomously. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [fact] Telegram, Discord, and iMessage are included as built-in channels in the research preview. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [problem] When Claude replies through a channel, the terminal displays the tool call and confirmation but not the actual reply text. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [actionable] Install a channel as a plugin and configure it with your own credentials to start using it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [fact] Unlike integrations that spawn fresh cloud sessions or wait for polling, events arrive directly in the existing open session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels
- [concept] Each supported channel is a plugin that requires Bun to run. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [fact] Telegram bot usernames must end in `bot`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [actionable] To add the marketplace, run `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [problem] If the install summary reports `Run /reload-plugins to activate.`, you must run that command to activate the configure command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [fact] Telegram bot tokens are saved to `~/.claude/channels/telegram/.env`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [actionable] To enable channels, restart Claude Code with the `--channels` flag. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [problem] If a bot does not respond, ensure Claude Code is running with `--channels` because the bot only replies while the channel is active. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [fact] Discord requires enabling the Message Content Intent under Privileged Gateway Intents. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [actionable] To invite a Discord bot, go to OAuth2 > URL Generator, select the `bot` scope, and enable required permissions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [fact] Discord bot tokens are saved to `~/.claude/channels/discord/.env`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [concept] The iMessage channel reads the Messages database directly and sends replies through AppleScript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [fact] The iMessage channel requires macOS and does not need a bot token or external service. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [problem] Without Full Disk Access, the iMessage server exits immediately with `authorization denied`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [actionable] Grant Full Disk Access via System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access if the prompt does not appear or was declined. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [fact] The iMessage database is located at `~/Library/Messages/chat.db`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [problem] The first reply from Claude triggers a macOS Automation prompt asking if the terminal can control Messages. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [actionable] To allow other senders, add their handle using the configure command; handles are phone numbers in `+country` format or Apple ID emails. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [fact] Self-chatting with iMessage bypasses access control and requires no setup. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [idea] Choose the user scope option during plugin installation so the plugin is available across all projects. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#supported-channels
- [concept] Every approved channel plugin maintains a sender allowlist where only added IDs can push messages while others are silently dropped. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [fact] Telegram and Discord bootstrap the allowlist by pairing a bot with a user via a pairing code exchanged in the Claude Code session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [actionable] To pair a Telegram or Discord bot, find it, send any message, approve the returned pairing code in your Claude Code session, and the sender ID will be added to the allowlist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [concept] iMessage bypasses the security gate automatically when texting yourself, while other contacts are added by handle using the `/imessage:access allow` command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [fact] Being listed in `.mcp.json` is insufficient to push messages; a server must also be explicitly named in the `--channels` flag. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [concept] Server enablement is controlled per session via the `--channels` flag, while organization-level availability is managed through `channelsEnabled` settings on Team and Enterprise plans or Console organizations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [problem] Anyone who can reply through a channel can approve or deny tool use if the channel declares permission relay, so only allowlist senders trusted with that authority should be permitted. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#security
- [fact] For claude.ai Team and Enterprise users, channels are blocked by default until an Owner enables them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [fact] For Anthropic Console users with API key authentication, channels are permitted by default unless the organization deploys managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [concept] Pro and Max users without an organization skip admin checks entirely; channels are available to them immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [fact] No channel runs until a user opts it in for the session using the `--channels` flag. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [actionable] Enable channels by navigating to claude.ai → Admin settings → Claude Code → Channels or by setting `channelsEnabled` to `true` in managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [fact] If the channel setting is disabled or unset, the MCP server connects and tools work, but channel messages will not arrive. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [problem] When the setting is disabled, a startup warning tells the user to have an admin enable the setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [concept] Admins on Team and Enterprise plans can replace the default Anthropic-maintained allowlist with their own by setting `allowedChannelPlugins` in managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [idea] Use `allowedChannelPlugins` to restrict official plugins, approve channels from an internal marketplace, or both. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [fact] Each entry in the allowlist must name a plugin and the marketplace it comes from. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [problem] Setting `allowedChannelPlugins` to an empty array blocks all channel plugins from the allowlist, though `--dangerously-load-development-channels` can still bypass this for local testing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [actionable] To block channels entirely including the development flag, leave `channelsEnabled` unset instead of setting an empty allowlist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [fact] The `allowedChannelPlugins` setting requires `channelsEnabled: true` to function. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [problem] If a user passes a plugin to `--channels` that is not on the approved list, Claude Code starts normally but the channel does not register. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [fact] Claude Code does not register a channel server that negotiates protocol revision 2026-07-28 when `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION` is set to `auto` on the v2 MCP client runtime. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#enterprise-controls
- [concept] Channels are a research preview feature with a rolling rollout schedule. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [fact] The `--channels` flag syntax and protocol contract may change based on feedback during the preview. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [problem] Neither `--channels` nor `--dangerously-load-development-channels` appears in `claude --help` while the feature is in preview. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [fact] The flags work even though they are not listed in the help output. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [concept] During the preview, `--channels` only accepts plugins from an Anthropic-maintained allowlist or an organization's allowlist if configured by an admin. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [fact] The default approved set of channel plugins is located in the `claude-plugins-official` repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [problem] If a plugin passed to `--channels` is not on the effective allowlist, Claude Code starts normally but the channel does not register. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [fact] A startup notice explains why a channel failed to register if it was not on the allowlist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [actionable] Use `--dangerously-load-development-channels` to test a channel you are building. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [question] How do I configure the `allowedChannelPlugins` setting? — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [actionable] Report issues or feedback on the Claude Code GitHub repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#research-preview
- [actionable] Build your own channel for systems that do not have plugins yet. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#next-steps
- [concept] Remote Control allows driving a local session from a phone instead of forwarding events into it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#next-steps
- [actionable] Use Scheduled tasks to poll on a timer instead of reacting to pushed events. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels#next-steps

- [fact] Telemetry destinations receive OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) metrics with token counts, model, user identity, and latency by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#why-claude-apps-gateway

- [concept] Clients speak the Anthropic Messages API to the gateway, which translates requests for various upstreams including Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#why-claude-apps-gateway
- [fact] The gateway supports failover between configured upstreams, allowing changes to regions or providers without developer reconfiguration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#why-claude-apps-gateway

- [fact] Telemetry, audit logs, managed settings, and IdP identity are controlled by the user and not sent to Anthropic unless the Anthropic API is an upstream. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#why-claude-apps-gateway

- [fact] Enabling the Chat tab via the policy's `desktop` block requires a gateway running Claude Code v2.1.227 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [problem] There is no service-token flow for unattended pipelines; CI jobs without a developer to approve the browser device flow cannot authenticate. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [actionable] For remote development boxes with no display, run `/login` over SSH and open the verification link in a browser on a laptop to authenticate. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [fact] Once signed in, every Claude Code invocation on that machine uses the gateway session, including non-interactive `claude -p` runs and Agent SDK sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [concept] Model access enforcement returns a 400 error for requests to models not granted by the policy, and the `/model` picker is filtered to the `availableModels` allowlist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [idea] Set `enforceAvailableModels: true` in the policy so the Default option resolves to a model inside `availableModels` instead of the built-in default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [fact] In sessions signed in through `/login`, CLI telemetry exports are sent to the gateway regardless of any locally set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [fact] The CLI attaches the gateway session token to telemetry exports only when the endpoint points at the gateway itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [idea] If you already collect Claude Code telemetry directly, add your collector as a `forward_to` destination to ensure signals are not discarded. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [fact] While signed in, the gateway token is the session's only credential; other credentials like `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` are ignored. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [fact] Developers do not need to log out of claude.ai first when signing in through the gateway because earlier login credentials are ignored. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [concept] Managed settings locked by policy cannot be overridden locally; the CLI applies the policy at startup and updates on each hourly poll. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [problem] Signed-in sessions exit with an error after about 10 seconds if the gateway is unreachable at startup, rather than starting without settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [fact] A session expires within `ttl_hours` when the next refresh fails after the user is disabled in the IdP. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [concept] Usage telemetry sent to the organization's collector includes developer identity, token counts, model, and latency but does not include prompt or completion content. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [idea] Organizations can choose to collect richer telemetry such as logs and traces including commands and file paths via per-destination configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#connect-developers
- [concept] The availability table documents which Claude Code features function when connecting through the gateway and what the gateway server itself supports. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#availability-and-limitations
- [fact] The gateway delivers anthropic-beta header values from the CLI to every upstream, eliminating the need for operators to maintain a beta allowlist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#availability-and-limitations
- [concept] For Amazon Bedrock, which ignores headers, the gateway transfers the beta values into the request body's anthropic_beta field instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#availability-and-limitations
- [fact] Upstreams other than Amazon Bedrock receive the anthropic-beta header exactly as sent by the CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#availability-and-limitations

- [parameter] `write_keys`: Required=No; Description=Array of `{id, key}`. An `x-api-key` matching one of these can list, set, and delete spend limits. Key values must be at least 32 characters; `id`s must be unique across `read_keys` and `write_keys`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `read_keys`: Required=No; Description=Array of `{id, key}`. Read-only: every `GET` endpoint, including listing caps, fetching one by ID, and reading [`/effective`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#%2Feffective) and [`/audit`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#%2Faudit). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `admin_groups`: Required=No; Description=IdP group names. A gateway JWT whose `groups` claim includes one of these has full admin access, read and write, and audits as `oidc:<sub>`. Use this for human admins; use API keys for machines. An empty entry in this list stops the gateway at boot. See [Matcher values that stop the gateway at boot](#matcher-values-that-stop-the-gateway-at-boot). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `blocked_message`: Required=No; Description=Appended verbatim to the `429 billing_error` a blocked developer sees. Write the whole instruction, such as a URL or a Slack channel. When unset, the gateway sends only the default message. See [How enforcement works](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#how-enforcement-works). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `audit_retention_days`: Required=No; Description=Default `365`. Older `admin_audit` rows are swept. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `spend_retention_months`: Required=No; Description=Default `13`. `spend` counter rows older than this are swept. The default keeps a full year plus the current partial month for year-over-year reporting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `identity_retention_days`: Required=No; Description=Default `90`. Last-seen TTL for `principal_emails` rows, which hold each developer's email, display name, and groups (PII). Deliberately shorter than spend retention so a deprovisioned identity ages out while its anonymous spend counters remain. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `group_limit_mode`: Required=No; Description=`min` (default) or `max`. When a developer is in several groups with caps, `min` enforces the most restrictive and `max` the least. Used by both enforcement and `/effective`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [parameter] `fail_closed_on_error`: Required=No; Description=Default `false`. Spend enforcement fails open on a Postgres outage, so inference stays up. Set `true` to fail closed: over-cap developers are blocked, but so is everyone else if the store is unreachable. Requires an [`admin:`](#admin) block: spend enforcement only runs when `admin` is configured, and the gateway refuses to start if you set this… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#enforcement
- [parameter] `multiplier`: Required=No; Description=Default `1`. The meter multiplies every metered amount by this, whether list-priced or overridden, so `0.85` bills 85% of the price. Must be greater than 0 and at most 1. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#pricing
- [parameter] `overrides`: Required=No; Description=Rows of `{upstream, model, input, output, cache_read, cache_write}` in USD per million tokens. All four rates are required and must be positive. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#pricing
- [parameter] `match: {}`: Matches every authenticated user. Start with one of these and add group-scoped policies above it later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#managed
- [parameter] `match: { groups: [a, b] }`: Matches if the JWT's `groups` claim contains any of the listed groups. Case-sensitive: groups must match the IdP's exact casing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#managed
- [parameter] `match: { email_domain: example.com }`: Matches the part after the last `@` in the JWT's `email` claim, case-insensitive. Accepts one domain per policy. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#managed
- [parameter] `match: { groups: [a], email_domain: example.com }`: Both conditions must match — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#managed
- [parameter] `availableModels`: Enforced by=Gateway + CLI; Effect=Model allowlist. Also checked at `/v1/messages`, so a patched client can't bypass it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#what-goes-in-cli
- [parameter] `permissions.allow` / `.deny`: Enforced by=CLI; Effect=Tool and command rules. See [Permissions](/docs/en/permissions). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#what-goes-in-cli
- [parameter] `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode`: Enforced by=CLI; Effect=Set to `disable` to block [`bypassPermissions`](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode), the mode that skips permission prompts, and the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#what-goes-in-cli
- [parameter] `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`: Enforced by=CLI; Effect=When `true`, user and project permission rules are ignored; only rules from this document apply — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#what-goes-in-cli
- [parameter] `env`: Enforced by=CLI; Effect=Environment variables merged into the CLI process. Use for telemetry, auto-update, and model-name overrides. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#what-goes-in-cli
- [parameter] `hooks`: Enforced by=CLI; Effect=Org-wide [hooks](/docs/en/hooks) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#what-goes-in-cli
- [parameter] `access_control`: Key=`allow_cidrs` / `deny_cidrs`; Default=empty; Description=Inbound IP allow/deny by client address, after `trusted_proxies` resolution. `deny_cidrs` is checked first; a client it matches is rejected even if `allow_cidrs` also matches. If `allow_cidrs` is non-empty the gateway is default-deny. `/healthz` and `/readyz` are exempt from `allow_cidrs`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [parameter] `limits`: Key=`max_request_bytes`; Default=32 MiB; Description=Max inbound request body; oversize requests get `413` before the body is buffered. Raise for large file or image requests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [parameter] `limits`: Key=`max_request_header_bytes`; Default=unset; Description=When set, oversize headers return `431` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [parameter] `limits`: Key=`max_url_length`; Default=unset; Description=When set, an over-long URL returns `414` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [parameter] `timeouts`: Key=`upstream_ttfb_ms`; Default=120000; Description=Max wait for the upstream's response headers (time to first byte). The response body then streams with no wall-clock cap. Applies to the direct Anthropic upstream path; every other provider is bounded by its provider SDK's own timeout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [parameter] `rate_limits`: Key=`device_authorization.max` / `.window_seconds`; Default=30 / 600; Description=Per-IP rate limit on the unauthenticated device-authorization endpoint. Raise for a large org behind a shared egress IP or NAT. These limits apply only to the device-grant sign-in flow, not to `/v1/messages` inference. See [User-code brute-force… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [parameter] `rate_limits`: Key=`device_verify.max` / `.window_seconds`; Default=10 / 600; Description=Per-IP rate limit on `user_code` submissions at `/device` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [parameter] macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json`, or the `com.anthropic.claudecode` managed preferences domain — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#client-side-managed-settings
- [parameter] Linux and WSL: `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#client-side-managed-settings
- [parameter] Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json`, or Group Policy via the HKLM registry — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#client-side-managed-settings
- [definition] Claude apps gateway configuration — Reference for every gateway.yaml option: listener and TLS, OIDC, session, Postgres store, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry upstreams, model routing, managed policies, and telemetry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#claude-apps-gateway-configuration
- [definition] File structure — Five sections are [required](#required-sections). Every other section is [optional](#optional-sections), and an omitted section takes its defaults. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [definition] Secret expansion — Don't write secrets such as `client_secret`, `jwt_secret`, or `postgres_url` directly in `gateway.yaml`. Reference them with one of the forms below, and the gateway resolves the value at boot from an environment variable or a file: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#secret-expansion
- [definition] `listen` — The `listen` block controls where the gateway serves: the bind address and port, the externally visible origin, and optional TLS termination. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#listen
- [definition] `oidc` — The `oidc` block connects the gateway to your identity provider and decides who can sign in. It names the issuer and OAuth client, maps the claims that carry email and groups, and restricts sign-in by email domain or group. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#oidc
- [definition] `session` — The `session` block shapes the bearer tokens the gateway mints after sign-in: the secret that signs them and how long they live. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#session
- [definition] `store` — The `store` block points the gateway at its PostgreSQL database, which holds device grants and rate-limit counters. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#store
- [definition] `upstreams` — `upstreams` is an ordered list. The gateway forwards inference to the first upstream that resolves the requested model. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#upstreams
- [definition] `admin` — Optional. Enables `/v1/organizations/spend_limits`, which mirrors Anthropic's public Admin API, and per-developer spend enforcement on `/v1/messages`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin
- [definition] `enforcement` — The `enforcement` block controls how spend-limit checks behave when the store is unavailable. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#enforcement
- [definition] `pricing` — The `pricing` block tells the spend meter what to charge instead of USD list price, so caps and [`/effective`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#%2Feffective) reflect your contracted rates. Amounts stay in USD and remain an estimate, not an invoice. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#pricing
- [definition] `models` — The `models` block is an optional admin-curated model list, served at `/v1/models` and used to translate model IDs per upstream. It is required for non-US Amazon Bedrock regions, Amazon Bedrock provisioned-throughput ARNs, and Microsoft Foundry deployment names. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#models
- [definition] `managed` — The `managed` block defines role-based access policies keyed on IdP groups or email domain. Policies are evaluated in order; the first match is selected, then merged onto the `match: {}` catch-all base described below. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#managed
- [definition] `telemetry` — The CLI sends OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) over HTTP metrics, logs, and, when enabled, traces to the gateway, which relays them verbatim to each configured destination. See [Monitoring usage](/docs/en/monitoring-usage) for the metrics and events the CLI emits. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#telemetry
- [definition] HTTP tuning — Four optional top-level blocks, `access_control`, `limits`, `timeouts`, and `rate_limits`, tune the HTTP surface. The defaults suit most deployments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#http-tuning
- [definition] Complete example — This full reference config exercises every core section; the [HTTP tuning blocks](#http-tuning) keep their defaults. Copy it, delete what you don't need, and fill in your values. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#complete-example
- [definition] Client-side managed settings — Everything above configures the gateway server. You point developer machines at the gateway separately, on each device, through Claude Code's [managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#client-side-managed-settings
- [concept] A Claude apps gateway deployment is configured by a single YAML file conventionally named `gateway.yaml`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config
- [fact] The gateway reads the configuration file once at startup using the command `claude gateway --config /path/to/gateway.yaml`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config
- [problem] Every option is validated against a schema at boot, so a malformed config fails at start with a field-level error rather than at first use. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config
- [actionable] To write your first configuration, start from the quickstart which builds a minimal working config and runs it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config
- [idea] Once you have a config you're happy with, use the deployment guide to cover containerizing and hosting it on Kubernetes, Cloud Run, or your own platform. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config
- [concept] The `gateway.yaml` file defines where the gateway listens, how developers sign in, where inference goes, and which policies and telemetry apply. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config
- [fact] The reference page covers options for listener and TLS, OIDC, session, Postgres store, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry upstreams, model routing, managed policies, and telemetry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config
- [concept] The configuration file consists of five required sections and several optional sections; omitted optional sections use defaults. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [fact] Unknown keys cause the gateway to fail boot, surfacing a named error rather than silently ignoring the setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [concept] The listen section configures the bind address, public URL, and TLS termination. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [concept] The oidc section defines the identity provider settings, including issuer, client, claim mapping, and sign-in permissions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [concept] The session section configures bearer tokens minted by the gateway, specifying the secret and token lifetime. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [fact] The store section requires PostgreSQL to persist device grants and rate-limit counters. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [concept] The upstreams section specifies where inference traffic is routed, supporting Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [idea] Only the five specified sections are required; all other sections are optional and can be omitted to use defaults. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [problem] A typo in a configuration key will cause the gateway to fail boot instead of being silently ignored. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#file-structure
- [concept] Secrets should not be written directly in gateway.yaml; instead, they must be referenced to allow the gateway to resolve values at boot time. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#secret-expansion
- [problem] Writing secrets such as client_secret, jwt_secret, or postgres_url directly in gateway.yaml is a practice to avoid. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#secret-expansion
- [fact] The gateway resolves referenced secret values at boot from either an environment variable or a file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#secret-expansion
- [concept] The Claude apps gateway overview page provides a quickstart and details developer connection. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#related
- [fact] The deployment guide covers IdP setup, container image configuration, Kubernetes, Cloud Run, and operations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#related
- [concept] Spend limits documentation details per-developer caps and the Admin API. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#related

- [definition] Claude apps gateway deployment and operations — Register the gateway with your IdP, build the container, deploy on Kubernetes or Cloud Run, and operate it: health checks, secret rotation, upgrades, and security. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#claude-apps-gateway-deployment-and-operations
- [definition] Identity provider setup — Register a confidential OAuth/OpenID Connect (OIDC) web application with a single redirect URI, `https://<gateway>/oauth/callback`, and assign it to the users or groups who should have gateway access. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#identity-provider-setup
- [definition] Deployment — The gateway is a single stateless Linux binary that coordinates through Postgres, so deploy it the way you deploy any other stateless service in your environment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#deployment
- [definition] Container image — Build your own image around the native `claude` binary from the standard Claude Code release: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#container-image
- [definition] Kubernetes — Run the gateway as a Deployment, like any stateless service: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#kubernetes
- [definition] Push the gateway URL to developer machines — Once the gateway is serving, push `forceLoginMethod`, `forceLoginGatewayUrl`, and `parentSettingsBehavior: "merge"` to each developer's machine through managed settings, via MDM or by writing the per-OS `managed-settings.json` directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#push-the-gateway-url-to-developer-machines
- [definition] Operations — Once the gateway is serving traffic, day-to-day operation is reading its logs, probing its health, and rotating its secrets on your schedule. The subsections cover each, plus what Postgres holds and how upgrades and rollbacks behave. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [definition] Logs — The gateway writes two streams to stderr, both JSON-friendly: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#logs
- [definition] Health — The gateway serves `GET /healthz` as a liveness probe and `GET /readyz` as a readiness probe; `/readyz` verifies the store is reachable. Both are exempt from `access_control.allow_cidrs`, so probes keep working on a locked-down listener. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#health
- [definition] Outage behavior — If Postgres goes down, the gateway itself keeps serving signed-in developers and new sign-ins fail. Whether developers actually keep working depends on how your orchestrator handles readiness: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#outage-behavior
- [definition] JWT secret rotation — Rotate the signing secret in three steps so existing sessions stay valid: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#jwt-secret-rotation
- [definition] Postgres — The gateway holds five data tables plus a `_migrations` table, all created by its boot-time migrations: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#postgres
- [definition] Upgrades — Replicas are stateless, so a rolling restart is safe at any time. The gateway runs schema migrations at boot, which means deploying the new binary self-migrates the database. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#upgrades
- [definition] Security — This section answers the questions a security review asks: what data flows through the gateway and where it goes, which attacks the design defends against, and which answers belong in a compliance questionnaire. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#security
- [definition] Threat model summary — The gateway sits inside your network perimeter, but individual developer laptops aren't treated as trusted. The design accounts for this in three ways: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#threat-model-summary
- [definition] User-code brute-force resistance — The `user_code` a developer types into the `/device` verification page is 8 characters drawn from a 20-character alphabet, which yields 20⁸ or about 2.56×10¹⁰ combinations, and it expires after 10 minutes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#user-code-brute-force-resistance

- [problem] Replacing the JWT secret without keeping the old one in the array invalidates every outstanding session immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [concept] The gateway holds five data tables plus a _migrations table, all created by boot-time migrations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [fact] A 30-second loop expires kv rows past their TTL, and an hourly sweep enforces retention windows on spend tables. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [idea] Point the gateway at a dedicated database or schema to keep the required grant narrow. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [actionable] To erase a departed developer immediately, run DELETE FROM principal_emails WHERE principal = '<sub>' directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [fact] Migrations are append-only, so rolling back to a prior binary that knows fewer migrations is safe as it ignores extra rows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [problem] Rolling back to an older binary fails boot if the config uses keys introduced by the newer release; remove the new key before rolling back. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations
- [idea] Include the gateway in the same patching cadence as other services holding production credentials to ensure security fixes are applied. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-deploy#operations

- [parameter] `Container manifest type … must support amd64/linux` at deploy: Cause=Image was built on a non-amd64 host, or buildx emitted an OCI image index; Fix=Build with `--platform=linux/amd64 --provenance=false` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-on-gcp#troubleshooting
- [parameter] Gateway boot exits with a Postgres connection-timeout error on Cloud Run: Cause=Service isn't attached to the VPC, or Cloud SQL has no private IP on that VPC; the store stops waiting after 5 seconds; Fix=Deploy with `--network` and `--subnet` for Direct VPC egress, and create the Cloud SQL instance with `--no-assign-ip` and `--network` pointing at the same VPC — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-on-gcp#troubleshooting
- [parameter] Google Cloud's Agent Platform requests return `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`: Cause=Runtime isn't using the `claude-gateway` service account, or the model isn't enabled in Model Garden for the project; Fix=Set `--service-account` on Cloud Run or bind Workload Identity on GKE, and enable each Claude model in Model Garden for the target region — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-on-gcp#troubleshooting
- [parameter] Streaming responses cut off after a fixed duration: Cause=Front-end request timeout: the load balancer backend service behind GKE Ingress defaults to 30 seconds and Cloud Run to 300 seconds; Fix=Attach a BackendConfig with a raised `timeoutSec` on GKE, or deploy with `--timeout=3600` on Cloud Run — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-on-gcp#troubleshooting
- [definition] Deploy Claude apps gateway on Google Cloud — A worked example of running Claude apps gateway on Google Cloud: Cloud Run or GKE, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, Secret Manager, and service-account auth to Google Cloud's Agent Platform. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-on-gcp#deploy-claude-apps-gateway-on-google-cloud

## Claude apps gateway spend limits
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits>

- [snippet] Set a cap: curl -sS https://claude-gateway.internal.example.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits \ — `curl -sS https://claude-gateway.internal.example.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits \` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#set-a-cap
- [snippet] Set a cap: curl -sS https://claude-gateway.internal.example.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits \ — `curl -sS https://claude-gateway.internal.example.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits \` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#set-a-cap
- [parameter] `scope.type`: Values=`user`, `rbac_group`, `organization`; Description=`user` targets one developer by their OpenID Connect (OIDC) `sub`, the stable user ID your identity provider assigns; pass it as `scope.user_id`. `rbac_group` targets an [IdP group](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#managed) by name; pass it as `scope.rbac_group_id`. `organization` is the org-wide default. The gateway… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#set-a-cap
- [parameter] `amount`: Values=Whole-number string of USD cents, or `null`; Description=`null` is unlimited. `"0"` is a zero cap, which blocks every request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#set-a-cap
- [parameter] `period`: Values=`daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`; Description=A scope can hold one cap per period, and each enforces independently: a developer is blocked if over any of them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#set-a-cap
- [parameter] `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits`: List configured caps, optionally filtered to one `scope_type` of `organization`, `rbac_group`, or `user`. Query: `?limit=&after_id=&before_id=&scope_type=`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#admin-api-reference
- [parameter] `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limits`: Create or replace a cap for `{scope, period}`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#admin-api-reference
- [parameter] `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/{id}`: Fetch one cap by its `spl_`-prefixed ID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#admin-api-reference
- [parameter] `DELETE /v1/organizations/spend_limits/{id}`: Delete one cap. Returns `{type: "spend_limit_deleted", id}`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#admin-api-reference
- [parameter] `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective`: Resolved cap and to-date spend per principal per period. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#admin-api-reference
- [parameter] `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/audit`: Admin mutation trail, newest-first. Query: `?limit=&after_id=`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#admin-api-reference
- [parameter] `user_ids[]`: Repeatable. Filter to specific principals by OIDC `sub`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#effective
- [parameter] `period[]`: Repeatable. Filter to `daily`, `weekly`, or `monthly` rows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#effective
- [parameter] `sort`: `spend_desc` lists top spenders first. Requires exactly one `period[]`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#effective
- [parameter] `q`: Case-insensitive substring filter over the OIDC `sub`, last-seen email, and last-seen display name. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#effective
- [parameter] `limit` / `page`: Page size, 1–1000 with a default of 20, and the opaque cursor from the previous response's `next_page`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#effective
- [parameter] `spend`: Contents=Per-principal period-to-date counters in cents; Retention=[`admin.spend_retention_months`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin), default 13 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#data-lifecycle
- [parameter] `spend_limits`: Contents=The configured caps; Retention=Until deleted via the API — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#data-lifecycle
- [parameter] `admin_audit`: Contents=The mutation trail; Retention=[`admin.audit_retention_days`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin), default 365 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#data-lifecycle
- [parameter] `principal_emails`: Contents=Each principal's last-seen email, display name, and IdP groups. Contains PII.; Retention=[`admin.identity_retention_days`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin) since last activity, default 90 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#data-lifecycle
- [definition] Claude apps gateway spend limits — Cap each developer's spend through the Claude apps gateway by day, week, or month. Set limits with an Admin API and the gateway enforces them live on every request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits
- [definition] Set a cap — With the [`admin:`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config#admin) block configured in `gateway.yaml`, the gateway serves an admin API at `/v1/organizations/spend_limits` and enforces caps live on every inference request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#set-a-cap
- [definition] How enforcement works — On each `/v1/messages` request, the gateway looks up the developer's caps and period-to-date spend in one Postgres query. A developer over any cap gets a `429` with `error.type: billing_error` and header `x-should-retry: false`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#how-enforcement-works
- [definition] How requests are priced — After each response, a usage meter reads the token counts and adds the cost to the daily, weekly, and monthly counters. It never touches the bytes sent to the client, so a metering failure can't break a response. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#how-requests-are-priced
- [definition] Postgres availability — The pre-check queries Postgres with a two-second timeout. If the store is unreachable or times out, enforcement fails open by default: the request proceeds, the gateway logs a warning, and the response carries no `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#postgres-availability
- [definition] Usage warnings in Claude Code — Claude Code warns a developer as they approach their cap: once utilization passes 75%, and again past 95% of their most-consumed cap. When the gateway blocks a request, Claude Code shows the gateway's `429` message as is, including your `admin.blocked_message`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#usage-warnings-in-claude-code
- [definition] Admin API reference — The endpoints below are served under `/v1/organizations/spend_limits`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#admin-api-reference
- [definition] `/effective` — `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective` returns Anthropic's `SpendSummary` schema: each row is a principal for a period, with the resolved cap, period-to-date spend, and an `actor` object. Gateway-specific differences: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#effective
- [definition] `/audit` — Returns the spend-limit mutation trail: who changed which cap, with before/after snapshots, newest-first. `has_more` is exact. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#audit
- [definition] Pagination — The raw list pages by `after_id` and `before_id`, which are mutually exclusive `spl_…` IDs; results are ordered by creation and `has_more` reflects the traversal direction. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#pagination
- [definition] Data lifecycle — The gateway holds four spend-related tables; an hourly sweep enforces the retention windows: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#data-lifecycle

- [definition] Manage context — Cloud sessions support [built-in commands](/docs/en/commands) that produce text output. Commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/plugin` or `/resume`, aren't available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#manage-context
- [definition] Permission modes in cloud sessions — You pick a cloud session's [permission mode](/docs/en/permission-modes) from the [mode dropdown](/docs/en/permission-modes#switch-permission-modes), both when you create the task and while the session runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#permission-modes-in-cloud-sessions
- [definition] Review changes — Each session shows a diff indicator with lines added and removed, like `+42 -18`. Select it to open the diff view, leave inline comments on specific lines, and send them to Claude with your next message. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#review-changes
- [definition] Share sessions — To share a session, toggle its visibility according to the account types below. After that, share the session link as-is. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#share-sessions
- [definition] Archive sessions — You can archive sessions to keep your session list organized. Archived sessions are hidden from the default session list but can be viewed by filtering for archived sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#archive-sessions
- [definition] Delete sessions — Deleting a session permanently removes the session and its data. This action can't be undone. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#delete-sessions
- [definition] Auto-fix pull requests — Claude can watch a pull request and automatically respond to CI failures and review comments. Claude subscribes to GitHub activity on the PR, and when a check fails or a reviewer leaves a comment, Claude investigates and pushes a fix if one is clear. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#auto-fix-pull-requests
- [definition] How Claude responds to PR activity — When auto-fix is active, Claude receives GitHub events for the PR including new review comments and CI check failures. For each event, Claude investigates and decides how to proceed: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#how-claude-responds-to-pr-activity
- [definition] Security and isolation — Each cloud session is separated from your machine and from other sessions through several layers: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [definition] Troubleshooting — For runtime API errors that appear in the conversation such as `API Error: 500`, `529 Overloaded`, `429`, or `Prompt is too long`, see the [Error reference](/docs/en/errors). Those errors and their fixes are shared with the CLI and Desktop app. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#troubleshooting
- [definition] Session creation failed — If a new session fails to start with `Session creation failed` or stalls at provisioning, Claude Code could not allocate a VM for the session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#session-creation-failed
- [definition] Unable to get organization UUID — `claude --cloud` and `claude --teleport` require sign-in with a claude.ai account. If you authenticate with an API key, or your stored account details are stale, these commands fail with `Unable to get organization UUID` or a message that API key authentication is not sufficient. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#unable-to-get-organization-uuid
- [definition] Remote Control session expired or access denied — `--teleport` connects through the same Remote Control session infrastructure that cloud sessions use, so authentication and session-expiry errors surface with Remote Control wording. You may see `Remote Control session expired` or `Access denied`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#remote-control-session-expired-or-access-denied
- [definition] Environment expired — Cloud sessions stop after a period of inactivity and the session's VM is reclaimed. On the web, the session is marked expired in the session list. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#environment-expired
- [definition] Limitations — Before relying on cloud sessions for a workflow, account for these constraints: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [concept] Claude Code on the web runs tasks on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure or on an organization's self-hosted environment when routed there. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [fact] The feature is in research preview for Pro, Max, and Team users, as well as Enterprise users with premium seats or Chat + Claude Code seats. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [fact] Sessions persist even if you close your browser and can be monitored from the Claude mobile app. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [actionable] Start with the Get started guide to connect your GitHub account and submit your first task. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [concept] You can move sessions between web and terminal using the `--cloud` and `--teleport` flags. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [fact] The web product supports auto-fixing pull requests to respond automatically to CI failures and review comments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [concept] The documentation covers permission modes, reviewing, sharing, archiving, and deleting sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [fact] GitHub authentication options include two distinct ways to connect GitHub. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [concept] The page details how sessions are isolated under the Security and isolation section. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [fact] Limitations include rate limits and platform restrictions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- [concept] Each cloud session is separated from your machine and other sessions via multiple layers including isolated virtual machines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [fact] In Anthropic-hosted environments, each session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed VM. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [concept] Self-hosted environment sessions run on the organization's own infrastructure rather than Anthropic-managed VMs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [fact] In self-hosted environments, isolation is the responsibility of the deployment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [concept] Network access controls limit or disable network access by default in Anthropic-hosted environments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [fact] In self-hosted environments, session egress is restricted at the organization's own network boundary. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [problem] When network access is disabled in Anthropic-hosted environments, Claude Code can still communicate with the Anthropic API, potentially allowing data to exit the VM. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [concept] Credential protection keeps git credentials and signing keys outside the sandbox in Anthropic-hosted environments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [fact] A proxy authenticates on behalf of the session using scoped credentials in Anthropic-hosted environments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [concept] In self-hosted environments, the deployment supplies git credentials rather than the system managing them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [fact] API credentials added to a cloud environment stay outside the sandbox and are attached to matching requests after they leave the session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [problem] Self-hosted environments do not have API credentials. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [concept] Code analysis and modification occur within the isolated session environment before PRs are created. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#security-and-isolation
- [fact] Claude Code on the web shares rate limits with all other Claude and Claude Code usage within your account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [problem] Running multiple tasks in parallel consumes more rate limits proportionately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [fact] There is no separate compute charge for the cloud VM used by Claude Code on the web. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [problem] You can only move sessions from web to local when you are authenticated to the same account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [fact] Repository cloning and pull request creation require GitHub. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [concept] Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server instances are supported for Team and Enterprise plans. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [problem] GitLab, Bitbucket, and other non-GitHub repositories can be sent to cloud sessions as a local bundle, but the session cannot push results back to the remote. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [problem] Cloud sessions call the Anthropic API from Anthropic-managed infrastructure, not your network. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [problem] If your organization has IP allowlisting enabled, every Anthropic-hosted cloud session fails with an authentication error. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [fact] The same IP allowlist restriction applies to Code Review and routines that run on Anthropic-hosted environments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [actionable] Contact Anthropic support to exempt Anthropic-hosted services from your organization's IP allowlist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#limitations
- [concept] Cloud environments configure network access, environment variables, and setup scripts for cloud sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources
- [concept] Ultrareview runs a deep multi-agent code review in a cloud sandbox. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources
- [concept] Routines automate work on a schedule, via API call, or in response to GitHub events. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources
- [concept] Hooks configuration runs scripts at session lifecycle events. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources
- [concept] Settings reference contains all configuration options available for the system. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources
- [fact] Security documentation covers isolation guarantees and data handling. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources
- [fact] Data usage documentation explains what Anthropic retains from cloud sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources
- [concept] Claude Tag is an organization-managed @Claude in Slack that runs on the same cloud infrastructure. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#related-resources

Holds snapshots for the 100 most recent checkpoints; snapshot files that no retained checkpoint references are deleted, except each file's first snapshot — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `plans/`: Plan files written during [plan mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#analyze-before-you-edit-with-plan-mode) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `debug/`: Per-session debug logs, written only when you start with `--debug` or run `/debug` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `paste-cache/`: Contents of large pastes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `image-cache/<session>/`: Attached images. On each sweep, Claude Code removes the directories of all other sessions, whatever their age. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `uploads/<session>/`: Files you attach from the web or mobile app, and photos you attach from the mobile app, when messaging a [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) session. An attachment to a [cloud session](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) is saved in that session's own cloud environment instead, not on your machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `session-env/`: Per-session environment metadata — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `tasks/`: Per-session task lists written by the task tools — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `shell-snapshots/`: Aliases, functions, and shell options captured at startup and applied by the [Bash tool](/docs/en/tools-reference#bash-tool-behavior) to each command. Removed on clean exit. The sweep clears any left after a crash. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `backups/`: Earlier versions of `~/.claude.json`, copied when Claude Code rewrites the file. Claude Code keeps the five newest, plus a copy of any version it couldn't parse. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `feedback-bundles/`: Redacted transcript archives written by `/feedback` on third-party providers or when no Anthropic credentials are configured, for sending to your Anthropic account team — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `feedback/drafts/`: Queued [Claude-drafted feedback](/docs/en/tools-reference#sendfeedback-tool-behavior) awaiting your review in `/feedback`. Swept after `cleanupPeriodDays` or 30 days, whichever is shorter. When the queue is at its 10-draft limit, Claude Code deletes the oldest draft to make room. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `usage-data/`: `report.html` and timestamped report copies written by [`/insights`](/docs/en/costs#analyze-your-usage-patterns), plus cached per-session analysis data used to build them — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `todos/`, `statsig/`, `logs/`: Legacy directories from older versions. No longer written. The sweep removes their contents and then the empty directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically
- [parameter] `history.jsonl`: Every prompt you've typed, with timestamp and project path. Used for up-arrow recall. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#kept-until-you-delete-them
- [parameter] `stats-cache.json`: Aggregated token and cost counts shown by `/usage` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#kept-until-you-delete-them
- [parameter] `remote-settings.json`: Cached copy of [server-managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings) for your organization, or `{}` when your organization has configured none. Only present when the session [fetches them](/docs/en/server-managed-settings#platform-availability). Claude Code checks for updates at startup and hourly during a session. Claude Code deletes it when you log out. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#kept-until-you-delete-them
- [parameter] `cache/changelog.md`: Cached copy of the Claude Code changelog, shown by `/release-notes`. Refreshed in the background. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#kept-until-you-delete-them
- [parameter] `policy-limits.json`: Cached feature policy settings for your organization. Only present for some account types. Refreshed automatically. Claude Code deletes it when you log out. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#kept-until-you-delete-them
- [parameter] `~/.claude/projects/`: Resume, continue, and rewind for past sessions, and auto memory for every project — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#clear-local-data

- [definition] Install the plugin — In a Claude Code session, install from the [official Anthropic marketplace](/docs/en/discover-plugins#official-anthropic-marketplace): — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#install-the-plugin

- [definition] Scan and fix your codebase — The plugin adds one command, `/claude-security`, which opens a menu of its three jobs: scanning the codebase, scanning a set of changes, and suggesting patches. The happy path runs a full scan, then turns its findings into patches: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#scan-and-fix-your-codebase
- [definition] Open the Claude Security menu — Run `/claude-security` and pick **Scan codebase**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#scan-and-fix-your-codebase
- [definition] Choose what to scan — The plugin reads your repository first, then offers the whole repository or a focused area, with each option's file count and relative cost stated. Pick the whole repository, or answer "I don't know" and the plugin picks a sensible default for your repository's size. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#scan-and-fix-your-codebase
- [definition] Confirm the run — A scan may take a while, may use a significant number of tokens, and needs Claude Code left open while it completes. Nothing runs until you confirm. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#scan-and-fix-your-codebase
- [definition] Read the report — While the scan runs, it reports each stage as it starts, with the detail available under [`/workflows`](/docs/en/workflows). - [definition] Apply the patches you accept — Apply each patch from your shell with `git apply`, in its own pull request. Patches are never applied automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#scan-and-fix-your-codebase
- [definition] Scan only your changes — When your branch has commits its base doesn't, the `/claude-security` menu offers to scan only that diff, so you can check a branch before merging. You can also scan one of your open pull requests, or a single commit by asking for it, such as "scan commit abc1234". — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#scan-only-your-changes
- [definition] Scope large repositories — On a large repository, scan one area at a time instead of the whole tree. Pick one of the focused scopes the plugin offers, such as your API layer or your authentication code, and the run sizes itself to what you pick. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#scope-large-repositories

- [definition] Fix findings — Start the fix flow by picking **Suggest patches** from the `/claude-security` menu, or ask in plain language, such as "fix finding F3", then pick which findings from the report to address. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#fix-findings
- [definition] Patches are never applied automatically — Applying a patch is always your decision. Patches land in the report's `patches/` folder, one `F<n>.patch` per finding with a note beside it explaining the change. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-security#patches-are-never-applied-automatically
