- [definition] Customize reviews — Code Review reads two files from your repository to guide what it flags. They differ in how strongly they influence the review: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [definition] CLAUDE.md — Code Review reads your repository's `CLAUDE.md` files and treats newly introduced violations as [nit-level](#severity-levels) findings. This works bidirectionally: if your PR changes code in a way that makes a `CLAUDE.md` statement outdated, Claude flags that the docs need updating too. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#claudemd
- [definition] REVIEW\.md — `REVIEW.md` is a file at your repository root that tailors Code Review to your repo. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#reviewmd
- [definition] View usage — Go to [claude.ai/analytics/code-review](https://claude.ai/analytics/code-review) to see Code Review activity across your organization. The dashboard shows: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#view-usage
- [definition] Pricing — Code Review is billed based on token usage. Each review averages \$15-25 in cost, scaling with PR size, codebase complexity, and how many issues require verification. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#pricing
- [definition] Troubleshooting — Review runs are best-effort. A failed run never blocks your PR, but it also doesn't retry on its own. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#troubleshooting
- [definition] Retrigger a failed or timed-out review — When the review infrastructure hits an internal error or exceeds its time limit, the check run completes with a title of **Code review encountered an error** or **Code review timed out**. The conclusion is still neutral, so nothing blocks your merge, but no findings are posted. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#retrigger-a-failed-or-timed-out-review
- [definition] Review didn't run and the PR shows a spend-cap message — When your organization's monthly spend cap is reached, Code Review posts a single comment on the PR explaining that the review was skipped. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#review-didnt-run-and-the-pr-shows-a-spend-cap-message
- [definition] Find issues that aren't showing as inline comments — If the check run title says issues were found but you don't see inline review comments on the diff, look in these other locations where findings are surfaced: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#find-issues-that-arent-showing-as-inline-comments
- [definition] Review a diff locally — The [`/code-review` command](/docs/en/commands) reviews a diff in your terminal without installing the GitHub App. It reports correctness bugs and reuse, simplification, and efficiency cleanups. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#review-a-diff-locally
- [definition] Run /code-review — From the session where you're working, run the command: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#review-a-diff-locally
- [definition] Keep working — The review runs as a background [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) with its own context window, so it doesn't fill your conversation. The findings arrive in your conversation when the review completes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#review-a-diff-locally
- [definition] Act on the findings — Ask Claude to fix what the review found. If you passed `--fix` or `--comment`, the review has already applied or posted its findings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#review-a-diff-locally
- [definition] What the review reads and edits — The review follows your `CLAUDE.md` like any Claude Code session, but it doesn't read [`REVIEW.md`](#review-md). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#what-the-review-reads-and-edits
- [definition] Tune effort and arguments — Pass an [effort level](/docs/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level) to trade coverage for confidence. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#tune-effort-and-arguments
- [definition] Run in the foreground — The review runs in the background by default; before v2.1.218, it ran inside your conversation. It runs in the foreground instead in cases like these: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#run-in-the-foreground
- [definition] Let Claude start the review — Claude can start `/code-review` on its own. Ask it to review your changes in plain language and it can run the skill without you typing the command, and a [scheduled task](/docs/en/scheduled-tasks) with `/code-review` as its prompt runs the review. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#let-claude-start-the-review
- [definition] Escalate to ultrareview — `/code-review ultra --fix` runs the deeper [ultrareview](/docs/en/ultrareview) in the cloud, then applies its findings to your working tree when they arrive back in your session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#escalate-to-ultrareview
- [concept] Code Review is an automated PR review feature using multi-agent analysis of the full codebase to catch logic errors, security vulnerabilities, and regressions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [fact] Code Review is in research preview and available only for Team and Enterprise subscriptions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [problem] The feature is not available for organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [actionable] Users on other plans can review a diff locally using the `/code-review` command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [concept] The system analyzes GitHub pull requests and posts findings as inline comments on specific lines of code where issues are found. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [concept] A fleet of specialized agents examines code changes within the context of the full codebase. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [fact] Findings are tagged by severity and do not approve or block pull requests, preserving existing review workflows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [idea] You can tune what Claude flags by adding a `CLAUDE.md` or `REVIEW.md` file to your repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [fact] For running Claude in your own CI infrastructure, refer to the GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD documentation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [fact] Repositories on a self-hosted GitHub instance should consult the GitHub Enterprise Server documentation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review
- [concept] Reviews trigger when a PR opens, on every push, or when manually requested, depending on the repository's configured behavior. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [actionable] Comment `@claude review` to start a review on a PR in any mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [concept] Multiple agents analyze the diff and surrounding code in parallel, then a verification step checks candidates against actual code behavior to filter false positives. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [fact] Results are deduplicated, ranked by severity, and posted as inline comments on specific lines with a summary in the review body. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [fact] If no issues are found, Code Review updates the GitHub check run to show that no issues were detected. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [fact] Reviews complete in 20 minutes on average and scale in cost with PR size and complexity. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [concept] Each finding is tagged with a severity level and includes a collapsible extended reasoning section to explain the flag and verification. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [fact] Clicking 👍 or 👎 on a review comment does not trigger a re-review or change anything on the PR. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [actionable] To request a fresh review without pushing, comment `@claude review` as a top-level PR comment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [fact] The check run always completes with a neutral conclusion so it never blocks merging through branch protection rules. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [actionable] List the commit's check runs with `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/<commit-sha>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | {id, name}'` to find the check run ID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [fact] The `normal` key in the machine-readable output holds the count of Important findings; a non-zero value means Claude found at least one bug worth fixing before merge. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [concept] By default, Code Review focuses on correctness: bugs that would break production, not formatting preferences or missing test coverage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [actionable] Expand what Code Review checks by adding guidance files to your repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#how-reviews-work
- [concept] An Owner enables Code Review once for an organization and selects which repositories to include. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] Users must have the Owner or Primary Owner role in their Claude organization and permission to install GitHub Apps in their GitHub organization. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [actionable] Go to claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code and find the Code Review section. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [actionable] Click Setup to begin the GitHub App installation flow. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [concept] To review a pull request, Claude reads repository contents via read access and posts comments and check runs via write access. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] During installation, you grant a broader permission set shared by other Claude features such as GitHub Actions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [actionable] Choose which repositories to enable for Code Review in the admin settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] If a repository does not appear, ensure you granted the Claude GitHub App access to it during installation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [concept] The Review Behavior dropdown allows choosing when reviews run for each repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] Once after PR creation runs a review once when a PR is opened or marked ready for review. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] After every push runs a review on every push to the PR branch, catching new issues and auto-resolving threads when fixed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] Manual mode requires commenting @claude review to request a review or @claude review always to subscribe the PR to reviews on subsequent pushes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] Claude reviews a pull request from a fork only when someone comments @claude review on it, regardless of trigger settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [idea] Reviewing on every push runs the most reviews and costs the most, while Manual mode is useful for high-traffic repos. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [fact] The repositories table shows the average cost per review for each repo based on recent activity. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [actionable] Use the row actions menu to turn Code Review on or off per repository, or to remove a repository entirely. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [actionable] Open a test PR to verify setup; if automatic trigger was chosen, a check run named Claude Code Review appears within a few minutes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [actionable] If Manual mode is chosen, comment @claude review on the PR to start the first review. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [problem] If no check run appears, confirm the repository is listed in admin settings and the Claude GitHub App has access to it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#set-up-code-review
- [concept] Code Review reads two files from the repository: CLAUDE.md for shared project context and REVIEW.md for review-only instructions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [fact] Violations of CLAUDE.md are treated as nit-level findings by default, but outdated statements in CLAUDE.md due to code changes are also flagged. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [concept] CLAUDE.md files are read at every level of the directory hierarchy, meaning rules in a subdirectory apply only to files under that path. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [fact] REVIEW.md is a file located at the repository root that tailors Code Review specifically for that repo. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [concept] Agents in the review pipeline use REVIEW.md alongside default guidance to find, verify, rank, and report findings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [problem] The @ import syntax is not expanded in REVIEW.md, and referenced files are not read along with it; rules must be written directly in the file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [idea] Redefine what 'Important' means for your repo to match its nature, such as narrowing the definition for docs or config repos. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [actionable] Cap nit volume by stating rules like 'report at most five nits, mention the rest as a count in the summary' to keep reviews actionable. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [idea] List paths, branch patterns, and finding categories to skip entirely, such as generated code, lockfiles, or vendored dependencies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [actionable] For paths requiring review but not full scrutiny, set a higher bar instead of skipping, e.g., 'in scripts/, only report if near-certain and severe.' — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [idea] Add repo-specific checks like 'new API routes must have an integration test' to ensure they land reliably on every PR. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [idea] Require evidence before posting findings, such as demanding a file:line citation for behavior claims to cut false positives. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [idea] Configure re-review convergence by suppressing new nits after the first review and posting only Important findings to prevent endless style rounds. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [actionable] Define summary shape by asking for a one-line tally like '2 factual, 4 style' at the start of the review body. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#customize-reviews
- [fact] Code Review activity across an organization can be viewed at claude.ai/analytics/code-review. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#view-usage
- [fact] Dashboard cost figures are estimates intended for monitoring activity rather than invoice-accurate spend. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#view-usage
- [actionable] Refer to your Anthropic bill for invoice-accurate spend information instead of the dashboard estimates. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#view-usage
- [actionable] Run `/code-review` in a local Claude Code session to check a diff before pushing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#related-resources
- [concept] GitHub Actions allows running Claude in custom workflows for automation beyond code review. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#related-resources
- [concept] GitLab CI/CD provides a self-hosted Claude integration for GitLab pipelines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#related-resources
- [concept] `CLAUDE.md` files define how Memory works across Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#related-resources
- [fact] Analytics tracks Claude Code usage beyond code review. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#related-resources
- [idea] Automated review serves as one layer within Anthropic's secure AI-native software development lifecycle. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#related-resources

- [snippet] Set CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER in settings: { — `{` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [definition] Run Claude Code behind a corporate launcher — Route the processes Claude Code starts from its own binary, including the background service and every agent view session, through a required launcher with CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER or the processWrapper setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#run-claude-code-behind-a-corporate-launcher
- [definition] What the launcher covers — With `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` set, Claude Code starts each of the following processes through your launcher: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [definition] Processes that start outside the launcher — The following processes don't start through the launcher: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#processes-that-start-outside-the-launcher
- [definition] Helper process names in process monitors — With a launcher configured, `ps` and Activity Monitor show the versioned binary name for the background helper processes instead of Claude Code's `claude bg-pty-host` and `claude bg-spare` labels, because the launcher's `exec` rebuilds the argument list. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#helper-process-names-in-process-monitors
- [definition] Write the launcher script — Create an executable script at an absolute path, such as `/opt/corp/launcher`. Claude Code runs it with the full Claude Code command as its arguments, and the script must end by calling `exec "$@"` so it replaces itself with Claude Code: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [definition] Set CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER in settings — Set the variable in the `env` block of a settings file so the detached background service inherits it. A shell `export` isn't enough: the background service starts on demand, outlives your shell, and never re-reads shell profiles. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [definition] Restart the background service and your sessions — A running background service and any open `claude` sessions read the variable once at startup, so they keep launching unwrapped processes until restarted. Run `claude daemon stop --any` to stop the on-demand service; the next command that needs it, such as `claude agents`, starts a wrapped one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [definition] Verify — Run `/status` in a session: the Self-exec entry shows the resolved launch command and warns when the running background service doesn't match it. `claude daemon status` prints the same information from the shell, including after you unset the variable, when `/status` no longer shows the entry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [definition] The launcher contract — When the launcher can't run, Claude Code refuses to start the process instead of starting it unwrapped. On Windows, [the variable is ignored](#what-the-launcher-covers) and processes start unwrapped. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#the-launcher-contract
- [definition] Format of the launcher value — `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` and the `processWrapper` setting take the same format. For most launchers, the value is the script's absolute path, like `/opt/corp/launcher`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#format-of-the-launcher-value
- [definition] Relationship to `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX` — `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` wraps Claude Code's own processes and passes the command through as separate argv tokens for the launcher to `exec`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#relationship-to-claude-code-shell-prefix
- [concept] CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER starts every process Claude Code launches from its own binary through a required launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher
- [fact] The wrapper applies to the background service, every agent view session, and relaunches after an update. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher
- [problem] A launcher wrapping the claude command on PATH cannot reach these processes because they start from the binary's direct path without looking up PATH. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher
- [fact] CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later; earlier versions ignore the variable and start every process unwrapped. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher
- [fact] The equivalent processWrapper setting requires v2.1.210 or later; earlier versions ignore it as an unknown key, apply no launcher, and report no error. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher
- [actionable] Set CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER to your launcher's absolute path so Claude Code runs the launcher with the command as arguments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher
- [idea] Use the Verify step after deploying either form to confirm the running version applies the launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher
- [concept] The launcher covers specific processes when the CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER environment variable is set. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] On Windows, the CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER variable is ignored because the launcher contract depends on exec, which Windows does not support. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [problem] If a launcher policy covers Windows, setting the variable does not satisfy it; machines with the variable set run every process unwrapped and only show a warning in the debug log. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] The background service that claude agents starts on demand is covered by the launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] Terminal hosts and Claude Code sessions inside every agent view row, including warm standby sessions, are covered by the launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] Sessions that the service respawns after an update or a crash are covered by the launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] The relaunch Claude Code performs of itself to finish installing an update, including the agent view's restart-for-update action, is covered by the launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] Session processes started by Remote Control are covered by the launcher, requiring Claude Code v2.1.210 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] Split-pane teammate sessions started by agent teams in tmux or iTerm2 are covered by the launcher, requiring Claude Code v2.1.210 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [problem] An installed background service whose unit was written before the launcher was configured starts via launchd or systemd from its unit file, not through the launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] /status and claude daemon status warn while the running service and the configured launcher do not match. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [actionable] To cover terminal sessions started by the user, put a script named claude in a directory earlier on PATH that runs your launcher with the real binary. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [problem] Do not replace the managed symlink when covering user-started sessions; self-spawns do not consult PATH, so two launchers never stack. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [problem] The first process of a claude-cli:// deep link starts directly via the operating system's protocol handler, bypassing the launcher. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [actionable] To close the deep link path entirely, prevent handler registration with the disableDeepLinkRegistration setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [problem] The relaunch performed by --worktree combined with --tmux starts via the terminal multiplexer, not Claude Code's binary. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [problem] The native-messaging host that Claude in Chrome registers is started by the browser, not Claude Code's binary. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [concept] With a launcher configured, ps and Activity Monitor show the versioned binary name for background helper processes instead of claude bg-pty-host or claude bg-spare labels. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] The renaming of process names in monitors is a side effect of the launcher's exec rebuilding the argument list, not concealment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [fact] Claude Code identifies its own processes by binary path, never by display name. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers
- [concept] The launcher script must end by calling `exec "$@"` to replace itself with Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] The launcher must be an executable script at an absolute path, such as `/opt/corp/launcher`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [problem] Replacing the `~/.local/bin/claude` symlink with a launcher causes the first wrapped session to start the background service through both launchers at once. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] When a symlink is replaced, auto-update leaves the file in place and cleanup of old versions stays disabled until the installer manages that path again. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [concept] The `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` variable must be set in the `env` block of a settings file so the detached background service inherits it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [problem] A shell `export` is insufficient because the background service starts on demand, outlives the shell, and never re-reads shell profiles. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] When more than one source sets the variable, the managed settings value overrides both `~/.claude/settings.json` and a value exported in the shell. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [concept] The `processWrapper` setting carries the same value as a named, top-level settings key and requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` takes precedence when both it and the `processWrapper` setting are set. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] An organization delivering `processWrapper` through remote managed settings sees it listed on the security approval dialog alongside other administrator-supplied executable settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [problem] Project and local settings cannot configure the launcher; Claude Code ignores `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` in `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` with a warning in the debug log. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [actionable] Run `claude daemon stop --any` to stop the on-demand service. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [actionable] Run `claude daemon status` from the shell to verify the resolved launch command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [actionable] Run `/status` in a session to see the Self-exec entry showing the resolved launch command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] An installed service requires `claude daemon stop` without the `--any` flag. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] On machines where a manual restart is not possible, the first session started after settings push retires a leftover unwrapped on-demand service automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [fact] An installed service always needs an explicit restart and will not retire automatically if no new session starts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#set-up-the-launcher
- [concept] CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER wraps Claude Code's own processes and passes commands through as separate argv tokens for the launcher to exec. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#relationship-to-claude-code-shell-prefix
- [concept] CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX wraps shell commands Claude runs on your behalf, such as Bash tool calls, hooks, and stdio MCP server start commands. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#relationship-to-claude-code-shell-prefix
- [fact] CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX passes each command as a single shell-quoted string in $1 for the wrapper to re-evaluate. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#relationship-to-claude-code-shell-prefix
- [problem] A launcher written for CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER does not work as CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX, and vice versa. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#relationship-to-claude-code-shell-prefix
- [concept] The Agent view covers background sessions and supervisor processes that the launcher manages. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#related-resources
- [fact] The `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` is a specific environment variable reference entry found in the Environment variables documentation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#related-resources
- [concept] Managed settings allow users to deliver an `env` block across a fleet of devices. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#related-resources
- [fact] The Launcher error reference contains refusal messages and recovery instructions specifically for `claude_code_process_wrapper-launcher-errors`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/corporate-launcher#related-resources

- [definition] Move instructions from CLAUDE.md to skills — Your [CLAUDE.md](/docs/en/memory) file is loaded into context at session start. If it contains detailed instructions for specific workflows (like PR reviews or database migrations), those tokens are present even when you're doing unrelated work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#move-instructions-from-claudemd-to-skills
- [definition] Adjust extended thinking — Extended thinking is enabled by default because it significantly improves performance on complex planning and reasoning tasks. Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens, and the default budget can be tens of thousands of tokens per request depending on the model. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#adjust-extended-thinking
- [definition] Delegate verbose operations to subagents — Running tests, fetching documentation, or processing log files can consume significant context. Delegate these to [subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents#isolate-high-volume-operations) so the verbose output stays in the subagent's context while only a summary returns to your main conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#delegate-verbose-operations-to-subagents
- [definition] Manage agent team costs — Agent teams use approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode, because each teammate maintains its own context window and runs as a separate Claude instance. Keep team tasks small and self-contained to limit per-teammate token usage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#manage-agent-team-costs
- [definition] Write specific prompts — Vague requests like "improve this codebase" trigger broad scanning. - [concept] Claude Code charges by API token consumption. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs

- [fact] The /compact command prints 'Not enough messages to compact.' in a fresh session because there is no conversation history to summarize yet. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Use /clear to start fresh when switching to unrelated work, and use /rename before clearing to easily find the session later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [fact] Sonnet costs less than Opus, while Opus is reserved for complex architectural decisions or multi-step reasoning. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Use /model to switch models mid-session or set a default in /config, and specify model: haiku for simple subagent tasks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [concept] MCP tool definitions are deferred by default, meaning only tool names and server instructions enter context until a specific tool is used. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [problem] CLI tools like gh, aws, gcloud, and sentry-cli are more context-efficient than MCP servers because they do not add per-tool listing overhead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Run /mcp to see configured servers and disable any you are not actively using to reduce context overhead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [concept] Code intelligence plugins provide precise symbol navigation instead of text-based search, reducing unnecessary file reads when exploring unfamiliar code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [fact] A single 'go to definition' call replaces what might otherwise be a grep followed by reading multiple candidate files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Create the folder ~/.claude/hooks, save filter-test-output.sh there, and make it executable with chmod +x ~/.claude/hooks/filter-test-output.sh. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Verify the hook setup by running /hooks to check it appears under PreToolUse, or start Claude Code with claude --debug-file ./claude-debug.txt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [problem] Detailed instructions in CLAUDE.md are loaded into context at session start, consuming tokens even during unrelated work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [idea] Move specialized instructions from CLAUDE.md to skills so they load on-demand only when invoked, keeping the base context smaller. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [fact] Aim to keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines by including only essentials to minimize token usage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [concept] Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens, and the default budget can be tens of thousands of tokens per request depending on the model. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Reduce costs by lowering the effort level with /effort or in /model, disabling thinking in /config, or setting MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=8000. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [problem] Disabling thinking is not available on Fable 5, which always uses extended thinking regardless of configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [concept] Delegate verbose operations like running tests or fetching documentation to subagents so the output stays in the subagent's context while only a summary returns. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [fact] Agent teams use approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode due to separate context windows and instances. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [problem] Vague requests like 'improve this codebase' trigger broad scanning, whereas specific requests allow efficient work with minimal file reads. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Press Shift+Tab to cycle to plan mode before implementation to explore the codebase and propose an approach for approval. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [actionable] Press Escape to stop immediately if Claude heads in the wrong direction, or use /rewind to restore conversation and code to a previous checkpoint. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#reduce-token-usage
- [concept] Claude Code uses tokens for background functionality even when idle. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#background-token-usage
- [fact] Background jobs summarize previous conversations to enable the `claude --resume` feature. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#background-token-usage
- [fact] Commands like `/usage` may generate requests to check status during background processing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#background-token-usage
- [fact] These background processes typically consume under $0.04 per session even without active interaction. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#background-token-usage
- [concept] Claude Code sends the full conversation history with every request and includes tool results in subsequent requests when tools are used. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [fact] With prompt caching enabled, Claude Code re-reads the full history at the cached token rate even for single-line questions in long sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [problem] A cache miss occurs when a message is sent after a break longer than the cache lifetime, forcing reprocessing of the full context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [fact] The default cache lifetime is one hour on subscriptions and five minutes when drawing on usage credits. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [fact] For API keys or cloud provider usage, the default cache lifetime is five minutes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [actionable] To maintain a one-hour cache lifetime while using usage credits, you must choose the TTL yourself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [concept] On Pro and Max plans, Claude Code offers to resume a large session from a summary after a long break to avoid sending full history. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [problem] Scheduled tasks fire on their interval even while the session is idle, sending the full context each time. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [concept] Cross-session messages are delivered as new turns when a session sits idle, triggering a request with the full context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [actionable] To hold inbound cross-session messages instead of delivering them, set `crossSessionInbound` to `hold`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [problem] Goal check-ins occur while background work is active, asking Claude to check on the work even when the session is idle. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [fact] Claude Code performs at most three idle check-ins per goal between prompts, a limit introduced in version v2.1.246. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [actionable] To turn off idle goal check-ins, set the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES` to `0`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [fact] Idle check-ins require Claude Code version v2.1.236 or later to function. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [problem] Each active agent teammate continues consuming tokens until it exits the session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [concept] The `/compact` command reads the conversation to summarize it, making compaction of large contexts a large request itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [fact] The `/clear` command costs nothing and is used when a fresh start is desired instead of continuity. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [idea] On Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plans, the `/usage` command flags behaviors accounting for 10% or more of recent usage with reduction tips. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#why-usage-climbs-in-a-long-session
- [concept] Claude Code regularly receives updates that may change how features work, including cost reporting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#understanding-changes-in-claude-code-behavior
- [actionable] Run `claude --version` to check your current version. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#understanding-changes-in-claude-code-behavior
- [fact] For billing questions about a specific account, users should contact Anthropic support through the in-product messenger. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#understanding-changes-in-claude-code-behavior
- [actionable] Subscription plan users (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) can sign in at claude.ai, click their initials in the lower left, and select Get help. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#understanding-changes-in-claude-code-behavior

- [parameter] On this machine: Over a per-session socket on macOS and Linux, or a per-session named pipe on native Windows, never through Anthropic servers — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-sessions-on-other-machines
- [parameter] On another of your machines: Through Anthropic servers, arriving over that machine's [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) connection — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-sessions-on-other-machines
- [parameter] On [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web): Through Anthropic servers, straight to the cloud session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-sessions-on-other-machines
- [parameter] `accept`: Claude Code delivers each message to Claude — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#control-inbound-messages
- [parameter] `hold`: Claude Code shows a notice for each message and doesn't deliver it. If an `accept` later applies, per the [precedence rules](/docs/en/settings-reference#crosssessioninbound), Claude Code releases the held messages — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#control-inbound-messages
- [parameter] `refuse`: Claude Code drops each message without delivering it — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#control-inbound-messages
- [definition] Message your other Claude Code sessions — Let Claude list and message your other Claude Code sessions on this machine, and reach your sessions on other machines or on the web. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-your-other-claude-code-sessions
- [definition] When to use cross-session messaging — Use messaging when one of your sessions has something another session needs mid-task. Claude can send a message on its own when it sees the need, for example after making a change that affects work another session is doing, or you can ask it to send one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#when-to-use-cross-session-messaging
- [definition] Message another session — When one of your sessions learns something another session needs, such as a finding, a status, or a decision, Claude passes it along instead of you copy-pasting between terminals. Claude discovers the target with `ListAgents` and sends with `SendMessage`, so you never call either tool yourself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [definition] Message delivery — The receiving Claude reads the message between tool calls during an active turn, so a running tool is never interrupted. When the receiving session is idle, Claude Code starts a new turn with the message. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-delivery
- [definition] Get a notice when another session goes idle — Claude can ask one of your sessions on this machine to send back one notice when that session next goes idle or exits. Idle here means the session finished a turn with nothing queued. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#get-a-notice-when-another-session-goes-idle
- [definition] See which sessions Claude can reach — Claude finds a message's target on its own, so you don't need to run anything before asking it to send. To see for yourself which sessions Claude can reach, run the `/list-agents` command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#see-which-sessions-claude-can-reach
- [definition] Message sessions on other machines — How a message travels, and whether it passes through Anthropic servers, depends on where the target session runs: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-sessions-on-other-machines
- [definition] How a session treats an incoming message — When session A messages session B, Claude Code tells B's Claude that the message came from another session, not from you, and limits what the message can do: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#how-a-session-treats-an-incoming-message
- [definition] What a message looks like — When a message arrives, Claude Code shows it in the conversation as a dim one-line preview, and the preview line stays in the conversation afterward. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#what-a-message-looks-like
- [definition] Control inbound messages — Set [`crossSessionInbound`](/docs/en/settings-reference#crosssessioninbound) to choose what a session does with messages arriving from your other sessions: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#control-inbound-messages
- [definition] Non-interactive sessions — Claude Code binds an inbox socket for a [`claude -p`](/docs/en/headless) session like an interactive one, so a long-running `-p` worker can receive messages and appears in the listing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#non-interactive-sessions
- [definition] The session's inbox socket — Read this section when a session you expect isn't in the agent list, when you want a script or hook to post into a session, or when a sandboxed command can't reach the socket. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#the-sessions-inbox-socket
- [definition] Restrict cross-session messaging — Beyond the per-message defaults, you can narrow messaging in two ways. Require your approval before any message leaves the machine, or turn messaging off for a session or an organization. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#restrict-cross-session-messaging
- [definition] Require approval for cross-machine messages — Set [`isolatePeerMachines`](/docs/en/settings-reference#isolatepeermachines) to `true` to require your explicit approval before any `SendMessage` reaches a session beyond this machine: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#require-approval-for-cross-machine-messages
- [definition] Turn off cross-session messaging — Receiving and sending are separate controls, so turn off whichever direction you need, or both. Use `crossSessionInbound` for messages that arrive, and permission rules for what Claude here can send or list: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#turn-off-cross-session-messaging
- [definition] Availability — Cross-session messaging requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later on macOS, Linux, and WSL 2, and v2.1.234 or later on native Windows. Availability, and which sessions Claude can message, also depend on your operating system, provider, and configuration: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#availability
- [definition] Limitations — The limits here are properties of the messaging channel itself and apply wherever the feature runs. For platform and provider gaps, see [Availability](#availability) instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [concept] Claude addresses a message on a name alone if exactly one live session answers to that name. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [concept] If several sessions share a name or Claude cannot check everywhere, it adds a short identifier to each row and uses that identifier in the address. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [fact] Starting a conversation with a session on another machine requires Claude Code v2.1.225 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [fact] Before version v2.1.225, Claude could only reply to a message that arrived from one of the sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [concept] Same-machine delivery works by having each session register itself in files on disk. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [problem] A container has its own filesystem, so a session inside it and a session on the host cannot reach each other. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [fact] Two sessions inside the same container can message each other, including on a self-hosted runner. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [problem] A session inside WSL 2 and a native Windows session on the same computer cannot reach each other because they register under different home directories and listen on different socket types. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [fact] When a session is connected to Remote Control, messages sent to another machine appear in that remote session's conversation under the Remote Control name of the sending session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [problem] If the sending session is not connected to Remote Control when messaging beyond its machine, the message goes through but lacks a reply address, so the receiving Claude cannot answer it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [actionable] Set `isolatePeerMachines` to require approval before any message goes beyond this machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#message-another-session
- [fact] Claude sends only plain text across sessions; structured agent team protocol messages stay within a team. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [fact] Serialized messages to a session on the same machine are refused if they exceed about one million characters. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [problem] Before version v2.1.236, Claude Code reported rapid burst sends as successful even when the receiving session dropped them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [fact] The receiving session rate-limits repeated messages per sender and drops identical repeats arriving within a short window. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [fact] The receiving session queues at most 50 accepted messages for Claude to read. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [problem] Rapid bursts of messages to a session on the same machine are refused once the session's inbox limit is reached. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [fact] When a message loop stops due to throttling, Claude Code identifies which specific message was dropped. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [actionable] If a rapid burst is refused, batch the remaining messages into one message or wait before resending. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [fact] The refusal for oversized messages names the exact sizes in the error documentation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [fact] When a message is dropped from an interactive session due to throttling, Claude Code instructs the sender not to resend immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#limitations
- [concept] Subagents and agent teams support messaging within a single session or team. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#related-resources
- [concept] Background agents allow dispatching and monitoring parallel sessions that can be messaged. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#related-resources
- [concept] Remote Control connects a session to reach sessions on other machines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#related-resources
- [fact] The `crossSessionInbound`, `isolatePeerMachines`, and `dialogExpiry` settings are available in the Settings reference. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#related-resources
- [concept] Permission modes define the two classes behind the inbound default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#related-resources
- [fact] The Tools reference includes `ListAgents` and `SendMessage` rows in the tools table. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#related-resources
- [concept] The Run agents in parallel documentation compares ways Claude Code runs multiple agents. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#related-resources

Transcripts shared via `/feedback`, or via `/bug` and `/share`, which report through the same path, are retained for 5 years. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#feedback-using-the-feedback-command
- [definition] Session quality surveys — When you see the "How is Claude doing this session?" prompt in Claude Code, responding to this survey, including selecting "Dismiss", records only your rating. We do not collect or store any conversation transcripts, inputs, outputs, or other session data as part of the rating prompt itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#session-quality-surveys
- [definition] Data retention — Anthropic retains Claude Code data based on your account type and preferences. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#data-retention
- [definition] Data access — For all first party users, you can learn more about what data is logged for [local Claude Code](#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies) and [remote Claude Code](#cloud-execution-data-flow-and-dependencies). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#data-access
- [definition] Local Claude Code: Data flow and dependencies — The diagram below shows how Claude Code connects to external services during installation and normal operation. Solid lines indicate required connections, while dashed lines represent optional or user-initiated data flows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [definition] Cloud execution: Data flow and dependencies — When using [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web), sessions run in Anthropic-managed virtual machines by default instead of locally. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#cloud-execution-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [definition] Telemetry services — Claude Code sends two kinds of operational telemetry: usage metrics and error reports. You can turn each off individually with the environment variables below, or disable all non-essential traffic at once by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [definition] Default behaviors by API provider — By default, error reporting, telemetry, and bug reporting are disabled when using Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or Claude Platform on AWS. Session quality surveys and the WebFetch domain safety check are exceptions and run regardless of provider. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [definition] WebFetch domain safety check — Before fetching a URL, the WebFetch tool sends the requested hostname to `api.anthropic.com` to check it against a safety blocklist maintained by Anthropic. Only the hostname is sent, not the full URL, path, or page contents. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#webfetch-domain-safety-check
- [fact] Remote Control sessions follow the local data flow since all execution happens on your machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#data-access
- [fact] While connected, the session transcript is stored on Anthropic servers to sync the conversation across devices. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#data-access
- [concept] For remote Claude Code, Claude accesses the repository where you initiate your Claude Code session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#data-access
- [problem] Claude does not access repositories that you have connected but have not started a session in. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#data-access
- [concept] The diagram illustrates how Claude Code connects to external services during installation and normal operation. Solid lines indicate required connections, while dashed lines represent optional or user-initiated data flows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [fact] Claude Code runs locally by default. To interact with the LLM, it sends data over the network including all user prompts and model outputs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [fact] Data sent to the LLM is encrypted in transit via TLS 1.2+. Claude Code is compatible with most popular VPNs and LLM proxies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [concept] Encryption at rest depends on your model provider. For details on API security controls, including API logging procedures, see the compliance artifacts in the Anthropic Trust Center. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [fact] When using Claude Code on the web, sessions run in Anthropic-managed virtual machines by default instead of locally. Sessions routed to a self-hosted environment run on infrastructure you control. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [fact] In cloud sessions, your repository is cloned to an isolated VM. Code and session data are subject to the retention and usage policies for your account type. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [fact] GitHub authentication is handled through a secure proxy in cloud sessions. Your GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [fact] All outbound traffic from cloud sessions goes through a security proxy for audit logging and abuse prevention. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [fact] In cloud sessions, prompts, code changes, and outputs follow the same data policies as local Claude Code usage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [concept] For what stays on your machines and what still goes to Anthropic in self-hosted environments, refer to the 'What stays on your infrastructure' section. For security details about cloud execution, see the Security documentation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#local-claude-code-data-flow-and-dependencies
- [concept] Claude Code sends two kinds of operational telemetry: usage metrics and error reports. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Setting DISABLE_TELEMETRY or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC disables the feature-flag evaluation that Remote Control depends on, but DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING does not. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Metrics include latency, reliability, and usage patterns sent to Anthropic and third-party logging infrastructure over TLS. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Metrics never include your code, prompts, or file paths. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [actionable] Set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to opt out of usage metrics. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Error reports contain error messages and stack traces from Claude Code's internals sent to a third-party service over TLS. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Claude Code redacts known patterns of secrets, file paths, email addresses, and other personal information before sending error reports. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [actionable] Set DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1 to opt out of error reporting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Error reporting is enabled only when the user has a Claude Pro or Max subscription, runs v2.1.198 or later, connects directly to the Claude API, and lacks a zero data retention or HIPAA agreement. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] The /feedback command sends conversation history including code to Anthropic via TLS and stores it in Google Cloud Storage encrypted at rest. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [actionable] Set DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1 to opt out of the /feedback, /bug, and /share commands. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] When using a third-party provider like Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform, /feedback writes reports to ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ instead of sending them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Reports written to the local archive redact known API key and token patterns before storage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [problem] When using a third-party provider, nothing leaves your machine until you manually send the file to an Anthropic representative or attach it to a support request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services
- [fact] Error reporting, telemetry, and bug reporting are disabled by default for Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and Claude Platform on AWS. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] Session quality surveys and the WebFetch domain safety check run regardless of the model provider used. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [problem] On a signed-in Claude apps gateway session, usage analytics, error reporting, and survey ratings are disabled by the credential itself with no setting to re-enable them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [actionable] Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` to opt out of all non-essential traffic including surveys at once. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] The `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` variable does not affect the WebFetch check or official plugin marketplace auto-install. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [actionable] Set `skipWebFetchPreflight` in settings to opt out of the WebFetch domain safety check. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [actionable] Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL` to opt out of official plugin marketplace auto-install. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] When a host platform sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST`, metrics default to on for Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, and Claude Platform on AWS. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] When `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST` is set, error reporting and `/feedback` reports remain off by default on those providers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [concept] The WebFetch tool sends the requested hostname to `api.anthropic.com` to check it against a safety blocklist before fetching a URL. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] Only the hostname is sent during the WebFetch check, not the full URL, path, or page contents. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] Claude Code caches a hostname that passes the WebFetch check for five minutes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] The WebFetch tool re-checks a blocked or failed hostname on the next request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [problem] If your network blocks `api.anthropic.com`, WebFetch requests fail until you allowlist the domain or set `skipWebFetchPreflight: true`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [idea] Combine disabling the WebFetch check with [`WebFetch` permission rules](/docs/en/permissions#webfetch) if you need to restrict which domains Claude can reach. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider
- [fact] All environment variables mentioned can be checked into `settings.json`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#default-behaviors-by-api-provider

- [parameter] Hook never fires: Cause=`matcher` is a JSON array instead of a string; Fix=Use a single string with `\|` to match multiple tools, for example `"Edit\|Write"`. See [matcher patterns](/docs/en/hooks#matcher-patterns). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Hook never fires: Cause=`matcher` uses `,` as a separator on a version before v2.1.191; Fix=Claude Code v2.1.191 or later treats `,` as a list separator like `\|`. Earlier versions evaluate a comma as a literal character, so `"Edit,Write"` matches nothing. Use `\|` instead, or upgrade Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Hook never fires: Cause=`matcher` value is lowercase, for example `"bash"`; Fix=Matching is case-sensitive. Tool names are capitalized: `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Read`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Hook never fires: Cause=Hooks are defined in a standalone file instead of `settings.json`; Fix=There is no standalone hooks file for project or user config. Define hooks under the `"hooks"` key in `settings.json`. Only [plugins](/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks) load a separate `hooks/hooks.json`. See [hook configuration](/docs/en/hooks). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Permissions, hooks, or env set globally are ignored: Cause=Configuration was added to `~/.claude.json`; Fix=`~/.claude.json` holds app state and UI toggles. `permissions`, `hooks`, and `env` belong in `~/.claude/settings.json`. These are two different files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] A `settings.json` value seems ignored: Cause=The same key is set in `settings.local.json`; Fix=`settings.local.json` overrides `settings.json`, and both override `~/.claude/settings.json`. See [settings precedence](/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Skill doesn't appear in `/skills`: Cause=Skill file is at `.claude/skills/name.md` instead of in a folder; Fix=Use a folder with `SKILL.md` inside: `.claude/skills/name/SKILL.md`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Skill appears in `/skills` but Claude never invokes it: Cause=Skill has `disable-model-invocation: true` in its frontmatter, or its description doesn't match how you phrase the request; Fix=Check the badge in `/skills`: a "user-only" label means Claude won't trigger it on its own. See [skill invocation](/docs/en/skills). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` instructions seem ignored: Cause=Subdirectory files load on demand, not at session start; Fix=They load when Claude reads a file in that directory with the Read tool, not at launch and not when writing or creating files there. See [how CLAUDE.md files load](/docs/en/memory#how-claude-md-files-load). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Subagent ignores `CLAUDE.md` instructions: Cause=The built-in Explore and Plan agents skip `CLAUDE.md`. Custom subagents load it the same way the main conversation does; Fix=For Explore or Plan, restate the instruction in your delegating prompt. For a custom subagent, put critical instructions in the agent file body, which becomes the agent's system prompt. - [parameter] Cleanup logic never runs at session end: Cause=No `SessionEnd` hook configured; Fix=Add a `SessionEnd` hook in `settings.json`. See the [hook events list](/docs/en/hooks#hook-events). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] MCP servers in `.mcp.json` never load: Cause=File is under `.claude/`, or its servers sit under a top-level `servers` key, as in VS Code's `mcp.json`, instead of `mcpServers`; Fix=Project MCP config goes at the repository root as `.mcp.json`, not inside `.claude/`, with servers under the `mcpServers` key. See [MCP configuration](/docs/en/mcp). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] MCP servers added under `mcpServers` in `settings.json` never appear: Cause=`settings.json` does not read an `mcpServers` key; Fix=Define project servers in `.mcp.json` at the repository root, or run `claude mcp add --scope user` for user-scoped servers. See [MCP configuration](/docs/en/mcp). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] Project MCP server added but doesn't appear: Cause=The one-time approval prompt was dismissed; Fix=Project-scoped servers require approval. Run `/mcp` to see status and approve. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] MCP server fails to start from some directories: Cause=`command` or `args` uses a relative file path; Fix=Use absolute paths for local scripts. Executables on your `PATH` like `npx` or `uvx` work as-is. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] MCP server starts without expected environment variables: Cause=The server's config entry doesn't set them, and they aren't in the environment Claude Code passes to stdio servers: its own environment, minus the [variables it strips from subprocesses](/docs/en/monitoring-usage#administrator-configuration); Fix=Set per-server `env` inside the server's `.mcp.json` entry, which doesn't depend on the… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes
- [parameter] `Bash(rm *)` deny rule doesn't block `/bin/rm` or `find -delete`: Cause=Prefix rules match the literal command string, not the underlying executable; Fix=Add explicit patterns for each variant, or use a [PreToolUse hook](/docs/en/hooks-guide) or the [sandbox](/docs/en/sandboxing) for a hard guarantee. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config#check-common-causes

- [fact] Managed settings apply first when present; among the rest, the closer scope overrides the broader one in the order local, then project, then user. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config

- [fact] Project-scoped servers in .mcp.json require a one-time approval; if the prompt was dismissed, the server stays disabled until you approve it from /mcp. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [problem] Relative file paths in command or args for MCP servers resolve against the directory you launched Claude Code from rather than the location of .mcp.json. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [actionable] Run `claude --debug=mcp` and read the server's stderr in the debug log at ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt if an MCP server shows as connected but lists zero tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [fact] Hooks go under the "hooks" key in a settings file, not in a standalone file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [problem] Before v2.1.191, a comma separator in the matcher field fell through to regex evaluation and the matcher never matched; use | if you aren't on v2.1.191 yet. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [problem] An array value in the matcher field is a schema error that causes Claude Code to reject the whole settings file and drop the hooks key from managed settings files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [fact] Edits to settings.json take effect in the running session after a brief file-stability delay without needing a restart. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [actionable] Start a session with `claude --debug` and trigger the tool call to watch hook evaluation live in the debug log. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [actionable] Use `claude --safe-mode` to launch a session with all customizations disabled, including CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, and custom commands. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [fact] Safe mode still applies managed hooks and settings policy from your organization, but turns off managed plugins, skills, CLAUDE.md, and MCP servers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [actionable] Point CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at an empty directory to bypass everything under ~/.claude and launch from a directory that has no .claude folder, .mcp.json, or CLAUDE.md. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [fact] On Linux and Windows, you'll be prompted to log in again when using a clean configuration directory because credentials are stored under the configuration directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [fact] On macOS, credentials are in the Keychain and carry over to the clean session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [idea] Use CLAUDE.md for guidance on how your project works, while using permissions or hooks for security boundaries and anything that must never happen. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config
- [problem] Adherence drops when an instruction is vague enough to interpret multiple ways, when two files give conflicting direction, or when the file has grown long enough that individual rules get less attention. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config

Use `%0A` for line breaks in multi-line prompts. Maximum 5,000 characters. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#build-a-link
- [parameter] `cwd`: Absolute path to use as the working directory. Network and UNC paths are rejected, and so are paths that contain invisible or bidirectional control characters. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#build-a-link
- [parameter] `repo`: A GitHub `owner/name` slug. Claude Code resolves it to a local clone it has seen before and starts there. If you have no matching clone, the session opens in your home directory instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#build-a-link
