- [parameter] Linux: `claude-code-url-handler.desktop` under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/applications`, defaulting to `~/.local/share/applications` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#registration-and-supported-platforms
- [parameter] Windows: `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\claude-cli` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#registration-and-supported-platforms
- [definition] Launch sessions from links — Open a Claude Code terminal session from a URL. Embed `claude-cli://` links in runbooks, alerts, and dashboards so a click opens Claude Code in the right repo with the right prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#launch-sessions-from-links
- [definition] How deep links work — The `claude-cli://` prefix is a custom URL scheme that Claude Code registers with your operating system, similar to how `mailto:` links open your email client. When you click a deep link: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#how-deep-links-work
- [definition] What a launched session shows — A deep link never executes anything on its own. The link only chooses a directory and fills the prompt box. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#what-a-launched-session-shows
- [definition] Build a link — Every deep link starts with `claude-cli://open`, which is the only path the handler accepts, followed by optional query parameters. The minimal form opens Claude Code in your home directory with an empty prompt: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#build-a-link
- [definition] Choose between `cwd` and `repo` — Use `cwd` when everyone who clicks the link has the project at the same absolute path, such as a standardized devcontainer or VM image. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#choose-between-cwd-and-repo
- [definition] Examples — The sections below show two common ways to use a deep link: as a Markdown link in a document and as a command in a script or shell alias. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#examples
- [definition] Embed a link in a runbook — A deep link in a runbook gives whoever is triaging a one-click way to start investigating in the right repository with a prepared prompt. The platform that renders the runbook must allow custom URL schemes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#embed-a-link-in-a-runbook
- [definition] Open a link from the shell — You can also open a deep link from a shell script, alias, or automation rather than by clicking it. Call your operating system's URL-opening command with the link as the argument. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#open-a-link-from-the-shell
- [definition] Registration and supported platforms — Claude Code registers the `claude-cli://` handler with your operating system on macOS, Linux, and Windows when you send your first prompt of an interactive session. Starting `claude` and exiting without sending a prompt doesn't register the handler. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#registration-and-supported-platforms
- [definition] Open a VS Code tab instead of a terminal — The VS Code extension registers its own handler at `vscode://anthropic.claude-code/open`, which opens a Claude Code editor tab rather than a terminal window. See [Launch a VS Code tab from other tools](/docs/en/vs-code#launch-a-vs-code-tab-from-other-tools) for that URL's parameters. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#open-a-vs-code-tab-instead-of-a-terminal
- [definition] Clicking the link does nothing — The handler likely isn't registered yet. Registration happens when you send your first prompt of an interactive session, not when the session starts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#clicking-the-link-does-nothing
- [definition] xdg-open is not found on Linux — The `xdg-open` command is part of the `xdg-utils` package, which minimal server images, containers, and WSL distributions often leave out. Install `xdg-utils` with your distribution's package manager, for example `sudo apt install xdg-utils`, then run the command again. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#xdg-open-is-not-found-on-linux
- [definition] The link renders as plain text instead of being clickable — Some Markdown renderers only allow `http` and `https` links and strip other URL schemes. GitHub does this in READMEs, issues, pull requests, and wikis: `[label](claude-cli://...)` renders as just `label`, with no link and the URL removed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#the-link-renders-as-plain-text-instead-of-being-clickable
- [definition] The session opens in my home directory instead of the repo — The `repo` parameter only resolves to clones Claude Code has already seen. Run `claude` inside the clone once so Claude Code records its path, or switch the link to use `cwd` with an absolute path. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#the-session-opens-in-my-home-directory-instead-of-the-repo
- [definition] The link opens the wrong terminal — On macOS, start `claude` in your preferred terminal once and the next deep link will use it. On Linux, set the `$TERMINAL` environment variable to your preferred emulator's command name. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#the-link-opens-the-wrong-terminal
- [definition] Learn more — These pages cover related ways to launch or extend Claude Code sessions: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links#learn-more

On macOS and Windows, download or update at [claude.com/download](https://claude.com/download); on Linux, update through your package manager ([instructions](/docs/en/desktop-linux)). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#enable-computer-use
- [definition] Turn on the toggle — In the desktop app, go to **Settings > General** (under **Desktop app**). Find the **Computer use** toggle and turn it on. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#enable-computer-use
- [definition] Grant macOS permissions — On macOS, grant two system permissions before the toggle takes effect: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#enable-computer-use
- [definition] App permissions — The first time Claude needs to use an app, a prompt appears in your session. Click **Allow for this session** or **Deny**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#app-permissions
- [definition] Manage sessions — Each session is an independent conversation with its own context and changes. You can run multiple sessions in parallel, branch off side chats, let Claude check on and message your other sessions, send work to the cloud, or let Dispatch start sessions for you from your phone. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#manage-sessions
- [definition] Work in parallel with sessions — Click **+ New session** in the sidebar, or press **Cmd+N** on macOS or **Ctrl+N** on Windows, to work on multiple tasks in parallel. Press **Ctrl+Tab** and **Ctrl+Shift+Tab** to cycle through sessions in the sidebar. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions
- [definition] Ask a side question without derailing the session — A side chat lets you ask Claude a question that uses your session's context but doesn't add anything back to the main conversation. Use it when you want to understand a piece of code, check an assumption, or explore an idea without steering the session off course. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#ask-a-side-question-without-derailing-the-session
- [definition] Watch background tasks — The tasks pane shows the background work running inside the current session: subagents, background shell commands, and [dynamic workflows](/docs/en/workflows). Open it from the **Views** menu or drag it into your layout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#watch-background-tasks
- [definition] Work across sessions — Claude can list your other Code tab sessions, read what each has been doing, and send messages between them. Ask in plain language: "which session touched the auth refactor?", "what did the API session conclude?", or "tell the payments session the schema changed". — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#work-across-sessions
- [definition] Run long-running tasks remotely — For large refactors, test suites, migrations, or other long-running tasks, select **Cloud** instead of **Local** when starting a session. Cloud sessions run on Anthropic-managed infrastructure by default and continue even if you close the app or shut down your computer. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#run-long-running-tasks-remotely
- [definition] Continue in another surface — The **Continue in** menu, accessible from the VS Code icon in the bottom right of the session toolbar, lets you move your session to another surface: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#continue-in-another-surface
- [definition] Sessions from Dispatch — [Dispatch](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13947068) is a persistent conversation with Claude that lives in the [Cowork](https://claude.com/product/cowork) tab. You message Dispatch a task, and it decides how to handle it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#sessions-from-dispatch
- [definition] Extend Claude Code — Connect external services, add reusable workflows, customize Claude's behavior, and configure preview servers. To manage connectors, skills, and plugins in one place, click **Customize** in the sidebar. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#extend-claude-code
- [definition] Connect external tools — For local and [SSH](#ssh-sessions) sessions, click the **+** button next to the prompt box and select **Connectors** to add integrations like Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and more. You can add connectors before or during a session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#connect-external-tools
- [definition] Use skills — [Skills](/docs/en/skills) extend what Claude can do. Claude loads them automatically when relevant, or you can invoke one directly: type `/` in the prompt box or click the **+** button and select **Slash commands** to browse what's available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#use-skills
- [definition] Install plugins — [Plugins](/docs/en/plugins) are reusable packages that add skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and LSP configurations to Claude Code. You can install plugins from the desktop app without using the terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#install-plugins
- [definition] Configure preview servers — Claude automatically detects your dev server setup and stores the configuration in `.claude/launch.json` at the root of the folder you selected when starting the session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#configure-preview-servers
- [definition] Environment configuration — The environment you pick when [starting a session](#start-a-session) determines where Claude executes and how you connect: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#environment-configuration
- [definition] Local sessions — The desktop app does not always inherit your full shell environment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#local-sessions
- [definition] Cloud sessions — Cloud sessions continue in the background even if you close the app. Usage counts toward your [subscription plan limits](/docs/en/costs) with no separate compute charges. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#cloud-sessions
- [definition] SSH sessions — SSH sessions let you run Claude Code on a remote machine while using the desktop app as your interface. This is useful for working with codebases that live on cloud VMs, dev containers, or servers with specific hardware or dependencies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#ssh-sessions
- [definition] Enterprise configuration — Organizations on Team or Enterprise plans can manage desktop app behavior through admin console controls, managed settings files, and device management policies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#enterprise-configuration
- [definition] Admin console controls — These settings are configured through the [admin settings console](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code): — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#admin-console-controls
- [definition] Managed settings — Managed settings override project and user settings and apply to Claude Code sessions in Desktop. You can set these keys in your organization's [managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings) file or push them remotely through the admin console. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#managed-settings
- [definition] Device management policies — IT teams can manage the desktop app through MDM on macOS or group policy on Windows. Available policies include enabling or disabling the Claude Code feature, controlling auto-updates, and setting a custom deployment URL. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#device-management-policies
- [definition] Network access requirements — Desktop loads its application code and user content from Anthropic CDN hosts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#network-access-requirements
- [definition] Authentication and SSO — Enterprise organizations can require SSO for all users. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#authentication-and-sso
- [definition] Data handling — Claude Code processes your code locally in local sessions, or in cloud sessions on Anthropic-managed infrastructure, unless your organization routes them to a [self-hosted environment](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#data-handling
- [definition] Deployment — Desktop can be distributed through enterprise deployment tools: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#deployment
- [definition] Coming from the CLI? — If you already use the Claude Code CLI, Desktop runs the same underlying engine with a graphical interface. You can run both simultaneously on the same machine, even on the same project. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop#coming-from-the-cli

- [definition] Requirements — The simulator pane uses Apple's simulator tooling, which the desktop app doesn't include. Before starting a session, make sure you have: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#requirements
- [definition] Run your app in the simulator — You don't need a command or setting to open the simulator pane. Claude opens it when it runs your app in a simulator. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#run-your-app-in-the-simulator

- [definition] Ask Claude to run or test the app — Phrase the task around running or verifying the app. For example: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#run-your-app-in-the-simulator
- [definition] Watch the app in the simulator pane — When the app launches in a simulator, the iOS Simulator pane opens next to the conversation. - [definition] Control the simulator yourself — The simulator pane is interactive, not only a viewer. While Claude works, or between tasks, you can: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#control-the-simulator-yourself
- [definition] How sessions manage devices — Each device belongs to the session that launched it, so [parallel sessions](/docs/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions) don't share a device: what you see in one session's pane reflects that session's work, not another's. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#how-sessions-manage-devices
- [definition] Grant Claude access to a device — Claude asks for your consent before it controls a device, while building the app or opening a URL on it follows your session's permission mode. You or your organization can also turn Claude's access off entirely. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#grant-claude-access-to-a-device
- [definition] Allow a device the first time — The first time Claude uses a simulator, the desktop app asks you to allow it. - [definition] Actions that follow your permission mode — Two actions follow your session's [permission mode](/docs/en/permissions#permission-modes) instead of the one-time consent: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#actions-that-follow-your-permission-mode
- [definition] Turn off simulator access — You can turn Claude's simulator access off in the desktop app's settings. Organizations have two ways to turn it off for everyone: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#turn-off-simulator-access
- [definition] Limitations — Claude drives simulated devices only and can't control a physical iPhone or iPad. To test on one, run the app on it from Xcode yourself, then describe what you see or attach a screenshot to the conversation for Claude to work from. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#limitations
- [definition] The simulator pane doesn't open when Claude runs the app — Claude may not have recognized that you wanted to run or test the app, or the simulator tooling may be missing. Check the following: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#the-simulator-pane-doesnt-open-when-claude-runs-the-app
- [definition] The simulator pane says no simulators were found — If `xcode-select` points at Xcode 27, the pane can report no simulators even though devices exist; see [The simulator pane fails with Xcode 27](#the-simulator-pane-fails-with-xcode-27). Otherwise, Xcode is installed but has no iOS simulators to list. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#the-simulator-pane-says-no-simulators-were-found
- [definition] The simulator pane fails with Xcode 27 — The pane doesn't yet work with Xcode 27, which replaces the Simulator app with Device Hub. With Xcode 27 selected, attaching a device fails, or the pane reports that no simulators were found even though devices exist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#the-simulator-pane-fails-with-xcode-27

## Get started with the desktop app
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart>

- [definition] Open the Code tab — Click the **Code** tab at the top center. - [definition] Choose an environment and folder — Select **Local** to run Claude on your machine using your files directly. Click **Select folder** and choose your project directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart#start-your-first-session
- [definition] Choose a model — Select a model from the dropdown next to the send button. See [models](/docs/en/model-config#available-models) for a comparison of the available models. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart#start-your-first-session
- [definition] Review and accept changes — What happens next depends on the [permission mode](/docs/en/desktop#choose-a-permission-mode) shown in the selector next to the send button: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart#start-your-first-session
- [definition] Now what? — You've made your first edit. For the full reference on everything Desktop can do, see [Use Claude Code Desktop](/docs/en/desktop). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart#now-what
- [definition] Coming from the CLI? — Desktop runs the same engine as the CLI with a graphical interface. You can run both simultaneously on the same project, and they share configuration (CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers, hooks, skills, and settings). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart#coming-from-the-cli
- [concept] The desktop app provides a graphical interface for running multiple Claude Code sessions side by side with an integrated terminal and file editor. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] The macOS installer is a Universal build supporting both Intel and Apple Silicon processors. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] The Windows installer supports x64 processors, while ARM64 users must download a specific ARM64 installer. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] Linux installation is available via apt or .deb for Ubuntu and Debian, currently in beta. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription to function. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [concept] The desktop app features three tabs: Chat for general conversation, Cowork for autonomous background agents, and Code for interactive coding assistance. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] On-device Cowork sessions run a sandboxed virtual machine on the user's computer, while remote sessions run on an Anthropic-managed VM. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] The desktop app includes Claude Code natively, so users do not need to install Node.js or the CLI separately for the app. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [problem] Clicking the Code tab may prompt a user to upgrade their subscription if they are not on a paid plan. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [problem] A 403 error in the Code tab indicates an authentication issue that requires troubleshooting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] On Windows, Git must be installed for local sessions to work, whereas most Macs include Git by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [concept] Cloud sessions run in the cloud and continue even if the desktop app is closed, using the same infrastructure as the web version. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] SSH sessions connect to remote machines where Desktop automatically installs Claude Code on the first connection. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] WSL sessions run inside a WSL 2 distribution, executing Claude Code, tools, and git on the Linux side with native paths. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [concept] A session is a conversation with Claude about code that tracks its own context and changes independently from other sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] In Auto or Accept edits permission modes, Claude applies file changes immediately, displaying a diff indicator like `+12 -1`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] In Manual permission mode, Claude proposes each change and waits for user approval before modifying files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [idea] Start with a small project you know well to quickly see what Claude Code can do. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [actionable] Type `@filename` in the prompt box to pull a specific file into the conversation for context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [actionable] Click the stop button to interrupt Claude immediately, or type a correction and press Enter to redirect without stopping. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [concept] Slash commands are invoked by typing `/` or clicking **+** → **Slash commands** to access built-in commands, custom skills, and plugins. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] The Plan permission mode allows Claude to propose an approach without editing any files, useful before large refactors. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [actionable] Open the terminal with Ctrl+` to run commands alongside your session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] Desktop shares configuration files like CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, hooks, skills, and settings with the CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart
- [fact] The Browser pane opens apps running in the dev server or external sites for Claude to view and test. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart

- [definition] Restrict network egress — You can limit the container's outbound traffic to only the domains Claude Code needs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#restrict-network-egress
- [definition] Run without permission prompts — Because the container runs Claude Code as a non-root user and confines command execution to the container, you can pass `--dangerously-skip-permissions` for unattended operation. The CLI rejects this flag when launched as root, so confirm `remoteUser` is set to a non-root account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#run-without-permission-prompts
- [definition] Try the reference container — The [`anthropics/claude-code`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/.devcontainer) repository includes an example dev container that combines the CLI, the egress firewall, persistent volumes, and a Zsh-based shell. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#try-the-reference-container
- [definition] Install prerequisites — Install VS Code and the [Dev Containers extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#try-the-reference-container
- [definition] Clone the reference — Clone the [Claude Code repository](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) and open it in VS Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#try-the-reference-container
- [definition] Reopen in container — When prompted, click **Reopen in Container**, or run **Dev Containers: Reopen in Container** from the Command Palette. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#try-the-reference-container
- [definition] Start Claude Code — Once the container finishes building, open a terminal with `` Ctrl+` `` and run `claude` to sign in and start your first session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#try-the-reference-container
- [definition] Next steps — Once Claude Code is running in your dev container, the pages below cover the rest of an organization rollout: choosing an authentication path, delivering managed policy outside the repository, monitoring usage, and understanding what Claude Code stores and sends. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [concept] A development container defines an identical, isolated environment that every engineer on a team can run to ensure consistency. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [fact] When Claude Code is installed in a dev container, commands execute inside the container rather than on the host machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [concept] Editors supporting the Dev Containers spec, such as VS Code or GitHub Codespaces, connect to the container so that terminals and build tools run inside it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [fact] Plain Vim is an editor without dev container support and is not part of this workflow. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [actionable] Use the Claude Code extension panel or run `claude` in the integrated terminal within VS Code to execute commands inside the container. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [fact] Both the extension panel and the integrated terminal share the same `~/.claude` configuration when running inside a dev container. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [problem] Using `--dangerously-skip-permissions` does not prevent a malicious project from exfiltrating credentials stored in `~/.claude` if accessible inside the container. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [idea] Only use dev containers when developing with trusted repositories and monitor Claude's activities. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [problem] Mounting host secrets such as `~/.ssh` or cloud credential files into the container is a security risk. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [idea] Prefer repository-scoped or short-lived tokens instead of mounting host secrets into the container. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer
- [concept] Claude Code installs into any dev container through the Claude Code Dev Container Feature, which works with tools supporting the Dev Containers spec like VS Code, GitHub Codespaces, or JetBrains IDEs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [fact] When opening a container in VS Code or Codespaces, the feature automatically adds the Claude Code VS Code extension, while other editors ignore that part. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [fact] The version tag in the feature reference (e.g., `:1.0`) pins the install script, not the Claude Code release itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [fact] By default, the feature installs the latest Claude Code and enables auto-updates inside the container. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [actionable] To pin a specific CLI version or disable auto-update, refer to the Enforce organization policy section. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [fact] The Claude Code feature automatically installs Node.js if the base image does not provide it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [problem] If the build stops with `Failed to install Node.js and npm`, you must add the Node feature to resolve it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [actionable] To fix a Node.js installation failure, add `{"ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node:1": {}}` to the `features` block above the Claude Code feature and rebuild. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [actionable] Rebuild the container by opening the VS Code Command Palette with `Cmd+Shift+P` (Mac) or `Ctrl+Shift+P` (Windows/Linux) and running **Dev Containers: Rebuild Container**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [actionable] Sign in to Claude Code by opening a terminal in the rebuilt container and running `claude` to follow the authentication prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [fact] For Anthropic providers, sign-in occurs through a browser using a Claude or Anthropic Console account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [fact] For Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry, authentication uses cloud provider credentials without a browser prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [idea] For cloud providers, pass credentials into the container as environment variables through `containerEnv`, a Codespaces secret, or workload identity instead of mounting credential files from the host. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [problem] If the browser sign-in completes but the callback never reaches the container, it is likely because the editor's port forwarding does not route the localhost callback. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [actionable] If the callback fails to reach the container, copy the code shown in the browser and paste it at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt in the terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#add-claude-code-to-your-dev-container
- [problem] By default, the container's home directory is discarded on rebuild, forcing engineers to sign in again each time. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [fact] Claude Code stores authentication tokens, user settings, and session history under the `~/.claude` directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [fact] OAuth accounts, personal MCP servers, and per-project trust are stored in `~/.claude.json`, which is separate from the `~/.claude` directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [problem] Mounting a volume at `~/.claude` alone does not keep the user signed in because `~/.claude.json` is stored outside that directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [actionable] Mount a named volume at `~/.claude` and set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable to the same path so Claude Code writes `.claude.json` inside the volume. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [actionable] Replace `/home/node` in the configuration example with the home directory of your container's `remoteUser`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [idea] If you have already set `containerEnv`, add `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to that object rather than adding a second environment variable definition. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [idea] To isolate state per project, include the `${devcontainerId}` variable in the source name of the volume mount. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [fact] The reference configuration uses `source=claude-code-config-${devcontainerId}` to isolate state per project. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [fact] In GitHub Codespaces, `~/.claude` persists when stopping and starting a codespace but is cleared when rebuilding the container. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [actionable] To carry authentication across codespaces, store `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` as a Codespaces secret. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [fact] You can generate a long-lived token using the command `claude setup-token`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [fact] Codespaces automatically exposes secrets as environment variables inside the container. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#persist-authentication-and-settings-across-rebuilds
- [concept] A dev container is a convenient place to apply organization policy because the same image and configuration run on every engineer's machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [fact] Claude Code reads `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` on Linux and applies it at the highest precedence in the settings hierarchy. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [fact] Values in `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` override anything an engineer sets in `~/.claude` or the project's `.claude/` directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [problem] Anyone with write access to the repository can change or remove the step that copies the managed settings file from the Dockerfile. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [idea] For policy that engineers cannot bypass by editing repository files, deliver managed settings through server-managed settings or your MDM instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [actionable] To set environment variables that apply to every Claude Code session in the container, add them to `containerEnv` in your `devcontainer.json`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [fact] Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` disables telemetry, error reporting, and auto-updating. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [problem] `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` also disables feature-flag evaluation, preventing sessions in the container from using Remote Control or other features that need feature-flag fetching. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [fact] The Dev Container Feature always installs the latest Claude Code release. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [actionable] To pin a specific Claude Code version for reproducible builds, install it from your Dockerfile with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@X.Y.Z` instead of using the feature. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [idea] To prevent auto-updating when pinning a version, set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` as shown in the example. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [concept] MCP servers can be made available inside the container by defining them at project scope in a `.mcp.json` file at the repository root. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [actionable] Install any binaries that local stdio servers depend on in your Dockerfile and add remote server domains to your network allowlist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#enforce-organization-policy
- [concept] The .claude directory is a volume mount that holds credentials, settings, and session history. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [fact] Engineers can bypass repository file edits by delivering managed policy from the Claude.ai admin console. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [concept] Permission modes range from plan mode to auto mode to bypass, each with specific use cases. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [fact] Claude Code exports OpenTelemetry metrics for usage monitoring and activity auditing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [concept] The security model integrates Claude Code's permission system, sandboxing, and prompt-injection protections. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [idea] Use environment variables to disable telemetry services that are sent by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [concept] Network access requires a full domain allowlist for proxies and firewalls. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps
- [fact] Sandbox environments include dev containers, the built-in Bash sandbox, custom containers, and VMs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer#next-steps

- [definition] Discover and install prebuilt plugins through marketplaces — Find and install plugins from marketplaces to extend Claude Code with new skills, agents, and capabilities. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#discover-and-install-prebuilt-plugins-through-marketplaces
- [definition] How marketplaces work — A marketplace is a catalog of plugins that someone else has created and shared. Using a marketplace is a two-step process: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#how-marketplaces-work
- [definition] Add the marketplace — This registers the catalog with Claude Code so you can browse what's available. No plugins are installed yet. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#how-marketplaces-work
- [definition] Install individual plugins — Browse the catalog and install the plugins you want. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#how-marketplaces-work
- [definition] Official Anthropic marketplace — Claude Code adds the official Anthropic marketplace (`claude-plugins-official`) automatically the first time you start it interactively. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#official-anthropic-marketplace
- [definition] Code intelligence — Code intelligence plugins enable Claude Code's built-in LSP tool, giving Claude the ability to jump to definitions, find references, and see type errors immediately after edits. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#code-intelligence
- [definition] External integrations — These plugins bundle pre-configured [MCP servers](/docs/en/mcp) so you can connect Claude to external services without manual setup: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#external-integrations
- [definition] Automatic security review — The `security-guidance` plugin reviews each change Claude makes for common vulnerabilities and instructs Claude to fix what it finds in the same session. See [Catch security issues as Claude writes code](/docs/en/security-guidance) for what it checks and how to add project-specific rules. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#automatic-security-review
- [definition] Development workflows — Plugins that add skills and agents for common development tasks: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#development-workflows
- [definition] Community marketplace — The community marketplace at [`anthropics/claude-plugins-community`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-community) hosts third-party plugins that have passed Anthropic's automated validation and safety screening. Each plugin is pinned to a specific commit SHA in the catalog. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#community-marketplace
- [definition] Try it: add the demo marketplace — Anthropic also maintains a [demo plugins marketplace](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins) (`claude-code-plugins`) with example plugins that show what's possible with the plugin system. Unlike the official marketplace, you need to add this one manually. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#try-it-add-the-demo-marketplace
- [definition] Add the marketplace — From within Claude Code, run the `plugin marketplace add` command for the `anthropics/claude-code` marketplace: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#try-it-add-the-demo-marketplace
- [definition] Browse available plugins — Run `/plugin` to open the plugin manager. This opens a tabbed interface with four tabs you can cycle through using **Tab**, or **Shift+Tab** to go backward: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#try-it-add-the-demo-marketplace
- [definition] Install a plugin — Select a plugin to view its details. The details pane shows what the plugin contains and what it costs: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#try-it-add-the-demo-marketplace
- [definition] Use your new plugin — Check the install summary: if it reports `Run /reload-plugins to activate.`, run `/reload-plugins`, and if that warns that the reload will re-read the conversation, rerun it as `/reload-plugins --force`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#try-it-add-the-demo-marketplace
- [definition] Add marketplaces — Use the `/plugin marketplace add` command to add marketplaces from different sources. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#add-marketplaces
- [definition] Add from GitHub — Add a GitHub repository that contains a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file using the `owner/repo` format, where `owner` is the GitHub username or organization and `repo` is the repository name. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#add-from-github
- [definition] Add from other Git hosts — Add a git marketplace repository by providing its full URL. For an `https://` URL, whether to include the `.git` suffix depends on the host: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#add-from-other-git-hosts
- [definition] Add from local paths — Add a local directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#add-from-local-paths
- [definition] Add from remote URLs — Add a remote `marketplace.json` file via URL: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#add-from-remote-urls
- [definition] Install plugins — Once you've added marketplaces, you can install a plugin by name: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#install-plugins
- [definition] Manage installed plugins — Run `/plugin` and go to the **Installed** tab to view, enable, disable, or uninstall your plugins. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#manage-installed-plugins
- [definition] Apply plugin changes without restarting — When the [install summary](#install-plugins) reports `Plugin is now active.`, Claude Code already activated the plugin, and you can skip this step. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#apply-plugin-changes-without-restarting

- [definition] Configure auto-updates — Claude Code can automatically update marketplaces and their installed plugins in the background after startup. - [fact] When installing by plugin name only via the shell command, Claude Code reads cached catalogs without refreshing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#install-plugins

- [fact] The summary `Run /reload-plugins to activate.` appears when activating a plugin would invalidate the prompt cache or if activation failed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins#install-plugins

- [parameter] Responses seem lower quality than usual: [Response quality](#responses-seem-lower-quality-than-usual) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#find-your-error
- [parameter] [`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES`](/docs/en/env-vars): Default=10; Effect=Number of retry attempts. Capped at 15 as of v2.1.186; as of v2.1.199 `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` raises the default and removes the cap. Lower it to surface failures faster in scripts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#tune-retry-behavior
- [parameter] [`CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG`](/docs/en/env-vars): Default=unset; Effect=Set to `1` in unattended sessions such as CI jobs to retry `429` and `529` capacity errors indefinitely instead of failing after `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES` attempts. Claude Code fails at once on a `429` that reports a spend limit or exhausted usage credits, even one from a [gateway spend cap](#spend-limit-reached) that… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#tune-retry-behavior
- [parameter] [`API_TIMEOUT_MS`](/docs/en/env-vars): Default=600000; Effect=Per-request timeout in milliseconds. Raise it for slow networks or proxies. It also bounds the [first-byte deadline](#no-response-from-api). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#tune-retry-behavior
- [parameter] [`CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS`](/docs/en/env-vars): Default=unset; Effect=Deadline in milliseconds for the first response byte of a streaming request. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later. For how Claude Code picks the deadline when this is unset, see [No response from API](#no-response-from-api). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#tune-retry-behavior

- [definition] Automatic retries — Claude Code retries transient failures up to 10 times with exponential backoff before showing you an error. It doesn't always retry a failure that arrives partway through Claude's response. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries

The label names the specific reason from the first attempt for failures you can act on right away: the network is down, a TLS handshake failed, or you hit a rate limit. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#what-you-see-while-claude-code-retries-or-waits

- [definition] Report an error — For errors from components this page doesn't cover, see the relevant guide: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [concept] This page lists runtime errors Claude Code displays and how to recover from each one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors
- [fact] Errors apply across the CLI, the Desktop app, and Claude Code on the web since all three wrap the same Claude Code CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors
- [problem] Wrapper and IDE errors are printed by the launching program rather than Claude Code itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors
- [concept] Most runtime errors map to an underlying API error code because Claude Code calls the Claude API for model responses. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors
- [fact] For raw HTTP status code definitions, see the Claude Platform error reference at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors
- [problem] Installation errors such as `command not found` or TLS failures during setup are not covered on this page. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors
- [actionable] For installation errors, see the Troubleshoot installation and login documentation at /docs/en/troubleshoot-install. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors
- [concept] Claude Code retries transient failures up to 10 times with exponential backoff before showing an error. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] It does not always retry a failure that arrives partway through Claude's response. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [problem] Server errors, overloaded responses, and request timeouts arriving before any response streams are retried. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] When a connection drops partway through a request before Claude completes its thinking, the request is re-issued with backoff. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [problem] If a connection drops after thinking but before text or tool calls start, the request is re-issued up to two times quickly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] A connection broken by the computer going to sleep is treated as a dropped connection. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [problem] If the computer goes to sleep after thinking but before text or tool calls, the turn ends with `Your computer went to sleep before a response was produced`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] A stalled response stream where headers arrive but no content is sent triggers an abort and one retry outside the 10-attempt budget. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [problem] If a response stalls a second time after thinking but before text or tool calls, the turn ends with `The response stalled before a response was produced`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] Requests where the API never returns headers are aborted at the first-byte deadline and re-sent at most once per model request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [concept] Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` removes the one-retry cap for requests waiting out `API_TIMEOUT_MS`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] Temporary 429 throttles are retried, but gateway spend-limit 429s are not considered throttles. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] Before v2.1.199, Claude Code only retried 429 throttles lacking quota headers for API key and Enterprise sign-ins. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [problem] Requests exceeding the context limit are retried with reduced `max_tokens` until no reduction fits or further shrinking is impossible. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] Before v2.1.218, Claude Code could retry a reduced request that still did not fit if the extended thinking budget exceeded remaining context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [problem] Expired or missing Google Cloud credentials trigger up to two retries and run `gcpAuthRefresh` if configured. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries

- [problem] TLS certificate validation failures are not retried; the error is reported on the first attempt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries
- [fact] Before v2.1.199, Claude Code retried certificate failures through the full retry budget before showing the error. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries

- [actionable] If Claude warns about a suspected prompt injection regarding context it adds automatically, run `claude update` and retry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#responses-seem-lower-quality-than-usual
- [fact] Before v2.1.201, Sonnet 5 refused some requests in the same way as suspected prompt injections. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#responses-seem-lower-quality-than-usual
- [idea] If a suspected prompt injection warning repeats after updating, report it rather than pasting the flagged content back into the prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#responses-seem-lower-quality-than-usual
- [fact] The MCP server failed to connect or authenticate errors are covered in the MCP guide. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [fact] Hook script failures that block tools are addressed in the Debug hooks documentation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [fact] Permission denied or filesystem errors during installation are covered in the Troubleshoot installation and login guide. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [actionable] Run `/feedback` inside Claude Code to send a transcript and description to Anthropic. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [fact] The `/feedback` command offers to open a prefilled GitHub issue. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [problem] Sending feedback via `/feedback` requires authentication with Anthropic credentials. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [fact] On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or when no Anthropic credentials are configured, `/feedback` saves a local archive. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error
- [actionable] Run `claude doctor` from your shell for a read-only diagnostic of your installation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#report-an-error

## Extend Claude Code
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview>

- [parameter] **CLAUDE.md**: What it does=Persistent context loaded every conversation; When to use it=Project conventions, "always do X" rules; Example="Use pnpm, not npm. Run tests before committing." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **Skill**: What it does=Instructions, knowledge, and workflows Claude can use; When to use it=Reusable content, reference docs, repeatable tasks; Example=`/deploy` runs your deployment checklist; API docs skill with endpoint patterns — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **Subagent**: What it does=Isolated execution context that returns summarized results; When to use it=Context isolation, parallel tasks, specialized workers; Example=Research task that reads many files but returns only key findings — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **[Dynamic workflow](/docs/en/workflows)**: What it does=Script Claude writes that runs many subagents in the background; When to use it=Work that outgrows a handful of subagents, or findings you want cross-checked; Example=Audit a whole codebase, with a second set of agents verifying each finding — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **[Cross-session messaging](/docs/en/cross-session-messaging)**: What it does=Claude delivers a message from one of your sessions to another; When to use it=Sessions you run yourself that need each other's findings mid-task; Example=One session warns another that a change it made breaks what the other is building on — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **[Code intelligence](/docs/en/tools-reference#lsp-tool-behavior)**: What it does=Language-server navigation and diagnostics; When to use it=Typed languages, large codebases where grep is slow or imprecise; Example=Jump to a symbol's definition instead of reading the whole file — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **MCP**: What it does=Connect to external services; When to use it=External data or actions; Example=Query your database, post to Slack, control a browser — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **Hook**: What it does=Script, HTTP request, MCP tool call, prompt, or subagent triggered by events; When to use it=Automation that must run on every matching event; Example=Run ESLint after every file edit — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] **[Artifact](/docs/en/artifacts)**: What it does=Publish session output as a private, interactive web page; When to use it=Output you want to see or share visually rather than as terminal text; Example=An incident timeline that updates as Claude investigates — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [parameter] Claude gets a convention or command wrong twice: Add it to [CLAUDE.md](/docs/en/memory) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time
- [parameter] You keep typing the same prompt to start a task: Save it as a user-invocable [skill](/docs/en/skills) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time
- [parameter] You paste the same playbook or multi-step procedure into chat for the third time: Capture it as a [skill](/docs/en/skills) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time
- [parameter] You keep copying data from a browser tab Claude can't see: Connect that system as an [MCP server](/docs/en/mcp) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time
- [parameter] Claude reads many files to find where a symbol is defined or used: Install a [code intelligence plugin](/docs/en/discover-plugins#code-intelligence) for your language — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time
- [parameter] A side task floods your conversation with output you won't reference again: Route it through a [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time
- [parameter] You want something to happen every time without asking: Write a [hook](/docs/en/hooks-guide) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time
- [parameter] A second repository needs the same setup: Package it as a [plugin](/docs/en/plugins) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time

- [parameter] **MCP servers**: When it loads=Session start; What loads=Tool names; full schemas on demand; Context cost=Low until a tool is used — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#context-cost-by-feature
- [parameter] **Code intelligence**: When it loads=After file edits and on demand; What loads=Diagnostics after edits; symbol locations on lookup; Context cost=Low; reduces file reads elsewhere — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#context-cost-by-feature
- [parameter] **Subagents**: When it loads=When spawned; What loads=Fresh context with specified skills, or the parent conversation for a [fork](/docs/en/sub-agents#fork-the-current-conversation); Context cost=Isolated from main session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#context-cost-by-feature
- [parameter] **Hooks**: When it loads=On trigger; What loads=Nothing (runs externally); Context cost=Zero, unless hook returns additional context — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#context-cost-by-feature

- [definition] Match features to your goal — Features range from always-on context that Claude sees every session, to on-demand capabilities you or Claude can invoke, to background automation that runs on specific events. - [definition] Compare similar features — Some features can seem similar. For a deeper walkthrough of choosing between them, see [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](https://claude.com/blog/steering-claude-code-skills-hooks-rules-subagents-and-more) on the blog. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#compare-similar-features
- [definition] Understand how features layer — Features can be defined at multiple levels: user-wide, per-project, via plugins, or through managed policies. You can also nest CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories or place skills in specific packages of a monorepo. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#understand-how-features-layer
- [definition] Combine features — Each extension solves a different problem: CLAUDE.md handles always-on context, skills handle on-demand knowledge and workflows, MCP handles external connections, subagents handle isolation, and hooks handle automation. Real setups combine them based on your workflow. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#combine-features
- [definition] Understand context costs — Every feature you add consumes some of Claude's context. Too much can fill up your context window, but it can also add noise that makes Claude less effective; skills may not trigger correctly, or Claude may lose track of your conventions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#understand-context-costs
- [definition] Context cost by feature — Each feature has a different loading strategy and context cost: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#context-cost-by-feature
- [definition] Understand how features load — Each feature loads at different points in your session. The tabs below explain when each one loads and what goes into context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#understand-how-features-load
- [definition] Learn more — Each feature has its own guide with setup instructions, examples, and configuration options. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#learn-more
- [concept] The extension layer of Claude Code includes CLAUDE.md, Skills, subagents, hooks, MCP, and plugins to customize capabilities. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview
- [concept] Built-in tools for file operations, search, execution, and web access cover most coding tasks within the core agentic loop. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview
- [fact] The extension layer is designed to connect Claude Code to external services and automate workflows beyond built-in capabilities. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview
- [actionable] Start with CLAUDE.md for project conventions if you are new to Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview
- [idea] Add other extensions as specific triggers come up rather than all at once. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview
- [concept] Plugins are the packaging layer that bundle skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into a single installable unit with namespaced skills. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] Plugin skills are namespaced (like `/my-plugin:review`) so multiple plugins can coexist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [concept] Skills are reusable content that can be reference or action types, where reference skills provide knowledge and action skills trigger specific workflows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [concept] Subagents are isolated workers that run separately from the main conversation, returning summaries to keep the context clean. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] Custom subagents can preload specific skills via the `skills:` field and have their own instructions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [actionable] Run a skill in isolated context using the `context: fork` parameter. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [concept] CLAUDE.md stores instructions that Claude should always know, such as coding conventions and build commands. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] The recommended rule of thumb is to keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [actionable] Move reference content to skills or split into `.claude/rules/` files if CLAUDE.md grows beyond 200 lines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [concept] Rules with `paths` frontmatter only load when Claude works with matching files, saving context compared to CLAUDE.md. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] Dynamic workflows are scripts that run many subagents in the background and return one result, whereas subagents decide turn by turn what runs next. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [actionable] Start a dynamic workflow by asking for it directly in your prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [concept] MCP connects Claude to external services with purpose-built tools, while skills provide knowledge on how to use those tools effectively. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] A `PreToolUse` hook that blocks an edit acts as enforcement, whereas instructions in CLAUDE.md or skills are merely requests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [concept] Hook output lands in context; for example, a `PostToolUse` hook running a linter feeds results back as text for Claude to read. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] CLAUDE.md files are additive, meaning all levels contribute content simultaneously with more specific instructions typically taking precedence. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] Skills override by name based on priority: managed > user > project. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] Subagents override by name based on priority: managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] MCP servers override by name with the hierarchy: local > project > user. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [fact] Hooks merge, meaning all registered hooks fire for their matching events regardless of source. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [concept] Real setups combine features where CLAUDE.md handles always-on context, skills handle on-demand knowledge, MCP handles external connections, subagents handle isolation, and hooks handle automation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal
- [actionable] Use `/<name>` to trigger a skill workflow like `/deploy`, `/review`, or `/release`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview#match-features-to-your-goal

## Run Claude Code through a gateway
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways>

- [definition] Run Claude Code through a gateway — Route Claude Code through a self-hosted gateway for centralized credentials, usage tracking, and cost controls. Covers the architecture, Anthropic's Claude apps gateway, and using other gateway products. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#run-claude-code-through-a-gateway
- [definition] How a gateway works — Each developer's Claude Code sends its requests to the gateway's address and authenticates with a gateway-issued credential. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#how-a-gateway-works
- [definition] Choose a gateway — Claude Code works with Anthropic's own gateway or with a gateway your organization already runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#choose-a-gateway
- [definition] Claude apps gateway — Claude apps gateway is Anthropic's self-hosted gateway, included in the `claude` binary. It routes to Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, or the Anthropic API as the upstream. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#claude-apps-gateway
- [definition] Other gateways — If your organization already runs an LLM gateway or API gateway, you can use it instead. Anthropic doesn't endorse, maintain, or audit other gateway products, and doesn't support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#other-gateways
- [definition] Subscriptions and gateways — When developers connect through a gateway with a gateway credential, usage is billed to your organization's provider account at API rates, and their claude.ai subscriptions aren't used or charged. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#subscriptions-and-gateways
- [definition] Configure separately from the gateway — A gateway routes model API requests. A few things you might expect it to handle are configured elsewhere: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#configure-separately-from-the-gateway
- [definition] Next steps — The next page depends on who runs the gateway. Anthropic's gateway runs from the `claude` binary and has its own setup guide; a gateway your organization already runs has a protocol to implement and an admin rollout checklist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways#next-steps
- [concept] A gateway is a proxy that sits between Claude Code and a model provider, forwarding API traffic using an organization-held credential instead of developer credentials. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [fact] Claude apps gateway is included in the `claude` binary and does not require adopting a separate gateway product. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [concept] Two kinds of credentials are involved: a developer credential issued by the gateway for authentication and usage tracking, and a provider credential held by the gateway for forwarding traffic. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [fact] The gateway can forward requests to Anthropic's API or cloud providers such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [idea] Use Claude apps gateway to avoid maintaining forwarding rules for changing headers and request fields, as it releases alongside the CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [problem] CI pipelines without a developer to approve a browser SSO sign-in cannot authenticate through Claude apps gateway because there is no service-token flow. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [fact] Agent SDK sessions and `claude -p` runs on a machine where a developer has signed in use that machine's gateway session and are governed by its policies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [problem] Anthropic does not endorse, maintain, or audit other gateway products, nor supports routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [fact] When connecting through a gateway with a gateway credential, usage is billed to the organization's provider account at API rates and claude.ai subscriptions are not used. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [actionable] Set `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for a gateway you run, or sign in to a Claude apps gateway with `/login`, to turn off subscription login for that session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [problem] Setting only `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` without a gateway credential routes requests through the gateway but keeps the saved claude.ai login active, applying subscription usage limits and billing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [concept] The gateway decides where requests go, but the developer selects which model answers using the `/model` command or model environment variables. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [fact] Claude Code sends version checks and downloads directly to Anthropic, separate from the gateway path. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [actionable] Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` to turn off optional streams like version checks if egress to required domains is not available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [fact] On a Claude apps gateway session, Claude Code sends no client analytics to Anthropic and disables the Anthropic-bound analytics when the session signs in. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [problem] If a corporate HTTP proxy is required, you must configure it in addition to the gateway; otherwise, Claude Code cannot connect to the gateway. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways
- [actionable] Add the gateway host to `NO_PROXY` if your network requires a proxy but the gateway host is not on a private network. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gateways

- [concept] In interactive mode, when no prompt input is provided, Claude waits for the trigger phrase @claude in issue comments, PR reviews, or new issue titles/bodies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [fact] In interactive mode, progress and results appear as a comment on the triggering issue or pull request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [concept] In automation mode, when a prompt input is provided, Claude runs without waiting for a mention. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [fact] By default in automation mode, results appear in the workflow run log rather than as a comment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes

- [fact] The Claude Code GitHub Action runs two checks on the triggering actor before starting: write access and human actor verification. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [problem] A run fails if either the write access check or the human actor check rejects the triggering user. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [fact] On issue and pull request events, the triggering user must have write access to the repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [actionable] To allow specific users without write access, set allowed_non_write_users and pass your own github_token input. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [fact] Events that no user authors, such as a schedule trigger, skip the write access check. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [problem] The action rejects bot actors on every event unless they are listed in allowed_bots to prevent bots from triggering Claude in a loop. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [fact] The human actor check applies to scheduled runs, which GitHub attributes to a repository user, usually the one who last changed the workflow's cron schedule. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes
- [actionable] If the user associated with the cron schedule is a bot, list it in allowed_bots. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions#interactive-and-automation-modes

- [definition] Manual setup — If the guided redirect flow is blocked by your network configuration, click **Add manually** instead of Connect. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#manual-setup
- [definition] Network requirements — For Anthropic-hosted sessions, your GHES instance must be reachable from Anthropic infrastructure so Claude can clone repositories and post review comments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#network-requirements
- [definition] Developer workflow — Once an Owner has connected the GHES instance, no developer-side configuration is needed. Claude Code detects your GHES hostname automatically from the git remote in your working directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#developer-workflow
- [definition] Teleport sessions to your terminal — Pull a web session into your local terminal with `claude --teleport`. Teleport verifies you're in a checkout of the same GHES repository before fetching the branch and loading the session history. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#teleport-sessions-to-your-terminal
- [definition] Plugin marketplaces on GHES — Host plugin marketplaces on your GHES instance to distribute internal tooling across your organization. The marketplace structure is identical to github.com-hosted marketplaces, but installation works differently depending on where you add the marketplace, and credentials differ across surfaces: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#plugin-marketplaces-on-ghes
- [definition] Add a GHES marketplace — The `owner/repo` shorthand always resolves to github.com. For GHES-hosted marketplaces, use the full git URL, replacing `github.example.com` and the repository path with your own. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#add-a-ghes-marketplace
- [definition] Pre-register GHES marketplaces with managed settings — The `extraKnownMarketplaces` setting pre-registers a marketplace so developers get it without manual setup. - [definition] Allowlist GHES marketplaces in managed settings — If your organization uses [managed settings](/docs/en/settings) to restrict which marketplaces developers can add, use the `hostPattern` source type to allow all marketplaces from your GHES instance without enumerating each repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#allowlist-ghes-marketplaces-in-managed-settings
- [definition] Limitations — A few features behave differently on GHES than on github.com. The [feature table](#what-works-with-github-enterprise-server) summarizes support; this section covers the workarounds. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#limitations
- [definition] Web session fails to clone repository — If `claude --cloud` fails with a clone error, verify that an Owner has completed setup for your GHES instance and that the GitHub App is installed on the repository you're working in. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#web-session-fails-to-clone-repository
- [definition] Marketplace add fails with a policy error — If `/plugin marketplace add` is blocked for your GHES URL, your organization has restricted marketplace sources. - [definition] Marketplace add on claude.ai fails with a GitHub access error — If adding a GHES marketplace from your user settings fails with a generic error like "Marketplace couldn't be added", check your GitHub Enterprise connection first. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-enterprise-server#marketplace-add-on-claudeai-fails-with-a-github-access-error
- [definition] GHES instance not reachable — If reviews or Anthropic-hosted web sessions time out, your GHES instance may not be reachable from Anthropic infrastructure. - [idea] Use repository-specific trust conditions and least-privilege service accounts when configuring Workload Identity Federation. This approach eliminates the need to store service account keys. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gitlab-ci-cd#configuration-examples
- [concept] For Google Cloud, the credential configuration's `credential_source` entry instructs Google's auth libraries to read the OIDC token from a file. - [problem] Workload Identity Federation requires specific prerequisites: the Agent Platform API must be enabled, and Workload Identity Federation must be configured to trust GitLab OIDC. - [question] Does the workflow support passing the desired model ID via job configuration or prompt for Amazon Bedrock? — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gitlab-ci-cd#configuration-examples
