- [concept] Claude responds to @claude commands when triggered manually, via MR events, or through a note event listener webhook. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gitlab-ci-cd#troubleshooting
- [fact] Authentication errors for the Claude API occur if the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is invalid or expired. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/gitlab-ci-cd#troubleshooting

## Keep Claude working toward a goal
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal>

- [snippet] Set a goal: /goal all tests in test/auth pass and the lint step is clean — `/goal all tests in test/auth pass and the lint step is clean` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#set-a-goal
- [snippet] Check status: /goal — `/goal` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#check-status
- [snippet] Clear a goal: /goal clear — `/goal clear` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#clear-a-goal
- [snippet] Run non-interactively: claude -p "/goal CHANGELOG.md has an entry for every PR merged this week" — `claude -p "/goal CHANGELOG.md has an entry for every PR merged this week"` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#run-non-interactively
- [parameter] `/goal`: Next turn starts when=The previous turn finishes, or an [idle check-in](#background-work-defers-evaluation) comes due while background work keeps the goal waiting, up to three times per goal between your prompts; Stops when=A model confirms the condition is met or judges it impossible, or a turn fails on [an error you have to fix](#errors-you-have-to-fix-clear-the-goal), or you run… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#compare-ways-to-keep-a-session-running
- [parameter] [`/loop`](/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#run-a-prompt-repeatedly-with-%2Floop): Next turn starts when=A time interval elapses; Stops when=You stop it, or Claude decides the work is done — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#compare-ways-to-keep-a-session-running
- [parameter] [Stop hook](/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks): Next turn starts when=The previous turn finishes; Stops when=Your own script or prompt decides — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#compare-ways-to-keep-a-session-running
- [definition] Keep Claude working toward a goal — Set a completion condition with /goal and Claude keeps working until it's met, a model judges it impossible, or an error you have to fix clears the goal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#keep-claude-working-toward-a-goal
- [definition] Compare ways to keep a session running — Three approaches keep the current session running between prompts. Pick based on what should start the next turn: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#compare-ways-to-keep-a-session-running
- [definition] Use `/goal` — One goal can be active per session. The same command sets, checks, and clears it depending on the argument. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#use-goal
- [definition] Set a goal — Run `/goal` followed by the condition you want satisfied. If a goal is already active, the new one replaces it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#set-a-goal
- [definition] Write an effective condition — The [evaluator](#how-evaluation-works) judges your condition against what Claude has surfaced in the conversation. It doesn't run commands or read files independently, so write the condition as something Claude's own output can demonstrate. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#write-an-effective-condition
- [definition] Check status — Run `/goal` with no arguments to see the current state. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#check-status
- [definition] Clear a goal — Run `/goal clear` to remove an active goal before it resolves. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#clear-a-goal
- [definition] Resume with an active goal — When you resume a session, Claude Code restores a goal that was still active when the session ended. Claude Code restores it on every resume route: `--continue`, `--resume` with a session ID or name, and the [session picker](/docs/en/sessions#use-the-session-picker). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#resume-with-an-active-goal
- [definition] Run non-interactively — `/goal` works in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless), in the [desktop app](/docs/en/desktop), and through [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control). Setting a goal with `-p` runs the loop to completion in a single invocation: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#run-non-interactively
- [definition] How evaluation works — `/goal` is a wrapper around a session-scoped [prompt-based Stop hook](/docs/en/hooks#prompt-based-hooks). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [definition] Errors you have to fix clear the goal — If a turn fails on an error that won't clear until you fix it, Claude Code clears the goal and prints a warning naming the cause. The warning starts with `Goal cleared after an unrecoverable error` and ends with `Run /goal again to continue`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#errors-you-have-to-fix-clear-the-goal
- [definition] Background work defers evaluation — If a subagent or a background shell command is still running when a turn ends, Claude Code skips the evaluation for that turn. It evaluates at the end of the next turn that finishes with no background work running. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#background-work-defers-evaluation
- [definition] Evaluation model and cost — To evaluate on a different model, set [`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`](/docs/en/model-config#environment-variables). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#evaluation-model-and-cost
- [definition] Requirements — Claude Code makes `/goal` available under the same [workspace trust rule as hooks in settings files](/docs/en/permissions#what-runs-before-you-trust-a-folder), because the evaluator is part of the hooks system. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#requirements
- [concept] The /goal command sets a completion condition and causes Claude to keep working toward it without requiring prompts for each step. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [fact] After each turn, a small fast model checks whether the completion condition holds. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [concept] If the model judges the condition is not yet met, Claude starts another turn instead of returning control to the user. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [fact] A goal clears automatically when the completion condition is met. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [fact] A goal clears automatically if the model judges the condition impossible to satisfy. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [problem] An error that requires user intervention will clear the goal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [idea] Use a goal for substantial work that has a verifiable end state. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [actionable] Run the /goal command to initiate a persistent task sequence. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
- [concept] `/goal` is a wrapper around a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook that triggers evaluation after each turn. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] The evaluator defaults to the Haiku model on the Claude API, but third-party providers may use different defaults. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [concept] The evaluator returns one of three verdicts: Not yet met, Met, or Impossible, each with a short reason. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] When the verdict is Met, Claude Code clears the goal and records an achieved entry in the transcript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] When the verdict is Impossible, Claude Code clears the goal, records a failed entry, and does not require manual clearing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [problem] If Claude answers without making progress (no tool use for several turns), the loop stops and prints a warning while leaving the goal set. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] Errors that won't clear until fixed, such as authentication failures managed by Claude Code, automatically clear the goal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [problem] An exhausted credit balance is one of four specific failure types that clears the goal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [problem] A context overflow that auto-compaction couldn't clear will cause the goal to be cleared. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] Transient errors like rate limits or overloaded servers do not clear the goal; it remains active after such failures. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [concept] If background work is running when a turn ends, evaluation is deferred until the next turn finishes with no background work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] A check-in is triggered if background work keeps the goal waiting for 30 minutes by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] After the first check-in, subsequent intervals double up to four times the initial interval (e.g., 1 hour, then 2 hours). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [actionable] Set `CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES` to change the first check-in interval or set it to `0` to turn check-ins off. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] Idle check-ins require Claude Code v2.1.236 or later and are capped at three per goal between prompts in version v2.1.246 and later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] Before v2.1.239, only idle check-ins used the backoff interval; turn-end check-ins recurred at the first interval. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [concept] To evaluate on a different model, set the `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` environment variable. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] The evaluator does not call tools and can only judge what Claude has already surfaced in the conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] Evaluation tokens are billed on the small fast model configured for your provider and are typically negligible compared to main-turn spend. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#how-evaluation-works
- [fact] The /goal command is available under the same workspace trust rule as hooks in settings files because the evaluator is part of the hooks system. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#requirements
- [problem] /goal is unavailable when disableAllHooks is true after settings precedence applies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#requirements
- [problem] /goal is unavailable when allowManagedHooksOnly is set in managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#requirements
- [fact] In cases where /goal is unavailable, the command tells you why instead of silently doing nothing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal#requirements

- [idea] For more restrictive permissions, create a custom role with only the aiplatform.endpoints.predict permission. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#iam-configuration
- [actionable] Create a dedicated GCP project for Claude Code to simplify cost tracking and access control. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#iam-configuration
- [concept] Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 support the 1M token context window on Google Cloud's Agent Platform. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#1m-token-context-window
- [fact] Sonnet 5 always runs with the 1M window and has no [1m] variant to select. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#1m-token-context-window
- [concept] For models other than Sonnet 5, Claude Code automatically enables the extended context window when a 1M model variant is selected. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#1m-token-context-window
- [actionable] To enable the 1M context option for a manually pinned model, append [1m] to the model ID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#1m-token-context-window
- [fact] The setup wizard offers a 1M context option when it pins models. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#1m-token-context-window
- [problem] Users may encounter 'Could not load the default credentials' errors when accessing Vertex AI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [actionable] Run `gcloud auth application-default login` to set up Application Default Credentials. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [actionable] Set the `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` environment variable to a service account key file path. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [problem] Users may encounter quota issues when making requests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [actionable] Check current quotas or request a quota increase through the Cloud Console. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [problem] Users may encounter 'model not found' 404 errors if the model is not enabled or available in the specified location. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [actionable] Confirm the model is Enabled in the Model Garden. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [fact] Some models are offered only on `global` or multi-region locations such as `eu` and `us`, not in specific regions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting

- [actionable] Specify a supported model via `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` for models that do not support global endpoints. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [actionable] Set a region or multi-region location using `VERTEX_REGION_<MODEL_NAME>` environment variables for models that do not support global endpoints. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [problem] Users may encounter 429 errors if the primary model and small/fast model are not supported in the selected region for regional endpoints. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting
- [idea] Consider switching to `CLOUD_ML_REGION=global` for better availability if encountering 429 errors on regional endpoints. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#troubleshooting

- [parameter] `StopFailure`: What the matcher filters=error type; Example matcher values=`rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `unknown` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#filter-hooks-with-matchers
- [parameter] `InstructionsLoaded`: What the matcher filters=load reason; Example matcher values=`session_start`, `nested_traversal`, `path_glob_match`, `include`, `compact` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#filter-hooks-with-matchers

- [parameter] `Bash(git *)`: Bash command=`git push`; Hook runs?=yes; Why=command name matches — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#filter-by-tool-name-and-arguments-with-the-if-field

- [definition] How hooks work — Claude Code fires hook events at specific points in its lifecycle. When an event fires, Claude Code runs all matching hooks in parallel; see [Hook handler fields](/docs/en/hooks#hook-handler-fields) for how duplicate handlers are treated. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#how-hooks-work
- [definition] Combine results from multiple hooks — When multiple hooks match the same event, every hook's command runs to completion before Claude Code merges the results. One hook returning `deny` doesn't stop sibling hooks from executing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#combine-results-from-multiple-hooks
- [definition] Read input and return output — Hooks communicate with Claude Code through stdin, stdout, stderr, and exit codes. When an event fires, Claude Code passes event-specific data as JSON to your script's stdin. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#read-input-and-return-output
- [definition] Filter hooks with matchers — Without a matcher, a hook fires on every occurrence of its event. Matchers let you narrow that down. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#filter-hooks-with-matchers
- [definition] Configure hook location — Where you add a hook determines its scope: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#configure-hook-location
- [definition] Prompt-based hooks — For decisions that require judgment rather than deterministic rules, use `type: "prompt"` hooks. Instead of running a shell command, Claude Code sends your prompt and the hook's input data to a Claude model, Haiku by default, to make the decision. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [definition] Agent-based hooks — Agent hooks are experimental. Behavior and configuration may change in future releases. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [definition] HTTP hooks — Use `type: "http"` hooks to POST event data to an HTTP endpoint instead of running a shell command. The endpoint receives the same JSON that a command hook would receive on stdin, and returns results through the HTTP response body using the same JSON format. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#http-hooks
- [definition] Limitations — Keep these constraints in mind when designing hooks: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#limitations
- [definition] Hooks and permission modes — `PreToolUse` hooks fire before any permission-mode check, in every [permission mode](/docs/en/permission-modes), including `dontAsk`. A hook that returns `permissionDecision: "deny"` blocks the tool even in `bypassPermissions` mode or with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#hooks-and-permission-modes
- [definition] Hook not firing — The hook is configured but never executes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#hook-not-firing
- [definition] Hook error in output — You see a message like "PreToolUse hook error: ..." in the transcript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#hook-error-in-output

- [definition] Stop hook hits the block cap — Claude keeps working instead of stopping, then ends the turn with a warning that the Stop hook blocked too many consecutive times. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#stop-hook-hits-the-block-cap
- [definition] Hook JSON has no effect — Your hook prints valid JSON, but the decision doesn't take effect and no error appears in the transcript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#hook-json-has-no-effect

- [concept] Hooks are user-defined shell commands that run automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide
- [fact] Hooks provide deterministic control, ensuring certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide
- [idea] Use hooks to enforce project rules, automate repetitive tasks, and integrate Claude Code with existing tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide
- [concept] For decisions requiring judgment rather than deterministic rules, use prompt-based or agent-based hooks that utilize a Claude model to evaluate conditions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide
- [fact] The Hooks guide covers common use cases and getting started, while the Hooks reference contains full event schemas, JSON formats, and advanced features like async hooks and MCP tool hooks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide
- [concept] Use type: "prompt" hooks for decisions requiring judgment rather than deterministic rules. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [fact] By default, Claude Code uses the Haiku model to process prompt-based hook decisions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [concept] The model's only job is to return a decision as JSON with an "ok" field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [fact] Setting "ok": true allows the action to proceed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [problem] If "ok": false, behavior depends on the event type and may end the turn or deny a tool call. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [fact] For Stop and SubagentStop events, the reason is fed back to Claude unless impossible is true. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [problem] Setting "impossible": true marks a condition as never satisfiable, causing the turn to end even for Stop events. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [fact] For PreToolUse events, denying a tool call by default ends the turn and shows the reason as a warning. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [idea] Set continueOnBlock: true on PreToolUse hooks to return the deny reason as a tool error instead of ending the turn. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [fact] Before version 2.1.210, PreToolUse deny reasons were returned as tool errors and turns continued by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [fact] For PostToolUse events, denying the action by default ends the turn and shows the reason as a warning. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [idea] Set continueOnBlock: true on PostToolUse hooks to feed the reason back to Claude and continue the turn. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [fact] For PostToolBatch, UserPromptSubmit, and UserPromptExpansion events, denying an action ends the turn and shows the reason as a warning. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#prompt-based-hooks
- [concept] Agent hooks are experimental hooks that spawn a subagent to inspect files or run commands for verification. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [fact] Agent hooks use the "ok" / "reason" response format and have a default timeout of 60 seconds with up to 50 tool-use turns. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [problem] Agent hooks do not support the prompt-hook `impossible` field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [fact] On `ok: false`, Claude Code handles an agent hook like a prompt hook with `continueOnBlock: true` on `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` events. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [problem] Agent hooks have no `continueOnBlock` field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [idea] For production workflows, prefer command hooks over agent hooks due to the experimental nature of agent hooks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [idea] Use prompt hooks when the hook input data alone is sufficient to make a decision. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [idea] Use agent hooks when you need to verify conditions against the actual state of the codebase. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [actionable] Replace the `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder in agent hook configuration with the hook's JSON input. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#agent-based-hooks
- [concept] The Hooks reference page provides full event schemas, JSON output format details, and documentation on async hooks and MCP tool hooks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#learn-more
- [fact] The Hooks reference page is located at /docs/en/hooks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#learn-more
- [concept] Security considerations must be reviewed before deploying hooks in shared or production environments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#learn-more
- [fact] The Security considerations section is located at /docs/en/hooks#security-considerations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#learn-more
- [idea] Review security considerations before deploying hooks in shared or production environments to ensure safety. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#learn-more
- [fact] A Bash command validator example is available as a complete reference implementation on GitHub. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#learn-more
- [concept] The Bash command validator example is located at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/examples/hooks/bash_command_validator_example.py. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#learn-more

What changes is where the code executes and how you interact with it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#environments-and-interfaces
- [definition] Execution environments — Claude Code runs in three environments, each with different tradeoffs for where your code executes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#execution-environments
- [definition] Interfaces — You can access Claude Code through the terminal, the [desktop app](/docs/en/desktop), [IDE extensions](/docs/en/vs-code), [claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code), [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control), [Slack](/docs/en/slack), and [CI/CD pipelines](/docs/en/github-actions). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#interfaces
- [definition] Work with sessions — Claude Code saves your conversation locally as you work. Each message, tool use, and result is written to a plaintext JSONL file under `~/.claude/projects/`, which enables [rewinding](#undo-changes-with-checkpoints), [resuming, and forking](#resume-or-fork-sessions) sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#work-with-sessions
- [definition] Work across branches — Each Claude Code conversation is a session tied to your current directory. The `/resume` picker shows sessions from the current worktree by default, with keyboard shortcuts to widen the list to other worktrees or projects. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#work-across-branches
- [definition] Resume or fork sessions — Resuming a session with `claude --continue` or `claude --resume` reopens it under the same session ID and appends new messages to the existing conversation. Forking with `--fork-session` or `/branch` copies the history into a new session ID, leaving the original unchanged. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#resume-or-fork-sessions
- [definition] The context window — Claude's context window holds your conversation history, file contents, command outputs, [CLAUDE.md](/docs/en/memory), [auto memory](/docs/en/memory#auto-memory), loaded skills, and system instructions. As you work, context fills up. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-context-window
- [definition] Stay safe with checkpoints and permissions — Claude has two safety mechanisms: checkpoints let you undo file changes, and permissions control what Claude can do without asking. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#stay-safe-with-checkpoints-and-permissions
- [definition] Control what Claude can do — Choose a permission mode to set what Claude can do without asking you. Press `Shift+Tab` to cycle through the permission modes: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#control-what-claude-can-do
- [definition] Work effectively with Claude Code — These tips help you get better results from Claude Code. For more on specific prompts, verification, and planning, see [Best practices](/docs/en/best-practices). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#work-effectively-with-claude-code
- [definition] Ask Claude Code for help — Claude Code can teach you how to use it. Ask questions like "how do I set up hooks?" or "what's the best way to structure my CLAUDE.md?" and Claude will explain. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#ask-claude-code-for-help
- [definition] It's a conversation — Claude Code is conversational. You don't need perfect prompts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#its-a-conversation
- [definition] Delegate, don't dictate — Think of delegating to a capable colleague. Give context and direction, then trust Claude to figure out the details: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#delegate-dont-dictate
- [concept] The agentic loop consists of three phases: gather context, take action, and verify results. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop
- [fact] Claude Code serves as the agentic harness that provides tools, context management, and execution environment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop
- [concept] The loop adapts to tasks; a question may only need context gathering while a bug fix cycles through all three phases repeatedly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop
- [fact] Users can interrupt the loop at any point to steer Claude, provide additional context, or ask for a different approach. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop
- [concept] The agentic loop is powered by models that reason and tools that act. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop
- [fact] Claude can read code in any language, understand component connections, and determine necessary changes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop
- [fact] For complex tasks, the model breaks work into steps, executes them, and adjusts based on new information. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop
- [idea] Use Sonnet for most coding tasks as it handles them well. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#the-agentic-loop

- [problem] As context fills up, detailed instructions from early in the conversation may be lost during automatic compaction. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#work-with-sessions
- [idea] Put persistent rules in CLAUDE.md rather than relying on conversation history to ensure they survive context compaction. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#work-with-sessions

- [actionable] Add a 'Compact Instructions' section to CLAUDE.md or run `/compact` with a focus (e.g., `/compact focus on the API changes`) to control what is preserved during compaction. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#work-with-sessions
- [concept] MCP tool definitions are deferred by default and loaded on demand via tool search, so only tool names and server instructions consume context until a specific tool is used. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#work-with-sessions

- [definition] Set up Claude Code in a monorepo or large codebase — Configure Claude Code for monorepos and large single-tree codebases with nested CLAUDE.md files, sparse worktrees, code intelligence, and per-package skills so Claude stays focused on the code you're working in. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#set-up-claude-code-in-a-monorepo-or-large-codebase
- [definition] What this guide covers — The [table below](#settings-on-this-page) lists each setting and what it accomplishes. The [file tree after it](#the-example-monorepo) is the example monorepo every code sample on this page refers to. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#what-this-guide-covers
- [definition] Settings on this page — Each setting below is independent. They layer rather than replace each other, so apply whichever fit your repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#settings-on-this-page
- [definition] The example monorepo — The examples throughout this page refer to a monorepo with three packages. The same patterns work in a large single-tree codebase: where an example uses `packages/api/`, substitute your own subsystem directory such as `src/backend/` or `lib/core/`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#the-example-monorepo
- [definition] Choose where to start Claude — Where you launch `claude` determines which files Claude can read and edit without an additional permission grant, which CLAUDE.md files load into context at startup, and which project settings apply. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#choose-where-to-start-claude
- [definition] Layer CLAUDE.md files by directory — In a large codebase, a single CLAUDE.md at the repository root tends to either grow to cover every subsystem's conventions, costing context on instructions unrelated to the current task, or stay too generic to be useful. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#layer-claudemd-files-by-directory
- [definition] Choose between per-directory CLAUDE.md and path-scoped rules — Per-directory `CLAUDE.md` files and [path-scoped rules](/docs/en/memory#path-specific-rules) under `.claude/rules/` both let you target instructions to part of the tree. They differ in where the file lives and when it loads. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#choose-between-per-directory-claudemd-and-path-scoped-rules
- [definition] Exclude irrelevant CLAUDE.md files — When you start Claude from the repository root, each subdirectory's CLAUDE.md loads as soon as Claude reads a file in that directory. The `claudeMdExcludes` setting skips specific files by path or glob pattern so they never load. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#exclude-irrelevant-claudemd-files
- [definition] Reduce what Claude reads — Instructions are only part of what ends up in Claude's context. File reads are another cost that grows with the codebase. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#reduce-what-claude-reads
- [definition] Block reads of generated and vendored code — Claude's content searches respect `.gitignore` by default, so paths already listed there, such as `node_modules/`, `dist/`, and `build/`, stay out of search results without additional configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#block-reads-of-generated-and-vendored-code
- [definition] Reduce file reads with code intelligence — In a large codebase, finding where a symbol is defined or used can cost many file reads and grep calls. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#reduce-file-reads-with-code-intelligence
- [definition] Scope worktrees and file access — These settings control what's on disk in worktrees and which directories Claude can read and write beyond your starting point. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [definition] Check out only the directories you need — The `--worktree` flag starts a session in a new git worktree so changes stay isolated from your main checkout. By default it checks out the entire repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#check-out-only-the-directories-you-need
- [definition] Grant access across packages or repositories — This section applies when you start Claude from a subdirectory, or when a task spans multiple checkouts. If you start from the repository root in a single large tree, Claude already has access to every file and you can skip this. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#grant-access-across-packages-or-repositories
- [definition] Add per-directory skills — Any subdirectory can define [skills](/docs/en/skills) scoped to its own stack. A skill loads on demand when Claude determines it's relevant, so API-specific tooling doesn't consume context during frontend work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#add-per-directory-skills
- [definition] Keep skills discoverable — With skills spread across many directories, the list Claude chooses from can grow large. Claude picks a skill by reading every discovered skill's name and description, and only the chosen skill's full content loads into context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#keep-skills-discoverable
- [definition] Centralize conventions when layering stops scaling — Per-directory CLAUDE.md files can become hard to govern as the codebase grows. Conventions drift, files go stale, and no one owns the root. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [definition] Recommend the right plugin at session start — Once conventions live in plugins, a teammate starting Claude in an unfamiliar part of the tree has no signal about which plugin that area's owners maintain. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#recommend-the-right-plugin-at-session-start
- [definition] Put it together — The combined configuration below uses the monorepo layout. The same files work for any subdirectory in a large single tree. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [definition] Scope and plan changes that span packages — The configuration above controls what Claude sees. When a single change touches several packages, such as updating a shared type along with every call site that uses it, how you scope and sequence the task also affects the result. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-and-plan-changes-that-span-packages
- [definition] Next steps — Once this configuration is in place, you can refine it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#next-steps
- [concept] The --worktree flag starts a session in a new git worktree to isolate changes from the main checkout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [fact] By default, a worktree checks out the entire repository, but the worktree.sparsePaths setting uses git sparse-checkout to write only listed directories and root-level files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [actionable] To add paths for yourself, use .claude/settings.local.json to merge lists with the committed settings without removing them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [idea] Add the worktree key alongside existing keys in .claude/settings.json rather than replacing the file if other settings like permissions.deny exist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [fact] Paths in sparsePaths are relative to the repository root regardless of which subdirectory you start Claude from, and any directory paths work here. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [concept] Subagents are parallel Claude instances spawned for subtasks that can run in lightweight worktrees sharing the same sparsePaths. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [fact] Root-level files like package.json, tsconfig.base.json, and lock files are always checked out alongside listed directories in a sparse worktree. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [problem] Before v2.1.207, the extensions.worktreeConfig git entry remained after the last worktree was removed, causing go-git-based tools like tea to fail opening the repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [actionable] To avoid duplicating large directories like node_modules, pair sparsePaths with symlinkDirectories in .claude/settings.json to create a symlink back to the main repository's copy. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [fact] The session's working directory becomes the worktree root after creation, so project settings inside the worktree load from the checked-out copy of the repository root's .claude/settings.json. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [concept] The additionalDirectories setting grants Claude access to directories outside the working directory, useful for tasks spanning multiple packages or repositories. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [actionable] Grant access at runtime without editing settings by passing --add-dir when you start Claude. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [problem] CLAUDE.md and rules files from directories added with --add-dir or /add-dir do not load by default unless the CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD environment variable is set. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [fact] The CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD environment variable has no effect on directories listed in the additionalDirectories setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [idea] Commit additionalDirectories to .claude/settings.json for sibling directories that everyone in the area needs, or use .claude/settings.local.json for personal selections. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-worktrees-and-file-access
- [problem] Per-directory CLAUDE.md files become hard to govern as codebases grow, leading to drifting conventions, stale files, and a lack of ownership at the root. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [concept] To solve governance issues, move conventions and reference content into mechanisms that load on demand rather than always-loaded CLAUDE.md files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [idea] Use Skills to provide reference material that Claude loads only when relevant to the task. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [idea] Use Plugins as versioned bundles of skills, hooks, and commands that a platform team owns centrally. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [idea] Expose code search or RAG indexes as MCP servers so Claude queries them instead of reading files directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [fact] Platform teams can enforce centralized settings using server-managed or endpoint-managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [problem] When conventions live in plugins, a teammate starting Claude in an unfamiliar part of the tree receives no signal about which plugin that area's owners maintain. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [concept] A SessionStart hook can close the gap by adding plain text to Claude's context before the first prompt via stdout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [actionable] Write a script that reads the launch directory from the hook input and looks it up in a path-to-plugin map committed to the repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [actionable] Register the script using the Automate actions with hooks guide to enable the SessionStart hook. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#centralize-conventions-when-layering-stops-scaling
- [concept] Each subdirectory's .claude/settings.json must be self-contained rather than layered on a root file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [fact] Sibling packages' CLAUDE.md files are out of scope when the session starts from packages/api/. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [actionable] Add claudeMdExcludes to the repository root's .claude/settings.local.json if you start sessions from the root. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [problem] The additionalDirectories entry does not load inside a worktree because the working directory becomes the worktree root. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [actionable] Copy deny rules to the repository root's .claude/settings.json so worktree sessions pick them up. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [fact] Starting Claude from packages/api/ loads the root CLAUDE.md and packages/api/CLAUDE.md but skips packages/web/CLAUDE.md. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [fact] The setup allows reading and editing files in packages/api/ and packages/shared/. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [fact] Reads of build output under dist/ and build/ in packages/api/ are skipped. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [fact] The api-testing skill is available on demand with this setup. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [concept] Worktrees created from a session contain .claude/, packages/api/, packages/shared/, and root-level files with deny rules applied across the worktree. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#put-it-together
- [concept] When a single change touches several packages, how you scope and sequence the task affects the result. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-and-plan-changes-that-span-packages
- [idea] Give Claude the whole change in one session to keep decisions behind each edit consistent rather than re-deriving them per package. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-and-plan-changes-that-span-packages
- [idea] Plan before editing by using plan mode, where Claude writes the plan to a file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-and-plan-changes-that-span-packages
- [concept] A long cross-package session compacts its context along the way. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-and-plan-changes-that-span-packages
- [fact] Claude Code re-injects the plan file after each compaction so the plan survives where conversation history may not. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#scope-and-plan-changes-that-span-packages
- [actionable] Use hooks to run per-directory linters or type-checkers after Claude edits files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#next-steps
- [fact] Codebase size affects token usage and spend limits can be set before a wider rollout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#next-steps
- [idea] Read the blog post on how Claude Code works in large codebases for organizational rollout patterns and ownership models. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases#next-steps

## Other LLM gateways
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway>

- [definition] Other LLM gateways — Route Claude Code through an LLM gateway your organization already runs. Covers connecting Claude Code to a gateway, rolling one out for your organization, and what Claude Code sends to a gateway. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway#other-llm-gateways
- [definition] What a gateway provides — A gateway gives your organization one place to manage: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway#what-a-gateway-provides
- [definition] Roll out a gateway — When you're ready to roll out an LLM gateway to your organization, the sequence is the same whichever gateway product you choose: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway#roll-out-a-gateway
- [definition] Subscriptions and gateways — While a [gateway credential variable](/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#set-the-credential-variable) or `apiKeyHelper` is active, a developer's claude.ai subscription isn't used: the credential replaces the subscription login for that session, and the subscription's usage limits don't apply. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway#subscriptions-and-gateways
- [concept] A gateway provides a central place to manage credentials, usage tracking, cost controls, audit logging, and provider switching for Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [fact] Anthropic does not endorse, maintain, or audit third-party gateway products. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [concept] Provider switching without reconfiguring developer machines requires the gateway to expose a single Anthropic-format endpoint regardless of the upstream provider. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [problem] If a gateway does not forward new capabilities added in Claude Code releases, those features will break. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [actionable] Deploy the gateway and provide it with your provider credential so it can authenticate forwarded requests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [actionable] Issue each developer a gateway credential to attribute usage and allow revocation during offboarding. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [actionable] Distribute the configuration via a managed settings file and secrets tooling so every machine receives the base URL and a credential. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [actionable] Have each developer check for the configuration in Claude Code to surface distribution problems before they depend on the gateway. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [fact] While a gateway credential variable or `apiKeyHelper` is active, the developer's claude.ai subscription is not used for that session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [fact] Traffic routed through a gateway is billed per token to the account owning the forwarded credential, such as an Anthropic Console or cloud provider account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [problem] Setting only `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` without a gateway credential does not replace the subscription; usage limits and billing still apply to the saved login. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [fact] Gateways that pass traffic to Anthropic must forward the OAuth capability in `anthropic-beta` request headers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [idea] Use a managed settings file and secrets tooling for configuration distribution to ensure developers do not need to configure anything manually. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway
- [concept] A gateway that exposes a provider's own format ties the client configuration to that specific provider, preventing easy switching. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway

- [definition] Connect Claude Code to an LLM gateway — Point Claude Code at your organization's LLM gateway. - [definition] Check for an existing configuration — Administrators can distribute the gateway address and credential through [managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings), device management, or an [`apiKeyHelper`](#rotate-credentials-with-apikeyhelper), so Claude Code picks them up at startup with nothing for you to set. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#check-for-an-existing-configuration
- [definition] Start Claude Code — Run `claude`. If it opens to the login screen instead of a session, no gateway credential was distributed; [configure it yourself](#configure-claude-code-yourself) below. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#check-for-an-existing-configuration
- [definition] Check the Status tab — If Claude Code started a session without showing the login screen, run `/status`, which opens on the **Status** tab, and check two lines: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#check-for-an-existing-configuration
- [definition] Send a test message — Close the `/status` menu and send any prompt in Claude Code. A normal response from Claude, with no error, confirms the gateway connection works. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#check-for-an-existing-configuration
- [definition] Configure Claude Code yourself — To configure Claude Code for the gateway yourself, you need from your gateway team: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [definition] Set the credential variable — To authenticate Claude Code to the gateway, set your credential in an environment variable. Which variable depends on what your gateway team told you: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#set-the-credential-variable
- [definition] Set the base URL and credential — Set the gateway's base URL and the credential variable you picked above as environment variables. The examples use `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`; swap it for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` if that's [the variable you picked](#set-the-credential-variable). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#set-the-base-url-and-credential
- [definition] Verify the connection — With the variables exported in your shell, send a one-token request to the gateway directly. This confirms the URL and credential work before you open Claude Code, so a failure points at the gateway rather than your configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#verify-the-connection
- [definition] How the credential variable maps to a header — Each variable sends the credential in a different HTTP header: `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in `Authorization: Bearer`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `x-api-key`, and `apiKeyHelper` in both. A credential in the wrong variable reaches the gateway in a header it doesn't read, and the request fails with `401`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#how-the-credential-variable-maps-to-a-header
- [definition] Conflicts with an existing login — A gateway credential variable takes precedence over a saved claude.ai login or Console key. Your claude.ai login stays saved and unused while the variable is set; unset the variable and Claude Code goes back to it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#conflicts-with-an-existing-login
- [definition] Configure each surface — The CLI reads the environment variables and settings files above. The other surfaces are the VS Code extension, the desktop app, GitHub Actions, the Agent SDK, and the cloud surfaces such as Slack and the web; the sections below cover whether those settings reach each one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [definition] VS Code extension — Set the gateway variables for the [VS Code extension](/docs/en/vs-code) in `claudeCode.environmentVariables`, in VS Code's own user settings opened with the **Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)** command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#vs-code-extension
- [definition] Desktop app — The desktop app reads gateway routing from its [third-party inference configuration](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/gateway), not from `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `settings.json`. That configuration can come from your organization or from a form in the app itself: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#desktop-app
- [definition] GitHub Actions — [Claude Code GitHub Actions](/docs/en/github-actions) reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` from the workflow's `env` block. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#github-actions
- [definition] Agent SDK — The [Agent SDK](/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) has no gateway-specific options; it passes environment variables to the Claude Code process it spawns. Each SDK accepts an `env` option that sets the spawned process's environment, and the TypeScript and Python SDKs treat it differently: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#agent-sdk
- [definition] Slack, web, and Remote Control — [Claude Code in Slack](/docs/en/slack) and [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) are Anthropic-hosted products that always use Anthropic's API; they aren't part of a gateway deployment. Gateway variables set in a cloud session's environment configuration are not applied. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#slack-web-and-remote-control
- [definition] Additional configuration — These settings cover cases beyond the base URL and credential. Set them only if your administrator's instructions, your network's egress rules, or the [troubleshooting table](#troubleshoot-gateway-errors) call for one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#additional-configuration
- [definition] Send additional headers — Some gateways route or tag requests using a custom header in addition to the credential, for example a tenant identifier or a routing key. To send one, set [`ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`](/docs/en/env-vars) with one `Name: Value` pair per line. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#send-additional-headers
- [definition] Add gateway models to the model picker — With model discovery enabled, Claude Code queries the gateway for its model list at startup and adds those names to the `/model` picker alongside the built-in entries. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#add-gateway-models-to-the-model-picker
- [definition] Rotate credentials with apiKeyHelper — An `apiKeyHelper` is a command Claude Code runs to fetch your gateway credential, instead of reading it from a static environment variable. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#rotate-credentials-with-apikeyhelper
- [definition] Turn off traffic outside the gateway path — The gateway carries model requests, but Claude Code also sends nonessential background traffic outside the gateway path, to Anthropic and to third-party services such as GitHub: version checks, telemetry, release notes, and similar requests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#turn-off-traffic-outside-the-gateway-path
- [definition] Route to a cloud provider through a gateway — These configurations point Claude Code at a gateway through a provider-specific base URL variable in place of `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#route-to-a-cloud-provider-through-a-gateway
- [definition] Troubleshoot gateway errors — These are the most common errors when running Claude Code through a gateway, with the gateway-side cause and the fix: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#troubleshoot-gateway-errors

- [concept] To configure Claude Code for a gateway, you need the gateway's base URL and a credential, which can be a key, token string, or a command to fetch one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] If the gateway team does not specify the credential type, use `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` as the default variable to try. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [actionable] Set the gateway's base URL and credential variable as environment variables using shell exports for a single session or in a settings file for persistence. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [concept] Shell exports apply only to the current terminal session and programs started from it, whereas settings files persist across all Claude Code runs including background agents. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [problem] An editor launched from the dock or Start menu will not see shell environment variables, and exporting only in the shell does not reliably reach background agents hosted by the supervisor. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [idea] Use a settings file for any gateway that background agents must always route through to ensure reliable configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] `~/.claude/settings.json` applies to all projects, while `.claude/settings.local.json` applies to a single project and is added to the global gitignore. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [problem] Do not put credentials in a project's `.claude/settings.json` because that file is committed and shared with everyone who clones the repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] When both a shell export and a settings-file `env` block set the same variable, the settings-file value takes precedence. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [actionable] Run `/status` to see which base URL and credential source Claude Code is currently using. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] A successful verification request returns a JSON response starting with `{"id":"msg_` and including a `"content":[...]` field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] An error naming an unknown model still proves the URL and credential work because the gateway authenticated the request before rejecting the model name. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [problem] A `401` error means the credential was rejected, often indicating you guessed the wrong variable and need to switch to the other one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [concept] `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` sends the credential in the `Authorization: Bearer` header, while `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` sends it in the `x-api-key` header. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] If your gateway expects keys in the `x-api-key` header, replace the `Authorization` header with `x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in Bash or the corresponding hashtable entry in PowerShell. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] A gateway credential variable takes precedence over a saved claude.ai login or Console key, leaving the saved login unused while the variable is set. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [fact] With `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, the variable takes precedence immediately, whereas with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` you are prompted once in interactive mode to approve the key. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself
- [actionable] Run `/logout` to clear a saved login so only the gateway credential remains. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-claude-code-yourself

- [concept] The VS Code extension checks credentials from `claudeCode.environmentVariables` in user settings before launching, which is the reliable place for gateway credentials. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] Values in `~/.claude/settings.json` reach the spawned process but do not reach the VS Code extension's own login check. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [actionable] Open User Settings (JSON) using the command **Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)** to configure gateway variables for the VS Code extension. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [concept] The desktop app reads gateway routing from a third-party inference configuration rather than `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `settings.json`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] An administrator-distributed configuration takes precedence and makes the local configuration form read-only. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [actionable] Enable Developer Mode via Help → Troubleshooting → Enable Developer Mode to access the Developer menu for configuring third-party inference. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] When the gateway configuration is active, the desktop app runs sessions locally only and does not offer SSH sessions or Anthropic-hosted cloud environments. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [problem] If the desktop app shows `Gateway was unreachable`, it could not reach the configured base URL at startup. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] For GitHub Actions, the action sets the `anthropic_api_key` input as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to reach the gateway in the `x-api-key` header. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] For a bearer-token gateway, pass the secret twice: as the `anthropic_api_key` input and as `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in the workflow `env` block. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] The GitHub Action requires `anthropic_api_key`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or workload identity federation before launching Claude Code and does not read `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for launch. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [concept] The Agent SDK has no gateway-specific options but passes environment variables to the spawned Claude Code process via an `env` option. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] In the TypeScript SDK, setting `options.env` replaces the environment entirely, requiring spreading `process.env` to keep gateway variables. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] In the Python SDK, `ClaudeAgentOptions(env=...)` merges on top of the inherited environment, allowing gateway variables to carry through without spreading. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [problem] Gateway variables set in a cloud session's environment configuration are not applied to Claude Code in Slack or on the web. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [idea] If traffic must stay on the gateway, do not enable Claude Code in Slack or on the web for those users. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] Remote Control and voice dictation rely on a claude.ai identity and are unavailable while `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or an `apiKeyHelper` is active. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] Remote Control is disabled while `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a non-Anthropic host, even if signed in with claude.ai. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [problem] Before version v2.1.196, a non-Anthropic base URL did not block Remote Control. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [actionable] To restore features, log in with claude.ai and unset the gateway variables that feature checks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [fact] The Remote Control section of `claude doctor` names what is currently blocking Remote Control. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#configure-each-surface
- [problem] If Claude Code prompts you to log in repeatedly after removing gateway configuration, the cause is usually credential storage rather than the gateway. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#troubleshoot-gateway-errors
- [actionable] See the authentication errors documentation for fixes regarding repeated login prompts after removing gateway configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#troubleshoot-gateway-errors

## Gateway protocol reference
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol>

- [definition] Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS — Microsoft Foundry and the [Claude Platform on AWS](/docs/en/claude-platform-on-aws) implement the Anthropic Messages format. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#foundry-and-claude-platform-on-aws
- [definition] Optional endpoints and startup traffic — Token-counting endpoints are the only optional ones: when they're absent, Claude Code falls back to counting context usage through the inference endpoint instead. Inference requests post to `/v1/messages?beta=true`, so match on the path, not the full URL. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#optional-endpoints-and-startup-traffic
- [definition] Streaming — Inference responses must stream. Claude Code consumes server-sent events as they arrive, so a gateway that buffers complete responses before relaying them stalls the client. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#streaming
- [definition] Format mismatch with the upstream — Which format the client speaks determines what your gateway receives. The common failure mode is a mismatch between the format the client sends to your gateway and the format the upstream provider behind it accepts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#format-mismatch-with-the-upstream
- [definition] Request headers — Claude Code includes these headers on API requests. Header names are case-insensitive on the wire. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#request-headers
- [definition] Forward as open lists — Treat the headers and body fields as open lists, not closed ones. Claude Code gains capabilities over releases, and they arrive as new `anthropic-beta` values, new request body fields, and occasionally new `anthropic-*` or `x-claude-code-*` headers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#forward-as-open-lists
- [definition] System prompt attribution block — Claude Code prepends a short attribution block to the system prompt containing the client version and a fingerprint derived from the conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#system-prompt-attribution-block
- [definition] Feature pass-through — Claude Code treats an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway as an Anthropic-format endpoint and sends it the beta headers and request body fields it sends to `api.anthropic.com`, except a small set of diagnostics and defaults reserved for direct connections, such as the fine-grained tool streaming default… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#feature-pass-through

- [definition] Disable pre-release capabilities — `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` stops Claude Code from sending pre-release capabilities and their body fields on every provider, including context management and the beta tool fields. The variable doesn't affect adaptive reasoning, which is selected by model rather than by beta. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#disable-pre-release-capabilities
- [definition] Model discovery — When `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a gateway that exposes the Anthropic Messages format, Claude Code can query the gateway's `/v1/models` endpoint at startup and add the returned models to the `/model` picker. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#model-discovery
- [definition] When discovery runs — Discovery applies only to the Anthropic Messages format. It doesn't run when: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#when-discovery-runs
- [definition] Request and response — The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential can't leak to a redirect target. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#request-and-response
