- [parameter] `--name "My Project"`: Set a custom session title visible in the session list at claude.ai/code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--remote-control-session-name-prefix <prefix>`: Prefix for auto-generated session names when no explicit name is set. Defaults to your machine's hostname, producing names like `myhost-graceful-unicorn`. Set `CLAUDE_REMOTE_CONTROL_SESSION_NAME_PREFIX` for the same effect. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `-c`, `--continue`: Bring back the session that the last server in this directory started with, instead of creating a new one. See [Resume sessions after stopping the server](#resume-sessions-after-stopping-the-server). Can't be combined with `--session-id`, `--spawn`, `--capacity`, or `--create-session-in-dir`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.200 or later; earlier versions reject the flag as an… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--session-id <id>`: Bring back one session by its ID. See [Resume sessions after stopping the server](#resume-sessions-after-stopping-the-server). Can't be combined with `--continue`, `--spawn`, `--capacity`, or `--create-session-in-dir`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.200 or later; earlier versions reject the flag as an unknown argument. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--spawn <mode>`: How the server creates sessions.<br />• `same-dir` (default): all sessions share the current working directory, so they can conflict if editing the same files.<br />• `worktree`: each on-demand session gets its own [git worktree](/docs/en/worktrees). Requires a git repository.<br />• `session`: single-session mode. Serves exactly one session and rejects additional connections.… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--capacity <N>`: Maximum number of concurrent sessions. Default is 32. Cannot be used with `--spawn=session`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--[no-]create-session-in-dir`: Pre-create one session in the current directory when the server starts, so you have somewhere to type immediately. In `worktree` mode this session stays in the current directory while on-demand sessions get isolated worktrees. On by default. If you pass `--no-create-session-in-dir` to start with none, Claude Code archives the server's sessions when you stop it, so… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--permission-mode <mode>`: Set the starting [permission mode](/docs/en/permission-modes) for the server's sessions, such as `acceptEdits`. Accepts `manual` as an alias for `default`; an unrecognized mode stops the server at startup and lists the valid modes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--debug-file <path>`: Write debug logs to the given file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--verbose`: Show detailed connection and session logs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] `--sandbox` / `--no-sandbox`: Enable or disable [sandboxing](/docs/en/sandboxing) for filesystem and network isolation. Off by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [parameter] [Dispatch](/docs/en/desktop#sessions-from-dispatch): Trigger=Message a task from the Claude mobile app; Claude runs on=Your machine (Desktop); Setup=[Pair the mobile app with Desktop](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13947068); Best for=Delegating work while you're away, minimal setup — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#choose-the-right-approach
- [parameter] [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control): Trigger=Drive a running session from [claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code) or the Claude mobile app; Claude runs on=Your machine (CLI or VS Code); Setup=Run `claude remote-control`; Best for=Steering in-progress work from another device — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#choose-the-right-approach
- [parameter] [Channels](/docs/en/channels): Trigger=Push events from a chat app like Telegram or Discord, or your own server; Claude runs on=Your machine (CLI); Setup=[Install a channel plugin](/docs/en/channels#quickstart) or [build your own](/docs/en/channels-reference); Best for=Reacting to external events like CI failures or chat messages — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#choose-the-right-approach
- [parameter] [Slack](/docs/en/slack): Trigger=Mention `@Claude` in a team channel; Claude runs on=Anthropic cloud; Setup=[Install the Slack app](/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack) with [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) enabled; Best for=PRs and reviews from team chat — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#choose-the-right-approach
- [parameter] [Self-hosted environments](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments): Trigger=Start a [cloud session](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) and pick your organization's environment; Claude runs on=Your organization's infrastructure; Setup=[Deploy runners](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-quickstart), on Team and Enterprise plans; Best for=Cloud sessions that must run inside your network — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#choose-the-right-approach
- [parameter] [Scheduled tasks](/docs/en/scheduled-tasks): Trigger=Set a schedule; Claude runs on=[CLI](/docs/en/scheduled-tasks), [Desktop](/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks), or [cloud](/docs/en/routines); Setup=Pick a frequency; Best for=Recurring automation like daily reviews — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#choose-the-right-approach
- [definition] Continue local sessions from any device with Remote Control — Continue a local Claude Code session from your phone, tablet, or any browser using Remote Control. Works with claude.ai/code and the Claude mobile app. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#continue-local-sessions-from-any-device-with-remote-control
- [definition] Requirements — Before using Remote Control, confirm that your environment meets these conditions: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#requirements
- [definition] Start a Remote Control session — You can start a Remote Control session from the CLI or the VS Code extension. The CLI offers three invocation modes; VS Code uses the `/remote-control` command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session
- [definition] Check connection status — In an interactive terminal session, a `/rc active` indicator sits in the footer below the input box while the connection is up, and is hidden if the terminal is too narrow to fit it. The indicator text is a link to the session on claude.ai. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#check-connection-status
- [definition] Session URL reminders — While Remote Control is connected, Claude Code reminds you of the session URL when switching to your phone or browser helps most, so you don't have to find the link in `/remote-control`. A reminder appears above the prompt box at either of these moments: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#session-url-reminders
- [definition] Connect from another device — Once a Remote Control session is active, you have a few ways to connect from another device: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#connect-from-another-device
- [definition] What connected devices see — A connected device shows the conversation in your terminal as it happens. These cases go beyond ordinary messages: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#what-connected-devices-see
- [definition] Enable Remote Control for all sessions — Remote Control only activates when you explicitly run `claude remote-control`, `claude --remote-control`, or `/remote-control`, unless auto-connect is turned on. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#enable-remote-control-for-all-sessions
- [definition] Resume sessions after stopping the server — When you stop `claude remote-control` with Ctrl+C, the sessions it was serving stop responding from your phone or browser. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#resume-sessions-after-stopping-the-server
- [definition] Connection and security — Your local Claude Code session makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports on your machine. When you start Remote Control, it registers with the Anthropic API and polls for work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#connection-and-security
- [definition] Trusted Devices — Trusted Devices is currently in beta. Features and functionality may evolve as the experience is refined. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#trusted-devices
- [definition] Enable Trusted Devices for your organization — An Owner enables the setting from the Claude Code admin console. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#enable-trusted-devices-for-your-organization
- [definition] Open Claude Code admin settings — Go to [claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code). The **Require trusted devices** toggle appears under the Remote Control setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#enable-trusted-devices-for-your-organization
- [definition] Turn on Require trusted devices — The setting applies to every member of the organization and to Remote Control sessions started after you enable it. Sessions that were already running before the toggle was turned on are not retroactively protected and continue without the device requirement until they end. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#enable-trusted-devices-for-your-organization
- [definition] Tell members what to expect — The first time a member views or steers a new Remote Control session from a browser, phone, or desktop app after the setting is enabled, they are prompted to enroll that device. Letting them know ahead of time avoids confusion. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#enable-trusted-devices-for-your-organization
- [definition] What members see — Enrollment is a one-time step per device. After that, the only visible change is an occasional biometric prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#what-members-see
- [definition] Manage enrolled devices — Members can review and revoke their own devices from account settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#manage-enrolled-devices
- [definition] Remote Control vs Claude Code on the web — Remote Control and [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) both use the claude.ai/code interface. The key difference is where the session runs: Remote Control executes on your machine, so your local MCP servers, tools, and project configuration stay available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-vs-claude-code-on-the-web
- [definition] Mobile push notifications — When Remote Control is active, Claude can send push notifications to your phone. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#mobile-push-notifications
- [definition] Install the Claude mobile app — Download the Claude app for [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/claude-by-anthropic/id6473753684) or [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.anthropic.claude). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#mobile-push-notifications
- [definition] Sign in with your Claude Code account — Use the same account and organization you use for Claude Code in the terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#mobile-push-notifications
- [definition] Allow notifications — Accept the notification permission prompt from the operating system. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#mobile-push-notifications
- [definition] Enable push in Claude Code — In your terminal, run `/config` and enable **Push when Claude decides** for proactive notifications, **Push when actions required** for permission prompts and questions, or both. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#mobile-push-notifications
- [definition] "Remote Control requires a claude.ai subscription" — You're not authenticated with a claude.ai account. Run `claude auth login` and choose the claude.ai option. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-requires-a-claudeai-subscription
- [definition] "Remote Control requires a full-scope login token" — You're authenticated with a long-lived token from `claude setup-token` or the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. These tokens can only make model requests, so they can't establish Remote Control sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-requires-a-full-scope-login-token
- [definition] "Unable to determine your organization for Remote Control eligibility" — Your cached account information is stale or incomplete. Run `claude auth login` to refresh it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#unable-to-determine-your-organization-for-remote-control-eligibility
- [definition] "Remote Control isn't enabled for this account" — Claude Code checked Remote Control availability for the account you're signed in with and the check came back off. The usual cause is cached entitlements that are out of date after a plan change. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-isnt-enabled-for-this-account
- [definition] "Couldn't verify Remote Control eligibility" — Claude Code could not reach the feature-flag service to check whether Remote Control is enabled for your account, typically because you are offline or a proxy is blocking the request. Retry once you have network access, or run `claude doctor` for details. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#couldnt-verify-remote-control-eligibility
- [definition] "Remote Control requires feature-flag evaluation" — One of these variables is set: [`DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, or `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK`](/docs/en/env-vars). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-requires-feature-flag-evaluation
- [definition] "Remote Control is only available when using Claude via api.anthropic.com" — The session isn't talking to the Anthropic API directly, so there is no claude.ai backend to pair with. This happens on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-is-only-available-when-using-claude-via-apianthropiccom
- [definition] "Remote Control is disabled by your organization's policy" — A policy blocks Remote Control. The message's own text tells you which: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-is-disabled-by-your-organizations-policy
- [definition] "Remote Control isn't available for your organization due to its compliance policy" — Your organization has a data retention or compliance configuration that is incompatible with Remote Control; the parenthetical at the end of the message names it. In this state the admin panel's Remote Control toggle is grayed out, so an Owner can't change it there. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-isnt-available-for-your-organization-due-to-its-compliance-policy
- [definition] "Remote credentials fetch failed" — Claude Code could not obtain a short-lived credential from the Anthropic API to establish the connection. Re-run with `--verbose` to see the full error: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-credentials-fetch-failed
- [definition] "Couldn't reconnect to your Remote Control session" — When you resume a conversation with `claude --resume` or `claude --continue`, Claude Code reconnects to the Remote Control session recorded in that conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#couldnt-reconnect-to-your-remote-control-session
- [definition] "Previous session is unavailable — run /remote-control to start a new one" — Claude Code couldn't bring back the previous Remote Control session and stopped instead of starting a new one on its own. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#previous-session-is-unavailable-run-remote-control-to-start-a-new-one
- [definition] "Remote Control got an unexpected server response" — The Remote Control server accepted a request but replied in a form this version of Claude Code couldn't read, while creating the remote session or fetching its credentials. Retrying on the same version fails the same way. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#remote-control-got-an-unexpected-server-response
- [definition] "Your organization requires Trusted Devices for Remote Control, but this device is not enrolled" — Your organization has [Trusted Devices](#trusted-devices) enabled and this machine has not enrolled yet. Run `/login` in Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#your-organization-requires-trusted-devices-for-remote-control-but-this-device-is-not-enrolled
- [definition] "session expired for trusted-device check" — Your sign-in is more than 18 hours old. Run `/login` in Claude Code, or confirm with Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, or a passkey when claude.ai or the mobile app prompts you. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#session-expired-for-trusted-device-check
- [definition] Choose the right approach — Claude Code offers several ways to work when you're not at your terminal. They differ in what triggers the work, where Claude runs, and how much you need to set up. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#choose-the-right-approach

- [parameter] Is merged: Whether the PR has been merged — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#filter-pull-requests
- [definition] Automate work with routines — Put Claude Code on autopilot. Define routines that run on a schedule, trigger on API calls, or react to GitHub events from cloud infrastructure. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#automate-work-with-routines
- [definition] Example use cases — Each example pairs a trigger type with the kind of work routines are suited to: unattended, repeatable, and tied to a clear outcome. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#example-use-cases
- [definition] Create a routine — Create a routine from the web at [claude.ai/code/routines](https://claude.ai/code/routines), from the Desktop app, or from the CLI. All three surfaces write to the same cloud account, so a routine you create in one shows up in the others immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-a-routine
- [definition] Open the creation form — Visit [claude.ai/code/routines](https://claude.ai/code/routines) and click **New routine**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-web
- [definition] Name the routine and write the prompt — Give the routine a descriptive name and write the prompt Claude runs each time. The prompt is the most important part: the routine runs autonomously, so the prompt must be self-contained and explicit about what to do and what success looks like. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-web
- [definition] Select repositories — Add one or more GitHub repositories for Claude to work in. Each repository is cloned at the start of a run, starting from the default branch. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-web
- [definition] Select an environment — Pick a [cloud environment](/docs/en/cloud-environments) for the routine. Environments control what the cloud session has access to: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-web
- [definition] Select a trigger — Under **Select a trigger**, choose how the routine starts. You can pick one trigger type or combine several. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-web
- [definition] Review connectors — Under **Connectors** at the bottom of the form, all of your connected [MCP connectors](/docs/en/mcp) are included by default. Remove any the routine doesn't need: Claude can use every tool from an included connector, including writes, without asking for permission during a run. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-web
- [definition] Create the routine — Click **Create**. The routine appears in the list and runs the next time one of its triggers matches. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-web
- [definition] Create from the CLI — Run `/schedule` in any session to create a scheduled routine conversationally. You can also pass a description directly, for a recurring routine like `/schedule daily PR review at 9am` or a one-off like `/schedule clean up feature flag in one week`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#create-from-the-cli
- [definition] Configure triggers — A routine starts when one of its triggers matches. You can attach any combination of schedule, API, and GitHub triggers to the same routine, and add or remove them at any time from the **Select a trigger** section of the routine's edit form. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#configure-triggers
- [definition] Add a schedule trigger — A schedule trigger runs the routine on a recurring cadence, or once at a specific future time. Pick a preset frequency in the **Select a trigger** section: hourly, daily, weekdays, or weekly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-a-schedule-trigger
- [definition] Add an API trigger — An API trigger gives a routine a dedicated HTTP endpoint. POSTing to the endpoint with the routine's bearer token starts a new session and returns a session URL. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-an-api-trigger
- [definition] Open the routine for editing — Go to [claude.ai/code/routines](https://claude.ai/code/routines), click the routine you want to trigger via API, then click the pencil icon to open **Edit routine**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-an-api-trigger
- [definition] Add an API trigger — Scroll to the **Select a trigger** section below the **Instructions** box, click **Add another trigger**, and choose **API**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-an-api-trigger
- [definition] Copy the URL and generate a token — The modal shows the URL for this routine along with a sample curl command. Copy the URL, then click **Generate token** and copy the token immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-an-api-trigger
- [definition] Call the endpoint — Send the token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header when you POST to the URL. The [Trigger a routine](#trigger-a-routine) section below shows a complete example. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-an-api-trigger
- [definition] Add a GitHub trigger — A GitHub trigger starts a new session automatically when a matching event occurs on a connected repository. Claude Code doesn't reuse sessions across events, so two PR updates produce two independent sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-a-github-trigger
- [definition] Open the routine for editing — Go to [claude.ai/code/routines](https://claude.ai/code/routines), click the routine, then click the pencil icon to open **Edit routine**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-a-github-trigger
- [definition] Add a GitHub event trigger — Scroll to the **Select a trigger** section, click **Add another trigger**, and choose **GitHub event**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-a-github-trigger
- [definition] Configure the trigger — Select the repository, choose an event from the [supported events](#supported-events) list, and optionally add filters. Save the trigger. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#add-a-github-trigger
- [definition] Manage routines — Click a routine in the list to open its detail page. The detail page shows the routine's repositories, connectors, prompt, schedule, API tokens, GitHub triggers, and a list of past runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#manage-routines
- [definition] View and interact with runs — Click any run to open it as a full session. From there you can see what Claude did, review changes, create a pull request, or continue the conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#view-and-interact-with-runs
- [definition] Manage routines from the CLI — The CLI supports managing existing routines. Run `/schedule list` to see all routines, `/schedule update` to change one, or `/schedule run` to trigger it immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#manage-routines-from-the-cli
- [definition] Repositories and branch permissions — Routines need GitHub access to clone repositories. When you create a routine from the CLI with `/schedule`, Claude checks whether your account has GitHub access for the repository you ran it from and, if it doesn't, adds a setup note naming how to grant it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#repositories-and-branch-permissions
- [definition] Connectors — Routines can use your connected MCP connectors to read from and write to external services during each run. For example, a routine that triages support requests might read from a Slack channel and create issues in Linear. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#connectors
- [definition] Environments and network access — Each routine uses a [cloud environment](/docs/en/cloud-environments) that controls network access, environment variables, and setup scripts. The routine inherits the environment's network policy on every run. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#environments-and-network-access
- [definition] Open the routine for editing — On the routine's detail page, click the pencil icon to open **Edit routine**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#environments-and-network-access
- [definition] Open the environment selector — Below the **Instructions** box, select the cloud icon showing your environment's name, such as **Default**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#environments-and-network-access
- [definition] Open the environment settings — Hover over the environment in the list and click the settings icon that appears on the right. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#environments-and-network-access
- [definition] Change the network access level — In the **Update cloud environment** dialog, change **Network access** to **Custom** and enter your domains in **Allowed domains**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#environments-and-network-access
- [definition] Save — Click **Save changes**. The new policy applies from the next run. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#environments-and-network-access
- [definition] Usage and limits — Routines draw down subscription usage the same way interactive sessions do. In addition to the standard subscription limits, routines have a daily cap on how many runs can start per account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#usage-and-limits
- [definition] `/schedule` returns "Unknown command" — The CLI hides `/schedule` when one of its requirements isn't met: the command menu shows `No commands match "/schedule"` while you type, and submitting it returns `Unknown command: /schedule` in every case below except a Console API key or an Anthropic profile with feature-flag fetching enabled. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#schedule-returns-unknown-command
- [definition] `/schedule` asks you to authenticate — If `/schedule` runs but Claude responds that you need to authenticate with a claude.ai account first, the CLI has no stored claude.ai login. API accounts aren't supported for routines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#schedule-asks-you-to-authenticate
- [definition] "Routines are disabled by your organization's policy" — An Owner in your Team or Enterprise organization has likely turned off the **Routines** toggle at [claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code). On Claude Code v2.1.227 or later, the same toggle also hides `/schedule` in the CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#routines-are-disabled-by-your-organizations-policy

- [parameter] `~/.claude/loop.md`: User-level. Applies in any project that does not define its own. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#customize-the-default-prompt-with-loopmd
- [parameter] `CronCreate`: Schedule a new task. Accepts a 5-field cron expression, the prompt to run, and whether it recurs or fires once. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#manage-scheduled-tasks
- [parameter] `CronList`: List all scheduled tasks with their IDs, schedules, and prompts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#manage-scheduled-tasks
- [parameter] `CronDelete`: Cancel a task by ID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#manage-scheduled-tasks
- [parameter] `*/5 * * * *`: Every 5 minutes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#cron-expression-reference
- [parameter] `0 * * * *`: Every hour on the hour — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#cron-expression-reference
- [parameter] `7 * * * *`: Every hour at 7 minutes past — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#cron-expression-reference
- [parameter] `0 9 * * *`: Every day at 9am local — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#cron-expression-reference
- [parameter] `0 9 * * 1-5`: Weekdays at 9am local — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#cron-expression-reference
- [parameter] `30 14 15 3 *`: March 15 at 2:30pm local — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#cron-expression-reference
- [definition] Run prompts on a schedule — Use /loop and the cron scheduling tools to run prompts repeatedly, poll for status, or set one-time reminders within a Claude Code session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#run-prompts-on-a-schedule
- [definition] Compare scheduling options — Claude Code offers three ways to schedule recurring or one-off work: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#compare-scheduling-options
- [definition] Run a prompt repeatedly with /loop — The `/loop` [bundled skill](/docs/en/commands) is the quickest way to run a prompt on repeat while the session stays open. Both the interval and the prompt are optional, and what you provide determines how the loop behaves. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#run-a-prompt-repeatedly-with-loop
- [definition] Run on a fixed interval — When you supply an interval, Claude converts it to a cron expression, schedules the job, and confirms the cadence and job ID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#run-on-a-fixed-interval
- [definition] Let Claude choose the interval — When you omit the interval, Claude chooses one dynamically instead of running on a fixed cron schedule. After each iteration it picks a delay between one minute and one hour based on what it observed: short waits while a build is finishing or a PR is active, longer waits when nothing is pending. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#let-claude-choose-the-interval
- [definition] Run the built-in maintenance prompt — When you omit the prompt, Claude uses a built-in maintenance prompt instead of one you supply. On each iteration it works through the following, in order: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#run-the-built-in-maintenance-prompt
- [definition] Customize the default prompt with loop.md — Create a `loop.md` file to replace the [built-in maintenance prompt](#run-the-built-in-maintenance-prompt) with your own instructions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#customize-the-default-prompt-with-loopmd
- [definition] Stop a loop — To stop a [self-paced `/loop`](#let-claude-choose-the-interval) while it is waiting for the next iteration, press `Esc`. This clears the pending wakeup so the loop does not fire again. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#stop-a-loop
- [definition] Set a one-time reminder — For one-shot reminders, describe what you want in natural language instead of using `/loop`. Claude schedules a single-fire task that deletes itself after running. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#set-a-one-time-reminder
- [definition] Manage scheduled tasks — Ask Claude in natural language to list or cancel tasks, or reference the underlying tools directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#manage-scheduled-tasks
- [definition] How scheduled tasks run — The scheduler checks every second for due tasks and enqueues them at low priority. A scheduled prompt fires between your turns, not while Claude is mid-response. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#how-scheduled-tasks-run
- [definition] Jitter — To avoid every session hitting the API at the same wall-clock moment, the scheduler adds a deterministic offset to fire times: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#jitter
- [definition] Seven-day expiry — Recurring tasks automatically expire 7 days after creation. The task fires one final time, then deletes itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#seven-day-expiry
- [definition] Cron expression reference — `CronCreate` accepts standard 5-field cron expressions: `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`. All fields support wildcards (`*`), single values (`5`), steps (`*/15`), ranges (`1-5`), and comma-separated lists (`1,15,30`). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#cron-expression-reference
- [definition] Disable scheduled tasks — Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1` in your environment to disable the scheduler entirely. The cron tools and `/loop` become unavailable, and any already-scheduled tasks stop firing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#disable-scheduled-tasks
- [definition] Limitations — Session-scoped scheduling has inherent constraints: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#limitations

## Security
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security>

- [definition] Security — Learn about Claude Code's security safeguards and best practices for safe usage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#security
- [definition] Security foundation — Your code's security is paramount. Claude Code is built with security at its core, developed according to Anthropic's comprehensive security program. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#security-foundation
- [definition] Permission-based architecture — In Manual mode, Claude Code starts with read-only permissions. When Claude Code needs to edit files, run tests, or execute commands, it asks you first, and you choose whether to approve the action once or allow it from then on. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#permission-based-architecture
- [definition] User responsibility — Claude Code only has the permissions you grant it. You're responsible for reviewing proposed code and commands for safety before approval. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#user-responsibility
- [definition] Protect against prompt injection — Prompt injection is a technique where an attacker attempts to override or manipulate an AI assistant's instructions by inserting malicious text. Claude Code includes several safeguards against these attacks: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#protect-against-prompt-injection
- [definition] Privacy safeguards — We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#privacy-safeguards
- [definition] MCP security — Claude Code allows users to configure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The list of allowed MCP servers is configured in your source code, as part of Claude Code settings engineers check into source control. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#mcp-security
- [definition] IDE security — See [VS Code security and privacy](/docs/en/vs-code#security-and-privacy) for more information on running Claude Code in an IDE. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#ide-security
- [definition] Cloud execution security — When using [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web), additional security controls are in place. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#cloud-execution-security
- [definition] Reporting security issues — If you discover a security vulnerability in Claude Code: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security#reporting-security-issues

- [parameter] `UserPromptSubmit`: Capture the working-tree baseline that the end-of-turn review diffs against — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-the-plugin-integrates-with-claude-code
- [parameter] `PostToolUse` on `Edit`, `Write`, and `NotebookEdit`: Per-edit pattern match — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-the-plugin-integrates-with-claude-code
- [parameter] `Stop`: End-of-turn diff review, run in the background — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-the-plugin-integrates-with-claude-code
- [parameter] `PostToolUse` on `Bash`, filtered to `git commit` and `git push`: Commit and push review, run in the background — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-the-plugin-integrates-with-claude-code
- [parameter] In session: Tool=Security guidance plugin; What it covers=Common vulnerabilities in code Claude writes, fixed in the same session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-this-fits-with-other-security-tools
- [parameter] On demand, single pass: Tool=[`/security-review`](/docs/en/commands#all-commands); What it covers=One-time security pass on the current branch, run when you ask — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-this-fits-with-other-security-tools
- [parameter] On demand, deep scan: Tool=[Claude Security plugin](/docs/en/claude-security); What it covers=Multi-agent vulnerability scan of a repository or diff, with independently reviewed findings and patches — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-this-fits-with-other-security-tools
- [parameter] On pull request: Tool=[Code Review](/docs/en/code-review), Team and Enterprise plans; What it covers=Multi-agent correctness and security review with full codebase context — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-this-fits-with-other-security-tools
- [parameter] In CI: Tool=Your existing static analysis and dependency scanners; What it covers=Language-specific rules, supply-chain checks, and policy enforcement the plugin does not attempt — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-this-fits-with-other-security-tools
- [definition] Catch security issues as Claude writes code — Install the security-guidance plugin to have Claude review its own code changes for vulnerabilities and fix them in the same session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#catch-security-issues-as-claude-writes-code
- [definition] Install the plugin — In a terminal Claude Code session, install from the [official Anthropic marketplace](/docs/en/discover-plugins#official-anthropic-marketplace): — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#install-the-plugin
- [definition] Enable in cloud sessions and shared repositories — User-scoped plugins do not carry into [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web), because those sessions run in the cloud rather than on your machine. To enable the plugin there, or to turn it on for everyone who clones a repository, declare it in the project's checked-in settings: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#enable-in-cloud-sessions-and-shared-repositories
- [definition] What the plugin checks — The plugin reviews Claude's work at three points, each at a different depth: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#what-the-plugin-checks
- [definition] On each file edit — When Claude writes to a file, the plugin scans the new content for known risky patterns. This is a pattern match with no model call, so it adds no usage cost. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#on-each-file-edit
- [definition] At the end of each turn — A turn is one round of Claude responding: you send a message, Claude works and replies, and the turn ends. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#at-the-end-of-each-turn
- [definition] On each commit or push Claude makes — When Claude runs `git commit` or `git push` through its Bash tool, the plugin runs a deeper agentic review of the change in the background. This review reads surrounding code, including callers, sanitizers, and related files, to decide whether a finding is real before reporting it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#on-each-commit-or-push-claude-makes
- [definition] Review independence and limits — The plugin does not ask the same Claude instance that wrote the code to grade itself. The per-edit check is a deterministic string match with no model involved. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#review-independence-and-limits
- [definition] Add your own rules — The plugin has two extension points: a Markdown guidance file for the model-backed reviews, and a YAML or JSON patterns file for the per-edit string match. Both are additive. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#add-your-own-rules
- [definition] Add guidance for the model-backed reviews — Create `.claude/claude-security-guidance.md` in your project and describe your threat model and review checklist in plain language. The model-backed reviews load it as additional context alongside the built-in vulnerability checklist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#add-guidance-for-the-model-backed-reviews
- [definition] Add custom per-edit patterns — Create `.claude/security-patterns.yaml` to add regex or substring rules to the [per-edit pattern check](#on-each-file-edit). These run as deterministic string matches alongside the built-in patterns: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#add-custom-per-edit-patterns
- [definition] Rule file lookup locations — The plugin looks for `claude-security-guidance.md` and `security-patterns.yaml` in the same locations, independently of how the plugin was enabled: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#rule-file-lookup-locations
- [definition] Usage cost — The [per-edit pattern check](#on-each-file-edit) makes no model call and adds no cost. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#usage-cost
- [definition] Disable or uninstall — To turn off individual layers while keeping the rest, set the matching environment variable: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#disable-or-uninstall
- [definition] How the plugin integrates with Claude Code — The plugin is built entirely on [hooks](/docs/en/hooks), the mechanism for running your own code at specific points in Claude's loop. It registers: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-the-plugin-integrates-with-claude-code
- [definition] How this fits with other security tools — The plugin is one layer in a defense-in-depth approach. It catches issues earliest, while code is still in the editor, but it is not a guarantee and does not replace later checks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#how-this-fits-with-other-security-tools
- [definition] Troubleshooting — The plugin writes runtime diagnostics to `~/.claude/security/log.txt`. Check there first if reviews are not appearing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#troubleshooting
- [definition] Related resources — To go deeper on the pieces this page touches: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-guidance#related-resources

- [parameter] **Server-managed settings**: Best for=Organizations without MDM, or users on unmanaged devices; Security model=Settings that Claude Code fetches from Anthropic's servers at startup and refreshes hourly during the session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#choose-between-server-managed-and-endpoint-managed-settings
- [parameter] **[Endpoint-managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings#delivery-mechanisms)**: Best for=Organizations with MDM or endpoint management; Security model=Settings deployed to devices via MDM configuration profiles, registry policies, or managed settings files — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#choose-between-server-managed-and-endpoint-managed-settings
- [parameter] User edits the cached settings file: Tampered file applies at startup, and the next server fetch restores the correct settings, except for the [keys that apply only at the next launch](#fetch-and-caching-behavior), such as `model` or a variable added to the `env` block, which stay in effect until relaunch. In Claude Code v2.1.198 or later, the [withheld environment… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [parameter] User deletes the cached settings file: [First-launch behavior](#fetch-and-caching-behavior) occurs — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [parameter] User runs a modified Claude Code binary: A user who can run a modified client can bypass any client-side control — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [parameter] User runs an older Claude Code version: Versions that predate server-managed settings don't fetch or apply them — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [parameter] API is unavailable: Cached settings apply if available. Without a cache, Claude Code enforces no server-managed settings until the next successful fetch and still applies any [endpoint-managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings#delivery-mechanisms) on the device. In Claude Code v2.1.198 or later, the [withheld environment variables](#fetch-and-caching-behavior) in the cached `env` block don't… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [parameter] User authenticates with a different organization: Settings are not delivered for accounts outside the managed organization — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [parameter] User configures a [third-party model provider](#platform-availability): Server-managed settings are bypassed. This includes setting `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS`, or a non-default `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [parameter] Network traffic is intercepted or redirected: Disabled TLS validation or intercepted traffic can alter the settings the client receives — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [definition] Configure server-managed settings — Centrally configure Claude Code for your organization through server-delivered settings, without requiring device management infrastructure. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#configure-server-managed-settings
- [definition] Requirements — To use server-managed settings, you need: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#requirements
- [definition] Choose between server-managed and endpoint-managed settings — Claude Code supports two approaches for centralized configuration. Server-managed settings deliver configuration from Anthropic's servers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#choose-between-server-managed-and-endpoint-managed-settings
- [definition] Open the admin console — In the claude.ai console, go to [**Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings**](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#configure-server-managed-settings
- [definition] Define your settings — Add your configuration as JSON. All [settings available in `settings.json`](/docs/en/settings-reference#all-settings) are supported except those restricted to OS-level policy delivery; see [Current limitations](#current-limitations) for that short list. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#configure-server-managed-settings
- [definition] Save and deploy — Save your changes. Claude Code clients receive the updated settings on their next startup or hourly polling cycle. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#configure-server-managed-settings
- [definition] Verify settings delivery — To confirm that settings are being applied, ask a user to restart Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#verify-settings-delivery
- [definition] Access control — The following roles can manage server-managed settings: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#access-control
- [definition] Managed-only settings — Most [settings keys](/docs/en/settings-reference#all-settings) work in any scope. A handful of keys are only read from managed settings and have no effect when placed in user or project settings files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#managed-only-settings
- [definition] Current limitations — Server-managed settings have the following limitations: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#current-limitations
- [definition] Settings precedence — Server-managed settings and [endpoint-managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings#delivery-mechanisms) both occupy the highest tier in the Claude Code [settings hierarchy](/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#settings-precedence
- [definition] Per-key exceptions across managed sources — Two kinds of keys are exceptions to the no-merge rule: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#per-key-exceptions-across-managed-sources
- [definition] Fetch and caching behavior — Claude Code fetches settings from Anthropic's servers at startup and polls for updates hourly during active sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#fetch-and-caching-behavior
- [definition] Invalid entries in delivered settings — Delivered payloads parse tolerantly with the same rules as the other managed sources. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#invalid-entries-in-delivered-settings
- [definition] Enforce fail-closed startup — By default, if the remote settings fetch fails at startup, the CLI continues with the settings cached from the last successful fetch, except for the [withheld environment variables](#fetch-and-caching-behavior), or without server-managed settings on a machine that has never fetched them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#enforce-fail-closed-startup
- [definition] Security approval dialogs — Certain settings that could pose security risks require explicit user approval before Claude Code applies them in an interactive session: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-approval-dialogs
- [definition] Platform availability — Server-managed settings require a direct connection to `api.anthropic.com`, and delivery requires the session to authenticate with a Team or Enterprise OAuth login, an OAuth token supplied through `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or a directly configured API key. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#platform-availability
- [definition] Audit logging — Audit log events for settings changes are available through the compliance API or audit log export. Contact your Anthropic account team for access. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#audit-logging
- [definition] Security considerations — Server-managed settings provide centralized policy enforcement, but they operate as a client-side control, not a security boundary. On unmanaged devices, a user doesn't need admin or sudo access to bypass them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations
- [definition] See also — Related pages for managing Claude Code configuration: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#see-also

- [definition] Access conversations from scripts — `/export` produces a rendered transcript for a person to read. The interfaces below produce structured data for a script to parse: a JSON result from a run, the path to a session's transcript file, or a live stream of events. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions#access-conversations-from-scripts
- [definition] Where transcripts are stored — By default, Claude Code stores transcripts as JSONL at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`, where `<project>` is your working directory path with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions#where-transcripts-are-stored
- [definition] Name the project directory yourself — By default, Claude Code derives the `<project>` name from the whole working directory path. To choose the name yourself, set `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` alongside `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions#name-the-project-directory-yourself
- [definition] See also — These pages cover related session and parallelism mechanics: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions#see-also

- [definition] Auto-updates — Claude Code checks for updates on startup and periodically while running. Updates download and install in the background, then take effect the next time you start Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#auto-updates
- [definition] Configure release channel — Control which release channel Claude Code follows for auto-updates and `claude update` with the `autoUpdatesChannel` setting: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#configure-release-channel
- [definition] Pin a minimum version — The `minimumVersion` setting establishes a floor. Background auto-updates and `claude update` refuse to install any version below this value, so moving to the `"stable"` channel does not downgrade you if you are already on a newer `"latest"` build. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#pin-a-minimum-version
- [definition] Disable auto-updates — Set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` to `"1"` in the `env` key of your [`settings.json`](/docs/en/settings-reference#all-settings) file: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#disable-auto-updates
- [definition] Update manually — To apply an update immediately without waiting for the next background check, run: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#update-manually

- [definition] Install a specific version — The native installer accepts either a specific version number or a release channel (`latest` or `stable`). The channel you choose at install time becomes your default for auto-updates. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#install-a-specific-version
- [definition] Install with Linux package managers — Claude Code publishes signed apt, dnf, and apk repositories. Each repository offers two channels: `stable` serves a version that is typically about one week old, skipping releases with major regressions, and `latest` serves every release as soon as it ships. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#install-with-linux-package-managers
- [definition] Install with npm — You can also install Claude Code as a global npm package. As of v2.1.198, the npm package requires [Node.js 22 or later](https://nodejs.org/en/download). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#install-with-npm
- [definition] Binary integrity and code signing — Each release publishes a `manifest.json` containing SHA256 checksums for every platform binary. The manifest is signed with an Anthropic GPG key, so verifying the signature on the manifest transitively verifies every binary it lists. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#binary-integrity-and-code-signing
- [definition] Download and import the public key — The release signing key is published at a fixed URL. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#verify-the-manifest-signature
- [definition] Download the manifest and signature — Set `VERSION` to the release you want to verify. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#verify-the-manifest-signature
- [definition] Verify the signature — Verify the detached signature against the manifest. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#verify-the-manifest-signature
- [definition] Check the binary against the manifest — Compare the SHA256 checksum of the binary with the value listed under `platforms.<platform>.checksum` in `manifest.json`. The commands below assume a `claude` binary in the current directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#verify-the-manifest-signature
- [definition] Uninstall Claude Code — To remove Claude Code, follow the instructions for your installation method. - [parameter] `$ARGUMENTS`: All arguments passed when invoking the skill. When no placeholder receives an argument, Claude Code appends them as `ARGUMENTS: <value>`. See [Pass arguments to skills](#pass-arguments-to-skills). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions
- [parameter] `$ARGUMENTS[N]`: Access a specific argument by 0-based index, such as `$ARGUMENTS[0]` for the first argument. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions

- [parameter] `$name`: Named argument declared in the [`arguments`](#frontmatter-reference) frontmatter list. Names map to positions in order, so with `arguments: [issue, branch]` the placeholder `$issue` expands to the first argument and `$branch` to the second. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions

- [parameter] `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}`: The current effort level: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`. Ultracode is not a distinct level and reports as `xhigh`. Use this to adapt skill instructions to the active effort setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions
- [parameter] `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`: The directory containing the skill's `SKILL.md` file. For plugin skills, this is the skill's subdirectory within the plugin, not the plugin root. Use this in bash injection commands to reference scripts or files bundled with the skill, regardless of the current working directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions
- [parameter] `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`: The project root directory. This is the same path [hooks](/docs/en/hooks#reference-scripts-by-path) and MCP servers receive as `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. Use this to reference project-local scripts or files, such as `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/helper.sh`, independent of where the skill is installed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions
- [parameter] `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`: The plugin's installation directory. Substituted only in plugin skills. Use this to reference scripts or files bundled anywhere in the plugin, including resources shared between the plugin's skills. See [plugin environment variables](/docs/en/plugins-reference#environment-variables). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions
- [parameter] `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`: The plugin's [persistent data directory](/docs/en/plugins-reference#persistent-data-directory), which survives plugin updates. Substituted only in plugin skills. Use this to reference installed dependencies, generated files, or caches that must outlive an update. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#available-string-substitutions
- [parameter] (default): You can invoke=Yes; Claude can invoke=Yes; When loaded into context=Description always in context, full skill loads when invoked — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#control-who-invokes-a-skill
- [parameter] `disable-model-invocation: true`: You can invoke=Yes; Claude can invoke=No; When loaded into context=Description not in context, full skill loads when you invoke — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#control-who-invokes-a-skill

- [parameter] Skill with `context: fork`: System prompt=From agent type; Task=SKILL.md content; Also loads=CLAUDE.md, except when the agent is Explore or Plan — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#run-skills-in-a-subagent

- [definition] Extend Claude with skills — Create, manage, and share skills to extend Claude's capabilities in Claude Code. Includes custom commands and bundled skills. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#extend-claude-with-skills
- [definition] Bundled skills — Claude Code includes a set of bundled skills, such as `/doctor`, `/code-review`, `/batch`, `/debug`, `/loop`, and `/claude-api`. Bundled skills are prompt-based: they give Claude detailed instructions and let it orchestrate the work using its tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#bundled-skills
- [definition] Run and verify your app — Three bundled skills work together to launch your app and confirm changes against the running app instead of just tests: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#run-and-verify-your-app
- [definition] Create your first skill — This example creates a skill that summarizes the uncommitted changes in your git repository and flags anything risky. It pulls the live diff into the prompt before Claude reads it, so the response is grounded in your actual working tree rather than what Claude can guess from open files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#create-your-first-skill
- [definition] Create the skill directory — Create a directory for the skill in your personal skills folder. Personal skills are available across all your projects. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#create-your-first-skill
- [definition] Write SKILL.md — Every skill needs a `SKILL.md` file with two parts: YAML frontmatter between `---` markers that tells Claude when to use the skill, and markdown content with the instructions Claude follows when the skill runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#create-your-first-skill
- [definition] Test the skill — Open a git project, make a small edit to any file, and start Claude Code by running `claude`. You can test the skill two ways. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#create-your-first-skill
- [definition] Where skills live — Where you store a skill determines who can use it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#where-skills-live
- [definition] Skills synced from claude.ai — This section applies to you if you enabled skills for your claude.ai account. In Cowork and cloud sessions, Claude Code loads those skills without any setup on your machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#skills-synced-from-claudeai
- [definition] Enable the skills for your claude.ai account — Enable each skill you want for your claude.ai account, as [Skills in Cowork and cloud sessions](#skills-in-cowork-and-cloud-sessions) describes. Claude Code downloads only the skills you enabled, and it needs your claude.ai sign-in to download them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#where-synced-skills-load
- [definition] Run Claude Code in non-interactive mode with syncing turned on — Claude Code downloads synced skills only when you run it in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with the `-p` flag and set [`CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS`](/docs/en/env-vars#variables) to `1`. The prompt you pass doesn't affect the download. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#where-synced-skills-load
- [definition] Confirm the skills load in a local session — Start an interactive session, without `CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS` set, and run `/skills`. The menu lists the downloaded skills under `claude.ai sync`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#where-synced-skills-load
- [definition] Remove a skill — How you remove a skill depends on where it came from: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#remove-a-skill
- [definition] Configure skills — Skills are configured through YAML frontmatter at the top of `SKILL.md` and the markdown content that follows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#configure-skills
- [definition] Types of skill content — Skill files can contain any instructions, but thinking about how you want to invoke them helps guide what to include: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#types-of-skill-content
- [definition] Frontmatter reference — Beyond the markdown content, you can configure skill behavior using YAML frontmatter fields between `---` markers at the top of your `SKILL.md` file: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#frontmatter-reference
- [definition] Add supporting files — Skills can include multiple files in their directory. This keeps `SKILL.md` focused on the essentials while letting Claude access detailed reference material only when needed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#add-supporting-files
- [definition] Control who invokes a skill — By default, both you and Claude can invoke any skill. You can type `/skill-name` to invoke it directly, and Claude can load it automatically when relevant to your conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#control-who-invokes-a-skill
- [definition] Skill content lifecycle — When you or Claude invoke a skill, the rendered `SKILL.md` content enters the conversation as a single message and stays there across later turns. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#skill-content-lifecycle
- [definition] Pre-approve tools for a skill — The `allowed-tools` field grants permission for the listed tools during the turn that invokes the skill, so Claude can use them without prompting you for approval. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#pre-approve-tools-for-a-skill
- [definition] Pass arguments to skills — Both you and Claude can pass arguments when invoking a skill. Arguments are available via the `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#pass-arguments-to-skills
- [definition] Inject dynamic context — The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude. The command output replaces the placeholder, so Claude receives actual data, not the command itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#inject-dynamic-context
- [definition] Run skills in a subagent — Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#run-skills-in-a-subagent
- [definition] Restrict Claude's skill access — By default, Claude can invoke any skill that doesn't have `disable-model-invocation: true` set. Skills that define `allowed-tools` grant Claude access to those tools without per-use approval during the turn that invokes the skill; the grant clears when you send your next message. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#restrict-claudes-skill-access
- [definition] Override skill visibility from settings — The `skillOverrides` setting controls skill visibility from your [settings](/docs/en/settings) instead of the skill's own frontmatter. - [definition] Evaluate and iterate on a skill — Seeing a skill trigger tells you Claude found it, not that it did what you intended. To know a skill is working, measure two things separately: whether Claude invokes it on the prompts it should, and whether the output matches what you expect when it does. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#evaluate-and-iterate-on-a-skill
- [definition] Run evals with skill-creator — The [`skill-creator` plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/skill-creator) automates the comparison loop inside Claude Code. - [definition] Share skills — Skills can be distributed at different scopes depending on your audience: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#share-skills
- [definition] Generate visual output — Skills can bundle and run scripts in any language, giving Claude capabilities beyond what's possible in a single prompt. One pattern is generating visual output: interactive HTML files that open in your browser for exploring data, debugging, or creating reports. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#generate-visual-output
- [definition] Skill not triggering — If Claude doesn't use your skill when expected: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#skill-not-triggering
- [definition] Skill triggers too often — If Claude uses your skill when you don't want it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#skill-triggers-too-often
- [definition] Skill descriptions are cut short — Claude Code loads a listing of skill names and descriptions into context so Claude knows what's available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#skill-descriptions-are-cut-short

## Claude Code in Slack
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack>

- [parameter] Claude Plan: Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise with Claude Code access (premium seats or Chat + Claude Code seats) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#prerequisites
- [parameter] Claude Code on the web: Access to [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) must be enabled — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#prerequisites
- [parameter] GitHub Account: Connected to Claude Code on the web with at least one repository authenticated — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#prerequisites
- [parameter] Slack Authentication: Your Slack account linked to your Claude account via the Claude app — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#prerequisites
- [parameter] **Code only**: Claude routes all @mentions to Claude Code sessions. Best for teams using Claude in Slack exclusively for development tasks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack
- [parameter] **Code + Chat**: Claude analyzes each message and intelligently routes between Claude Code (for coding tasks) and Claude Chat (for writing, analysis, and general questions). Best for teams who want a single @Claude entry point for all types of work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack
- [parameter] Claude Code Sessions: Each user runs sessions under their own Claude account — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#user-level-access
- [parameter] Usage & Rate Limits: Sessions count against the individual user's plan limits — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#user-level-access
- [parameter] Repository Access: Users can only access repositories they've personally connected — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#user-level-access
- [parameter] Session History: Sessions appear in your Claude Code history on claude.ai/code — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#user-level-access
- [parameter] App installation: Workspace admins decide whether to install the Claude app from the Slack App Marketplace — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#workspace-level-access
- [parameter] Enterprise Grid distribution: For Enterprise Grid organizations, organization admins can control which workspaces have access to the Claude app — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#workspace-level-access
- [parameter] App removal: Removing the app from a workspace immediately revokes access for all users in that workspace — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#workspace-level-access
- [definition] Claude Code in Slack — Delegate coding tasks directly from your Slack workspace. Anthropic is retiring this earlier version for Team and Enterprise workspaces in favor of Claude Tag; it remains the setup path on Pro and Max plans. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#claude-code-in-slack
- [definition] Prerequisites — Before using Claude Code in Slack, ensure you have the following: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#prerequisites
- [definition] Install the Claude App in Slack — A workspace administrator must install the Claude app from the Slack App Marketplace. Visit the [Slack App Marketplace](https://slack.com/marketplace/A08SF47R6P4) and click "Add to Slack" to begin the installation process. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack
- [definition] Connect your Claude account — After the app is installed, authenticate your individual Claude account: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack
- [definition] Configure Claude Code on the web — Ensure your Claude Code on the web is properly configured: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack
- [definition] Choose your routing mode — After connecting your accounts, configure how Claude handles your messages in Slack. Navigate to the Claude App Home in Slack to find the **Routing Mode** setting. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack
- [definition] Add Claude to channels — Claude is not automatically added to any channels after installation. To use Claude in a channel, invite it by typing `/invite @Claude` in that channel. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#setting-up-claude-code-in-slack
- [definition] Automatic detection — In Code + Chat routing mode, when you mention @Claude in a Slack channel or thread, Claude automatically detects whether your message is a coding task. Coding tasks go to Claude Code on the web. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#automatic-detection
- [definition] Session flow — 1. **Initiation**: You @mention Claude with a coding request 2. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#session-flow
- [definition] Repository selection — Claude automatically selects a repository based on context from your Slack conversation. If multiple repositories could apply, Claude may display a dropdown allowing you to choose the correct one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#repository-selection

- [definition] Channel-based access control — Installing the app doesn't add Claude to any channels. Claude responds to @mentions only in channels where it has been added; invite it with `/invite @Claude`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#channel-based-access-control

- [definition] Authentication errors — 1. Disconnect and reconnect your Claude account in the App Home 2. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slack#authentication-errors

What Claude receives depends on where the subagent ran: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#api-errors-in-subagents
- [definition] Subagent output scanning — Claude Code scans each subagent's final report before Claude reads it. A subagent may have read files, web pages, or command output you never reviewed, and text from those sources can carry instructions aimed at the main conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#subagent-output-scanning
- [definition] Let subagents spawn their own subagents — By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents
- [definition] Concurrent subagent limit — Two limits control subagent use, each with its own variable: this one stops Claude from spawning more subagents while too many are running, and the [depth limit](#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents) caps how deeply subagents nest. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#concurrent-subagent-limit
- [definition] Fork the current conversation — Run a forked subagent with `/subtask`, which requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#fork-the-current-conversation
- [definition] Observe and steer running forks — Running forks appear in a panel below the prompt input, with one row for the main session and one for each fork. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#observe-and-steer-running-forks
- [definition] How forks differ from other subagents — A fork inherits everything the main session has at the moment it spawns. Any other subagent starts fresh from its definition. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#how-forks-differ-from-other-subagents
- [definition] Turn fork mode on or off — Claude Code turns fork mode on by default in interactive sessions and leaves it off by default in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with `-p` and in the Agent SDK. The interactive default requires Claude Code v2.1.232 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#turn-fork-mode-on-or-off
- [definition] Example subagents — These examples demonstrate effective patterns for building subagents. Use them as starting points, or generate a customized version with Claude. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#example-subagents
- [definition] Code reviewer — A read-only subagent that reviews code without modifying it. This example shows how to design a focused subagent with limited tool access that excludes Edit and Write, and a detailed prompt that specifies exactly what to look for and how to format output. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#code-reviewer
- [definition] Debugger — A subagent that can both analyze and fix issues. Unlike the code reviewer, this one includes Edit because fixing bugs requires modifying code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#debugger
- [definition] Data scientist — A domain-specific subagent for data analysis work. This example shows how to create subagents for specialized workflows outside of typical coding tasks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#data-scientist
- [definition] Database query validator — A subagent that allows Bash access but validates commands to permit only read-only SQL queries. This example shows how to use `PreToolUse` hooks for conditional validation when you need finer control than the `tools` field provides. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#database-query-validator
- [definition] Next steps — Now that you understand subagents, explore these related features: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#next-steps

- [definition] Configure proxies and gateways — Most organizations can use a cloud provider directly without additional configuration. - [definition] Invest in documentation and memory — We strongly recommend investing in documentation so that Claude Code understands your codebase. - [definition] Simplify deployment — If you have a custom development environment, we find that creating a "one click" way to install Claude Code is key to growing adoption across an organization. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations#simplify-deployment
- [definition] Start with guided usage — Encourage new users to try Claude Code for codebase Q\&A, or on smaller bug fixes or feature requests. Ask Claude Code to make a plan. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations#start-with-guided-usage
- [definition] Pin model versions for cloud providers — If you deploy through [Amazon Bedrock](/docs/en/amazon-bedrock), [Google Cloud's Agent Platform](/docs/en/google-vertex-ai), [Microsoft Foundry](/docs/en/microsoft-foundry), or [Claude Platform on AWS](/docs/en/claude-platform-on-aws), pin specific model versions using… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations#pin-model-versions-for-cloud-providers
- [definition] Configure security policies — Security teams can configure managed permissions for what Claude Code is and is not allowed to do, which cannot be overwritten by local configuration. [Learn more](/docs/en/security). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations#configure-security-policies
- [definition] Use MCP for integrations — MCP is a great way to give Claude Code more information, such as connecting to ticket management systems or error logs. We recommend that one central team configures MCP servers and checks a `.mcp.json` configuration into the codebase so that all users benefit. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations#use-mcp-for-integrations
- [definition] Next steps — Once you've chosen a deployment option and configured access for your team: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations#next-steps
