- [definition] Troubleshoot installation and login — Fix command not found, PATH, permission, network, and authentication errors when installing or signing in to Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#troubleshoot-installation-and-login
- [definition] Find your error — Match the error message or symptom you're seeing to a fix: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#find-your-error
- [definition] Check network connectivity — The installer downloads from `downloads.claude.ai`. Verify you can reach it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#check-network-connectivity
- [definition] Verify your PATH — If installation succeeded but you get a `command not found` or `not recognized` error when running `claude`, the install directory isn't in your PATH. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#verify-your-path
- [definition] Check for conflicting installations — Multiple Claude Code installations can cause version mismatches or unexpected behavior. Check what's installed: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#check-for-conflicting-installations
- [definition] Check directory permissions — The installer needs write access to `~/.local/bin/` and `~/.claude/` on macOS and Linux. On Windows the install location is under `%USERPROFILE%`, which is writable by your user by default, so this section rarely applies there. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#check-directory-permissions
- [definition] Verify the binary works — If `claude --version` prints a version but `claude` crashes or hangs on startup, run these checks to narrow down the cause. If `claude --version` says command not found, go to [Verify your PATH](#verify-your-path) first; the commands below assume `claude` is on your PATH. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#verify-the-binary-works
- [definition] Common installation issues — These are the most frequently encountered installation problems and their solutions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#common-installation-issues
- [definition] Install script returns HTML instead of a shell script — When running the install command, you may see one of these errors: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#install-script-returns-html-instead-of-a-shell-script
- [definition] `command not found: claude` after installation — The install finished but `claude` doesn't work. The exact error varies by platform: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#command-not-found-claude-after-installation
- [definition] `curl: (56) Failure writing output to destination` — The `curl ... | bash` command downloads the script and pipes it to Bash for execution. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#curl-56-failure-writing-output-to-destination
- [definition] Homebrew cask unavailable or outdated — Homebrew reports `Error: Cask 'claude-code' is unavailable: No Cask with this name exists` when your local copy of the Homebrew cask index predates the cask's publication. Refresh the index and retry: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#homebrew-cask-unavailable-or-outdated
- [definition] TLS or SSL connection errors — Errors like `curl: (35) TLS connect error`, `schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed`, or PowerShell's `Could not establish trust relationship for the SSL/TLS secure channel` indicate TLS handshake failures. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#tls-or-ssl-connection-errors
- [definition] `Failed to fetch version from downloads.claude.ai` — The installer couldn't reach the download server. This typically means `downloads.claude.ai` is blocked on your network. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#failed-to-fetch-version-from-downloadsclaudeai
- [definition] Wrong install command on Windows — If you see `'irm' is not recognized`, `The token '&&' is not valid`, `A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'fsSL'`, or `'bash' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet`, you copied the install command for a different shell or operating system. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#wrong-install-command-on-windows
- [definition] `running scripts is disabled on this system` — Installing or running Claude Code through npm on Windows can fail with a `SecurityError`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#running-scripts-is-disabled-on-this-system
- [definition] `The process cannot access the file` during Windows install — If the PowerShell installer fails with `Failed to download binary: The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process`, the installer couldn't write to `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\downloads`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#the-process-cannot-access-the-file-during-windows-install
- [definition] Install killed on low-memory Linux servers — A `Killed` message during install usually means the Linux out-of-memory (OOM) killer terminated the `claude install` step because the system ran out of free memory. This is common on small VPS and cloud instances. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#install-killed-on-low-memory-linux-servers
- [definition] Install hangs in Docker — When installing Claude Code in a Docker container, installing as root into `/` can cause hangs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#install-hangs-in-docker
- [definition] `Raw mode is not supported` during install — When your organization's [server-managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings) include changes that need [security approval](/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-approval-dialogs), Claude Code versions before 2.1.246 try to show the approval dialog during `claude install`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#raw-mode-is-not-supported-during-install
- [definition] `claude update` or `claude doctor` hangs — `claude update` and `claude doctor` scan your shell configuration files for an outdated `claude` alias: `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, and `~/.config/fish/config.fish`, plus on macOS the first of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, or `~/.profile` that exists. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#claude-update-or-claude-doctor-hangs
- [definition] Claude Desktop overrides the `claude` command on Windows — If you installed an older version of Claude Desktop, it may register a `Claude.exe` in the `WindowsApps` directory that takes PATH priority over Claude Code CLI. Running `claude` opens the Desktop app instead of the CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#claude-desktop-overrides-the-claude-command-on-windows
- [definition] Claude Code on Windows requires either Git for Windows (for bash) or PowerShell — Git for Windows is optional. Claude Code uses the [PowerShell tool](/docs/en/tools-reference#powershell-tool) when Git Bash is absent, so this error means neither shell was found. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#claude-code-on-windows-requires-either-git-for-windows-for-bash-or-powershell
- [definition] Claude Code does not support 32-bit Windows — Windows includes two PowerShell entries in the Start menu: `Windows PowerShell` and `Windows PowerShell (x86)`. The x86 entry runs as a 32-bit process and triggers this error even on a 64-bit machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#claude-code-does-not-support-32-bit-windows
- [definition] Linux musl or glibc binary mismatch — If you see errors about missing shared libraries like `libstdc++.so.6` or `libgcc_s.so.1` after installation, the installer may have downloaded the wrong binary variant for your system. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#linux-musl-or-glibc-binary-mismatch
- [definition] `Illegal instruction` — If running `claude` or the installer prints `Illegal instruction`, the native binary uses CPU instructions your processor doesn't support. There are two distinct causes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#illegal-instruction
- [definition] `dyld: cannot load` on macOS — If you see `dyld: Symbol not found`, `dyld: cannot load`, or `Abort trap: 6` during installation, the binary is incompatible with your macOS version or hardware. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#dyld-cannot-load-on-macos
- [definition] `Exec format error` on WSL1 — If running `claude` in WSL prints `cannot execute binary file: Exec format error`, you're on WSL1 and hitting a known native-binary regression tracked in [issue #38788](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/38788). The binary's program headers changed in a way WSL1's loader can't handle. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#exec-format-error-on-wsl1
- [definition] npm install errors in WSL — These issues apply if you installed Claude Code with `npm install -g` inside WSL. If you used the [native installer](/docs/en/setup), skip this section. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#npm-install-errors-in-wsl
- [definition] Permission errors during installation — If the native installer fails with permission errors, the target directory may not be writable. See [Check directory permissions](#check-directory-permissions). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#permission-errors-during-installation
- [definition] Native binary not found after npm install — The `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` npm package downloads the native binary as a per-platform optional dependency, such as `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#native-binary-not-found-after-npm-install
- [definition] npm `ENOTEMPTY` error during update or reinstall — When you run `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` over an existing installation, npm can fail while moving the old package directory aside: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#npm-enotempty-error-during-update-or-reinstall
- [definition] Login and authentication — These sections address login failures, OAuth errors, and token issues. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#login-and-authentication
- [definition] Reset your login — When login fails and the cause isn't obvious, a clean re-authentication resolves most cases: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#reset-your-login
- [definition] OAuth error: Invalid code — If you see `OAuth error: Invalid code. Please make sure the full code was copied`, the login code expired or was truncated during copy-paste. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#oauth-error-invalid-code
- [definition] 403 Forbidden after login — If you see `API Error: 403 {"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}` after logging in: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#403-forbidden-after-login
- [definition] This organization has been disabled with an active subscription — If you see `API Error: 400 ... "This organization has been disabled"` despite having an active Claude subscription, an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable is overriding your subscription. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#this-organization-has-been-disabled-with-an-active-subscription
- [definition] OAuth login fails in WSL2, SSH, or containers — When Claude Code runs in WSL2, on a remote machine over SSH, or inside a container, the browser usually opens on a different host and its redirect can't reach Claude Code's local callback server. After you sign in, the browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#oauth-login-fails-in-wsl2-ssh-or-containers
- [definition] Not logged in or token expired — If Claude Code prompts you to log in again after a session, your OAuth token may have expired. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#not-logged-in-or-token-expired
- [definition] Bedrock, Agent Platform, or Foundry credentials not loading — If you configured Claude Code to use a cloud provider and see `Could not load credentials from any providers` on Amazon Bedrock, `Could not load the default credentials` on Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or `ChainedTokenCredential authentication failed` on Microsoft Foundry, your cloud provider… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#bedrock-agent-platform-or-foundry-credentials-not-loading
- [definition] Still stuck — If none of the above resolves your issue: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#still-stuck

- [definition] Troubleshooting — Fix high CPU or memory usage, hangs, auto-compact thrashing, and search problems in Claude Code, and find the right page for other issues. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#troubleshooting
- [definition] Performance and stability — These sections cover issues related to resource usage, responsiveness, and search behavior. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#performance-and-stability
- [definition] High CPU or memory usage — Claude Code is designed to work with most development environments, but may consume significant resources when processing large codebases. If you're experiencing performance issues: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#high-cpu-or-memory-usage
- [definition] Large tables are cut off in the terminal — A Markdown table with more than 200 rows renders its first 200 rows followed by a `… N more rows not shown` line. Only the display is capped: the full table stays in the conversation, and [`/copy`](/docs/en/commands) copies every row. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#large-tables-are-cut-off-in-the-terminal
- [definition] Auto-compaction stops with a thrashing error — If you see `Autocompact is thrashing: the context refilled to the limit...`, automatic compaction succeeded but a file or tool output immediately refilled the context window several times in a row. Claude Code stops retrying to avoid wasting API calls on a loop that isn't making progress. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#auto-compaction-stops-with-a-thrashing-error
- [definition] Garbled or corrupted text in an editor's integrated terminal — If characters render as boxes, smears, or the wrong glyphs when running Claude Code in the VS Code, Cursor, or Devin Desktop integrated terminal, the terminal's GPU renderer is likely the cause. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#garbled-or-corrupted-text-in-an-editors-integrated-terminal
- [definition] Search and discovery issues — If the Search tool, `@file` mentions, custom agents, or custom skills aren't finding files, the bundled `ripgrep` binary may not run on your system. Install your platform's `ripgrep` package and tell Claude Code to use it instead: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#search-and-discovery-issues
- [definition] Slow or incomplete search results on WSL — Disk read performance penalties when [working across file systems on WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/filesystems) may result in fewer-than-expected matches when using Claude Code on WSL. Search still functions, but returns fewer results than on a native filesystem. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#slow-or-incomplete-search-results-on-wsl
- [definition] Get more help — If you're experiencing issues not covered here: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting#get-more-help

- [snippet] Pass a request in plain words: /code-review ultra check my auth changes — `/code-review ultra check my auth changes` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#pass-a-request-in-plain-words

- [parameter] Max: Included free runs=3 free runs; After free runs=billed as [usage credits](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-extra-usage-for-paid-claude-plans) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#pricing-and-free-runs
- [parameter] Team and Enterprise: Included free runs=none; After free runs=billed as [usage credits](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-extra-usage-for-paid-claude-plans) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#pricing-and-free-runs
- [parameter] `--json`: Print the raw `bugs.json` payload instead of the formatted findings — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#run-ultrareview-non-interactively
- [parameter] `--timeout <minutes>`: Maximum minutes to wait for the review to finish. Defaults to 30 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#run-ultrareview-non-interactively
- [parameter] `--post`: [Post the finished findings](#post-findings-to-the-pull-request) to the pull request as one plain comment from your GitHub account. Works on `github.com` pull request targets; on other targets, Claude Code ignores the flag and says so. Requires Claude Code v2.1.227 or later — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#run-ultrareview-non-interactively
- [parameter] `--no-post`: Don't post the findings. This is the default, and if you pass both flags, Claude Code doesn't post. Requires Claude Code v2.1.227 or later — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#run-ultrareview-non-interactively
- [parameter] Target: `/code-review`=your working diff, a pull request, a branch, or a path; `/code-review ultra`=your working diff or a pull request — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#how-ultrareview-compares-to-code-review
- [parameter] Runs: `/code-review`=locally in your session; `/code-review ultra`=remotely in a cloud sandbox — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#how-ultrareview-compares-to-code-review
- [parameter] Depth: `/code-review`=scales with the effort argument; `/code-review ultra`=multi-agent fleet with independent verification — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#how-ultrareview-compares-to-code-review
- [parameter] Duration: `/code-review`=seconds to a few minutes; `/code-review ultra`=roughly 5 to 10 minutes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#how-ultrareview-compares-to-code-review
- [parameter] Cost: `/code-review`=counts toward normal usage; `/code-review ultra`=free runs, then roughly \$5 to \$25 per review as usage credits — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#how-ultrareview-compares-to-code-review
- [parameter] Best for: `/code-review`=quick feedback while iterating; `/code-review ultra`=pre-merge confidence on substantial changes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#how-ultrareview-compares-to-code-review
- [definition] Find bugs with ultrareview — Run a deep, multi-agent code review in the cloud with /code-review ultra to find and verify bugs before you merge. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#find-bugs-with-ultrareview
- [definition] Review against a different base — To compare against a base other than the default branch, pass the branch name. This example reviews your current branch against `develop` instead: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#review-against-a-different-base
- [definition] Review a pull request — To review a GitHub pull request instead of a local branch, pass the PR number: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#review-a-pull-request
- [definition] Post findings to the pull request — On Claude Code v2.1.227 or later, when you review a pull request on `github.com`, you can have Claude post the finished findings to the PR as a single plain comment from your own GitHub account. The comment isn't a review or an approval, and it ends with a "Generated by Claude Code" note. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#post-findings-to-the-pull-request
- [definition] Pass a request in plain words — On Claude Code v2.1.218 or later, you can also describe what you're working on in plain words: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#pass-a-request-in-plain-words
- [definition] Diff limits and fallbacks — Ultrareview checks the diff before any review work runs and tells you when it can't review it as-is: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#diff-limits-and-fallbacks
- [definition] Pricing and free runs — Ultrareview is a premium feature that bills against usage credits rather than your plan's included usage. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#pricing-and-free-runs
- [definition] Track a running review — A review typically takes 5 to 10 minutes. The review runs as a background task, so you can keep working in your session, start other commands, or close the terminal entirely. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#track-a-running-review
- [definition] Run ultrareview non-interactively — Use the `claude ultrareview` subcommand to start an ultrareview from CI or a script without an interactive session. The subcommand launches the same review as `/code-review ultra`, blocks until the remote review finishes, and prints the findings to stdout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#run-ultrareview-non-interactively
- [definition] How ultrareview compares to /code-review — Both reviews examine code, but you use them at different stages of your workflow. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview#how-ultrareview-compares-to-code-review

- [definition] Customize your workflow — You can reposition the Claude panel, run multiple conversations, organize the sessions list into groups, or switch to terminal mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#customize-your-workflow

- [definition] Run multiple conversations — Use **Open in New Tab** or **Open in New Window** from the Command Palette to start additional conversations. - [definition] Organize sessions into groups — In the sessions list in the Activity Bar, you can collect related sessions into named, collapsible groups. Requires Claude Code v2.1.229 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#organize-sessions-into-groups
- [definition] Switch to terminal mode — By default, the extension opens a graphical chat panel. If you prefer the CLI-style interface, open the [Use Terminal setting](vscode://settings/claudeCode.useTerminal) and check the box. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#switch-to-terminal-mode
- [definition] Manage plugins — The VS Code extension includes a graphical interface for installing and managing [plugins](/docs/en/plugins). Type `/plugins` in the prompt box to open the **Manage plugins** interface. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#manage-plugins

- [definition] VS Code commands and shortcuts — Open the Command Palette (`Cmd+Shift+P` on Mac or `Ctrl+Shift+P` on Windows/Linux) and type "Claude Code" to see all available VS Code commands for the Claude Code extension. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#vs-code-commands-and-shortcuts
- [definition] Launch a VS Code tab from other tools — The extension registers a URI handler at `vscode://anthropic.claude-code/open`. - [definition] Configure settings — The extension has two types of settings: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#configure-settings
- [definition] Extension settings — VS Code reads `initialPermissionMode` from your user settings and ignores workspace values. Before v2.1.225, VS Code defaulted the setting to `default` and applied workspace values. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#extension-settings
- [definition] Use a screen reader — The extension's chat panel works with screen readers. You don't need to turn anything on: the extension announces conversation activity for every user, with no visual change. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#use-a-screen-reader
- [definition] VS Code extension vs. Claude Code CLI — Claude Code is available as both a VS Code extension (graphical panel) and a CLI (command-line interface in the terminal). Some features are only available in the CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#vs-code-extension-vs-claude-code-cli
- [definition] Rewind with checkpoints — The VS Code extension supports checkpoints, which track Claude's file edits and let you rewind to a previous state. Hover over any message to reveal the rewind button, then choose from three options: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#rewind-with-checkpoints
- [definition] Run CLI in VS Code — To use the CLI while staying in VS Code, open the integrated terminal (`` Ctrl+` `` on Windows/Linux or `` Cmd+` `` on Mac) and run `claude`. The CLI automatically integrates with your IDE for features like diff viewing and diagnostic sharing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#run-cli-in-vs-code
- [definition] Switch between extension and CLI — The extension and CLI share the same conversation history. To continue an extension conversation in the CLI, run `claude --resume` in the terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#switch-between-extension-and-cli
- [definition] Include terminal output in prompts — Reference terminal output in your prompts using `@terminal:name` where `name` is the terminal's title. - [definition] Monitor background processes — Visibility for background tasks in the extension is limited compared to the CLI. For better visibility, have Claude output the command so you can run it in VS Code's integrated terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#monitor-background-processes
- [definition] Connect to external tools with MCP — MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers give Claude access to external tools, databases, and APIs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#connect-to-external-tools-with-mcp
- [definition] Work with git — Claude Code integrates with git to help with version control workflows directly in VS Code. Ask Claude to commit changes, create pull requests, or work across branches. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#work-with-git
- [definition] Create commits and pull requests — Claude can stage changes, write commit messages, and create pull requests based on your work: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#create-commits-and-pull-requests
- [definition] Use third-party providers — By default, Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic's API. If your organization uses Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry to access Claude, configure the extension to use your provider instead: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#use-third-party-providers
- [definition] Disable login prompt — Open the [Disable Login Prompt setting](vscode://settings/claudeCode.disableLoginPrompt) and check the box. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#use-third-party-providers
- [definition] Configure your provider — Follow the setup guide for your provider: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#use-third-party-providers
- [definition] Security and privacy — Your code stays private. Claude Code processes your code to provide assistance but does not use it to train models. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#security-and-privacy
- [definition] The built-in IDE MCP server — When the extension is active, it runs a local MCP server that the CLI connects to automatically. This is how the CLI opens diffs in VS Code's native diff viewer, reads your current selection for `@`-mentions, and — when you're working in a Jupyter notebook — asks VS Code to execute cells. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#the-built-in-ide-mcp-server
- [definition] Spark icon not visible — The Spark icon appears in the **Editor Toolbar** (top-right of editor) when you have a file open. If you don't see it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#spark-icon-not-visible
- [definition] Cmd+Esc does nothing on macOS — On macOS Tahoe and later, the system Game Overlay shortcut is bound to `Cmd+Esc` by default and intercepts the keypress before it reaches VS Code. To free the shortcut: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#cmdesc-does-nothing-on-macos
- [definition] Claude Code never responds — If Claude Code isn't responding to your prompts: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#claude-code-never-responds
- [definition] Next steps — Now that you have Claude Code set up in VS Code: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#next-steps

- [parameter] `environment`: Name or ID of the [environment](#connect-github) to preselect. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#pre-fill-sessions
- [definition] Get started with Claude Code on the web — Run Claude Code in the cloud from your browser or phone. Connect a GitHub repository, submit a task, and review the PR without local setup. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#get-started-with-claude-code-on-the-web
- [definition] How sessions run — The steps below describe Anthropic-hosted sessions. In a [self-hosted environment](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments), the clone and everything after it run on your organization's own runners, where network boundaries, setup, and push behavior are operator-configured. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#how-sessions-run
- [definition] Compare ways to run Claude Code — Claude Code behaves the same everywhere. What changes is where code executes and whether your local config is available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#compare-ways-to-run-claude-code
- [definition] Connect GitHub — Connecting GitHub is a one-time step. If you already use the GitHub CLI, you can [do this from your terminal](#connect-from-your-terminal) instead of the browser. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#connect-github
- [definition] Visit claude.ai/code — Go to [claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code) and sign in with your claude.ai account. - [definition] Sign in with GitHub — After you sign in, claude.ai/code prompts you to connect GitHub. Follow the prompt, and claude.ai/code sends you to GitHub's authorization page. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#connect-github
- [definition] Set up your Default environment — A [cloud environment](/docs/en/cloud-environments) is the saved configuration that controls what network access Claude has during sessions and what runs when a session starts. What happens after you connect GitHub depends on your plan: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#connect-github
- [definition] Connect from your terminal — If you already use the GitHub CLI (`gh`), you can set up Claude Code on the web without opening a browser. This requires the [Claude Code CLI](/docs/en/quickstart). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#connect-from-your-terminal
- [definition] Authenticate with the GitHub CLI — In your shell, authenticate the GitHub CLI if you haven't already: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#connect-from-your-terminal
- [definition] Sign in to Claude — In the Claude Code CLI, run `/login` to sign in with your claude.ai account. Skip this step if you're already signed in with a claude.ai account. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#connect-from-your-terminal
- [definition] Start a task — With GitHub connected and an environment created, you're ready to submit tasks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#start-a-task
- [definition] Select a repository and branch — From [claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code) or the Code tab in the Claude mobile app, click the repository selector below the input box and choose a repository for Claude to work in. Each repository shows a branch selector. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#start-a-task
- [definition] Choose a permission mode — The mode dropdown next to the input shows the mode the session will run in: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#start-a-task
- [definition] Describe the task and submit — Type a description of what you want and press Enter. Be specific: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#start-a-task
- [definition] Pre-fill sessions — You can prefill the prompt, repositories, and environment for a new session by adding query parameters to the [claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code) URL. Use this to build integrations such as a button in your issue tracker that opens Claude Code with the issue description as the prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#pre-fill-sessions
- [definition] Review and iterate — When Claude finishes, review the changes, leave feedback on specific lines, and keep going until the diff looks right. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#review-and-iterate
- [definition] Open the diff view — A diff indicator shows lines added and removed across the session, for example `+42 -18`. Select it to open the diff view, with a file list on the left and changes on the right. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#review-and-iterate
- [definition] Leave inline comments — Select any line in the diff, type your feedback, and press Enter. Comments queue up until you send your next message, then they're bundled with it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#review-and-iterate
- [definition] Create a pull request — When the diff looks right, select **Create PR** at the top of the diff view. You can open it as a full PR, a draft, or jump to GitHub's compose page with a generated title and description. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#review-and-iterate
- [definition] Keep iterating after the PR — The session stays live after the PR is created. Paste CI failure output or reviewer comments into the chat and ask Claude to address them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#review-and-iterate
- [definition] No repositories appear after connecting GitHub — A cloud session can use any repository the connected GitHub account can see, regardless of which repositories the Claude GitHub App is installed on. If a repository is missing, verify the connected GitHub account has access to it on GitHub. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#no-repositories-appear-after-connecting-github
- [definition] The page only shows a GitHub login button — Cloud sessions require a connected GitHub account. Connect via the browser flow above, or run `/web-setup` from your terminal if you use the GitHub CLI. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#the-page-only-shows-a-github-login-button
- [definition] "Not available for the selected organization" — Enterprise organizations may need an Owner to enable Claude Code on the web. Contact your Anthropic account team. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#not-available-for-the-selected-organization
- [definition] `/web-setup` says "Not signed in to Claude" — If `/web-setup` responds with "Not signed in to Claude. Run /login first.", the CLI doesn't have a valid claude.ai sign-in. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#web-setup-says-not-signed-in-to-claude
- [definition] `/web-setup` warns that your token doesn't have the `workflow` scope — If `/web-setup` says your GitHub CLI token doesn't have the `workflow` scope, you can continue, but GitHub can reject some pushes made with that token, such as pushes that change GitHub Actions workflow files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#web-setup-warns-that-your-token-doesnt-have-the-workflow-scope
- [definition] `/web-setup` shows "No commands match" or "Unknown command" — `/web-setup` runs inside the Claude Code CLI, not your shell. Launch `claude` first, then type `/web-setup` at the prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#web-setup-shows-no-commands-match-or-unknown-command
- [definition] "Could not create a cloud environment" or "No cloud environment available" when using `--cloud` — Remote-session features create a default cloud environment automatically if you don't have one. If you see "Could not create a cloud environment", automatic creation failed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#could-not-create-a-cloud-environment-or-no-cloud-environment-available-when-using-cloud
- [definition] Setup script failed — The setup script exited with a non-zero status, which blocks the session from starting. Common causes: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#setup-script-failed
- [definition] New sessions hang or time out during setup — If new sessions stall on the setup script step or fail with a generic container error before the script finishes, the script is likely exceeding the roughly five-minute time budget for building the [environment cache](/docs/en/cloud-environments#environment-caching). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#new-sessions-hang-or-time-out-during-setup
- [definition] Session keeps running after closing the tab — This is by design. Closing the tab or navigating away doesn't stop the session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#session-keeps-running-after-closing-the-tab
- [definition] Next steps — Now that you can submit and review tasks, these pages cover what comes next: starting cloud sessions from your terminal, scheduling recurring work, and giving Claude standing instructions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart#next-steps

- [snippet] What the saved script looks like: export const meta = { — `export const meta = {` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#what-the-saved-script-looks-like
- [parameter] What it is: Subagents=A worker Claude spawns; Skills=Instructions Claude follows; Agent teams=A lead agent supervising peer sessions; Workflows=A script the runtime executes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#when-to-use-a-workflow
- [parameter] Who decides what runs next: Subagents=Claude, turn by turn; Skills=Claude, following the prompt; Agent teams=The lead agent, turn by turn; Workflows=The script — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#when-to-use-a-workflow
- [parameter] Where intermediate results live: Subagents=Claude's context window; Skills=Claude's context window; Agent teams=A shared task list; Workflows=Script variables — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#when-to-use-a-workflow
- [parameter] What's repeatable: Subagents=The worker definition; Skills=The instructions; Agent teams=The team definition; Workflows=The orchestration itself — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#when-to-use-a-workflow
- [parameter] Scale: Subagents=A few delegated tasks per turn; Skills=Same as subagents; Agent teams=A handful of long-running peers; Workflows=Dozens to hundreds of agents per run — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#when-to-use-a-workflow
- [parameter] Interruption: Subagents=Restarts the turn; Skills=Restarts the turn; Agent teams=Teammates keep running; Workflows=Resumable in the same session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#when-to-use-a-workflow
- [parameter] `/deep-research <question>`: Fans out web searches on a question across several angles, fetches and cross-checks the sources it finds, votes on each claim, and returns a cited report with claims that didn't survive cross-checking filtered out. Requires the [WebSearch tool](/docs/en/tools-reference#websearch-tool-behavior) to be available — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#bundled-workflows
- [parameter] `↑` / `↓`: Select a phase or agent — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `Enter` or `→`: Drill into the selected phase, then into an agent to read its prompt, recent tool calls, and result — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `Esc` or `←`: Back out one level. In v2.1.203 through v2.1.205, `←` didn't step back out of a phase or agent; use `Esc` on those versions — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `j` / `k`: Scroll within the agent detail when it overflows — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `f`: Filter the agent list in the selected phase by status. Press again to cycle — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `p`: Pause or resume the run — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `x`: Stop the selected agent, or stop the whole workflow when focus is on the run — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `r`: Restart the selected running agent — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] `s`: [Save](#save-the-workflow-for-reuse) the run's script as a command — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [parameter] Auto: First launch only. Any **Yes** records consent in your user settings, and later launches start without prompting. Skipped entirely when ultracode is on — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#approve-the-plan-before-it-runs
- [parameter] Manual, accept edits: Every run, unless you've selected **Yes, and don't ask again** for that workflow in this project — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#approve-the-plan-before-it-runs
- [parameter] Bypass permissions: Claude Code doesn't prompt you. The run starts immediately — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#approve-the-plan-before-it-runs
- [parameter] `claude -p`, Agent SDK: Claude Code doesn't prompt you — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#approve-the-plan-before-it-runs
- [parameter] No mid-run user input: Only agent permission prompts can pause a run. For sign-off between stages, run each stage as its own workflow — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [parameter] No direct filesystem or shell access from the workflow itself: Agents read, write, and run commands. The script coordinates the agents — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [parameter] No module loading: a script that contains `import()` fails before the run starts: The script body is plain JavaScript. Put work that needs a library in an agent's task — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [parameter] Up to 16 concurrent agents, fewer when Claude Code has fewer CPUs available, including inside a CPU-limited container: Bounds local resource use — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [parameter] In a fan-out, agents that share the first agent's prompt-cache prefix start up to 5 seconds after it by default: All but the first read the [prefix the first agent cached](#prompt-caching-in-a-fan-out) instead of each processing it uncached — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [parameter] Up to 4,096 items in a single `parallel()` or `pipeline()` call: the runtime rejects a longer list with an error: A silent cap would drop part of the workload without telling the script — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [parameter] 1,000 agents total per run: Prevents runaway loops — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [parameter] `unrestricted`: No guideline: Claude sizes the workflow to the task — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#set-a-size-guideline
- [parameter] `small`: Fewer than 5 agents — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#set-a-size-guideline
- [parameter] `medium`: Fewer than 15 agents — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#set-a-size-guideline
- [parameter] `large`: Fewer than 50 agents — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#set-a-size-guideline
- [definition] Orchestrate subagents at scale with dynamic workflows — Dynamic workflows orchestrate many subagents from a script Claude writes and you can rerun. Use them for codebase audits, large migrations, and cross-checked research. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#orchestrate-subagents-at-scale-with-dynamic-workflows
- [definition] When to use a workflow — [Subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents), [skills](/docs/en/skills), [agent teams](/docs/en/agent-teams), and workflows can all run a multi-step task. The difference is who holds the plan: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#when-to-use-a-workflow
- [definition] Run a bundled workflow — The quickest way to see a workflow in action is to run `/deep-research`, the [built-in workflow](#bundled-workflows) Claude Code includes for investigating a question across many sources. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#run-a-bundled-workflow
- [definition] Run the workflow — Run `/deep-research` with a question you want investigated. It fans out web searches across several angles, fetches and cross-checks the sources it finds, and synthesizes a cited report. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#run-a-bundled-workflow
- [definition] Allow workflows — Claude Code asks whether to allow the workflow. Select **Yes** to continue. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#run-a-bundled-workflow
- [definition] Watch progress — The run starts in the background. Run `/workflows`, use the arrow keys to select the run, and press Enter to open its progress view: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#run-a-bundled-workflow
- [definition] Read the report — When the run finishes, the report lands in your session. It cites the sources each claim came from, with claims that didn't survive cross-checking already filtered out. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#run-a-bundled-workflow
- [definition] Bundled workflows — Claude Code includes `/deep-research` as a built-in workflow: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#bundled-workflows
- [definition] Watch the run — Workflows run in the background, so the session stays responsive while agents work. Run `/workflows` at any time to list running and completed workflows, then select one to open its progress view. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#watch-the-run
- [definition] Have Claude write a workflow — You can have Claude write a workflow for your task in two ways: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#have-claude-write-a-workflow
- [definition] Ask for a workflow in your prompt — To run a single task as a workflow without changing the session's effort level, include the keyword `ultracode` in your prompt. Asking in your own words, for example "use a workflow" or "run a workflow", also works: Claude treats a direct request as the same opt-in. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#ask-for-a-workflow-in-your-prompt
- [definition] Let Claude decide with ultracode — Ultracode is a Claude Code setting that combines `xhigh` [reasoning effort](/docs/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level) with automatic workflow orchestration. With it on, Claude plans a workflow for each substantive task instead of waiting for you to ask. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#let-claude-decide-with-ultracode
- [definition] Approve the plan before it runs — In the CLI, the per-run prompt shows the planned phases and these options: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#approve-the-plan-before-it-runs
- [definition] Save the workflow for reuse — When Claude writes a workflow for a task you'll repeat, you can save that run's script as a command. A process like a review you run on every branch then runs the same orchestration each time. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#save-the-workflow-for-reuse
- [definition] Distribute a workflow in a plugin — To share a workflow across teams or repositories, include it in a [plugin](/docs/en/plugins). - [definition] Pass input to a saved workflow — A saved workflow can accept input through the `args` parameter. The script reads it as a global named `args`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#pass-input-to-a-saved-workflow
- [definition] Example workflow prompts — A workflow fits best when the task is larger than one agent can hold in context, or when the same step needs to run across many items. The prompts below show common shapes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#example-workflow-prompts
- [definition] Audit many files for the same issue — Fan out one agent per file, then collect and verify the findings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#audit-many-files-for-the-same-issue
- [definition] Keep fixing until a check passes — Run a checker, fix what failed, and repeat until it passes or stops making progress. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#keep-fixing-until-a-check-passes
- [definition] Migrate many files in parallel — Discover the files to migrate, transform each one in an isolated copy so edits don't conflict, and verify each result. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#migrate-many-files-in-parallel
- [definition] Review every changed file and write one summary — Run a reviewer per file, then hand all the findings to one agent that ranks and deduplicates them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#review-every-changed-file-and-write-one-summary
- [definition] Research a topic across many sources — Fan out readers across changelogs, issues, and docs, then synthesize. The bundled `/deep-research` workflow does this; you can also describe a narrower version. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#research-a-topic-across-many-sources
- [definition] Find issues until the list stops growing — Keep searching in rounds and stop when new rounds turn up nothing new. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#find-issues-until-the-list-stops-growing
- [definition] What the saved script looks like — When you [save a workflow](#save-the-workflow-for-reuse), the file in `.claude/workflows/` holds a `meta` block followed by a script body that orchestrates subagents. You usually don't need to edit it, but here is the shape of a small one so you can recognize what Claude generated: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#what-the-saved-script-looks-like
- [definition] Edit a saved script — To change a [workflow you saved](#save-the-workflow-for-reuse), edit its `.js` file or ask Claude to make the change. Before you edit or ask, run the `/workflow-authoring` [bundled skill](/docs/en/skills#bundled-skills) to load the script-writing reference Claude works from. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#edit-a-saved-script
- [definition] How a workflow runs — The workflow runtime executes the script in an isolated environment, separate from your conversation. Intermediate results stay in script variables instead of landing in Claude's context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#how-a-workflow-runs
- [definition] Prompt caching in a fan-out — Agents in the same run can read each other's [prompt cache](/docs/en/prompt-caching#subagents-and-the-cache). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#prompt-caching-in-a-fan-out
- [definition] Behavior and limits — The runtime applies the following constraints: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#behavior-and-limits
- [definition] Manage runs — Once a run starts, you manage it from the `/workflows` view, or by expanding its progress line in the task panel below the input box. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#manage-runs
- [definition] Resume after a pause — Resume a paused run from `/workflows` by selecting it and pressing `p`. For a run you stopped, ask Claude to relaunch the workflow with the same script. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#resume-after-a-pause
- [definition] Cost — A workflow spawns many agents, so a single run can use meaningfully more tokens than working through the same task in conversation. Runs count toward your plan's usage and rate limits like any other session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#cost
- [definition] Set a size guideline — A size guideline tells Claude how many agents to aim for when it writes a dynamic workflow. Claude Code sends the guideline to Claude as advice, not a cap, so a prompt that calls for a different scale still overrides it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#set-a-size-guideline
- [definition] Turn workflows off — Workflows are available in the CLI, the Desktop app, the IDE extensions, [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with `claude -p`, and the [Agent SDK](/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview). The same disable settings apply on every surface. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#turn-workflows-off

- [parameter] `Your worktree <path> no longer exists`: The worktree directory was removed. The session continues in the current directory without isolation, and Claude Code clears the worktree binding. No action needed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#the-session-resumes-outside-its-worktree
- [parameter] `Could not verify your worktree <path> this time`: Claude Code couldn't verify the worktree, usually for a transient reason; the binding is kept, and the session continues in the current directory without isolation. Resume again to retry; if it keeps happening, enter the worktree in a new session and match the refusal message under [Claude Code refuses to use a… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#the-session-resumes-outside-its-worktree
- [parameter] `Did not re-enter your worktree <path>`: Claude Code refused the worktree binding as unsafe; it clears the binding and the session continues without isolation. The message includes the specific refusal: match it under [Claude Code refuses to use a worktree](#claude-code-refuses-to-use-a-worktree), since the fix is recreation for some refusals and a path change for others. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#the-session-resumes-outside-its-worktree
- [parameter] `Could not re-enter your worktree <path>`: Claude Code couldn't vouch for the worktree from where you launched, most commonly because you launched from inside it; the binding is kept. The rest of the message names the fix; match it under [Claude Code refuses to use a worktree](#claude-code-refuses-to-use-a-worktree). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#the-session-resumes-outside-its-worktree
- [definition] Run parallel sessions with worktrees — Isolate parallel Claude Code sessions in separate git worktrees so changes don't collide. - [definition] Start Claude in a worktree — Pass `--worktree` or `-w` with a name to create an isolated worktree and start Claude in it. By default, the worktree is created under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` at your repository root, on a new branch named `worktree-<name>`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#start-claude-in-a-worktree

- [definition] Clean up worktrees — When you exit an interactive worktree session, Claude checks the worktree for work that removal would delete: changed or untracked files, and new commits. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#clean-up-worktrees
- [definition] Resume a worktree session — When you resume a session that was inside a worktree, Claude Code returns the session to that worktree. - [definition] How Claude Code enforces isolation — While a session is isolated in a worktree, Claude Code blocks the tool calls the checks below define. - [definition] Isolate subagents with worktrees — Subagents can run in their own worktrees so parallel edits don't conflict. - [definition] Clean up subagent and background-session worktrees — Claude Code runs a periodic sweep that removes worktrees that Claude created for subagents and [background sessions](/docs/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated) once they are older than your [`cleanupPeriodDays`](/docs/en/settings-reference#cleanupperioddays) setting, following the [retention… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#clean-up-subagent-and-background-session-worktrees
- [definition] Customize worktree creation — Claude Code's defaults for creating worktrees cover most sessions: it creates them under `.claude/worktrees/`, branches them from your repository's default branch, and checks out only tracked files. The options in this section change those defaults. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#customize-worktree-creation
- [definition] Choose the base branch — New worktrees branch from the repository's default branch, so most sessions don't need this setting. Set `worktree.baseRef` in [settings](/docs/en/settings-reference#worktree) to branch from your current work instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#choose-the-base-branch
- [definition] Branch from a pull request — To branch from a specific pull request or merge request, pass `--worktree` the number prefixed with `#`, a GitHub pull request URL, or a GitLab merge request URL such as `https://gitlab.com/group/repo/-/merge_requests/123`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#branch-from-a-pull-request
- [definition] Copy gitignored files into worktrees — A worktree is a fresh checkout, so untracked files like `.env` or `.env.local` from your main repository are not present. - [definition] Replace worktree creation with a hook — Configure a [`WorktreeCreate` hook](/docs/en/hooks#worktreecreate) to replace the default `git worktree` logic entirely, including placing worktrees somewhere other than `.claude/worktrees/`. - [definition] Manage worktrees manually — Create worktrees with Git directly when you need to check out a specific existing branch or place the worktree outside the repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#manage-worktrees-manually
- [definition] Non-git version control — Worktree isolation uses git by default. - [definition] Troubleshooting — Claude Code reports the errors below when it creates a worktree, enters one at startup, or returns a resumed session to one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#troubleshooting
- [definition] Claude Code can't enter the worktree at startup — When Claude Code can't enter the worktree directory at startup, it prints an error naming the path and exits with code 1. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#claude-code-cant-enter-the-worktree-at-startup
- [definition] Worktree creation fails on a symlinked path — Claude Code refuses to create a worktree when `.claude`, `.claude/worktrees`, or the worktree directory itself is a symlink, and the error names the symlinked path. Remove the symlink and retry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#worktree-creation-fails-on-a-symlinked-path
- [definition] Git LFS files are pointer files in a worktree Claude Code created — If you set up [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com) with `git lfs install --local`, a worktree that Claude Code creates contains LFS pointer files instead of the real files. The `--local` flag writes the LFS filter into the repository's own `.git/config` rather than your global git config. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#git-lfs-files-are-pointer-files-in-a-worktree-claude-code-created
- [definition] Claude Code refuses to use a worktree — An error starting `Refusing to use <path> as an isolation worktree` means Claude Code checked the directory's git identity before adopting it as a session's or subagent's isolated checkout, and declined it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#claude-code-refuses-to-use-a-worktree

## Zero data retention
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention>

- [parameter] Chat on claude.ai: Chat conversations through the Claude for Enterprise web interface are not covered by ZDR. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#what-zdr-does-not-cover
- [parameter] Cowork: Cowork sessions are not covered by ZDR. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#what-zdr-does-not-cover
- [parameter] Claude Code Analytics: Does not store prompts or model responses, but collects productivity metadata such as account emails and usage statistics. Contribution metrics are not available for ZDR organizations; the [analytics dashboard](/docs/en/analytics) shows usage metrics only. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#what-zdr-does-not-cover
- [parameter] User and seat management: Administrative data such as account emails and seat assignments is retained under standard policies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#what-zdr-does-not-cover
- [parameter] Third-party integrations: Data processed by third-party tools, MCP servers, or other external integrations is not covered by ZDR. Review those services' data handling practices independently. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#what-zdr-does-not-cover
- [parameter] [Claude Code on the Web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web): Requires server-side storage of conversation history. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#features-disabled-under-zdr
- [parameter] [Cloud sessions](/docs/en/desktop#cloud-sessions) from the Desktop app: Requires persistent session data that includes prompts and completions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#features-disabled-under-zdr
- [parameter] [Claude Tag](/docs/en/claude-tag): Retains channel memory and session transcripts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#features-disabled-under-zdr
- [parameter] [Artifacts](/docs/en/artifacts): Requires storing published page content on Anthropic-operated infrastructure. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#features-disabled-under-zdr
- [parameter] Feedback submission (`/feedback`, `/bug`, `/share`): Submitting feedback sends conversation data to Anthropic. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#features-disabled-under-zdr
- [parameter] [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control): Stores the session transcript on Anthropic servers to sync the conversation across devices. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#features-disabled-under-zdr
- [definition] Zero data retention — Learn about Zero Data Retention (ZDR) for Claude Code, available to qualified accounts on Claude for Enterprise, including scope, disabled features, and how to request enablement. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#zero-data-retention
- [definition] ZDR scope — ZDR covers Claude Code inference on Claude for Enterprise. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#zdr-scope
- [definition] Route Claude Code traffic to your ZDR organization — ZDR applies to requests that authenticate into a ZDR-enabled organization. If a developer signs in to Claude Code with a personal account or with an API key from a different organization, those sessions are not covered. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#route-claude-code-traffic-to-your-zdr-organization
- [definition] What ZDR covers — ZDR covers model inference calls made through Claude Code on Claude for Enterprise. When you use Claude Code in your terminal, the prompts you send and the responses Claude generates are not retained by Anthropic. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#what-zdr-covers
- [definition] What ZDR does not cover — ZDR does not extend to the following, even for organizations with ZDR enabled. These features follow [standard data retention policies](/docs/en/data-usage#data-retention): — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#what-zdr-does-not-cover
- [definition] Features disabled under ZDR — When ZDR is enabled for a Claude Code organization on Claude for Enterprise, certain features that require storing prompts or completions are automatically disabled at the backend level: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#features-disabled-under-zdr
- [definition] Model availability under ZDR — Claude Fable 5 is not available for organizations with zero data retention enabled. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#model-availability-under-zdr
- [definition] Data retention for policy violations — Even with ZDR enabled, Anthropic may retain data where required by law or to address Usage Policy violations. If a session is flagged for a policy violation, Anthropic may retain the associated inputs and outputs for up to 2 years, consistent with Anthropic's standard ZDR policy. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#data-retention-for-policy-violations
- [definition] Request ZDR — To request ZDR for Claude Code on Claude for Enterprise, [contact sales](https://www.anthropic.com/contact-sales?utm_source=claude_code\&utm_medium=docs\&utm_content=zero_data_retention_request) or your Anthropic account team. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention#request-zdr

- [parameter] Haiku main + Opus advisor: Lowest-cost main model with strong planning. Expect higher cost than Haiku alone but lower than switching the main model to Sonnet or Opus — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#common-model-pairings

- [parameter] Fable main + Fable advisor: Highest-capability pairing when Fable 5 is available (v2.1.170+). Fable is a higher tier than Opus and Sonnet, so it is the only accepted advisor for a Fable main model — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#common-model-pairings

- [definition] When to use the advisor — The advisor fits long, multi-step tasks where most turns are routine but plan quality determines the outcome. - [definition] Use the `--advisor` flag — To set the advisor for a single session without changing your saved setting, launch with the flag: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#use-the-advisor-flag

- [definition] Fable advisor and usage credits — On some plans, Fable 5 usage bills to usage credits, and Claude Code asks for your [one-time consent to bill Fable 5 usage to usage credits](/docs/en/model-config#fable-5-and-usage-credits) when you select Fable 5 with `/model`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#fable-advisor-and-usage-credits
- [definition] Common model pairings — Any accepted pairing works. These combinations balance cost against capability in different ways: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#common-model-pairings
- [definition] When Claude consults the advisor — Claude decides when to call the advisor. - [definition] Cost — When Claude calls the advisor, the advisor model reads the conversation, so each call consumes tokens at the advisor model's rates in addition to your main model's usage. - [definition] Impact on prompt caching — Enabling or disabling the advisor mid-session does not invalidate your main model's [prompt cache](/docs/en/prompt-caching). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#impact-on-prompt-caching
- [definition] Requirements — The advisor tool requires all of the following: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#requirements

- [definition] Compare with related features — The advisor is one of several ways to combine model strengths. Pick based on when you want a second model involved. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor#compare-with-related-features

- [definition] Turns and messages — A turn is one round trip inside the loop: Claude produces output that includes tool calls, the SDK executes those tools, and the results feed back to Claude automatically. This happens without yielding control back to your code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#turns-and-messages
- [definition] Message types — As the loop runs, the SDK yields a stream of messages. Each message carries a type that tells you what stage of the loop it came from. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#message-types
- [definition] Handle messages — Which messages you handle depends on what you're building: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#handle-messages
- [definition] Tool execution — Tools give your agent the ability to take action. Without tools, Claude can only respond with text. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#tool-execution
- [definition] Built-in tools — The SDK includes the same tools that power Claude Code: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#built-in-tools
- [definition] Tool permissions — Claude determines which tools to call based on the task, but you control whether those calls are allowed to execute. You can auto-approve specific tools, block others entirely, or require approval for everything. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#tool-permissions
- [definition] Parallel tool execution — When Claude requests multiple tool calls in a single turn, both SDKs can run them concurrently or sequentially depending on the tool. Read-only tools (like `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, and MCP tools marked as read-only) can run concurrently. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#parallel-tool-execution
- [definition] Control how the loop runs — You can limit how many turns the loop takes, how much it costs, how deeply Claude reasons, and whether tools require approval before running. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#control-how-the-loop-runs
- [definition] Effort level — The `effort` option controls how much reasoning Claude applies. Lower effort levels use fewer tokens per turn and reduce cost. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#effort-level
- [definition] Permission mode — The permission mode option (`permission_mode` in Python, `permissionMode` in TypeScript) controls whether the agent asks for approval before using tools: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#permission-mode
- [definition] Model — If you don't set `model`, the SDK uses Claude Code's default, which depends on your authentication method and subscription. Set it explicitly (for example, `model="claude-sonnet-5"`) to pin a specific model or to use a smaller model for faster, cheaper agents. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#model
- [definition] The context window — The context window is the total amount of information available to Claude during a session. It does not reset between turns within a session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#the-context-window
- [definition] What consumes context — Here's how each component affects context in the SDK: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#what-consumes-context
- [definition] Automatic compaction — When the context window approaches its limit, the SDK automatically compacts the conversation: it summarizes older history to free space, keeping your most recent exchanges and key decisions intact. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#automatic-compaction
- [definition] Keep context efficient — A few strategies for long-running agents: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#keep-context-efficient
- [definition] Sessions and continuity — Each interaction with the SDK creates or continues a session. Capture the session ID from `ResultMessage.session_id` (available in both SDKs) to resume later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#sessions-and-continuity
- [definition] Handle the result — When the loop ends, the `ResultMessage` tells you what happened and gives you the output. The `subtype` field (available in both SDKs) is the primary way to check termination state. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#handle-the-result
- [definition] Hooks — [Hooks](/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks) are callbacks that fire at specific points in the loop: before a tool runs, after it returns, when the agent finishes, and so on. Some commonly used hooks are: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#hooks
- [definition] Put it all together — This example combines the key concepts from this page into a single agent that fixes failing tests. It configures the agent with allowed tools (auto-approved so the agent runs autonomously), project settings, and safety limits on turns and reasoning effort. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#put-it-all-together
- [definition] Next steps — Now that you understand the loop, here's where to go depending on what you're building: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#next-steps

- [definition] Track cost and usage — Learn how to track token usage, estimate costs, and configure prompt caching with the Claude Agent SDK. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-cost-and-usage

- [definition] Track costs in streaming input mode — In [streaming input mode](/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode), one `query()` call carries multiple user turns and each turn emits its own result message. The result fields differ in scope: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-costs-in-streaming-input-mode
- [definition] Get the total cost of a query — The result message, typed as [`SDKResultMessage`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkresultmessage) in TypeScript and [`ResultMessage`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/python#resultmessage) in Python, marks the end of the agent loop for a `query()` call. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#get-the-total-cost-of-a-query
- [definition] Track per-step and per-model usage — The examples in this section use TypeScript field names. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-per-step-and-per-model-usage
- [definition] Track per-step usage — Each assistant message contains a nested `BetaMessage` (accessed via `message.message`) with an `id` and `usage` object with token counts. When Claude uses tools in parallel, multiple messages share the same `id` with identical usage data. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-per-step-usage
- [definition] Break down usage per model — The result message includes [`modelUsage`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#modelusage), a map of model name to per-model token counts and cost. This is useful when you run multiple models (for example, Haiku for subagents and Opus for the main agent) and want to see where tokens are going. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#break-down-usage-per-model
- [definition] Accumulate costs across multiple calls — Each `query()` call returns its own `total_cost_usd`. The SDK doesn't provide a session-level total, so if your application makes multiple `query()` calls, for example in a multi-turn session or across different users, accumulate the totals yourself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#accumulate-costs-across-multiple-calls
- [definition] Handle errors, caching, and output token counts — For accurate cost tracking, account for the placeholder output count on assistant messages, the tokens a failed conversation consumed, and cache token pricing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#handle-errors-caching-and-output-token-counts
- [definition] Read output tokens from the result message — Claude Code builds each assistant message from the usage the API reported when the response began, so the message's `output_tokens` is only the count the API had reported at `message_start`, before the response was generated. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#read-output-tokens-from-the-result-message
- [definition] Track costs on failed conversations — Both success and error result messages include `usage` and `total_cost_usd`; in Python both fields are typed as optional, so check that they aren't `None` before you read them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-costs-on-failed-conversations
- [definition] Recover totals after a session crash — When the Claude Code process crashes, it emits a final `error_during_execution` result and exits, in single-shot and streaming input mode alike. That result may carry zeroed `usage`, `total_cost_usd`, and `modelUsage`, so recover the call's totals from what arrived before it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#recover-totals-after-a-session-crash
- [definition] Track cache tokens — The Agent SDK automatically uses [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) to reduce costs on repeated content. You do not need to configure caching yourself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-cache-tokens
- [definition] Extend the prompt cache TTL to one hour — Your own turns fall in the [main conversation TTL bucket](/docs/en/prompt-caching#which-ttl-each-request-gets), together with the helpers Claude Code runs inline with them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#extend-the-prompt-cache-ttl-to-one-hour

- [parameter] Let Claude call tools in parallel: Set `readOnlyHint: true` on tools with no side effects. See [Add tool annotations](#add-tool-annotations). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#quick-reference
