- [parameter] `readOnlyHint`: Default=`false`; Meaning=Tool does not modify its environment. Controls whether the tool can be called in parallel with other read-only tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#add-tool-annotations
- [parameter] `destructiveHint`: Default=`true`; Meaning=Tool may perform destructive updates. Informational only. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#add-tool-annotations
- [parameter] `idempotentHint`: Default=`false`; Meaning=Repeated calls with the same arguments have no additional effect. Informational only. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#add-tool-annotations
- [parameter] `openWorldHint`: Default=`true`; Meaning=Tool reaches systems outside your process. Informational only. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#add-tool-annotations
- [parameter] `tools: ["Read", "Grep"]`: Layer=Availability; Effect=Only the listed built-ins are in Claude's context. Unlisted built-ins are removed. MCP tools are unaffected. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#configure-allowed-tools
- [parameter] `tools: []`: Layer=Availability; Effect=All built-ins are removed. Claude can only use your MCP tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#configure-allowed-tools
- [parameter] allowed tools: Layer=Permission; Effect=Listed tools run without a permission prompt. Other unlisted tools remain available; calls go through the [permission flow](/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#configure-allowed-tools
- [parameter] disallowed tools: Layer=Both; Effect=A bare tool name such as `"Bash"` removes the tool from Claude's context, the same as omitting it from `tools`. A scoped rule such as `"Bash(rm *)"` leaves the tool in context and denies only matching calls. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#configure-allowed-tools
- [parameter] Handler throws an uncaught exception: The MCP server converts it to an error result carrying the raw exception message. Claude sees that message, and the agent loop continues. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#handle-errors
- [parameter] Handler catches the error and returns `isError: true` (TS) / `"is_error": True` (Python): Claude sees the message you compose. You can add context the raw exception lacks, such as which request failed or what to try instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#handle-errors
- [parameter] `type`: Type=`"image"` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#images
- [parameter] `data`: Type=`string`; Notes=Base64-encoded bytes. Raw base64 only, no `data:image/...;base64,` prefix — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#images
- [parameter] `mimeType`: Type=`string`; Notes=Required. For example `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, `image/gif` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#images
- [parameter] `type`: Type=`"resource"` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#resources
- [parameter] `resource.uri`: Type=`string`; Notes=Identifier for the content. Any URI scheme — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#resources
- [parameter] `resource.text`: Type=`string`; Notes=The content, if it's text. Provide this or `blob`, not both — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#resources
- [parameter] `resource.blob`: Type=`string`; Notes=The content base64-encoded, if it's binary. TypeScript only: the Python SDK drops binary resources from the tool result and logs a warning — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#resources
- [parameter] `resource.mimeType`: Type=`string`; Notes=Optional — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#resources
- [definition] Give Claude custom tools — Define custom tools with the Claude Agent SDK's in-process MCP server so Claude can call your functions, hit your APIs, and perform domain-specific operations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#give-claude-custom-tools
- [definition] Create a custom tool — A tool is defined by four parts, passed as arguments to the [`tool()`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#tool) helper in TypeScript or the [`@tool`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/python#tool) decorator in Python: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#create-a-custom-tool
- [definition] Weather tool example — This example defines a `get_temperature` tool and wraps it in an MCP server. It only sets up the tool; to pass it to `query` and run it, see [Call a custom tool](#call-a-custom-tool) below. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#weather-tool-example
- [definition] Call a custom tool — Pass the MCP server you created to `query` via the `mcpServers` option. The key in `mcpServers` becomes the `{server_name}` segment in each tool's fully qualified name: `mcp__{server_name}__{tool_name}`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#call-a-custom-tool
- [definition] Add more tools — A server holds as many tools as you list in its `tools` array. With more than one tool on a server, you can list each one in `allowedTools` individually or use the wildcard `mcp__weather__*` to cover every tool the server exposes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#add-more-tools
- [definition] Add tool annotations — [Tool annotations](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools#tool-annotations) are optional metadata describing how a tool behaves. Pass them as the fifth argument to `tool()` helper in TypeScript or via the `annotations` keyword argument for the `@tool` decorator in Python. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#add-tool-annotations
- [definition] Control tool access — The [weather tool example](#weather-tool-example) registered a server and listed tools in `allowedTools`. This section covers how to scope access when you have multiple tools or want to restrict built-ins. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#control-tool-access
- [definition] Configure allowed tools — The `tools` option and the allowed/disallowed lists affect two layers: availability, which controls whether a tool appears in Claude's context, and permission, which controls whether a call is approved once Claude attempts it. `tools` and bare-name `disallowedTools` entries change availability. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#configure-allowed-tools
- [definition] Handle errors — A handler error doesn't stop the agent loop. The SDK's in-process MCP server catches uncaught exceptions and returns them as error results, so how you report an error determines what Claude reads, not whether the query fails: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#handle-errors
- [definition] Return images and resources — The `content` array in a tool result accepts `text`, `image`, `audio`, `resource`, and `resource_link` blocks. You can mix them in the same response. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#return-images-and-resources
- [definition] Images — An image block carries the image bytes inline, encoded as base64. There is no URL field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#images
- [definition] Resources — A resource block embeds a piece of content identified by a URI. The URI is a label for Claude to reference; the actual content rides in the block's `text` or `blob` field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#resources
- [definition] Return structured data — `structuredContent` is an optional JSON object on the result, separate from the `content` array. Use it to return raw values that Claude can read as exact fields instead of parsing them out of a text string or image. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#return-structured-data
- [definition] Example: unit converter — This tool converts values between units of length, temperature, and weight. A user can ask "convert 100 kilometers to miles" or "what is 72°F in Celsius," and Claude picks the right unit type and units from the request. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#example-unit-converter
- [definition] Next steps — You can mix the patterns on this page in the same server: a single server can hold a database tool, an API gateway tool, and an image renderer alongside each other. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools#next-steps

- [definition] Rewind file changes with checkpointing — Track file changes during agent sessions and restore files to any previous state — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#rewind-file-changes-with-checkpointing
- [definition] How checkpointing works — When you enable file checkpointing, the SDK creates backups of files before modifying them through the Write, Edit, or NotebookEdit tools. User messages in the response stream include a checkpoint UUID that you can use as a restore point. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#how-checkpointing-works
- [definition] Implement checkpointing — To use file checkpointing, enable it in your options, capture checkpoint UUIDs from the response stream, then call `rewindFiles()` (TypeScript) or `rewind_files()` (Python) when you need to restore. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#implement-checkpointing
- [definition] Enable checkpointing — Configure your SDK options to enable checkpointing and receive checkpoint UUIDs: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#implement-checkpointing
- [definition] Capture checkpoint UUID and session ID — With the `replay-user-messages` option set (shown above), each user message in the response stream has a UUID that serves as a checkpoint. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#implement-checkpointing
- [definition] Rewind files — To rewind after the stream completes, resume the session with an empty prompt and call `rewind_files()` (Python) or `rewindFiles()` (TypeScript) with your checkpoint UUID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#implement-checkpointing
- [definition] Common patterns — These patterns show different ways to capture and use checkpoint UUIDs depending on your use case. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#common-patterns
- [definition] Checkpoint before risky operations — This pattern keeps only the most recent checkpoint UUID, updating it before each agent turn. If something goes wrong during processing, you can immediately rewind to the last safe state and break out of the loop. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#checkpoint-before-risky-operations
- [definition] Multiple restore points — If Claude makes changes across multiple turns, you might want to rewind to a specific point rather than all the way back. For example, if Claude refactors a file in turn one and adds tests in turn two, you might want to keep the refactor but undo the tests. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#multiple-restore-points
- [definition] Try it out — This complete example creates a small utility file, has the agent add documentation comments, shows you the changes, then asks if you want to rewind. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#try-it-out

- [definition] Checkpointing options not recognized — If `enableFileCheckpointing` or `rewindFiles()` isn't available, you may be on an older SDK version. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#checkpointing-options-not-recognized
- [definition] User messages don't have UUIDs — If `message.uuid` is `undefined` or missing, you're not receiving checkpoint UUIDs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#user-messages-dont-have-uuids
- [definition] "No file checkpoint found for this message" error — This error occurs when the checkpoint data doesn't exist for the specified user message UUID. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#no-file-checkpoint-found-for-this-message-error
- [definition] "File rewinding is not enabled" error — This error occurs when you attempt a non-interactive rewind without checkpointing enabled: running bare `claude -p` with `--rewind-files`, or running an SDK session, including a resumed one, whose options don't enable checkpointing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#file-rewinding-is-not-enabled-error
- [definition] "ProcessTransport is not ready for writing" error — This error occurs when you call `rewindFiles()` or `rewind_files()` after you've finished iterating through the response. The connection to the CLI process closes when the loop completes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing#processtransport-is-not-ready-for-writing-error

- [definition] An event fires — Something happens during agent execution and the SDK fires an event: a tool is about to be called (`PreToolUse`), a tool returned a result (`PostToolUse`), a subagent started or stopped, the agent is idle, or execution finished. See the [full list of events](#available-hooks). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#how-hooks-work
- [definition] The SDK collects registered hooks — The SDK checks for hooks registered for that event type. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#how-hooks-work
- [definition] Matchers filter which hooks run — If a hook has a [`matcher`](#matchers) pattern (like `"Write|Edit"`), the SDK tests it against the event's target (for example, the tool name). Hooks without a matcher run for every event of that type. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#how-hooks-work
- [definition] Callback functions execute — Each matching hook's [callback function](#callback-functions) receives input about what's happening: the tool name, its arguments, the session ID, and other event-specific details. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#how-hooks-work
- [definition] Your callback returns a decision — After performing any operations (logging, API calls, validation), your callback returns an [output object](#outputs) that tells the agent what to do: allow the operation, block it, modify the input, or inject context into the conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#how-hooks-work
- [definition] Available hooks — The SDK provides hooks for different stages of agent execution. Some hooks are available in both SDKs, while others are TypeScript-only. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#available-hooks
- [definition] Configure hooks — To configure a hook, pass it in the `hooks` field of your agent options (`ClaudeAgentOptions` in Python, the `options` object in TypeScript). This snippet assumes you have already defined a hook callback, like `protect_env_files` in Python or `protectEnvFiles` in TypeScript from the example above: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#configure-hooks
- [definition] Matchers — Use matchers to filter when your callbacks fire. The `matcher` field matches against a different value depending on the hook event type. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#matchers
- [definition] Examples — Several examples in this section show only the callback function. To run one, register the callback under the matching event in the `hooks` field of your options, as shown in [Configure hooks](#configure-hooks). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#examples
- [definition] Modify tool input — This example intercepts Write tool calls and rewrites the `file_path` argument to prepend `/sandbox`, redirecting all file writes to a sandboxed directory. The callback returns `updatedInput` with the modified path and `permissionDecision: 'allow'` to auto-approve the rewritten operation: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#modify-tool-input
- [definition] Add context and block a tool — This example blocks writes to the `/etc` directory and explains why to both the model and the user: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#add-context-and-block-a-tool
- [definition] Auto-approve specific tools — By default, the agent may prompt for permission before using certain tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#auto-approve-specific-tools
- [definition] Register multiple hooks — When an event fires, all matching hooks run in parallel. For permission decisions, the most restrictive result applies: a single `deny` blocks the tool call regardless of what the other hooks return. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#register-multiple-hooks
- [definition] Filter with multi-tool matchers — Use multi-tool matchers to share one callback across related tools. This example registers three matchers with different scopes: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#filter-with-multi-tool-matchers
- [definition] Track subagent activity — Use `SubagentStop` hooks to monitor when subagents finish their work. See the full input type in the [TypeScript](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#hookinput) and [Python](/docs/en/agent-sdk/python#hookinput) SDK references. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#track-subagent-activity
- [definition] Make HTTP requests from hooks — Hooks can perform asynchronous operations like HTTP requests. Catch errors inside your hook instead of letting them propagate, since an unhandled exception can interrupt the agent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#make-http-requests-from-hooks
- [definition] Forward notifications to Slack — Use `Notification` hooks to receive system notifications from the agent and forward them to external services. In SDK sessions, Claude Code runs this hook for the following notification types: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#forward-notifications-to-slack
- [definition] Matcher not filtering as expected — Matchers only match tool names, not file paths or other arguments. To filter by file path, check `tool_input.file_path` inside your hook: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#matcher-not-filtering-as-expected
- [definition] Hook timeout — Claude Code runs each callback with a timeout, which you set in seconds with the `timeout` field on its `HookMatcher`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#hook-timeout
- [definition] Session hooks not available in Python — `SessionStart` and `SessionEnd` can be registered as SDK callback hooks in TypeScript, but aren't available in the Python SDK because its `HookEvent` type omits them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#session-hooks-not-available-in-python
- [definition] Subagent permission prompts multiplying — When spawning multiple subagents, each one may request permissions separately for its own tool calls. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#subagent-permission-prompts-multiplying
- [definition] Recursive hook loops with subagents — A `UserPromptSubmit` hook that spawns subagents can create infinite loops if those subagents trigger the same hook. To prevent this: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#recursive-hook-loops-with-subagents
- [definition] systemMessage not appearing in output — The `systemMessage` field shows a message to the user, not the model. On Claude Code v2.1.227 or later, a hook's `systemMessage` can surface in the message stream as an [`SDKInformationalMessage`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkinformationalmessage). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#systemmessage-not-appearing-in-output

- [parameter] Session transcripts: `~/.claude/projects/`, or the `projects/` directory under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if set — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#state-that-lives-on-local-disk
- [parameter] `CLAUDE.md` memory files: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` for the user tier and the session's working directory for the project tier — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#state-that-lives-on-local-disk
- [parameter] Working-directory artifacts: The session's working directory — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#state-that-lives-on-local-disk
- [parameter] No top-level session timeout: A session does not time out on its own. Set `maxTurns` in `Options` to bound how many tool-use round trips the agent takes before stopping. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#known-limitations
- [parameter] Memory growth over long sessions: Cap session length or recycle subprocesses periodically. See [Scaling and concurrency](#scaling-and-concurrency). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#known-limitations
- [parameter] Large parallel-subagent fanouts can hit rate limits: Break work into smaller batches rather than issuing one wide dispatch. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#known-limitations
- [parameter] No per-subagent wall-clock deadline: Cap each [subagent](/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents) with `maxTurns` in its `AgentDefinition`. For background subagents only, `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` sets a stall watchdog that fires when a `run_in_background` subagent stops producing output; it is not a total-runtime deadline. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#known-limitations
- [definition] Hosting the Agent SDK — Deploy the Agent SDK in production: subprocess architecture, session persistence, scaling, observability, and multi-tenant isolation for Docker, Kubernetes, and sandbox providers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#hosting-the-agent-sdk
- [definition] The subprocess model — Every hosting decision on this page follows from how the SDK runs the agent. When your code calls `query()`, the SDK spawns a separate `claude` CLI process and talks to it over stdio. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#the-subprocess-model
- [definition] State that lives on local disk — Three kinds of agent state live on the container's filesystem by default. None of them survive a container restart, a scale-down, or a move to a different node. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#state-that-lives-on-local-disk
- [definition] Choose a session pattern — These four patterns cover session lifecycle: how long a container lives relative to the sessions it serves. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#choose-a-session-pattern
- [definition] Ephemeral sessions — Create a container for each user task and destroy it when the task completes. Best for one-off tasks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#ephemeral-sessions
- [definition] Long-running sessions — Run persistent container instances, often hosting multiple SDK processes per container, to serve ongoing work. Best for agents that take autonomous action, serve content, or handle high-volume message streams. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#long-running-sessions
- [definition] Hybrid sessions — Ephemeral containers that hydrate from a [`SessionStore`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage) on startup and persist updates back. Best for sessions that span many interactions but sit idle between them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#hybrid-sessions
- [definition] Multi-agent container — Run multiple SDK subprocesses inside one container. Best for agents that must collaborate closely, for example multi-agent simulations where the agents interact with each other in a shared environment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#multi-agent-container
- [definition] Container-based sandboxing — Run the SDK inside a sandboxed container for process isolation, resource limits, network control, and an ephemeral filesystem. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#container-based-sandboxing
- [definition] Runtime dependencies — The container needs your SDK's language runtime: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#runtime-dependencies
- [definition] Resources — 1 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk, and 1 CPU per agent is a reasonable starting point for a freshly started instance. Memory usage grows with session length and tool activity, so size for the session lengths and concurrency you actually need rather than the idle baseline. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#resources
- [definition] Network — The SDK needs outbound HTTPS to `api.anthropic.com`, or to your provider's regional endpoint when running on Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform. If your agents use [MCP servers](/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp) or external tools, they need outbound access to those endpoints as well. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#network
- [definition] Handle production concerns — Work through these decisions before shipping a self-hosted agent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#handle-production-concerns
- [definition] Session and state persistence — Default local disk is lost on restart, scale-down, or a move to a different node. For any session a user expects to resume, mirror the transcript to durable storage with a [`SessionStore` adapter](/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#session-and-state-persistence
- [definition] Observability — Agent SDK agents are long-lived processes that spawn tool calls across many API round-trips. Without telemetry you cannot see which tools ran, how long they took, or where a session stalled. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#observability
- [definition] Auth and secrets — Three auth concerns matter at hosting time: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#auth-and-secrets
- [definition] Scaling and concurrency — Each session runs in its own subprocess, so concurrency on a host is bounded by how many subprocesses its RAM can hold. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#scaling-and-concurrency
- [definition] Cost — Anthropic token cost typically dominates container infrastructure cost by an order of magnitude or more. A minimally provisioned container runs roughly \$0.05 per hour, while a single long agent session can spend dollars in tokens. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#cost
- [definition] Multi-tenant isolation — Default SDK behavior reads settings and `CLAUDE.md` memory files from the filesystem. In a shared container that serves multiple tenants, those files can leak one tenant's context into another tenant's session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#multi-tenant-isolation
- [definition] Known limitations — Plan around these in your deployment design. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#known-limitations
- [definition] Troubleshoot deployment failures — Use this section when an agent that works on your machine fails in a deployed service. Each item below names a failure and links the entry that covers it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting#troubleshoot-deployment-failures

- [parameter] stdio server, or HTTP/SSE server without a cached tool list: Delays the first turn?=Yes, until it connects; First-turn wait timeout=[`MCP_TIMEOUT`](/docs/en/env-vars), 30 seconds by default; the connection fails at that deadline — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#connection-timing
- [parameter] Remote server with a cached tool list, saved by Claude Code from a previous connection: Delays the first turn?=No; the cached tools are available from the first turn; First-turn wait timeout=None; connects on its first tool call, and that deferred connect has its own timeout — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#connection-timing
- [parameter] In-process [SDK server](#sdk-mcp-servers): Delays the first turn?=No; never delays the first turn; First-turn wait timeout=None — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#connection-timing
- [definition] Connect to external tools with MCP — Configure MCP servers to extend your agent with external tools. Covers transport types, tool search for large tool sets, authentication, and error handling. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#connect-to-external-tools-with-mcp
- [definition] Quickstart — This example connects to the [Claude Code documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs) MCP server using [HTTP transport](#http%2Fsse-servers) and uses [`allowedTools`](#allow-mcp-tools) with a wildcard to permit all tools from the server. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#quickstart
- [definition] Add an MCP server — You can configure MCP servers in code when calling `query()`, or in a `.mcp.json` file loaded via [`settingSources`](#from-a-config-file). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#add-an-mcp-server
- [definition] In code — Pass MCP servers directly in the `mcpServers` option: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#in-code
- [definition] From a config file — Create a `.mcp.json` file at your project root. The file is picked up when the `project` setting source is enabled, which it is for default `query()` options. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#from-a-config-file
- [definition] Connection timing — Claude Code registers the servers you pass in `options.mcpServers` at startup and emits the [init message](#error-handling) once the first-turn wait, if any, resolves. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#connection-timing
- [definition] Allow MCP tools — MCP tools require explicit permission before Claude can use them. Without permission, Claude will see that tools are available but won't be able to call them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#allow-mcp-tools
- [definition] Tool naming convention — MCP tools follow the naming pattern `mcp__<server-name>__<tool-name>`. For example, a GitHub server named `"github"` with a `list_issues` tool becomes `mcp__github__list_issues`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#tool-naming-convention
- [definition] Auto-approve with allowedTools — Use `allowedTools` to auto-approve specific MCP tools so Claude can use them without a permission prompt: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#auto-approve-with-allowedtools
- [definition] Discover available tools — To see what tools an MCP server provides, check the server's documentation or inspect the `tools` array in the `system` init message. MCP tool names start with `mcp__`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#discover-available-tools
- [definition] Transport types — MCP servers communicate with your agent using different transport protocols. Check the server's documentation to see which transport it supports: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#transport-types
- [definition] stdio servers — Local processes that communicate via stdin/stdout. Use this for MCP servers you run on the same machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#stdio-servers
- [definition] HTTP/SSE servers — Use HTTP or SSE for cloud-hosted MCP servers and remote APIs. For the `.mcp.json` form, use the same fields as the example at [HTTP headers for remote servers](#http-headers-for-remote-servers), with `"type": "sse"` for an SSE server. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#httpsse-servers
- [definition] SDK MCP servers — Define custom tools directly in your application code instead of running a separate server process. See the [custom tools guide](/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools) for implementation details. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#sdk-mcp-servers
- [definition] MCP tool search — When you have many MCP tools configured, tool definitions can consume a significant portion of your context window. Tool search solves this by withholding tool definitions from context and loading only the ones Claude needs for each turn. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#mcp-tool-search
- [definition] Authentication — Most MCP servers require authentication to access external services. Pass credentials through environment variables in the server configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#authentication
- [definition] Pass credentials via environment variables — Use the `env` field to pass API keys, tokens, and other credentials to the MCP server: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#pass-credentials-via-environment-variables
- [definition] HTTP headers for remote servers — For HTTP and SSE servers, pass authentication headers directly in the server configuration: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#http-headers-for-remote-servers
- [definition] OAuth2 authentication — The [MCP specification supports OAuth 2.1](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/authorization) for authorization. The SDK doesn't open a browser or run an interactive OAuth flow. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#oauth2-authentication
- [definition] List issues from a repository — This example connects to the remote [GitHub MCP server](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server) to list recent issues. The example includes debug logging to verify the MCP connection and tool calls. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#list-issues-from-a-repository
- [definition] Query a database — This example uses [DBHub](https://github.com/bytebase/dbhub) to query a Postgres database. The agent automatically discovers the database schema, writes the SQL query, and returns the results. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#query-a-database
- [definition] Error handling — MCP servers can fail to connect for various reasons: the server process might not be installed, credentials might be invalid, or a remote server might be unreachable. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#error-handling
- [definition] Server shows "failed" status — Check the `init` message to see which servers failed to connect: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#server-shows-failed-status
- [definition] Tools not being called — If Claude sees tools but doesn't use them, check that you've granted permission with `allowedTools`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#tools-not-being-called
- [definition] Connection timeouts — MCP server connections time out after 30 seconds by default. To change how long a running tool call may take, set [`MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`](/docs/en/env-vars). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#connection-timeouts
- [definition] Tool output exceeds maximum allowed tokens — The SDK applies the same MCP output limit as Claude Code. When a tool result is larger than 25,000 tokens, the full output is saved to a file and the tool result is replaced with an error message that names the file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp#tool-output-exceeds-maximum-allowed-tokens

- [definition] Modifying system prompts — Choose between the `claude_code` preset and a custom system prompt, and customize behavior with CLAUDE.md, output styles, append, or a fully custom prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#modifying-system-prompts
- [definition] How system prompts work — A system prompt is the initial instruction set that shapes how Claude behaves throughout a conversation. The Agent SDK has three starting points for it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#how-system-prompts-work
- [definition] Decide on a starting point — The deciding factor is how closely your agent resembles Claude Code: a coding agent operating in a repository, with a human watching streaming output and steering the work. The further your product is from that, the more you'll want to write your own prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#decide-on-a-starting-point
- [definition] Customize agent behavior — Output styles, `append`, and a custom prompt string each change the system prompt directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#customize-agent-behavior
- [definition] CLAUDE.md files for project-level instructions — CLAUDE.md files give Claude persistent project context and instructions. The SDK injects their content into the conversation and leaves the system prompt untouched, so they work with any system prompt configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#claudemd-files-for-project-level-instructions
- [definition] Output styles for persistent configurations — Output styles are saved configurations that modify Claude's system prompt. They're stored as markdown files and can be reused across sessions and projects. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#output-styles-for-persistent-configurations
- [definition] Append to the `claude_code` preset — You can use the Claude Code preset with an `append` property to add your custom instructions while preserving all built-in functionality. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#append-to-the-claude-code-preset
- [definition] Custom system prompts — You can provide a custom string as `systemPrompt` to replace the default entirely with your own instructions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#custom-system-prompts
- [definition] Compare the four approaches — The four customization methods differ in where they live, how they're shared, and what they preserve from the `claude_code` preset. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#compare-the-four-approaches
- [definition] Combine approaches — The approaches compose. A persistent output style or CLAUDE.md sets the long-lived behavior, and `append` layers session-specific instructions on top without touching the saved configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#combine-approaches
- [definition] Combine an output style with session-specific additions — The example below assumes a Code Reviewer output style is already active. The `append` block layers session-specific focus areas on top of the persona, so a single review session can prioritize OAuth and token storage without changing the saved output style: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#combine-an-output-style-with-session-specific-additions

- [parameter] `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1`: Tool input arguments (file paths, shell commands, search patterns) on `claude_code.tool_result` events — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#control-sensitive-data-in-exports
- [parameter] `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1`: Full tool input and output bodies as span events on `claude_code.tool`, truncated at 60 KB by default, configurable via `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH`, which requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later. Requires [tracing](#read-agent-traces) to be enabled — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#control-sensitive-data-in-exports
- [parameter] `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES`: Full Anthropic Messages API request and response JSON as `claude_code.api_request_body` and `claude_code.api_response_body` log events. Set to `1` for inline bodies truncated at 60 KB by default, or `file:<dir>` for untruncated bodies on disk with a `body_ref` path in the event. `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH` configures the inline truncation limit, and requires… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#control-sensitive-data-in-exports
- [definition] Observability with OpenTelemetry — Export traces, metrics, and events from the Agent SDK to your observability backend using OpenTelemetry. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#observability-with-opentelemetry
- [definition] How telemetry flows from the SDK — The Agent SDK runs the Claude Code CLI as a child process and communicates with it over a local pipe. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#how-telemetry-flows-from-the-sdk
- [definition] Enable telemetry export — Telemetry is off until you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and choose at least one exporter. The most common configuration sends all three signals over OTLP HTTP to a collector. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#enable-telemetry-export
- [definition] Flush telemetry from short-lived calls — The CLI batches telemetry and exports on an interval. On a clean process exit it attempts to flush pending data, but the flush is bounded by a short timeout, so spans can still be dropped if the collector is slow to respond. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#flush-telemetry-from-short-lived-calls
- [definition] Read agent traces — Traces give you the most detailed view of an agent run. With `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1` set, each step of the agent loop becomes a span you can inspect in your tracing backend: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#read-agent-traces
- [definition] Link traces to your application — The SDK automatically propagates W3C trace context into the CLI subprocess. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#link-traces-to-your-application
- [definition] Tag telemetry from your agent — By default, the CLI reports `service.name` as `claude-code`. If you run several agents, or run the SDK alongside other services that export to the same collector, override the service name and add resource attributes so you can filter by agent in your backend. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#tag-telemetry-from-your-agent
- [definition] Attribute actions to your end users — The CLI attaches [identity attributes](/docs/en/monitoring-usage#standard-attributes) to every event based on the credential it uses to call Anthropic. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#attribute-actions-to-your-end-users
- [definition] Control sensitive data in exports — Telemetry is structural by default. Durations, model names, and tool names are recorded on every span; token counts are recorded when the underlying API request returns usage data, so spans for failed or aborted requests may omit them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#control-sensitive-data-in-exports
- [definition] Related documentation — These guides cover adjacent topics for monitoring and deploying agents: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability#related-documentation

## Agent SDK overview
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview>

- [parameter] Building an agent without implementing the tool loop yourself: Use=**Agent SDK**; Why=A library that runs the agent loop in your own process, in Python or TypeScript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview#compare-the-agent-sdk-to-other-claude-tools
- [parameter] Doing interactive development or running one-off tasks from a terminal: Use=[**Claude Code CLI**](/docs/en/overview); Why=The terminal interface, built for daily interactive use. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview#compare-the-agent-sdk-to-other-claude-tools
- [parameter] Calling the API directly and implementing the tool loop yourself: Use=[**Client SDK**](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/client-sdks); Why=Direct access to the Anthropic API rather than to Claude Code. You implement the tool loop yourself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview#compare-the-agent-sdk-to-other-claude-tools
- [parameter] Running long-running or asynchronous agents without managing your own sandbox or session infrastructure: Use=[**Managed Agents**](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview); Why=Hosted REST API, a separate product from the Agent SDK. Anthropic runs the agent and the sandbox. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview#compare-the-agent-sdk-to-other-claude-tools
- [parameter] Built-in tools: What it does=Read, write, edit files, run commands, and search the web; Learn more=[Tools reference](/docs/en/tools-reference) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview#capabilities

- [parameter] Subagents: What it does=Spawn specialized agents for focused subtasks; Learn more=[Subagents](/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview#capabilities
- [parameter] MCP: What it does=Connect external tools and data sources via the Model Context Protocol; Learn more=[MCP](/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview#capabilities

## Configure permissions
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions>

- [snippet] Allow and deny rules: const options = { — `const options = {` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules
- [snippet] Python: import asyncio — `import asyncio` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#set-permission-mode
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk"; — `import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#set-permission-mode
- [snippet] Python: import asyncio — `import asyncio` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#set-permission-mode
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk"; — `import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#set-permission-mode
- [parameter] `allowed_tools=["Read", "Grep"]`: `Read` and `Grep` are auto-approved. Other tools not listed here still exist and fall through to the permission mode and `canUseTool`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules
- [parameter] `disallowed_tools=["Bash"]`: The `Bash` tool definition is removed from the request. Claude does not see the tool and cannot attempt it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules
- [parameter] `disallowed_tools=["Bash(rm *)"]`: `Bash` stays available. Calls matching `rm *` are denied in every permission mode, including `bypassPermissions`. Other `Bash` calls fall through to the permission mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules
- [parameter] `disallowed_tools=["*"]`: Every tool definition is removed from the request. Tool-name globs are supported in deny rules: `"*"` matches every tool and `"mcp__*"` matches every MCP tool across all servers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules
- [parameter] `default`: Description=Standard permission behavior; Tool behavior=No auto-approvals; unmatched tools trigger your `canUseTool` callback — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#available-modes
- [parameter] `dontAsk`: Description=Deny instead of prompting; Tool behavior=Anything not pre-approved by `allowed_tools` or rules is denied; connector tools [your organization set to `ask`](/docs/en/mcp#organization-controls-on-connector-tools) and tools that require user interaction are denied even if you've pre-approved them, as are `rm` and `rmdir` removals targeting a [critical… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#available-modes
- [parameter] `acceptEdits`: Description=Auto-accept file edits; Tool behavior=File edits and [filesystem operations](#accept-edits-mode-acceptedits) (`mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, etc.) are automatically approved — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#available-modes
- [parameter] `bypassPermissions`: Description=Bypass permission checks; Tool behavior=Tools run without permission prompts, except for the [actions no mode auto-approves](/docs/en/permission-modes#actions-no-mode-auto-approves). Use with caution — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#available-modes
- [parameter] `plan`: Description=Planning mode; Tool behavior=Claude explores and plans without editing your source files; file edits are never auto-approved and prompt through your `canUseTool` callback — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#available-modes
- [parameter] `auto`: Description=Model-classified approvals; Tool behavior=A model classifier approves or denies permission prompts. See [Auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) for availability — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#available-modes
- [definition] Configure permissions — Control how your agent uses tools with permission modes, hooks, and declarative allow/deny rules. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#configure-permissions
- [definition] How permissions are evaluated — When Claude requests a tool, the SDK checks permissions in this order: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated
- [definition] Hooks — Run [hooks](/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks) first. A hook can deny the call outright or pass it on. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated
- [definition] Deny rules — Check `deny` rules (from `disallowed_tools` and [settings.json](/docs/en/settings-reference#permission-settings)). If a deny rule matches, the tool is blocked, even in `bypassPermissions` mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated
- [definition] Ask rules — Check `ask` rules from [settings.json](/docs/en/settings-reference#permission-settings). If an ask rule matches, the call falls through to your [`canUseTool` callback](/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input) for confirmation, even in `bypassPermissions` mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated
- [definition] Permission mode — Apply the active [permission mode](#permission-modes). `bypassPermissions` approves everything that reaches this step except `rm` and `rmdir` removals targeting a [critical path](/docs/en/permission-modes#critical-paths), which fall through instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated
- [definition] Allow rules — Check `allow` rules (from `allowed_tools` and settings.json). If a rule matches, the tool is approved. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated
- [definition] canUseTool callback — If not resolved by any of the above, call your [`canUseTool` callback](/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input) for a decision. In `dontAsk` mode, this step is skipped and the tool is denied. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated
- [definition] Allow and deny rules — `allowed_tools` and `disallowed_tools` (TypeScript: `allowedTools` / `disallowedTools`) add entries to the allow and deny rule lists in the evaluation flow above. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules
- [definition] Permission modes — Permission modes provide global control over how Claude uses tools. You can set the permission mode when calling `query()` or change it dynamically during streaming sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#permission-modes
- [definition] Available modes — The SDK supports these permission modes: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#available-modes
- [definition] Set permission mode — You can set the permission mode once when starting a query, or change it dynamically while the session is active. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#set-permission-mode
- [definition] Related resources — For the other steps in the permission evaluation flow: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#related-resources

- [parameter] Network: Restrict to specific endpoints via proxy — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#least-privilege
- [parameter] Credentials: Inject via proxy rather than exposing directly — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#least-privilege
- [parameter] System capabilities: Drop Linux capabilities in containers — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#least-privilege
- [parameter] Sandbox runtime: Isolation strength=Good (secure defaults); Performance overhead=Very low; Complexity=Low — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#isolation-technologies
- [parameter] Containers (Docker): Isolation strength=Setup dependent; Performance overhead=Low; Complexity=Medium — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#isolation-technologies
- [parameter] gVisor: Isolation strength=Excellent (with correct setup); Performance overhead=Medium/High; Complexity=Medium — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#isolation-technologies
- [parameter] VMs (Firecracker, QEMU): Isolation strength=Excellent (with correct setup); Performance overhead=High; Complexity=Medium/High — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#isolation-technologies
- [parameter] `--cap-drop ALL`: Removes Linux capabilities like `NET_ADMIN` and `SYS_ADMIN` that could enable privilege escalation — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--security-opt no-new-privileges`: Prevents processes from gaining privileges through setuid binaries — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--security-opt seccomp=...`: Restricts available syscalls; Docker's default blocks \~44, custom profiles can block more — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--read-only`: Makes the container's root filesystem immutable, preventing the agent from persisting changes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--tmpfs /tmp:...`: Provides a writable temporary directory that's cleared when the container stops — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--network none`: Removes all network interfaces; the agent communicates through the mounted Unix socket below — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--memory 2g`: Limits memory usage to prevent resource exhaustion — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--pids-limit 100`: Limits process count to prevent fork bombs — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--user 1000:1000`: Runs as a non-root user — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `-v ...:/workspace:ro`: Mounts code read-only so the agent can analyze but not modify it. **Avoid mounting sensitive host directories like `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, or `~/.config`** — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `-v .../proxy.sock:...`: Mounts a Unix socket connected to a proxy running outside the container (see below) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--userns-remap`: Maps container root to unprivileged host user; requires daemon configuration but limits damage from container escape — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] `--ipc private`: Isolates inter-process communication to prevent cross-container attacks — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [parameter] CPU-bound computation: \~0% (no syscall interception) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#gvisor
- [parameter] Simple syscalls: \~2× slower — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#gvisor
- [parameter] File I/O intensive: Up to 10-200× slower for heavy open/close patterns — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#gvisor
- [parameter] `.env`, `.env.local`: API keys, database passwords, secrets — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `~/.git-credentials`: Git passwords/tokens in plaintext — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `~/.aws/credentials`: AWS access keys — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`: Google Cloud ADC tokens — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `~/.azure/`: Azure CLI credentials — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `~/.docker/config.json`: Docker registry auth tokens — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `~/.kube/config`: Kubernetes cluster credentials — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`: Package registry tokens — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `*-service-account.json`: GCP service account keys — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [parameter] `*.pem`, `*.key`: Private keys — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [definition] Securely deploying AI agents — A guide to securing Claude Code and Agent SDK deployments with isolation, credential management, and network controls — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#securely-deploying-ai-agents
- [definition] Threat model — Agents can take unintended actions due to prompt injection (instructions embedded in content they process) or model error. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#threat-model
- [definition] Built-in security features — Claude Code includes several security features that address common concerns. See the [security documentation](/docs/en/security) for full details. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#built-in-security-features
- [definition] Security principles — For deployments that require additional hardening beyond Claude Code's defaults, these principles guide the available options. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#security-principles
- [definition] Security boundaries — A security boundary separates components with different trust levels. For high-security deployments, you can place sensitive resources (like credentials) outside the boundary containing the agent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#security-boundaries
- [definition] Least privilege — When needed, you can restrict the agent to only the capabilities required for its specific task: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#least-privilege
- [definition] Defense in depth — For high-security environments, layering multiple controls provides additional protection. Options include: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#defense-in-depth
- [definition] Isolation technologies — Different isolation technologies offer different tradeoffs between security strength, performance, and operational complexity. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#isolation-technologies
- [definition] Sandbox runtime — For lightweight isolation without containers, [sandbox-runtime](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime) enforces filesystem and network restrictions at the OS level. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#sandbox-runtime
- [definition] Containers — Containers provide isolation through Linux namespaces. Each container has its own view of the filesystem, process tree, and network stack, while sharing the host kernel. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#containers
- [definition] gVisor — Standard containers share the host kernel: when code inside a container makes a system call, it goes directly to the same kernel that runs the host. This means a kernel vulnerability could allow container escape. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#gvisor
- [definition] Virtual machines — VMs provide hardware-level isolation through CPU virtualization extensions. Each VM runs its own kernel, creating a strong boundary. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#virtual-machines
- [definition] Cloud deployments — For cloud deployments, you can combine any of the above isolation technologies with cloud-native network controls: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#cloud-deployments
- [definition] Credential management — Agents often need credentials to call APIs, access repositories, or interact with cloud services. The challenge is providing this access without exposing the credentials themselves. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#credential-management
- [definition] The proxy pattern — The recommended approach is to run a proxy outside the agent's security boundary that injects credentials into outgoing requests. The agent sends requests without credentials, the proxy adds them, and forwards the request to its destination. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#the-proxy-pattern
- [definition] Configuring Claude Code to use a proxy — Claude Code supports two methods for routing sampling requests through a proxy: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#configuring-claude-code-to-use-a-proxy
- [definition] Implementing a proxy — You can build your own proxy or use an existing one: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#implementing-a-proxy
- [definition] Credentials for other services — Beyond sampling from the Claude API, agents often need authenticated access to other services, such as git repositories, databases, and internal APIs. There are two main approaches: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#credentials-for-other-services
- [definition] Filesystem configuration — Filesystem controls determine what files the agent can read and write. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#filesystem-configuration
- [definition] Read-only code mounting — When the agent needs to analyze code but not modify it, mount the directory read-only: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#read-only-code-mounting
- [definition] Writable locations — If the agent needs to write files, you have a few options depending on whether you want changes to persist: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#writable-locations

- [parameter] `append`: Required=Yes; Called when=After each batch of transcript entries is written locally. Entries are JSON-safe objects, one per line in the local JSONL. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface
- [parameter] `load`: Required=Yes; Called when=Before the subprocess spawns when `resume` is set or `continue: true` resolves the newest store session, and once per session when listing falls back from `listSessionSummaries`. Return `null` if the session is unknown. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface
- [parameter] `listSessions`: Required=No; Called when=By `listSessions({ sessionStore })` and by `query()`/`startup()` with `continue: true`. If undefined, `continue: true` throws, and `listSessions({ sessionStore })` throws unless `listSessionSummaries` is implemented. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface
- [parameter] `listSessionSummaries`: Required=No; Called when=By `listSessions({ sessionStore })` to read metadata for all sessions in one call. Maintain the summaries inside `append`. If undefined, listing falls back to `listSessions` plus a per-session `load`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface
- [parameter] `delete`: Required=No; Called when=By `deleteSession({ sessionStore })`. Deleting the main key (no `subpath`) must cascade to all subkeys for that session and also remove the session's summary entry, so a deleted session stops appearing in `listSessionSummaries`. If undefined, deletion is a no-op, which suits append-only backends. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface
- [parameter] `listSubkeys`: Required=No; Called when=During resume, to discover subagent transcripts. If undefined, only the main transcript is restored. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface
- [parameter] [`S3SessionStore`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/tree/main/examples/session-stores/s3): Backend client=`@aws-sdk/client-s3`; Storage model=One JSONL part file per `append()`; `load()` lists, sorts, and concatenates. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#reference-implementations
- [parameter] [`RedisSessionStore`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/tree/main/examples/session-stores/redis): Backend client=`ioredis`; Storage model=`RPUSH`/`LRANGE` list per transcript, plus a sorted-set session index. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#reference-implementations
- [parameter] [`PostgresSessionStore`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/tree/main/examples/session-stores/postgres): Backend client=`pg`; Storage model=One row per entry in a `jsonb` table, ordered by `BIGSERIAL`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#reference-implementations
- [definition] Persist sessions to external storage — Mirror session transcripts to S3, Redis, or your own backend so other hosts can resume your sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#persist-sessions-to-external-storage
- [definition] The `SessionStore` interface — A `SessionStore` is an object with two required methods, `append` and `load`, and four optional methods. The SDK calls `append` to write transcript entries during a query and `load` to read them back for resume. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface
- [definition] Quick start — The SDK ships an `InMemorySessionStore` for development and testing. The example below runs a query with the store attached, captures the session ID from the result message, then resumes from the store in a second `query()` call. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#quick-start
- [definition] Write your own adapter — Implement `append` and `load` against your backend. Add `listSessions`, `listSessionSummaries`, `delete`, and `listSubkeys` if you want `listSessions()`, one-call metadata reads, `deleteSession()`, and subagent resume to work against the store. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#write-your-own-adapter
- [definition] Reference implementations — The TypeScript SDK repository includes runnable reference adapters for S3, Redis, and Postgres under [`examples/session-stores/`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/tree/main/examples/session-stores). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#reference-implementations
- [definition] Validate your adapter — Both SDKs ship a conformance suite that asserts the behavioral contract `append`, `load`, and the optional methods must satisfy. Tests for optional methods skip automatically when those methods are not implemented. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#validate-your-adapter
- [definition] Dual-write architecture — The Claude Code subprocess always writes each batch of transcript entries to local disk first, and the SDK then forwards the same batch to your store's `append()`, so the store is a mirror of the local transcript rather than a replacement for it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#dual-write-architecture
- [definition] Resume from the store — When you pass `resume`, or `continue: true` in TypeScript or `continue_conversation=True` in Python, together with a store, the SDK asks the store for a transcript before it spawns the subprocess: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#resume-from-the-store
- [definition] Mirror writes are best-effort — If `append()` rejects, the SDK retries the batch up to two more times with a short backoff, for at most three attempts in total. A call that times out isn't retried, since the original call may still land. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#mirror-writes-are-best-effort
- [definition] `getSessionMessages` returns the post-compaction chain — `getSessionMessages({ sessionStore })` returns the linked message chain the agent would see on resume. After auto-compaction, earlier turns are replaced by a summary, so a session whose store holds 503 raw entries may return 18 messages from `getSessionMessages`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#getsessionmessages-returns-the-post-compaction-chain
- [definition] `forkSession` is not a byte copy — `forkSession({ sessionStore })` reads the source entries, rewrites every `sessionId` field and remaps message UUIDs, then appends the transformed entries under a new key. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#forksession-is-not-a-byte-copy
- [definition] Subagent transcripts — Subagent transcripts are mirrored under `subpath: "subagents/agent-<id>"`. `listSubagents({ sessionStore })` requires the adapter to implement `listSubkeys`; `getSubagentMessages({ sessionStore })` uses it when available but falls back to the direct subpath when it is undefined. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#subagent-transcripts
- [definition] Retention — The SDK never deletes from your store on its own. Retention is the adapter's responsibility: implement TTLs, S3 lifecycle policies, or scheduled cleanup according to your compliance requirements. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#retention
- [definition] Supported on — The following TypeScript SDK functions accept a `sessionStore` option and operate against the store instead of the local filesystem when it is provided: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#supported-on

- [definition] TypeScript: `continue: true` — The TypeScript SDK doesn't have a session-holding client object like Python's `ClaudeSDKClient`. - [definition] Fork to explore alternatives — Forking creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history but diverges from that point. The fork gets its own session ID; the original's ID and history stay unchanged. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions#fork-to-explore-alternatives

## Scale to many tools with tool search
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search>

- [snippet] TypeScript: import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk"; — `import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [snippet] Python: import asyncio — `import asyncio` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [snippet] TypeScript: options: { — `options: {` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#optimize-tool-discovery
- [snippet] Python: options = ClaudeAgentOptions( — `options = ClaudeAgentOptions(` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#optimize-tool-discovery
- [parameter] (unset): Tool search is on. Tool definitions are deferred and discovered on demand. Falls back to loading upfront on Google Cloud's Agent Platform models earlier than the Claude 4.5 generation, a non-first-party `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, or a Microsoft Foundry deployment hosted on Azure. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [parameter] `true`: Tool search is always on, except on a Microsoft Foundry deployment hosted on Azure, where the server-side rejection still forces upfront loading, and on Google Cloud's Agent Platform models earlier than the Claude 4.5 generation, where the SDK keeps loading tool definitions upfront. The SDK sends the beta header through proxies, and requests fail on proxies that don't support… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [parameter] `auto`: Counts the tokens in the tool definitions that tool search can defer and compares the total against the model's context window. When the total reaches 10% of the window, tool search activates. Below that, the SDK loads every tool definition into context upfront. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [parameter] `auto:N`: Same as `auto` with a custom percentage. `auto:5` activates when those definitions reach 5% of the context window. Lower values activate sooner. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [parameter] `false`: Tool search is off. All tool definitions are loaded into context on every turn. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [definition] Scale to many tools with tool search — Scale your agent to thousands of tools by discovering and loading only what's needed, on demand. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#scale-to-many-tools-with-tool-search
- [definition] How tool search works — Tool search is on by default, with the exceptions listed in [Configure tool search](#configure-tool-search). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#how-tool-search-works
- [definition] Configure tool search — Tool search is on by default. For models on the SDK's unsupported-model list, the SDK loads tool definitions upfront instead, and no `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` value overrides that. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#configure-tool-search
- [definition] Optimize tool discovery — The search mechanism matches queries against tool names and descriptions. Names like `search_slack_messages` surface for a wider range of requests than `query_slack`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search#optimize-tool-discovery

- [definition] Troubleshooting — Fix Agent SDK errors by the exact message you see, with the cause and fix for each error in the TypeScript and Python SDKs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#troubleshooting
- [definition] CLINotFoundError: Claude Code not found — The Python SDK launches the Claude Code CLI as a subprocess. When it can't find a `claude` executable, connecting fails with a `CLINotFoundError`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#clinotfounderror-claude-code-not-found
- [definition] CLIConnectionError: Refusing to execute batch script — On Windows, connecting fails with a `CLIConnectionError` when the CLI path the Python SDK uses is a `.bat` or `.cmd` batch script, including the `claude.cmd` shim that an npm install creates: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#cliconnectionerror-refusing-to-execute-batch-script
- [definition] CLIConnectionError: Failed to start Claude Code — The SDK found a file at the resolved path but couldn't launch it. Python raises these failures as a `CLIConnectionError`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#cliconnectionerror-failed-to-start-claude-code
- [definition] CLIConnectionError: Not connected — Calling a `ClaudeSDKClient` method in Python before the client has connected, or after it has disconnected, raises a `CLIConnectionError` with this message: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#cliconnectionerror-not-connected
- [definition] CLI process exit — The entries in this section mean the Claude Code process ended while your application was using it. Which error you see depends on the SDK language and on whether the CLI reported an error result before it exited. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#cli-process-exit
- [definition] ProcessError: Command failed with exit code — The Python SDK raises a `ProcessError` when the Claude Code process exits with a nonzero code: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#processerror-command-failed-with-exit-code
- [definition] Claude Code process exited with code N — IDE wrappers print this message too, and the [error reference](/docs/en/errors#claude-code-process-exited-with-code-n) covers it for VS Code and other launchers. This entry covers what your TypeScript SDK code receives. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#claude-code-process-exited-with-code-n
- [definition] Claude Code returned an error result — Both SDKs replace the process-exit error with this message when the CLI reported an error result before exiting: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#claude-code-returned-an-error-result
- [definition] structured\_output is None but the result says success — A result message can end with `subtype: "success"` while `structured_output` is `None` in Python or `undefined` in TypeScript. The run completes, but no validated output exists. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#structured-output-is-none-but-the-result-says-success
- [definition] Report a new issue — If your error isn't covered here, check the open issues or file a new one in the SDK repositories: [claude-agent-sdk-typescript](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/issues) or [claude-agent-sdk-python](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/issues). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#report-a-new-issue

- [definition] `SDKInformationalMessage` — Generic text banner emitted by the loop. Carries non-error status lines, hook feedback such as a `UserPromptSubmit` hook's block reason, and command output. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkinformationalmessage
- [definition] `SDKWorkerShuttingDownMessage` — Emitted on graceful worker teardown so remote clients can show why the worker exited instead of waiting for heartbeat timeout. The `reason` is a short snake\_case string set by the host CLI, such as `"host_exit"` or `"remote_control_disabled"`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkworkershuttingdownmessage
- [definition] `SDKPluginInstallMessage` — Plugin installation progress event. Emitted when [`CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL`](/docs/en/env-vars) is set, so your Agent SDK application can track marketplace plugin installation before the first turn. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkplugininstallmessage
- [definition] `SDKPermissionDeniedMessage` — Stream event emitted when the permission system denies a tool call without an interactive prompt. Use it to render the denial in your UI as it happens, rather than only observing the `is_error` tool result that follows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkpermissiondeniedmessage
- [definition] `SDKContextUsage` — Structured form of the `/context` report, carried as `context_usage` on the [`SDKAssistantMessage`](#sdkassistantmessage) that delivers a `/context` result. Agent SDK v0.3.232 and later export the type. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkcontextusage

- [definition] `SDKMessageOrigin` — Provenance of a user-role message. This appears as `origin` on [`SDKUserMessage`](#sdkusermessage) and is forwarded onto the corresponding [`SDKResultMessage`](#sdkresultmessage) so you can tell what triggered a given turn. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkmessageorigin
