- [definition] `SDKTaskProgressMessage` — Emitted periodically while a subagent or background task is running. The `summary` field is populated only when [`agentProgressSummaries`](#options) is enabled. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdktaskprogressmessage
- [definition] `SDKTaskUpdatedMessage` — Emitted when a background task's state changes, such as when it transitions from `running` to `completed`. Merge `patch` into your local task map keyed by `task_id`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdktaskupdatedmessage
- [definition] `SDKBackgroundTasksChangedMessage` — Emitted whenever the set of live background tasks changes: a task starts, completes, is killed, a foreground agent is backgrounded, or a task's `ambient` flag changes. - [definition] `SDKThinkingTokensMessage` — Emitted while Claude is producing a thinking block, including a redacted one, carrying a running estimate of the thinking tokens generated so far. `estimated_tokens` is the running total for the current thinking block and `estimated_tokens_delta` is the increment carried by this frame. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkthinkingtokensmessage
- [definition] `SDKFilesPersistedEvent` — Emitted when file checkpoints are persisted to disk. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkfilespersistedevent
- [definition] `SDKRateLimitEvent` — Emitted when the session encounters a rate limit. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkratelimitevent
- [definition] `SDKLocalCommandOutputMessage` — Output from a local command such as `/voice` or `/usage`. Displayed as assistant-style text in the transcript. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdklocalcommandoutputmessage
- [definition] `SDKCommandsChangedMessage` — Emitted when the set of available commands changes mid-session, such as when Claude Code discovers skills as the agent enters a subdirectory. The `commands` array is the full updated list, so replace any cached command list with this payload. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkcommandschangedmessage
- [definition] `SDKPromptSuggestionMessage` — Emitted after a turn when [`promptSuggestions`](#options) is enabled and Claude Code generated a suggestion for that turn. Contains the predicted next user prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkpromptsuggestionmessage
- [definition] `SDKConversationResetMessage` — Emitted when the session's conversation is replaced without ending the session. In a `query()` call, only `/clear` and its aliases produce this message. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkconversationresetmessage
- [definition] `AbortError` — Custom error class for abort operations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#aborterror
- [definition] `SandboxSettings` — Configuration for sandbox behavior. Use this to enable command sandboxing and configure network restrictions programmatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sandboxsettings
- [definition] `SandboxNetworkConfig` — Network-specific configuration for sandbox mode. These settings apply to sandboxed Bash commands when `enabled` is `true` in the parent [`SandboxSettings`](#sandboxsettings). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sandboxnetworkconfig
- [definition] `SandboxFilesystemConfig` — Filesystem-specific configuration for sandbox mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sandboxfilesystemconfig

In TypeScript, `signal` is an `AbortSignal`; in Python, the signal field is reserved for future use. See [`ToolPermissionContext`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/python#toolpermissioncontext) for Python. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-tool-approval-requests
- [parameter] `Bash`: `command`, `description`, `timeout` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-tool-approval-requests
- [parameter] `Write`: `file_path`, `content` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-tool-approval-requests
- [parameter] `Edit`: `file_path`, `old_string`, `new_string` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-tool-approval-requests
- [parameter] `Read`: `file_path`, `offset`, `limit` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-tool-approval-requests
- [parameter] **Allow**: Python=`PermissionResultAllow(updated_input=...)`; TypeScript=`{ behavior: "allow", updatedInput }` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#respond-to-tool-requests
- [parameter] **Deny**: Python=`PermissionResultDeny(message=...)`; TypeScript=`{ behavior: "deny", message }` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#respond-to-tool-requests
- [parameter] `question` field (e.g., `"How should I format the output?"`): Key — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [parameter] Selected option's `label` field (e.g., `"Summary"`): Value — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [parameter] `question`: The full question text to display — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#question-format
- [parameter] `header`: Short label for the question (max 12 characters) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#question-format
- [parameter] `options`: Array of 2-4 choices, each with `label` and `description`. TypeScript: optionally `preview` (see [below](#option-previews-typescript)) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#question-format
- [parameter] `multiSelect`: If `true`, users can select multiple options — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#question-format
- [parameter] unset (default): Field is absent. Claude does not generate previews. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#option-previews-typescript
- [parameter] `"markdown"`: ASCII art and fenced code blocks — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#option-previews-typescript
- [parameter] `"html"`: A styled `<div>` fragment (the SDK rejects `<script>`, `<style>`, and `<!DOCTYPE>` before your callback runs) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#option-previews-typescript
- [parameter] `questions`: Pass through the original questions array (required for tool processing) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#response-format
- [parameter] `answers`: Object where keys are question text and values are selected labels — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#response-format
- [parameter] `response`: Optional freeform reply the user typed instead of answering the structured questions — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#response-format
- [definition] Handle approvals and user input — Surface Claude's approval requests and clarifying questions to users, then return their decisions to the SDK. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-approvals-and-user-input
- [definition] Detect when Claude needs input — Pass a `canUseTool` callback in your query options. The callback fires whenever Claude needs user input, receiving the tool name and input as arguments: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#detect-when-claude-needs-input
- [definition] Handle tool approval requests — Once you've passed a `canUseTool` callback in your query options, it fires when Claude wants to use a tool that nothing earlier in the permission flow has approved. Your callback receives three arguments: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-tool-approval-requests
- [definition] Respond to tool requests — Your callback returns one of two response types: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#respond-to-tool-requests
- [definition] Handle clarifying questions — When Claude needs more direction on a task with multiple valid approaches, it calls the `AskUserQuestion` tool. This triggers your `canUseTool` callback with `toolName` set to `AskUserQuestion`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [definition] Pass a canUseTool callback — Pass a `canUseTool` callback in your query options. By default, `AskUserQuestion` is available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [definition] Detect AskUserQuestion — In your callback, check if `toolName` equals `AskUserQuestion` to handle it differently from other tools: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [definition] Parse the question input — The input contains Claude's questions in a `questions` array. Each question has a `question` (the text to display), `options` (the choices), and `multiSelect` (whether multiple selections are allowed): — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [definition] Collect answers from the user — Present the questions to the user and collect their selections. How you do this depends on your application: a terminal prompt, a web form, a mobile dialog, etc. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [definition] Return answers to Claude — Build the `answers` object as a record where each key is the `question` text and each value is the selected option's `label`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-clarifying-questions
- [definition] Question format — The input contains Claude's generated questions in a `questions` array. Each question has these fields: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#question-format
- [definition] Response format — Return an `answers` object mapping each question's `question` field to the selected option's `label`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#response-format
- [definition] Complete example — Claude asks clarifying questions when it needs user input to proceed. For example, when asked to help decide on a tech stack for a mobile app, Claude might ask about cross-platform vs native, backend preferences, or target platforms. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#complete-example
- [definition] Other ways to get user input — The `canUseTool` callback and `AskUserQuestion` tool cover most approval and clarification scenarios, but the SDK offers other ways to get input from users: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#other-ways-to-get-user-input
- [definition] Streaming input — Use [streaming input](/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode) when you need to: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#streaming-input
- [definition] Custom tools — Use [custom tools](/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools) when you need to: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#custom-tools

- [parameter] Stay informed during long tasks: Configure a Stop hook to receive a desktop notification when a long-running task completes. See [Hooks](/docs/en/hooks-guide). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#quick-reference-sheet

- [definition] Champion kit — A playbook for engineers advocating Claude Code internally: what to share, how to answer questions, and how to grow adoption on your team. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#champion-kit
- [definition] The champion role — The role consists of three behaviors that reinforce one another. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#the-champion-role
- [definition] What this should cost you — Set expectations with yourself and with your lead. The activities below are intended to fit inside a normal working week, and the role should remain a multiplier on your existing work rather than an additional support responsibility. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#what-this-should-cost-you
- [definition] Share what you discover — Your own experience is the most persuasive material your colleagues will encounter, because it is specific to the codebase, workflows, and problems you all share. Documentation tells people what is possible; your posts show them what is actually working in your environment. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#share-what-you-discover
- [definition] What is worth sharing — The most useful posts describe a technique a colleague can reuse tomorrow rather than an outcome that is already complete. Techniques compound as they spread through a team; status updates do not. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#what-is-worth-sharing
- [definition] Where to share it — Post wherever your team already reads. The goal is to place examples in the path of normal work rather than to create a destination. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#where-to-share-it
- [definition] The format that works — A screenshot accompanied by a single line of context, or a brief before-and-after description, is generally the right level of detail. Keep each post short enough that someone scrolling past still absorbs the point. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#the-format-that-works
- [definition] Be the person people ask — Once you have shared a few examples, questions will follow. This is where a champion helps the most, because a good answer to one person frequently unblocks several others who are watching the same channel. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#be-the-person-people-ask
- [definition] Answer with a prompt rather than an explanation — When a colleague asks how you accomplished something, the most useful response is the prompt you actually used. They will learn more from running that prompt against their own problem than from any description you could write, and it gives them something they can act on immediately. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#answer-with-a-prompt-rather-than-an-explanation
- [definition] Point at the feature rather than the documentation — A response such as "Try plan mode, press `Shift+Tab` until you see it" is more useful in the moment than a link to the documentation. If the person needs more depth later they will find it on their own; right now they need the single thing that unblocks them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#point-at-the-feature-rather-than-the-documentation
- [definition] Grow the circle — The objective is to establish a small number of lightweight habits that allow momentum to continue after you have stopped actively driving it. You don't need to build a program or own a rollout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#grow-the-circle
- [definition] Thirty-day playbook — If a loose plan is helpful, the sequence below reflects what tends to work across most teams. Adjust freely to fit your context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#thirty-day-playbook
- [definition] Week 1: Seed the channel — Create the channel, pin the [Quickstart](/docs/en/quickstart), and post two or three of your own examples with the prompts included. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#thirty-day-playbook
- [definition] Week 2: Start the rhythm — Start the weekly show-and-tell thread, answer every question publicly, and share one custom skill or `CLAUDE.md` snippet. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#thirty-day-playbook
- [definition] Week 3: Pair and consolidate — Offer two or three short pairing sessions and consolidate the most common questions and answers into a pinned FAQ message. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#thirty-day-playbook
- [definition] Week 4: Hand off — Identify a second champion and share a brief summary of what is working and what is not with your lead or administrator. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#thirty-day-playbook
- [definition] When someone wants to go deeper — You are the warm introduction rather than the onboarding program. When a colleague moves past "should I try this" into "how do I become effective with it," point them to the [Quickstart](/docs/en/quickstart) and [Common workflows](/docs/en/common-workflows) pages. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#when-someone-wants-to-go-deeper
- [definition] Respond to common concerns — Healthy skepticism is expected; engineers should be cautious about tools that touch their code. The most effective response is rarely to argue the general case. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#respond-to-common-concerns
- [definition] Quick-reference sheet — The techniques below are the ones that most reliably move someone from a first trial to daily use. Pin this table in a channel or share it on its own. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/champion-kit#quick-reference-sheet

- [parameter] `request_id`: Five lowercase letters drawn from `a`-`z` without `l`, so it never reads as a `1` or `I` when typed on a phone. Include it in your outgoing prompt so it can be echoed in the reply. Claude Code only accepts a verdict that carries an ID it issued. The local terminal dialog doesn't display this ID, so your outbound handler is the only way to learn it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#permission-request-fields
- [parameter] `tool_name`: Name of the tool Claude wants to use, for example `Bash` or `Write`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#permission-request-fields
- [parameter] `description`: Human-readable summary of what this specific tool call does, never the command itself. For a Bash call this is Claude's description of the command; when the model gives no description, the field is the constant `Run shell command` and carries zero command detail. Render `input_preview` when you have room. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#permission-request-fields
- [parameter] `input_preview`: The tool's arguments as JSON-shaped display text, keyed per top-level field. For Bash this is the command; for Write, the file path and the content. Omit it from your prompt if you only have room for a one-line message. Your server decides what to show. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#permission-request-fields
- [definition] Channels reference — Build an MCP server that pushes webhooks, alerts, and chat messages into a Claude Code session. Reference for the channel contract: capability declaration, notification events, reply tools, sender gating, and permission relay. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#channels-reference
- [definition] Overview — A channel is an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that runs on the same machine as Claude Code. Claude Code spawns it as a subprocess and communicates over stdio. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#overview
- [definition] What you need — The only hard requirement is the [`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk) package and a Node.js-compatible runtime. [Bun](https://bun.sh), [Node](https://nodejs.org), and [Deno](https://deno.com) all work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#what-you-need
- [definition] Example: build a webhook receiver — This walkthrough builds a single-file server that listens for HTTP requests and forwards them into your Claude Code session. By the end, anything that can send an HTTP POST, like a CI pipeline, a monitoring alert, or a `curl` command, can push events to Claude. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#example-build-a-webhook-receiver
- [definition] Create the project — The permission relay examples later on this page import `zod` directly, so it installs alongside the MCP SDK. Create a new directory and install both: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#example-build-a-webhook-receiver
- [definition] Write the channel server — Create a file called `webhook.ts`. This is your entire channel server: it connects to Claude Code over stdio, and it listens for HTTP POSTs on port 8788. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#example-build-a-webhook-receiver
- [definition] Register your server with Claude Code — Add the server to your MCP config so Claude Code knows how to start it. For a project-level `.mcp.json` in the same directory, use a relative path. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#example-build-a-webhook-receiver
- [definition] Test it — During the research preview, custom channels aren't on the allowlist, so start Claude Code with the development flag: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#example-build-a-webhook-receiver
- [definition] Test during the research preview — During the research preview, every channel must be on the [approved allowlist](/docs/en/channels#research-preview) to register. The development flag bypasses the allowlist for specific entries after a confirmation prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#test-during-the-research-preview
- [definition] Server options — A channel sets these options in the [`Server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/server-concepts) constructor. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#server-options
- [definition] Notification format — Your server emits `notifications/claude/channel` with two params: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#notification-format
- [definition] Expose a reply tool — If your channel is two-way, like a chat bridge rather than an alert forwarder, expose a standard [MCP tool](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools) that Claude can call to send messages back. Nothing about the tool registration is channel-specific. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#expose-a-reply-tool
- [definition] Enable tool discovery — In your `Server` constructor in `webhook.ts`, add `tools: {}` to the capabilities so Claude Code knows your server offers tools: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#expose-a-reply-tool
- [definition] Register the reply tool — Add the following to `webhook.ts`. The `import` goes at the top of the file with your other imports; the two handlers go between the `Server` constructor and `mcp.connect()`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#expose-a-reply-tool
- [definition] Update the instructions — Update the `instructions` string in your `Server` constructor so Claude knows to route replies back through the tool. This example tells Claude to pass `chat_id` from the inbound tag: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#expose-a-reply-tool
- [definition] Gate inbound messages — An ungated channel is a prompt injection vector. Anyone who can reach your endpoint can put text in front of Claude. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#gate-inbound-messages
- [definition] Relay permission prompts — When Claude calls a tool that needs approval, the local terminal dialog opens and the session waits. A two-way channel can opt in to receive the same prompt in parallel and relay it to you on another device. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#relay-permission-prompts
- [definition] How relay works — When a permission prompt opens, the relay loop has four steps: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#how-relay-works
- [definition] Permission request fields — The outbound notification from Claude Code is `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request`. Like the [channel notification](#notification-format), the transport is standard MCP but the method and schema are Claude Code extensions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#permission-request-fields
- [definition] Add relay to a chat bridge — Adding permission relay to a two-way channel takes three components: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#add-relay-to-a-chat-bridge
- [definition] Declare the permission capability — In your `Server` constructor, add `claude/channel/permission: {}` alongside `claude/channel` under `experimental`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#add-relay-to-a-chat-bridge
- [definition] Handle the incoming request — Register a notification handler between your `Server` constructor and `mcp.connect()`. Claude Code calls it with the [four request fields](#permission-request-fields) when a permission dialog opens. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#add-relay-to-a-chat-bridge
- [definition] Intercept the verdict in your inbound handler — Your inbound handler is the loop or callback that receives messages from your platform: the same place you [gate on sender](#gate-inbound-messages) and emit `notifications/claude/channel` to forward chat to Claude. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#add-relay-to-a-chat-bridge
- [definition] Full example — The assembled `webhook.ts` below combines all three extensions from this page: the reply tool, sender gating, and permission relay. If you're starting here, you'll also need the [project setup and `.mcp.json` entry](#example-build-a-webhook-receiver) from the initial walkthrough. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#full-example
- [definition] Package as a plugin — To make your channel installable and shareable, wrap it in a [plugin](/docs/en/plugins) and publish it to a [marketplace](/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces). Users install it with `/plugin install`, then enable it per session with `--channels plugin:<name>@<marketplace>`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference#package-as-a-plugin

## Checkpointing
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing>

- [snippet] Bash command changes not tracked: rm file.txt — `rm file.txt` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#bash-command-changes-not-tracked
- [definition] Checkpointing — Track, rewind, and summarize Claude's edits and conversation to manage session state. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#checkpointing
- [definition] How checkpoints work — As you work with Claude, checkpointing automatically captures the state of your code before each user prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#how-checkpoints-work
- [definition] Automatic tracking — Claude Code tracks all changes made by its file editing tools: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#automatic-tracking
- [definition] Rewind and summarize — Run `/rewind`, or press `Esc` twice when the prompt input is empty, to open the rewind menu. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#rewind-and-summarize
- [definition] Common use cases — Checkpoints are particularly useful when: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#common-use-cases
- [definition] Bash command changes not tracked — Checkpointing does not track files modified by bash commands. For example, if Claude Code runs: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#bash-command-changes-not-tracked
- [definition] Subagent edits not restored — A [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) makes edits with Claude's file editing tools, but Claude Code usually doesn't capture those edits in your session's checkpoints. Whether rewinding restores them depends on how the subagent runs: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#subagent-edits-not-restored
- [definition] External changes not tracked — Checkpointing only tracks files that have been edited within the current session. Manual changes you make to files outside of Claude Code and edits from other concurrent sessions are normally not captured, unless they happen to modify the same files as the current session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#external-changes-not-tracked
- [definition] Symlinked and hard-linked paths not restored — Checkpointing doesn't rewind symlinked or hard-linked files. When you pick **Restore code** or **Restore code and conversation** from the `/rewind` menu, Claude Code skips any tracked path that is a symlink or hard link and shows a `Restored the code, but skipped N files` warning. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#symlinked-and-hard-linked-paths-not-restored
- [definition] Not a replacement for version control — Checkpoints are designed for quick, session-level recovery. For permanent version history and collaboration, continue using version control, such as Git, for commits, branches, and long-term history. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing#not-a-replacement-for-version-control

- [definition] GitHub proxy — In Anthropic-hosted environments, all GitHub operations go through a dedicated proxy that keeps your real GitHub credentials outside the session's VM, independent of the environment's [access level](#access-levels). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#github-proxy
- [definition] Security proxy — Cloud sessions in Anthropic-hosted environments run behind an HTTP/HTTPS network proxy for security and abuse prevention purposes; in a [self-hosted environment](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-deploy#default-deny-egress), outbound traffic leaves through your own network boundary instead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#security-proxy
- [definition] What's available in cloud sessions — In Anthropic-hosted environments, each session gets a fresh virtual machine (VM) running Ubuntu 24.04 on x86\_64, regardless of your own operating system and CPU architecture, with your repository cloned and common toolchains pre-installed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#whats-available-in-cloud-sessions
- [definition] What carries over from your setup — Cloud sessions start from a fresh clone of your repository. Anything you commit to the repo is available. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#what-carries-over-from-your-setup
- [definition] Installed tools — Cloud sessions come with common language runtimes, build tools, and databases pre-installed. The table below summarizes what's included by category. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#installed-tools
- [definition] Work with GitHub issues and pull requests — Cloud sessions include built-in GitHub tools that let Claude read issues, list pull requests, fetch diffs, and post comments without any setup. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#work-with-github-issues-and-pull-requests
- [definition] Link output back to the session — Each cloud session has a transcript URL on claude.ai, and the session can read its own ID from the `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` environment variable. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#link-output-back-to-the-session
- [definition] Run tests, start services, and add packages — You don't get a shell into the session VM. Claude runs every command for you, so phrase the tasks in this section as requests in your prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#run-tests-start-services-and-add-packages
- [definition] Resource limits — Cloud sessions in Anthropic-hosted environments run with approximate resource ceilings that may change over time: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#resource-limits
- [definition] Setup scripts — A setup script is a Bash script that runs when a new cloud session starts, before Claude Code launches. Use setup scripts to install dependencies, configure tools, or fetch anything the session needs that isn't pre-installed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#setup-scripts
- [definition] Script requirements — A setup script has three constraints to write around: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#script-requirements
- [definition] Environment caching — The setup script runs the first time you start a session in an environment. After it completes, Anthropic snapshots the filesystem and reuses that snapshot as the starting point for later sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#environment-caching
- [definition] Setup scripts vs. SessionStart hooks — Use a setup script to provision the VM itself: toolchains and CLI tools that aren't [pre-installed](#installed-tools). Use a [SessionStart hook](/docs/en/hooks#sessionstart) for project setup that should run everywhere, cloud and local, like `npm install`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#setup-scripts-vs-sessionstart-hooks
- [definition] Install dependencies with a SessionStart hook — To install dependencies only in cloud sessions, pair a SessionStart hook with a script that checks where it's running. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#install-dependencies-with-a-sessionstart-hook
- [definition] Default allowed domains — With **Trusted** network access, sessions can reach the following domains by default. Domains marked with `*` indicate wildcard subdomain matching, so `*.gcr.io` allows any subdomain of `gcr.io`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#default-allowed-domains

- [definition] Set environment variables — A variable you set in your shell lasts for that terminal session, while a variable in a settings file applies every time `claude` runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars#set-environment-variables
- [definition] In your shell — Set the variable before launching `claude`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars#in-your-shell
- [definition] In settings files — Add variables under the `env` key in a `settings.json` file, creating the file if it doesn't exist. Claude Code reads them directly from the file, so they take effect no matter how `claude` was launched. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars#in-settings-files
- [definition] Precedence — Some behaviors have both an environment variable and a dedicated settings key, and which one Claude Code reads first differs per key. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars#precedence
- [definition] Variables — Numeric variables such as timeouts, token budgets, and retry counts accept scientific notation and digit-separator spellings in addition to plain digits, except where a variable's row notes it takes plain digits only. For example, Claude Code reads `2e3` as 2000 and `64_000` as 64000. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars#variables
- [definition] Features that need feature-flag fetching — Claude Code turns some features on through feature flags it fetches from Anthropic. Claude Code skips that fetch in these sessions: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching
- [definition] First session after an install or upgrade — In your first session after you install Claude Code, or upgrade to a version that adds a feature, a [flag-gated feature](#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching) can be missing, and a session can start in Manual mode on a plan that otherwise starts in auto mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars#first-session-after-an-install-or-upgrade

- [definition] What changes — Fullscreen rendering changes how the CLI draws to your terminal. The input box stays fixed at the bottom of the screen instead of moving as output streams in. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen#what-changes
- [definition] Use the mouse — Fullscreen rendering captures mouse events and handles them inside Claude Code: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen#use-the-mouse

- [definition] Auto-follow — Scrolling up pauses auto-follow so new output doesn't pull you back to the bottom. - [definition] Mouse wheel scrolling — Mouse wheel scrolling requires your terminal to forward mouse events to Claude Code. Most terminals do this whenever an application requests it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen#mouse-wheel-scrolling

- [definition] Keep native text selection — Mouse capture is the most common friction point, especially over SSH or inside tmux. When Claude Code captures mouse events, your terminal's native copy-on-select stops working. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen#keep-native-text-selection
- [definition] Stale or misplaced text on screen — Fullscreen rendering sends only the cells that changed between frames. - [definition] `Claude Code's fullscreen renderer didn't finish starting last time` appears at startup — If a fullscreen session on this machine crashes before it has started successfully, Claude Code starts your next session in the classic renderer and prints one of two lines. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen#claude-codes-fullscreen-renderer-didnt-finish-starting-last-time-appears-at-startup
- [definition] Research preview — Fullscreen rendering is a research preview feature. It has been tested on common terminal emulators, but you may encounter rendering issues on less common terminals or unusual configurations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen#research-preview

## Glossary
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary>

- [parameter] Headless mode: Now called=[Non-interactive mode](#non-interactive-mode); Notes=Same `-p` flag, same behavior — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#deprecated-and-renamed-terms
- [parameter] Custom commands: Now called=[Skills](#skill); Notes=`.claude/commands/` files still work — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#deprecated-and-renamed-terms
- [parameter] Slash commands: Now called=Commands; Notes="Slash" dropped from product copy — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#deprecated-and-renamed-terms
- [definition] Glossary — Definitions for Claude Code terminology. Learn what agentic loop, compaction, CLAUDE.md, hooks, subagents, MCP, and other core concepts mean. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#glossary
- [definition] Agent teams — Multiple independent Claude Code sessions coordinated by a team lead, with a shared task list and peer-to-peer messaging. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#agent-teams
- [definition] Agentic coding — A workflow where the AI can read files, run commands, and make changes autonomously while you watch, redirect, or step away, as opposed to chat-based assistants that only respond with text you must apply yourself. Claude Code is agentic because it has [tools](#tool) that let it act, not just advise. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#agentic-coding
- [definition] Agentic harness — The tools, context management, and execution environment that turn a language model into a capable coding agent. Claude Code is the harness; Claude is the model inside it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#agentic-harness
- [definition] Agentic loop — The cycle Claude works through for every task: gather context, take action, verify results, and repeat until done. Each tool use returns information that informs the next step. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#agentic-loop
- [definition] Artifact — A live, interactive web page Claude Code publishes from your session to a private URL on claude.ai, so you can see output visually or share it instead of reading terminal text. The page updates in place when the session republishes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#artifact
- [definition] Auto memory — Notes Claude writes for itself based on your corrections and preferences, stored per git repository under `~/.claude/projects/`. All worktrees of the same repository share one auto memory directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#auto-memory
- [definition] Auto mode — A [permission mode](#permission-mode) where a separate classifier model reviews actions instead of you, so Claude Code runs most of them without asking you. Claude Code still asks you before actions your explicit ask rules match. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#auto-mode
- [definition] Bare mode — With `--bare`, Claude Code starts without loading hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, or CLAUDE.md, apart from skills in a directory you pass with `--add-dir`. Recommended for CI and scripted calls where you need the same result on every machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#bare-mode
- [definition] Bundled skills — Prompt-based playbooks included with Claude Code, such as `/batch`, `/code-review`, `/debug`, and `/loop`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#bundled-skills
- [definition] Channel — An [MCP server](#mcp-model-context-protocol) that pushes events into your running session so Claude can react to things that happen while you're away from the terminal. Channels can be two-way: Claude reads an inbound event and replies back through the same channel. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#channel
- [definition] Checkpoint — A restore point created at each prompt you send. Claude Code snapshots files before every edit so a checkpoint can revert them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#checkpoint
- [definition] `.claude` directory — The directory where Claude Code reads project-scoped configuration: settings, hooks, skills, subagents, rules, and auto memory. A project has `.claude/` at its root; your user-level defaults are at `~/.claude/`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#claude-directory
- [definition] CLAUDE.md — A markdown file of persistent instructions you write for Claude, loaded at the start of every session as a user message after the system prompt. Put project conventions, architecture notes, and "always do X" rules here. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#claudemd
- [definition] Command — A reusable instruction you invoke by typing `/name` in the prompt. Built-in commands such as `/clear`, `/model`, and `/compact` control the session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#command
- [definition] Compaction — Automatic summarization of your conversation when the [context window](#context-window) approaches its limit. Older tool outputs are cleared first, then the conversation is summarized. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#compaction
- [definition] Connector — An [MCP server](#mcp-server) added to your claude.ai account rather than configured in Claude Code. When you sign in to Claude Code with that account, your connectors appear in `/mcp` alongside the servers you added locally. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#connector
- [definition] Context window — The working memory for a session, holding conversation history, file contents, command outputs, CLAUDE.md, auto memory, loaded skills, and system instructions. As you work, context fills up until [compaction](#compaction) summarizes it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#context-window
- [definition] Dispatch — A phone-initiated task router that spawns a Claude Code session in the Desktop app when you send a coding task from the Claude mobile app. Your prompt routes to the right tool automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#dispatch
- [definition] Effort level — A setting that controls how much of the adaptive-reasoning thinking budget Claude uses on each turn. Higher effort means more thinking tokens and deeper reasoning; lower effort is faster and cheaper. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#effort-level
- [definition] Extended thinking — Visible step-by-step reasoning the model performs before responding. You can adjust it with the [effort level](#effort-level), or cap thinking tokens with `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` on models with a fixed thinking budget. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#extended-thinking
- [definition] Hook — A user-defined handler that executes automatically at a specific point in Claude Code's lifecycle, such as before a tool runs, after a file edit, or at session start. Handlers can be a shell command, HTTP endpoint, MCP tool, LLM prompt, or subagent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#hook
- [definition] Managed settings — Settings enforced org-wide by IT or DevOps, delivered from Anthropic's servers through the admin console or deployed to devices at an OS-level path outside `~/.claude`. User and project settings cannot override managed settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#managed-settings
- [definition] MCP (Model Context Protocol) — An open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources and services. MCP servers give Claude new tools for Slack, Jira, databases, browsers, and hundreds of other integrations. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#mcp-model-context-protocol
- [definition] MCP server — A program that gives Claude tools, prompts, or resources over [MCP](#mcp-model-context-protocol). You add servers with `claude mcp add`, in `.mcp.json`, through a [plugin](#plugin), or as a claude.ai [connector](#connector). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#mcp-server
- [definition] MCP Tool Search — A context-saving mechanism that defers MCP tool schemas until needed. Only tool names and server instructions load at startup; Claude fetches the full schema on demand when it decides to use a specific tool. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#mcp-tool-search
- [definition] Non-interactive mode — A mode that executes a single prompt and exits without an interactive prompt, invoked with `-p` or `--print`. Used for CI, scripts, and piping. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#non-interactive-mode
- [definition] Output style — A configuration that modifies Claude's system prompt to change response behavior, tone, or format. Unlike [CLAUDE.md](#claude-md), which Claude Code delivers as a user message after the system prompt, an output style changes the system prompt itself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#output-style
- [definition] Permission mode — The baseline approval behavior for the session. Cycle with `Shift+Tab` in the CLI or use the mode selector in VS Code, Desktop, and claude.ai. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#permission-mode
- [definition] Permission rule — A settings entry that allows, asks about, or denies a tool invocation based on the tool name and argument pattern. Rules are evaluated deny→ask→allow, first match wins. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#permission-rule
- [definition] Plan mode — A [permission mode](#permission-mode) where Claude researches and proposes changes without editing your source files. It can read, search, and run exploration commands, then presents a plan for approval before touching anything. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#plan-mode
- [definition] Plugin — A bundle of skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers packaged as a single installable unit. Plugin skills are namespaced as `plugin-name:skill-name` so multiple plugins coexist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#plugin
- [definition] Project trust — A dialog accepting a directory before Claude Code loads its configuration. Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#project-trust
- [definition] Prompt injection — Hostile instructions embedded in a file, web page, or tool result that attempt to redirect Claude toward actions you never asked for. Claude Code's defenses include the permission system, command injection detection, and trust verification. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#prompt-injection
- [definition] Remote Control — A way to continue a local Claude Code session from your phone or browser via claude.ai. Your code execution and files stay on your machine; the interface is remote. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#remote-control
- [definition] Rules — Modular instruction files in `.claude/rules/` that load alongside CLAUDE.md. A rule can be path-scoped with YAML `paths:` frontmatter so it only loads when Claude reads a matching file, keeping context lean until it's relevant. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#rules
- [definition] Sandboxing — OS-level filesystem and network isolation for the Bash tool. Commands run inside a boundary you define upfront, so Claude can work freely within it without per-command approval prompts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#sandboxing
- [definition] Session — A conversation tied to your current directory, with its own independent [context window](#context-window). Sessions can be resumed with `claude -c`, forked with `--fork-session` to preserve history under a new session ID, or run in parallel across terminals. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#session
- [definition] Settings layers — The hierarchy Claude Code reads configuration from, in precedence order from highest to lowest: [managed policy](#managed-settings), command-line arguments, local settings at `.claude/settings.local.json`, project settings at `.claude/settings.json`, then user settings at `~/.claude/settings.json`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#settings-layers
- [definition] Skill — A `SKILL.md` file containing instructions, knowledge, or a workflow that Claude adds to its toolkit. Claude loads a skill automatically when relevant, or you invoke it directly with `/skill-name`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#skill
- [definition] Subagent — A specialized AI assistant that runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions. It works on a delegated task and returns a summary to the main conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#subagent
- [definition] Surface — Any place you access Claude Code: the CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, Desktop, or claude.ai. All surfaces share the same engine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#surface
- [definition] Teleport — A command, `/teleport`, that pulls a cloud Claude Code session into your local terminal. Claude fetches the branch, loads the conversation history, and resumes from the web session's last state. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#teleport
- [definition] Tool — An action Claude can take: read a file, edit code, run a shell command, search the web, spawn a subagent. Tools are what make Claude Code agentic. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#tool
- [definition] Turn — One complete response from Claude within a [session](#session). A turn begins when you send a message and ends when Claude finishes responding, with any number of [tool](#tool) calls in between. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#turn
- [definition] Verification loop — How a session knows the work is actually done rather than just plausible. You give Claude a check it can run, such as a test suite, a build, or a screenshot comparison, and Claude iterates until the check passes instead of stopping after one attempt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#verification-loop
- [definition] Worktree isolation — An isolation mode that runs Claude in a separate git worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`, enabled with the `-w` flag or `isolation: worktree` in subagent config. Changes stay on a separate branch in a separate directory, so parallel agents don't overwrite each other's files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#worktree-isolation
- [definition] Deprecated and renamed terms — These terms appear in older docs, blog posts, and community content. Use the current name when searching this site. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#deprecated-and-renamed-terms

- [parameter] `PermissionRequest`: When a tool call needs a permission decision — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PermissionDenied`: When auto mode denies a tool call, including denials without a classifier verdict. Use JSON `hookSpecificOutput.retry: true` to tell the model it may retry the denied tool call. Claude Code ignores `retry` when the classifier produced no verdict — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PostToolUse`: After a tool call succeeds — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PostToolUseFailure`: After a tool call fails — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PostToolBatch`: After a full batch of parallel tool calls resolves, before the next model call — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `Notification`: When Claude Code sends a notification — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `MessageDisplay`: While assistant message text is displayed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `SubagentStart`: When a subagent is spawned — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `SubagentStop`: When a subagent finishes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `TaskCreated`: When a task is being created via `TaskCreate` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `TaskCompleted`: When a task is being marked as completed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `Stop`: When Claude finishes responding — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `StopFailure`: When the turn ends due to an API error — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `TeammateIdle`: When an [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate is about to go idle — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `InstructionsLoaded`: When a CLAUDE.md or `.claude/rules/*.md` file is loaded into context. Fires at session start and when files are lazily loaded during a session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `ConfigChange`: When a configuration file changes during a session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `CwdChanged`: When the working directory changes, for example when Claude executes a `cd` command. Useful for reactive environment management with tools like direnv — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `DirectoryAdded`: When a working directory is added mid-session via `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `FileChanged`: When a watched file changes on disk. The `matcher` field specifies which filenames to watch — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `WorktreeCreate`: When a worktree is being created via `--worktree`, `isolation: "worktree"`, or for a background session. Replaces default git behavior — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `WorktreeRemove`: When a worktree is being removed at session exit, when a subagent finishes, or when you delete a background session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PreCompact`: Before context compaction — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PostCompact`: After context compaction completes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PreModelSwitch`: Before Claude Code applies a model switch that you or a client requested. Can block the switch — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `PostModelSwitch`: After the session's model changes, including changes Claude Code makes on its own, such as restoring the model when you resume a session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `Elicitation`: When an MCP server requests user input during a tool call — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `ElicitationResult`: After a user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `SessionEnd`: When a session terminates — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [parameter] `~/.claude/settings.json`: Scope=All your projects; Shareable=No, local to your machine — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-locations
- [parameter] `.claude/settings.json`: Scope=Single project; Shareable=Yes, can be committed to the repo — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-locations
- [parameter] `.claude/settings.local.json`: Scope=Single project; Shareable=No, gitignored when Claude Code saves a setting to it — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-locations

- [parameter] Only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,`, and `\|`: Evaluated as=Exact string, or list of exact strings separated by `\|` or `,` with optional surrounding whitespace; Example=`Bash` matches only the Bash tool; `Edit\|Write` and `Edit, Write` each match either tool exactly; `code-reviewer` matches only that agent type — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#matcher-patterns
- [parameter] Contains any other character: Evaluated as=JavaScript regular expression, unanchored; Example=`^Notebook` matches any tool whose name starts with `Notebook`; `mcp__memory__.*` matches every tool from the `memory` server — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#matcher-patterns

- [parameter] `StopFailure`: What the matcher filters=error type; Example matcher values=`rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `unknown` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#matcher-patterns

- [parameter] `Elicitation`: Can block?=Yes; What happens on exit 2=Denies the elicitation — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event
- [parameter] `ElicitationResult`: Can block?=Yes; What happens on exit 2=Blocks the response (action becomes decline) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event
- [parameter] `WorktreeCreate`: Can block?=Yes; What happens on exit 2=Any non-zero exit code causes worktree creation to fail — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event
- [parameter] `WorktreeRemove`: Can block?=No; What happens on exit 2=Failures are logged in debug mode only — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event
- [parameter] `InstructionsLoaded`: Can block?=No; What happens on exit 2=Exit code is ignored — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event
- [parameter] `MessageDisplay`: Can block?=No; What happens on exit 2=The original text is displayed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event
- [parameter] `continue`: Default=`true`; Description=If `false`, Claude stops processing entirely after the hook runs. Takes precedence over any event-specific decision fields — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#json-output
- [parameter] `stopReason`: Default=none; Description=Message shown to the user when `continue` is `false`. Not shown to Claude — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#json-output
- [parameter] `suppressOutput`: Default=`false`; Description=Has no effect: Claude Code accepts the field but doesn't act on it. A successful hook's stdout is never shown in the transcript and is recorded in the debug log — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#json-output
- [parameter] `systemMessage`: Default=none; Description=Warning message shown to the user. In [Agent SDK](/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) and [`--output-format stream-json`](/docs/en/headless) output, it can arrive as an [`SDKInformationalMessage`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkinformationalmessage) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#json-output
- [parameter] `terminalSequence`: Default=none; Description=A terminal escape sequence for Claude Code to emit on your behalf, such as a desktop notification, window title, or bell. Restricted to OSC `0`/`1`/`2`/`9`/`99`/`777` and BEL. If the value contains anything outside the allowlist, the field is ignored. Use this instead of writing to `/dev/tty`, which is unavailable to hooks — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#json-output
- [parameter] UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Stop, SubagentStop, ConfigChange, PreCompact: Decision pattern=Top-level `decision`; Key fields=`decision: "block"`, `reason`. Stop and SubagentStop also accept `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` for [non-error feedback that continues the conversation](#stop-decision-control) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] TeammateIdle, TaskCompleted: Decision pattern=Exit code or `continue: false`; Key fields=Exit code 2 blocks the action with stderr feedback. - [parameter] TaskCreated: Decision pattern=Exit code or top-level `decision`; Key fields=Exit code 2 or `decision: "block"` [cancels the task](#taskcreated-decision-control) and returns the message to Claude. `continue: false` is ignored — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] PreToolUse: Decision pattern=`hookSpecificOutput`; Key fields=`permissionDecision` (allow/deny/ask/defer), `permissionDecisionReason` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] PreModelSwitch: Decision pattern=`hookSpecificOutput` or top-level `decision`; Key fields=`permissionDecision` (allow/deny/ask), `permissionDecisionReason`. `decision: "block"` also [cancels the switch](#premodelswitch-decision-control) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] PermissionRequest: Decision pattern=`hookSpecificOutput`; Key fields=`decision.behavior` (allow/deny) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] PermissionDenied: Decision pattern=`hookSpecificOutput`; Key fields=`retry: true` tells the model it may retry the denied tool call; Claude Code ignores it for [no-verdict denials](#permissiondenied-decision-control) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] WorktreeCreate: Decision pattern=path return; Key fields=Command hook prints path on stdout; HTTP hook returns `hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath`. Hook failure or missing path fails creation — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] Elicitation: Decision pattern=`hookSpecificOutput`; Key fields=`action` (accept/decline/cancel), `content` (form field values for accept) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] ElicitationResult: Decision pattern=`hookSpecificOutput`; Key fields=`action` (accept/decline/cancel), `content` (form field values override) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] MessageDisplay: Decision pattern=`hookSpecificOutput`; Key fields=`displayContent` replaces the displayed text on screen. Display-only: the transcript and what Claude sees keep the original — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] SessionStart, SubagentStart, PostModelSwitch: Decision pattern=Context only; Key fields=`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` adds context for Claude. No blocking or decision control — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
- [parameter] Setup, WorktreeRemove, Notification, SessionEnd, PostCompact, InstructionsLoaded, StopFailure, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged: Decision pattern=None; Key fields=No decision control. Used for side effects like logging or cleanup — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#decision-control
