- [definition] Hooks reference — Reference for Claude Code hook events, configuration schema, JSON input/output formats, exit codes, async hooks, HTTP hooks, prompt hooks, and MCP tool hooks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hooks-reference
- [definition] Hook lifecycle — Claude Code runs hooks at specific points during a session. When an event fires and a matcher matches, Claude Code passes JSON context about the event to your hook handler. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle
- [definition] How a hook resolves — To see how the event, the matcher, and the handler fit together, consider this `PreToolUse` hook that blocks destructive shell commands. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-a-hook-resolves
- [definition] Event fires — The `PreToolUse` event fires. Claude Code sends the tool input as JSON on stdin to the hook: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-a-hook-resolves
- [definition] Matcher checks — The matcher `"Bash"` matches the tool name, so this hook group activates. If you omit the matcher or use `"*"`, the group activates on every occurrence of the event. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-a-hook-resolves
- [definition] If condition checks — The `if` condition `"Bash(rm *)"` matches because `rm -rf /tmp/build` is a subcommand matching `rm *`, so this handler spawns. If the command had been `npm test`, the `if` check would fail and `block-rm.sh` would never run, avoiding the process spawn overhead. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-a-hook-resolves
- [definition] Hook handler runs — The script inspects the full command and finds `rm -rf`, so it prints a decision to stdout: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-a-hook-resolves
- [definition] Claude Code acts on the result — Claude Code reads the JSON decision, blocks the tool call, and shows Claude the reason. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-a-hook-resolves
- [definition] Configuration — Hooks are defined in JSON settings files. The configuration has three levels of nesting: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#configuration
- [definition] Hook locations — Where you define a hook determines its scope: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-locations
- [definition] Matcher patterns — The `matcher` field filters when hooks fire. How a matcher is evaluated depends on the characters it contains: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#matcher-patterns
- [definition] Hook handler fields — Each object in the inner `hooks` array is a hook handler: the shell command, HTTP endpoint, MCP tool, LLM prompt, or agent that runs when the matcher matches. There are five types: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-handler-fields
- [definition] Reference scripts by path — Use these placeholders to reference hook scripts relative to the project or plugin root, regardless of the working directory when the hook runs: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#reference-scripts-by-path
- [definition] Hooks in skills and agents — In addition to settings files and plugins, hooks can be defined directly in [skills](/docs/en/skills) and [subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents) using frontmatter, in the same configuration format as settings-based hooks. How long Claude Code keeps them registered depends on the component: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hooks-in-skills-and-agents
- [definition] The `/hooks` menu — Type `/hooks` in Claude Code to open a read-only browser for your configured hooks. The menu shows every hook event with a count of configured hooks, lets you drill into matchers, and shows the full details of each hook handler. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#the-hooks-menu
- [definition] Disable or remove hooks — To remove a hook, delete its entry from the settings JSON file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#disable-or-remove-hooks
- [definition] Hook input and output — Command hooks receive JSON data via stdin and communicate results through exit codes, stdout, and stderr. HTTP hooks receive the same JSON as the POST request body and communicate results through the HTTP response body. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-input-and-output
- [definition] Common input fields — Hook events receive these fields as JSON, in addition to event-specific fields documented in each [hook event](#hook-events) section. For command hooks, this JSON arrives via stdin. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#common-input-fields
- [definition] Exit code output — The exit code from your hook command tells Claude Code whether the action should proceed, be blocked, or be ignored. The exit code doesn't act alone. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-output
- [definition] HTTP response handling — HTTP hooks use HTTP status codes and response bodies instead of exit codes and stdout. The outcomes below apply to most events; an event with its own failure contract in the [per-event table](#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event), such as `WorktreeCreate`, applies that contract to a failed HTTP hook too: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#http-response-handling
- [definition] JSON output — Exit codes only let you block or stay silent, but JSON output gives you finer-grained control. Instead of exiting with code 2 to block, exit 0 and print a JSON object to stdout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#json-output
- [definition] Hook events — Each event corresponds to a point in Claude Code's lifecycle where hooks can run. The sections below are ordered to match the lifecycle: from session setup through the agentic loop to session end. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-events
- [definition] SessionStart — Runs when Claude Code starts a new session or resumes an existing session. Useful for loading development context like existing issues or recent changes to your codebase, or setting up environment variables. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#sessionstart
- [definition] Setup — Fires only when you launch Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with the `-p` flag. It doesn't fire on normal startup. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#setup
- [definition] InstructionsLoaded — Fires when a `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/rules/*.md` file is loaded into context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#instructionsloaded
- [definition] UserPromptSubmit — Runs when the user submits a prompt, before Claude processes it. This allows you to add additional context based on the prompt/conversation, validate prompts, or block certain types of prompts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#userpromptsubmit
- [definition] UserPromptExpansion — Runs when a user-typed command expands into a prompt before reaching Claude. Use this to block specific commands from direct invocation, inject context for a particular skill, or log which commands users invoke. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#userpromptexpansion
- [definition] MessageDisplay — Runs while an assistant message streams to the screen. Claude Code displays the message in increments: each time a batch of newly completed lines is ready to render, the hook runs once with those lines and Claude Code renders the hook's replacement text in their place. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#messagedisplay
- [definition] PreToolUse — Runs after Claude creates tool parameters and before processing the tool call. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#pretooluse
- [definition] PermissionRequest — Runs when Claude Code is about to ask you for permission to use a tool. In sessions that can't show a prompt, such as background subagents in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless), Claude Code still runs these hooks, and if no hook returns a decision, it denies the tool call. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#permissionrequest
- [definition] PostToolUse — Runs immediately after a tool completes successfully. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#posttooluse
- [definition] PostToolUseFailure — Runs when a tool that started executing fails: the tool threw an error, or an MCP tool returned an error result. Use this to log failures, send alerts, or provide corrective feedback to Claude. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#posttoolusefailure
- [definition] PostToolBatch — Runs once after every tool call in a batch has resolved, before Claude Code sends the next request to the model. `PostToolUse` fires once per tool, which means it fires concurrently when Claude makes parallel tool calls. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#posttoolbatch
- [definition] PermissionDenied — Runs when [auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) denies a tool call, including when it denies without a classifier verdict because [a safety check separate from auto mode refused the classifier's own… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#permissiondenied
- [definition] Notification — Runs when Claude Code sends notifications. Matches on notification type. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#notification
- [definition] SubagentStart — Runs when a Claude Code subagent is spawned via the Agent tool. Supports matchers to filter by agent type name. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart
- [definition] SubagentStop — Runs when a Claude Code subagent has finished responding. Matches on agent type, same values as SubagentStart. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstop
- [definition] TaskCreated — Runs when a task is being created via the `TaskCreate` tool. Use this to enforce naming conventions, require task descriptions, or prevent certain tasks from being created. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#taskcreated
- [definition] TaskCompleted — Runs when a task is being marked as completed. This fires in two situations: when any agent explicitly marks a task as completed through the TaskUpdate tool, or when an [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate finishes its turn with in-progress tasks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#taskcompleted
- [definition] Stop — Runs when the main Claude Code agent has finished responding. Does not run if the stoppage occurred due to a user interrupt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#stop
- [definition] StopFailure — Runs instead of [Stop](#stop) when the turn ends due to an API error. Claude Code ignores the hook's output and exit code, apart from [`terminalSequence`](#emit-terminal-notifications). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#stopfailure
- [definition] TeammateIdle — Runs when an [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate is about to go idle after finishing its turn. Use this to enforce quality gates before a teammate stops working, such as requiring passing lint checks or verifying that output files exist. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#teammateidle
- [definition] ConfigChange — Runs when a configuration file changes during a session. Use this to audit settings changes, enforce security policies, or block unauthorized modifications to configuration files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#configchange
- [definition] CwdChanged — Runs when the working directory changes during a session, for example when Claude executes a `cd` command. Use this to react to directory changes: reload environment variables, activate project-specific toolchains, or run setup scripts automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#cwdchanged
- [definition] DirectoryAdded — Runs after you add a working directory mid-session with the `/add-dir` command, or after an SDK client adds one with the `register_repo_root` control request. Use this to prepare a newly added repository, for example by installing its dependencies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#directoryadded
- [definition] FileChanged — Runs when a watched file changes on disk. Claude Code detects changes with a filesystem watcher, not by inspecting tool calls, so it runs the hook no matter what changed the file: an `Edit` or `Write` tool call, a script Claude runs with `Bash`, or a process outside Claude Code entirely. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#filechanged
- [definition] WorktreeCreate — Runs when a worktree is being created, whether from `claude --worktree`, from a [subagent using `isolation: "worktree"`](/docs/en/sub-agents#choose-the-subagent-scope), or for a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated) that Claude Code isolates in its own worktree. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#worktreecreate
- [definition] WorktreeRemove — Runs when a worktree is being removed. This is the cleanup counterpart to [WorktreeCreate](#worktreecreate). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#worktreeremove
- [definition] PreCompact — Runs before Claude Code is about to run a compact operation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#precompact
- [definition] PostCompact — Runs after Claude Code completes a compact operation. Use this event to react to the new compacted state, for example to log the generated summary or update external state. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#postcompact
- [definition] PreModelSwitch — Runs before Claude Code applies a model switch that you or a client requested. Use it to block a switch, require confirmation, or show what the switch will cost before it happens. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#premodelswitch
- [definition] PostModelSwitch — Runs after the session's model changes. Use it to give Claude model-specific guidance without editing every CLAUDE.md, for example an organization-wide instruction that applies on certain models. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#postmodelswitch
- [definition] SessionEnd — Runs when a Claude Code session ends. Useful for cleanup tasks, logging session statistics, or saving session state. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#sessionend
- [definition] Elicitation — Runs when an MCP server requests user input mid-task. By default, Claude Code shows an interactive dialog for the user to respond. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#elicitation
- [definition] ElicitationResult — Runs after a user responds to an MCP elicitation. Hooks can observe, modify, or block the response before it is sent back to the MCP server. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#elicitationresult
- [definition] Prompt-based hooks — In addition to command, HTTP, and MCP tool hooks, Claude Code supports prompt-based hooks (`type: "prompt"`) that use an LLM to evaluate whether to allow or block an action, and agent hooks (`type: "agent"`) that spawn an agentic verifier with tool access. Not all events support every hook type. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#prompt-based-hooks
- [definition] How prompt-based hooks work — Instead of executing a Bash command, prompt-based hooks: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-prompt-based-hooks-work
- [definition] Prompt hook configuration — Set `type` to `"prompt"` and provide a `prompt` string instead of a `command`. Use the `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder to inject the hook's JSON input data into your prompt text. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#prompt-hook-configuration
- [definition] Response schema — The LLM must respond with JSON containing: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#response-schema
- [definition] Check multiple conditions before stopping — This `Stop` hook uses a detailed prompt to check three conditions before allowing Claude to stop. `SubagentStop` hooks use the same format to evaluate whether a [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) should stop. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#check-multiple-conditions-before-stopping
- [definition] Agent-based hooks — Agent hooks are experimental. Behavior and configuration may change in future releases. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#agent-based-hooks
- [definition] Agent hook configuration — Set `type` to `"agent"` and provide a `prompt` string. The configuration fields are the same as [prompt hooks](#prompt-hook-configuration), except that agent hooks have a longer default timeout and no `continueOnBlock` field: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#agent-hook-configuration
- [definition] Run hooks in the background — By default, hooks block Claude's execution until they complete. For long-running tasks like deployments, test suites, or external API calls, set `"async": true` to run the hook in the background while Claude continues working. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#run-hooks-in-the-background
- [definition] Configure an async hook — Add `"async": true` to a command hook's configuration to run it in the background without blocking Claude. This field is only available on `type: "command"` hooks. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#configure-an-async-hook
- [definition] How async hooks execute — When an async hook fires, Claude Code starts the hook process and immediately continues without waiting for it to finish. The hook receives the same JSON input via stdin as a synchronous hook. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#how-async-hooks-execute
- [definition] Run tests after file changes — This hook starts a test suite in the background whenever Claude writes a file, then reports the results back to Claude when the tests finish. Save this script to `.claude/hooks/run-tests-async.sh` in your project and make it executable with `chmod +x`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#run-tests-after-file-changes
- [definition] Limitations — Async hooks have additional constraints compared to synchronous hooks: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#limitations
- [definition] Disclaimer — Command hooks execute shell commands with your full user permissions. They can modify, delete, or access any files your user account can access. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#disclaimer
- [definition] Workspace trust — Claude Code checks workspace trust before it runs any hook from a settings file. What counts as trusted depends on the session type: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#workspace-trust
- [definition] Security best practices — Keep these practices in mind when writing hooks: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#security-best-practices
- [definition] Windows PowerShell tool — On Windows, you can run individual hooks in PowerShell by setting `"shell": "powershell"` on a command hook. Claude Code auto-detects `pwsh.exe`, the PowerShell 7 and later executable, and falls back to `powershell.exe` for Windows PowerShell 5.1. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#windows-powershell-tool
- [definition] Debug hooks — Hook execution details, including which hooks matched, their exit codes, and full stdout and stderr, are written to the debug log file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#debug-hooks

- [definition] Interactive mode — Complete reference for keyboard shortcuts, input modes, and interactive features in Claude Code sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#interactive-mode
- [definition] Keyboard shortcuts — Keyboard shortcuts may vary by platform and terminal. In [fullscreen rendering](/docs/en/fullscreen), press `?` in the transcript viewer to see available shortcuts there. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#keyboard-shortcuts
- [definition] Make editing keys follow readline conventions — Set [`keybindingFlavor`](/docs/en/settings-reference#keybindingflavor) to `"readline"` to make the prompt's editing keys follow GNU readline conventions, as in Bash. The default value is `"classic"`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#make-editing-keys-follow-readline-conventions
- [definition] Transcript viewer — When the transcript viewer is open (toggled with `Ctrl+O`), these shortcuts are available. Run `/tui` with no argument to check which renderer is active. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#transcript-viewer
- [definition] Commands — Type `/` in Claude Code to see the commands available to you, or type `/` followed by any letters to filter. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#commands
- [definition] Vim editor mode — Enable vim-style editing via `/config` → Editor mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#vim-editor-mode
- [definition] Remap INSERT-mode key sequences — The [`vimInsertModeRemaps`](/docs/en/settings-reference#viminsertmoderemaps) setting maps a two-key INSERT-mode sequence to Escape, so a mapping like `jj` returns you to NORMAL mode. Requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#remap-insert-mode-key-sequences
- [definition] Text objects (NORMAL mode) — Text objects work with operators like `d`, `c`, and `y`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#text-objects-normal-mode
- [definition] Visual mode — Press `v` for character-wise selection or `V` for line-wise selection. Motions extend the selection, and operators act on it directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#visual-mode
- [definition] Command history — Claude Code keeps a history of the prompts you type, and Up-arrow recall reaches prompts from past sessions of the same project: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#command-history
- [definition] Reverse search with Ctrl+R — Press `Ctrl+R` to interactively search through your command history. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#reverse-search-with-ctrlr
- [definition] Background Bash commands — Claude Code supports running Bash commands in the background, allowing you to continue working while long-running processes execute. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#background-bash-commands
- [definition] How backgrounding works — When Claude Code runs a command in the background, it runs the command asynchronously and immediately returns a background task ID. Claude Code can respond to new prompts while the command continues executing in the background. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#how-backgrounding-works
- [definition] Shell mode with `!` prefix — Run shell commands directly without going through Claude by prefixing your input with `!`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#shell-mode-with-prefix
- [definition] Queue messages while Claude works — Type a message and press `Enter` while Claude is working. Claude Code queues the message instead of interrupting the turn, and lists the queued entries above the input box until it sends them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#queue-messages-while-claude-works
- [definition] When Claude Code sends what you queued — When a queued entry reaches Claude depends on what you queued. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#when-claude-code-sends-what-you-queued
- [definition] Take back what you queued — Press `Up` from the first line of the input box to take back the queued messages and commands. Claude Code removes them from the queue and puts them in the input box, one per line, ahead of any text you had typed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#take-back-what-you-queued
- [definition] Prompt suggestions — When you first open a session, Claude Code shows a grayed-out example command in the prompt input to help you get started. It picks this from your project's git history, so the example reflects files you've been working on recently. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#prompt-suggestions
- [definition] When Claude Code skips suggestions — In interactive mode, Claude Code leaves prompt suggestions off by default and hides the **Prompt suggestions** toggle in `/config` in a [session that doesn't fetch feature flags](/docs/en/env-vars#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching), such as one on a third-party provider or through a Claude… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#when-claude-code-skips-suggestions
- [definition] Turn prompt suggestions off — To disable prompt suggestions entirely, use any of the following: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#turn-prompt-suggestions-off
- [definition] Emoji shortcodes — Type a `:` followed by an emoji shortcode in the prompt input to insert the emoji. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#emoji-shortcodes
- [definition] Check spelling as you type — Claude Code can underline misspelled words in the prompt input while you type. It checks only the text in the input box, never Claude's replies or your files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#check-spelling-as-you-type
- [definition] Turn spell checking on or off — Claude Code reads the [`spellcheck`](/docs/en/settings-reference#spellcheck) setting from three places, and ignores it in a project's `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`. Turn it on from whichever one you use: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#turn-spell-checking-on-or-off
- [definition] What Claude Code underlines — Shortly after you pause typing, Claude Code underlines the words the dictionary doesn't know. It leaves the word you're still typing alone until you move past it, and it never changes your text. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#what-claude-code-underlines
- [definition] When Claude Code underlines nothing — Claude Code underlines nothing when it can't keep a checker running: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#when-claude-code-underlines-nothing
- [definition] Side questions with /btw — Use `/btw` to ask a question about your current work without adding to the conversation history. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#side-questions-with-btw
- [definition] Task list — The task list is Claude's to-do checklist: items Claude created to plan multi-step work, with indicators showing what's pending, in progress, or complete. It's separate from the background-task view. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#task-list
- [definition] Session recap — When you return to the terminal after stepping away, Claude Code shows a one-line recap of what happened in the session so far. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#session-recap
- [definition] Wait for a usage limit to reset — When a claude.ai [usage limit](/docs/en/errors#youve-hit-your-session-limit) stops Claude mid-task, Claude Code waits in the open session and continues the task on its own after the limit resets. Automatic continue is on by default in interactive sessions signed in with a claude.ai subscription. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#wait-for-a-usage-limit-to-reset
- [definition] Cancel the wait — Press `Esc` at an empty prompt, or `Ctrl+C`, while the line shows, or run [`/rate-limit-options`](/docs/en/commands#all-commands) and pick **Don't continue automatically**. Claude Code confirms with a line that starts `Automatic continue cancelled`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#cancel-the-wait
- [definition] Start a wait yourself — Claude Code doesn't start the wait on its own in these cases: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#start-a-wait-yourself
- [definition] Turn automatic continue off — In `/config`, turn off **Continue automatically at usage limit**, or set [`autoContinueAtUsageLimit`](/docs/en/settings-reference#autocontinueatusagelimit) to `false` in your user settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#turn-automatic-continue-off
- [definition] PR review status — When working on a branch with an open pull request, Claude Code displays a clickable PR link in the footer, such as "PR #446". The link has a colored underline indicating the review state: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#pr-review-status
- [definition] GitLab merge requests — When you work on a branch with an open GitLab merge request, Claude Code shows a clickable `MR !N` badge in the footer slot that otherwise holds the GitHub PR link. `!N` is GitLab's own reference syntax for merge request number N. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#gitlab-merge-requests

- [definition] Can customers offer Claude Code in their products? — Unless we've mutually agreed otherwise, preinstalling or running Claude Code in your products or services (e.g. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#can-customers-offer-claude-code-in-their-products
- [definition] Healthcare compliance (BAA) — If a customer has executed a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with Anthropic and has [Zero Data Retention (ZDR)](/docs/en/zero-data-retention) enabled for the relevant organization, that BAA extends to the customer's API traffic through Claude Code. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#healthcare-compliance-baa
- [definition] Acceptable use — Claude Code usage is subject to the [Anthropic Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup). Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#acceptable-use
- [definition] Authentication and credential use — Claude Code authenticates with Anthropic's servers using OAuth tokens or API keys. These authentication methods serve different purposes: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#authentication-and-credential-use
- [definition] Trust and safety — You can find more information in the [Anthropic Trust Center](https://trust.anthropic.com) and [Transparency Hub](https://www.anthropic.com/transparency). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#trust-and-safety
- [definition] Security vulnerability reporting — Anthropic manages our security program through HackerOne. [Use this form to report vulnerabilities](https://hackerone.com/4f1f16ba-10d3-4d09-9ecc-c721aad90f24/embedded_submissions/new). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#security-vulnerability-reporting

- [definition] Switch permission modes — Each interface has its own control for switching permission modes during a session and its own way of choosing the permission mode new sessions start in. - [definition] Auto-approve file edits with acceptEdits mode — `acceptEdits` mode lets Claude create and edit files in your working directory without prompting. The status bar shows `⏵⏵ accept edits on` while this mode is active. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#auto-approve-file-edits-with-acceptedits-mode
- [definition] Analyze before you edit with plan mode — Plan mode tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them. Claude reads files, runs shell commands to explore, and writes a plan, but does not edit your source. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#analyze-before-you-edit-with-plan-mode
- [definition] Review and approve a plan — When the plan is ready, Claude presents it and asks how to proceed. From that prompt you can choose: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#review-and-approve-a-plan
- [definition] Set plan mode as the default — To make plan mode the default for a project's terminal sessions, set `defaultMode` to `plan` in `.claude/settings.json`, placed as the example under [Start in a different permission mode](#start-in-a-different-mode) shows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#set-plan-mode-as-the-default
- [definition] Eliminate permission prompts with auto mode — Auto mode lets Claude execute without routine permission prompts. A separate classifier model reviews actions before they run, blocking anything that escalates beyond your request, targets unrecognized infrastructure, or appears driven by hostile content Claude read. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-permission-prompts-with-auto-mode
- [definition] Auto mode on Bedrock, Agent Platform, or Foundry — On [Amazon Bedrock](/docs/en/amazon-bedrock), [Google Cloud's Agent Platform](/docs/en/google-vertex-ai), [Microsoft Foundry](/docs/en/microsoft-foundry), and signed-in [Claude apps gateway](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) sessions, auto mode appears in the `Shift+Tab` cycle by default. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#auto-mode-on-bedrock-agent-platform-or-foundry
- [definition] What the classifier blocks by default — The classifier trusts your working directory and the remotes that were configured for it when the session started. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#what-the-classifier-blocks-by-default
- [definition] Boundaries you state in conversation — The classifier treats boundaries you state in the conversation as a block signal. If you tell Claude "don't push" or "wait until I review before deploying", the classifier blocks matching actions even when the default rules would allow them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#boundaries-you-state-in-conversation
- [definition] When auto mode falls back — When auto mode can't approve your session's actions, what happens depends on the case: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#when-auto-mode-falls-back
- [definition] Allow only pre-approved tools with dontAsk mode — If you set `dontAsk` mode, Claude Code auto-denies every tool call that would otherwise prompt you. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#allow-only-pre-approved-tools-with-dontask-mode
- [definition] Skip all checks with bypassPermissions mode — `bypassPermissions` mode disables permission prompts and safety checks so tool calls execute immediately, including writes to [protected paths](#protected-paths). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode
- [definition] Protected paths — Writes to a small set of paths are never auto-approved, except in `bypassPermissions` mode and in planning sessions with [bypass permissions](#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) available. This prevents accidental corruption of repository state and Claude's own configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#protected-paths
- [definition] Critical paths — Claude Code never lets a [`permissions.allow`](/docs/en/permissions#manage-permissions) rule or a [`PreToolUse` hook](/docs/en/permissions#extend-permissions-with-hooks) that returns `"allow"` approve an `rm` or `rmdir` command that targets a critical path, even in modes that skip other prompts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#critical-paths
- [definition] Remove-Item in PowerShell — When you enable the [PowerShell tool](/docs/en/tools-reference#powershell-tool), Claude Code gives `Remove-Item` its own check, separate from the `rm` critical-path list. The outcome depends on the target, and the first matching case applies: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#remove-item-in-powershell

Doesn't change which hosts sandboxed commands can reach.; In `deny`=Claude Code removes the `WebFetch` tool, so Claude can't fetch at all. - [parameter] `WebFetch(domain:*)`: In `allow`=Claude fetches without prompting you, and sandboxed commands can reach any host.; In `deny`=Claude Code keeps the tool and refuses each fetch, and sandboxed commands can't reach any host. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#allow-or-deny-every-fetch
- [parameter] `Cd(~/code/*)`: Matches=`~/code/app`; Does not match=`~/code/app/src`, `~/code` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#cd
- [parameter] `Cd(~/code/**)`: Matches=`~/code` and any directory under it; Does not match=directories outside `~/code` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#cd
- [parameter] `Cd(**/node_modules)`: Matches=any `node_modules` directory at any depth; Does not match=`node_modules/pkg` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#cd

- [parameter] [Command files](/docs/en/skills#where-skills-live) in `.claude/commands/`: Yes, without live reload. - [parameter] Servers in `.mcp.json`, including ones the repository [approves in its own settings](/docs/en/mcp#project-server-approvals-and-workspace-trust): You trusted only a parent folder=Claude Code asks you before connecting them. - [definition] Configure permissions — Control what Claude Code can access and do with fine-grained permission rules, modes, and managed policies. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#configure-permissions
- [definition] Permission system — Claude Code uses a tiered permission system to balance power and safety. The table shows, for each tool type, whether Manual mode asks before the action runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#permission-system
- [definition] Add a comment when you answer a permission prompt — You can attach a note to Claude when you approve or deny a single action. On most permission prompts, including Bash, PowerShell, file, and MCP tool prompts, move to **Yes** or **No** and press `Tab` to open a comment field on that option. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#add-a-comment-when-you-answer-a-permission-prompt
- [definition] Manage permissions — You can view and manage Claude Code's tool permissions with `/permissions`. The dialog lists all permission rules and the `settings.json` file each rule comes from. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#manage-permissions
- [definition] Permission modes — Claude Code supports several permission modes that control how it approves tool calls. See [Permission modes](/docs/en/permission-modes) for when to use each one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#permission-modes
- [definition] Permission rule syntax — Permission rules follow the format `Tool` or `Tool(specifier)`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#permission-rule-syntax
- [definition] Match all uses of a tool — To match all uses of a tool, use only the tool name without parentheses: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#match-all-uses-of-a-tool
- [definition] Use specifiers for fine-grained control — Add a specifier in parentheses to match specific tool uses: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#use-specifiers-for-fine-grained-control
- [definition] Match by input parameter — Deny and ask rules can match a top-level input parameter on any built-in tool with `Tool(param:value)`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#match-by-input-parameter
- [definition] Wildcard patterns — A `*` in a Bash rule matches any text, including spaces, so one rule covers a family of commands. A rule with no `*` matches one exact command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#wildcard-patterns
- [definition] Tool name wildcards — Deny and ask rules also accept glob patterns in the tool-name position. The pattern must match the full tool name: `"*"` matches every tool, and `"mcp__*"` matches every MCP tool across all servers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#tool-name-wildcards
- [definition] Bash — Bash rules match the whole command text, with `*` standing in for any text. [Wildcard patterns](#wildcard-patterns) shows which commands each rule shape matches and where to put the `*`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#bash
- [definition] PowerShell — PowerShell permission rules use the same shape as Bash rules. Wildcards with `*` match at any position, the `:*` suffix is equivalent to a trailing ` *`, and a bare `PowerShell` or `PowerShell(*)` matches every command. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#powershell
- [definition] Read and Edit — To block Claude's file tools from reading a file or directory, add a `Read` deny rule for its path, such as `Read(./.env)` or `Read(./secrets/**)`; [Exclude sensitive files](/docs/en/settings-reference#exclude-sensitive-files) has a paste-ready example. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#read-and-edit
- [definition] WebFetch — WebFetch rules use a `domain:` prefix and match against the hostname of the requested URL. Matching is case-insensitive, supports `*` wildcards, and strips a trailing `.` from both the rule and the hostname so `example.com.` and `example.com` are treated the same. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#webfetch
- [definition] MCP — MCP rules use the server name as configured in Claude Code, optionally followed by the name of a tool from that server. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#mcp
- [definition] Agent (subagents) — Use `Agent(AgentName)` rules to control which [subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents) Claude can use: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#agent-subagents
- [definition] Cd — `Cd` rules control which directories the [`/cd` command](/docs/en/commands) can move the session to. `Cd` is not a model-invocable tool: Claude can't call it, and the rules apply only when you run `/cd` yourself. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#cd
- [definition] Extend permissions with hooks — [Claude Code hooks](/docs/en/hooks-guide) let you register custom shell commands that evaluate permissions at runtime. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#extend-permissions-with-hooks
- [definition] Working directories — By default, Claude has access to files in the directory where you launched it. That directory is the session's primary working directory until you [move the session with `/cd`](#move-the-session-to-another-directory). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#working-directories
- [definition] Move the session to another directory — To move the session to a different primary working directory, rather than [adding a directory](#working-directories) alongside the current one, run `/cd <path>`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#move-the-session-to-another-directory
- [definition] Additional directories grant file access, not configuration — Adding a directory extends where Claude can read and edit files. It doesn't make that directory a full configuration root: most `.claude/` configuration is not discovered from additional directories, though a few types are loaded as exceptions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#additional-directories-grant-file-access-not-configuration
- [definition] How permissions interact with sandboxing — Permissions and [sandboxing](/docs/en/sandboxing) are complementary security layers: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#how-permissions-interact-with-sandboxing
- [definition] Managed settings — For organizations that need centralized control, administrators deploy managed settings that user and project settings can't override, apart from a few [security-sensitive keys](/docs/en/settings#exceptions-to-managed-settings-precedence). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#managed-settings
- [definition] Settings precedence — Permission rules follow the same [settings precedence](/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence) as all other Claude Code settings, with managed settings highest: no other level, including command line arguments, can override a managed permission rule. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#settings-precedence
- [definition] Project allow rules and workspace trust — `permissions.allow` rules and `permissions.additionalDirectories` entries in a project's `.claude/settings.json` grant capability, so Claude Code applies them only after you accept the [workspace trust dialog](/docs/en/security#additional-safeguards) for that folder. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#project-allow-rules-and-workspace-trust
- [definition] When your local settings file needs trust — `.claude/settings.local.json` is normally your own file, so Claude Code applies its allow rules and additional directories without the trust step. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#when-your-local-settings-file-needs-trust
- [definition] What runs before you trust a folder — Each row is one kind of content a repository can supply. The columns are the two situations in which you haven't trusted the folder itself: you trusted only a parent folder, or you ran `claude -p` or the SDK there, which never shows the trust dialog. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#what-runs-before-you-trust-a-folder
- [definition] Example configurations — This [repository](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/examples/settings) includes starter settings configurations for common deployment scenarios. Use these as starting points and adjust them to fit your needs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#example-configurations

- [parameter] `SessionStart`: When a session begins or resumes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks

- [parameter] `PostToolUseFailure`: After a tool call fails — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks

- [parameter] `MessageDisplay`: While assistant message text is displayed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `SubagentStart`: When a subagent is spawned — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `SubagentStop`: When a subagent finishes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `TaskCreated`: When a task is being created via `TaskCreate` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `TaskCompleted`: When a task is being marked as completed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `Stop`: When Claude finishes responding — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `StopFailure`: When the turn ends due to an API error — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `TeammateIdle`: When an [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate is about to go idle — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `InstructionsLoaded`: When a CLAUDE.md or `.claude/rules/*.md` file is loaded into context. Fires at session start and when files are lazily loaded during a session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `ConfigChange`: When a configuration file changes during a session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `CwdChanged`: When the working directory changes, for example when Claude executes a `cd` command. Useful for reactive environment management with tools like direnv — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `DirectoryAdded`: When a working directory is added mid-session via `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `FileChanged`: When a watched file changes on disk. The `matcher` field specifies which filenames to watch — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `WorktreeCreate`: When a worktree is being created via `--worktree`, `isolation: "worktree"`, or for a background session. Replaces default git behavior — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `WorktreeRemove`: When a worktree is being removed at session exit, when a subagent finishes, or when you delete a background session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `PreCompact`: Before context compaction — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `PostCompact`: After context compaction completes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `PreModelSwitch`: Before Claude Code applies a model switch that you or a client requested. Can block the switch — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `PostModelSwitch`: After the session's model changes, including changes Claude Code makes on its own, such as restoring the model when you resume a session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `Elicitation`: When an MCP server requests user input during a tool call — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `ElicitationResult`: After a user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `SessionEnd`: When a session terminates — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [parameter] `command`: The LSP binary to execute (must be in PATH) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `extensionToLanguage`: Maps file extensions to language identifiers — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `args`: Command-line arguments for the LSP server — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `transport`: Communication transport: `stdio` (default) or `socket`. Claude Code accepts `socket` but runs every server over stdio, so the stdout protocol rules apply to all servers — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `env`: Environment variables to set when starting the server — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `initializationOptions`: Options passed to the server during initialization — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `settings`: Settings passed via `workspace/didChangeConfiguration` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `workspaceFolder`: Workspace folder path for the server — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `startupTimeout`: Max time to wait for server startup (milliseconds) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `shutdownTimeout`: Max time to wait for graceful shutdown (milliseconds). When the timeout elapses, Claude Code terminates the server process. When unset, no timeout applies — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `restartOnCrash`: Whether to restart the server after it crashes. Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to leave a crashed server stopped instead of restarting it — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `maxRestarts`: Maximum number of restart attempts before giving up — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `diagnostics`: Whether to push diagnostics into Claude's context after edits (default `true`). Set to `false` to keep code navigation but suppress automatic diagnostic injection. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `pyright-lsp`: Language server=Pyright (Python); Install command=`pip install pyright` or `npm install -g pyright` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `typescript-lsp`: Language server=TypeScript Language Server; Install command=`npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `rust-analyzer-lsp`: Language server=rust-analyzer; Install command=[See rust-analyzer installation](https://rust-analyzer.github.io/manual.html#installation) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [parameter] `name`: Identifier unique within the plugin. Prevents duplicate processes when the plugin reloads or a skill is invoked again — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#monitors
- [parameter] `command`: Shell command run as a persistent background process in the session working directory — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#monitors

- [parameter] **Explicit version**: How=Set `"version": "2.1.0"` in `plugin.json`; Update behavior=Users get updates only when you bump this field. - [parameter] **Commit-SHA version**: How=Omit `version` from both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry; Update behavior=Users get updates whenever the source's resolved commit changes; Best for=Internal or team plugins under active development — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#version-management
- [parameter] **Digest version**: How=Use an [`archive` source](/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#zip-archives) and omit `version` from both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry; Update behavior=With a `sha256` pin, users get updates when you change the pin. Without one, users get updates whenever the hosted zip file's bytes change; Best for=Plugins published as zip files to a static server or artifact repository — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#version-management

- [definition] Skills — Plugins add skills to Claude Code, creating `/name` shortcuts that you or Claude can invoke. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#skills
- [definition] Agents — Plugins can provide specialized subagents for specific tasks that Claude can invoke automatically when appropriate. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#agents
- [definition] Hooks — Plugins can provide event handlers that respond to Claude Code events automatically. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#hooks
- [definition] MCP servers — Plugins can bundle Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to connect Claude Code with external tools and services. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#mcp-servers
- [definition] LSP servers — Looking to use LSP plugins? Install them from the official marketplace: search for "lsp" in the `/plugin` Discover tab. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers
- [definition] Monitors — Plugins can declare background monitors that Claude Code starts automatically when the plugin is active. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#monitors
- [definition] Themes — Plugins can ship color themes that appear in `/theme` alongside the built-in presets and the user's local themes. A theme is a JSON file in `themes/` with a `base` preset and a sparse `overrides` map of color tokens. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#themes
- [definition] Plugin installation scopes — When you install a plugin, you choose a **scope** that determines where the plugin is available and who else can use it: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-installation-scopes
- [definition] Skills-directory plugins — Any folder under a skills directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest is loaded as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` on the next session, with no marketplace and no install step. Scaffold one with [`plugin init`](#plugin-init). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#skills-directory-plugins
- [definition] Edit, reload, and disable a skills-directory plugin — Changes you make to a skill's `SKILL.md` take effect immediately in the current session. Changes to the plugin's other components, such as `hooks/`, `.mcp.json`, `agents/`, and `output-styles/`, do not. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#edit-reload-and-disable-a-skills-directory-plugin
- [definition] Plugins synced from claude.ai — In [Cowork](https://claude.com/product/cowork) and [cloud sessions](/docs/en/cloud-environments#what-carries-over-from-your-setup), Claude Code downloads the plugins enabled for your claude.ai account into `~/.claude/plugins/synced/` in the session's own environment and loads each one as… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugins-synced-from-claudeai
- [definition] Plugin manifest schema — The `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` file defines your plugin's metadata and configuration. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-manifest-schema
- [definition] Required fields — If you include a manifest, `name` is the only required field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#required-fields
- [definition] Unrecognized fields — Claude Code ignores top-level fields it does not recognize. You can keep metadata from another ecosystem in `plugin.json` and the plugin still loads. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#unrecognized-fields
- [definition] Default enablement — Set `defaultEnabled: false` in `plugin.json` to ship a plugin that installs disabled. The user turns it on with `claude plugin enable <plugin>` or the `/plugin` interface. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#default-enablement
- [definition] Experimental components — Components under the `experimental` key, `themes` and `monitors`, have a manifest schema that may change between releases while they stabilize. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#experimental-components
- [definition] User configuration — The `userConfig` field declares values that Claude Code prompts the user for when the plugin is enabled. Use this instead of requiring users to hand-edit `settings.json`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#user-configuration
- [definition] Channels — The `channels` field lets a plugin declare one or more message channels that inject content into the conversation. Each channel binds to an MCP server that the plugin provides. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#channels
- [definition] Path behavior rules — Whether a custom path replaces or extends the plugin's default directory depends on the field: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#path-behavior-rules
- [definition] Environment variables — Claude Code provides three variables for referencing paths: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#environment-variables
- [definition] Plugin caching and file resolution — Plugins are specified in one of two ways: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-caching-and-file-resolution
- [definition] Node.js package dependencies — When Claude Code copies a plugin into the cache, it also installs the plugin's Node.js package dependencies there, so the plugin's hooks and MCP servers can load them. This section covers the npm and Bun packages a plugin declares in its own `package.json`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#nodejs-package-dependencies
- [definition] Path traversal limitations — Claude Code doesn't let a plugin reference files outside its own directory. It rejects a component path that resolves outside the plugin root, such as `../shared-utils`, whether the path is declared in `plugin.json` or in a [marketplace entry](/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#plugin-entries). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#path-traversal-limitations
- [definition] Share files within a marketplace with symlinks — If your plugin needs to share files with other parts of the same marketplace, you can create symbolic links inside your plugin directory. How a symlink is handled when the plugin is copied into the cache depends on where its target resolves: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#share-files-within-a-marketplace-with-symlinks
- [definition] Standard plugin layout — A complete plugin follows this structure: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#standard-plugin-layout
- [definition] CLI commands reference — Claude Code provides CLI commands for non-interactive plugin management, useful for scripting and automation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#cli-commands-reference
- [definition] plugin init — Scaffold a new plugin at `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`. On the next Claude Code session it loads automatically as `<name>@skills-dir` and appears in `/plugin` and `claude plugin list` with no install step. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-init
- [definition] plugin install — Install a plugin from available marketplaces. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-install
- [definition] plugin prune — Remove auto-installed plugin dependencies that are no longer required by any installed plugin. Dependencies that Claude Code pulled in to satisfy another plugin's [`dependencies`](/docs/en/plugin-dependencies) field are removed; plugins you installed directly are never touched. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-prune
- [definition] plugin enable — Enable a disabled plugin. When the target is installed from a marketplace and declares [dependencies](/docs/en/plugin-dependencies), Claude Code enables them transitively at the same scope. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-enable
- [definition] plugin disable — Disable a plugin without uninstalling it. When the target is installed from a marketplace, the command fails if another enabled plugin [depends on](/docs/en/plugin-dependencies#enable-or-disable-a-plugin-with-dependencies) it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-disable
- [definition] plugin list — List installed plugins with their version, source marketplace, and enable status. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-list
- [definition] plugin details — Show a plugin's component inventory and projected token cost. The output lists all components the plugin contributes, grouped as Skills, Agents, Hooks, MCP servers, and LSP servers, along with an estimate of how many tokens it adds to each session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-details
- [definition] plugin tag — Create a release git tag for a plugin. By default the command tags the plugin in the current directory; pass a path to tag a plugin elsewhere. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-tag
- [definition] Debugging commands — Use `claude --debug` to see plugin loading details: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#debugging-commands
- [definition] Version management — Claude Code uses the plugin's version as the cache key that determines whether an update is available. When you run `/plugin update` or auto-update fires, Claude Code computes the current version and skips the update if it matches what's already installed. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#version-management

## Choose a sandbox environment
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments>

- [snippet] Set up and launch the runtime: mkdir -p ~/.claude && echo '{}' > ~/.claude.json — `mkdir -p ~/.claude && echo '{}' > ~/.claude.json` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#set-up-and-launch-the-runtime
- [snippet] Set up and launch the runtime: npx @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime claude — `npx @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime claude` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#set-up-and-launch-the-runtime
- [parameter] [Sandboxed Bash tool](#sandboxed-bash-tool): What is isolated=Bash commands and their child processes; Requires Docker=No; Setup effort=Minimal on macOS; low on Linux and WSL2 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#compare-sandboxing-approaches
- [parameter] [Sandbox runtime](#sandbox-runtime): What is isolated=The whole Claude Code process, including file tools, MCP servers, and hooks; Requires Docker=No; Setup effort=Low — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#compare-sandboxing-approaches
- [parameter] [Dev container](#dev-containers): What is isolated=Full development environment; Requires Docker=Yes; Setup effort=Medium — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#compare-sandboxing-approaches
- [parameter] [Custom container](#custom-container): What is isolated=Full development environment; Requires Docker=Yes; Setup effort=Medium to high — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#compare-sandboxing-approaches
- [parameter] [Virtual machine](#virtual-machine): What is isolated=Full operating system; Requires Docker=No; Setup effort=High — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#compare-sandboxing-approaches
- [parameter] [Claude Code on the web](#claude-code-on-the-web): What is isolated=Full operating system, hosted by Anthropic; Requires Docker=No; Setup effort=None; requires a Claude subscription, and GitHub when you launch from the web interface — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#compare-sandboxing-approaches
- [parameter] Reduce permission prompts during everyday work on your own machine: The [sandboxed Bash tool](/docs/en/sandboxing), configured with `/sandbox` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [parameter] Let Claude work unattended with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or auto mode: The preconfigured [dev container](/docs/en/devcontainer), any container or VM, or the [sandbox runtime](#sandbox-runtime) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [parameter] Isolate MCP servers and hooks as well as Bash, without Docker: The sandbox runtime — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [parameter] Work on an untrusted repository: A dedicated virtual machine, or [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) if you have a Claude subscription; GitHub is only required when you launch from the web interface — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [parameter] Standardize a sandboxed environment across a team: The preconfigured [dev container](/docs/en/devcontainer), copied into your repository — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [parameter] Use Claude Code from a device with no local setup: [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web), which requires a Claude subscription and a connected GitHub account — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [parameter] Require isolation for every developer in your organization: [Enforce isolation across an organization](#enforce-isolation-across-an-organization) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [parameter] Work on a native Windows host: A container or VM, or run the Bash sandbox inside WSL2 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [definition] Choose a sandbox environment — Compare Claude Code sandbox options: the built-in sandboxed Bash tool, sandbox runtime, dev containers, Docker, and VMs. Choose the right isolation for your threat model. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-a-sandbox-environment
- [definition] Compare sandboxing approaches — The first two approaches in the table below run on the host operating system without containers. The rest place Claude Code inside a container or virtual machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#compare-sandboxing-approaches
- [definition] Choose an approach — Match your goal to a row below, then read the detail section that follows. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#choose-an-approach
- [definition] How isolation relates to permission modes — [Permission modes](/docs/en/permission-modes) decide whether a tool call runs and whether you are prompted first. Isolation restricts what a command can access once it runs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#how-isolation-relates-to-permission-modes
- [definition] Sandboxed Bash tool — This option does not support native Windows. On Windows hosts, use WSL2 or one of the container or VM approaches below. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#sandboxed-bash-tool
- [definition] Sandbox runtime — The [`@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime) package wraps an entire process in the same Seatbelt or bubblewrap isolation that the built-in Bash sandbox uses. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#sandbox-runtime
- [definition] Set up and launch the runtime — On Linux and WSL2, the runtime relies on the same `bubblewrap` and `socat` packages as the built-in sandbox, plus `ripgrep`, which Claude Code bundles but the standalone runtime resolves from your PATH. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#set-up-and-launch-the-runtime
- [definition] What the runtime blocks on its own — The runtime blocks the highest-risk writes without any configuration from you: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#what-the-runtime-blocks-on-its-own
- [definition] After unattended runs — Review the paths you kept writable. On Linux and WSL2, also review anything the session created. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#after-unattended-runs
- [definition] Dev containers — A dev container runs Claude Code inside a Docker container that VS Code or a compatible editor manages, with your project mounted in. You can define your own with a `.devcontainer/` directory in your repository. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#dev-containers
- [definition] Custom container — You can run Claude Code in any Docker or OCI container image with your own network policies, mounted volumes, and seccomp profiles. This is the most common path for organizations with existing container infrastructure or CI runners. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#custom-container
- [definition] Virtual machine — A dedicated virtual machine provides the strongest separation, with its own kernel and, in cloud or microVM deployments, its own virtualized hardware. Options include cloud instances, local hypervisors, and microVMs such as Firecracker. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#virtual-machine
- [definition] Claude Code on the web — [Claude Code on the web](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) runs each session in an isolated, Anthropic-managed virtual machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#claude-code-on-the-web
- [definition] Enforce isolation across an organization — Individual developers can opt into any of the sandboxing approaches on this page. What an organization can enforce, and with which tools, depends on the approach: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#enforce-isolation-across-an-organization
- [definition] See also — These pages cover configuration and policy details for the sandboxing approaches on this page. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#see-also
