- [definition] `worktree.sparsePaths` — Check out only the listed directories in each worktree through git sparse-checkout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#worktreesparsepaths
- [definition] `worktree.bgIsolation` — Choose how [background sessions](/docs/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated) isolate their file edits. With `"worktree"`, Claude Code blocks `Edit` and `Write` in the main checkout until the session calls `EnterWorktree`; with `"none"`, background jobs edit the working copy directly. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#worktreebgisolation
- [definition] Remote, desktop, and notifications — Configure Remote Control, cloud environments, the desktop app, and the notifications Claude Code sends when it needs you. See [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#remote-desktop-and-notifications
- [definition] `agentPushNotifEnabled` — Allow Claude to send a push notification to your phone when it decides one is worth sending, for example when a long task finishes. Claude Code syncs this choice to your account, and pushes arrive while [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) is connected. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#agentpushnotifenabled
- [definition] `awaySummaryEnabled` — Show a one-line session recap when you return to the terminal after a few minutes away. Set it to `false`, or turn off **Session recap** in `/config`, to stop the recap. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#awaysummaryenabled
- [definition] `disableArtifact` — Deprecated, and replaced by [`enableArtifact`](#enableartifact). Claude Code still honors `disableArtifact: true` as equivalent to `enableArtifact: false`, and ignores `disableArtifact: false`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disableartifact
- [definition] `disableDeepLinkRegistration` — Stop Claude Code from registering the `claude-cli://` protocol handler with the operating system, which it otherwise does after you send the first prompt of an interactive session. [Deep links](/docs/en/deep-links) let external tools open a Claude Code session with a pre-filled prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disabledeeplinkregistration
- [definition] `disableDesktopLocalSessions` — Turn off Code sessions that run on the device in the [desktop app](/docs/en/desktop#local-sessions-on-managed-devices), for deployments where developers should work on remote machines over SSH. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disabledesktoplocalsessions
- [definition] `disableRemoteControl` — Turn off [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control): Claude Code then refuses `claude remote-control`, the `--remote-control` flag, auto-start, and the in-session toggle, and reports that your organization's policy disabled it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disableremotecontrol
- [definition] `enableArtifact` — Turn off the [Artifact](/docs/en/artifacts) tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. When you turn the **Artifacts** row off in `/config`, Claude Code writes this key to your user settings, so you don't usually edit it by hand. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#enableartifact
- [definition] `inputNeededNotifEnabled` — Get a push notification on your phone when a permission prompt or question is waiting for your input. Claude Code sends these only while [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) is connected. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#inputneedednotifenabled
- [definition] `preferredNotifChannel` — Choose how Claude Code notifies you when a task completes or a permission prompt is waiting. Appears in `/config` as **Local notifications**. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#preferrednotifchannel
- [definition] `remote.defaultEnvironmentId` — Pick the default [cloud environment](/docs/en/cloud-environments) for cloud sessions you create from the CLI, such as with `claude --cloud`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#remotedefaultenvironmentid
- [definition] `remoteControlAtStartup` — Connect [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) automatically when each interactive session starts, instead of waiting for `/remote-control`. Set it to `true` to turn auto-connect on, `false` to turn it off. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#remotecontrolatstartup
- [definition] `sshConfigs` — Add SSH connections to the [Desktop](/docs/en/desktop#pre-configure-ssh-connections-for-your-team) environment dropdown. Administrators use it to distribute shared connections to a team. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#sshconfigs
- [definition] `sshHostAllowlist` — Limit the hosts a [Desktop SSH session](/docs/en/desktop#restrict-which-ssh-hosts-users-can-connect-to) can connect to. Only the Desktop app reads this key; the CLI doesn't. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#sshhostallowlist
- [definition] Authentication and providers — Supply credentials through helper scripts and, for organizations, force a login method or organization. See [Authentication](/docs/en/authentication). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#authentication-and-providers
- [definition] `apiKeyHelper` — Run your own command to produce the credential Claude Code sends with model requests. Claude Code runs the command through the system shell, `/bin/sh` on macOS and Linux and `cmd` on Windows, and sends its output as both the `X-Api-Key` and `Authorization: Bearer` headers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#apikeyhelper
- [definition] `awsAuthRefresh` — Run your own command, such as `aws sso login`, to refresh the credentials in your `.aws` directory when the ones Claude Code has for [Amazon Bedrock](/docs/en/amazon-bedrock) stop working. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#awsauthrefresh
- [definition] `awsCredentialExport` — Run your own command that prints AWS credentials as JSON, so Claude Code can call [Amazon Bedrock](/docs/en/amazon-bedrock) with credentials that don't live in your `.aws` directory. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#awscredentialexport
- [definition] `forceLoginMethod` — Restrict which kind of account people can log in with. Set `"claudeai"` to allow only claude.ai accounts, `"console"` to allow only Claude Console accounts, or `"gateway"` to send people to a [cloud gateway](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) instead of a first-party login. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginmethod
- [definition] `forceLoginGatewayUrl` — Set the gateway URL the `/login` Cloud gateway screen connects to, so people reach your [cloud gateway](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) without typing its address. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forcelogingatewayurl
- [definition] `forceLoginOrgUUID` — From a managed source, require claude.ai account logins to belong to one Anthropic organization, a single UUID, or to any of several, an array. From any settings file, a single UUID also pre-selects that organization during a claude.ai or Claude Console login; an array pre-selects nothing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginorguuid
- [definition] `gcpAuthRefresh` — Run your own command to refresh Google Cloud Application Default Credentials when Claude Code finds they've expired or can't be loaded, so [Google Cloud's Agent Platform](/docs/en/google-vertex-ai) requests keep working without you re-authenticating by hand. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#gcpauthrefresh
- [definition] `otelHeadersHelper` — Run your own command to generate the headers Claude Code sends with OpenTelemetry exports, for backends whose tokens rotate. Claude Code runs it at startup and periodically after that, and expects a JSON object of string header values on stdout. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#otelheadershelper
- [definition] Updates and versioning — Choose an update channel and, for organizations, pin the versions people can run. See [Update Claude Code](/docs/en/setup#update-claude-code). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#updates-and-versioning
- [definition] `autoUpdatesChannel` — Choose which [release channel](/docs/en/setup#configure-release-channel) background auto-updates and `claude update` follow. Set `"stable"` for a version that is typically about one week old and skips releases with major regressions, or `"latest"` for the most recent release. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#autoupdateschannel
- [definition] `minimumVersion` — Keep background auto-updates and `claude update` from installing any version below this one, so moving to the `"stable"` channel doesn't downgrade you from a newer `"latest"` build. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#minimumversion
- [definition] `requiredMaximumVersion` — Set the newest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is newer, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to install an approved version through your organization's approved method; `claude install <version>` may also work. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#requiredmaximumversion
- [definition] `requiredMinimumVersion` — Set the oldest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is older, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to update through your organization's approved method. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#requiredminimumversion
- [definition] Tools — Turn off specific tools in the [Claude Code desktop app](/docs/en/desktop). The terminal CLI ignores these keys. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#tools
- [definition] `browserExternalPageTools` — Stop Claude from using its tools to read or act on external pages in the desktop app's [Browser pane](/docs/en/desktop#browse-external-sites). People in your organization can still open external sites themselves, and local dev server previews keep working with Claude's tools. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#browserexternalpagetools
- [definition] `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` — Turn off external browsing in the desktop app's [Browser pane](/docs/en/desktop#browse-external-sites) for people and Claude alike. Localhost dev server previews keep working. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disablebrowserexternalnavigation
- [definition] `disableMobileSimulatorTools` — Block Claude's tools for the desktop app's [iOS Simulator pane](/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#turn-off-simulator-access). People keep manual use of the pane; only Claude's access is removed, and nobody can turn it back on from inside the app. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disablemobilesimulatortools
- [definition] Privacy and telemetry — Control how long Claude Code keeps session data and what it sends. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#privacy-and-telemetry
- [definition] `cleanupPeriodDays` — Set how many days Claude Code keeps [session transcripts and other application data](/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically) before deleting them. Claude Code runs the deletion as a background sweep after a session starts, as long as it can safely determine the retention period. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#cleanupperioddays
- [definition] `desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays` — Set an age limit in days for the transcripts of sessions you started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork. Without this key, Claude Code [keeps those transcripts at any age](/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#desktopsessioncleanupperioddays
- [definition] `feedbackDrafts` — Control [Claude-drafted feedback](/docs/en/tools-reference#sendfeedback-tool-behavior): whether Claude can queue feedback drafts for you to review, and whether Claude Code shows a card when Claude queues one. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#feedbackdrafts
- [definition] `feedbackSurveyRate` — Set the probability that the [session quality survey](/docs/en/data-usage#session-quality-surveys) appears when a session is eligible for it. Set `0` to keep the survey from appearing. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#feedbacksurveyrate
- [definition] `skipWebFetchPreflight` — Skip the [WebFetch domain safety check](/docs/en/data-usage#webfetch-domain-safety-check), which sends each requested hostname to `api.anthropic.com` before fetching. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#skipwebfetchpreflight
- [definition] Enterprise and managed settings — Keys an organization uses to compute, refresh, and combine managed settings. See [Set up managed settings](/docs/en/admin-setup). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#enterprise-and-managed-settings
- [definition] `disableSideloadFlags` — Reject the `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, `--agents`, and `--mcp-config` CLI flags at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass [`strictKnownMarketplaces`](#strictknownmarketplaces) for a single run. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disablesideloadflags
- [definition] `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` — Block CLI startup until Claude Code has freshly fetched [server-managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings). If the fetch fails, Claude Code exits instead of continuing with cached or no settings. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceremotesettingsrefresh
- [definition] `managedSourcesBehavior` — Choose whether Claude Code applies only the highest-priority [managed source](/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources) your organization delivers, or combines every admin source it delivers. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#managedsourcesbehavior
- [definition] `parentSettingsBehavior` — Choose whether Claude Code applies managed settings supplied by an embedding host process, such as the Agent SDK or an IDE extension, when an admin-deployed managed tier is also present. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#parentsettingsbehavior
- [definition] `policyHelper` — Run an executable you deploy that computes managed settings at startup, so you can derive policy from device posture, identity, or a remote service instead of a static file. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#policyhelper
- [definition] `policyHelper.path` — Name the helper executable Claude Code runs. Claude Code refuses to start when the path isn't absolute, or on Windows when it doesn't end in `.exe`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#policyhelperpath
- [definition] `policyHelper.timeoutMs` — Set how long Claude Code waits for the helper before treating the run as failed. A timed-out run fails the same way as a non-zero exit, so at startup Claude Code refuses to start. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#policyhelpertimeoutms
- [definition] `policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs` — Have Claude Code re-run the helper in the background on an interval so policy changes reach a running session. When a refresh succeeds, its output replaces the previous managed settings without a restart; when a refresh fails, Claude Code keeps the policy it already has. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#policyhelperrefreshintervalms
- [definition] `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` — Have Claude Code on WSL read managed settings from the Windows policy chain, with HKLM and the Windows managed settings file taking priority over `/etc/claude-code` and HKCU below it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#wslinheritswindowssettings
- [definition] Global config settings — Save these keys in `~/.claude.json`, not in a settings file. Claude Code ignores them anywhere else. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#global-config-settings
- [definition] `autoConnectIde` — Connect to a running IDE automatically when you start Claude Code from an external terminal. Appears in `/config` as **Auto-connect to IDE (external terminal)** when you run Claude Code outside a VS Code or JetBrains terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#autoconnectide
- [definition] `autoInstallIdeExtension` — Install the Claude Code IDE extension automatically when you run Claude Code from a VS Code terminal. Appears in `/config` as **Auto-install IDE extension** when you run Claude Code inside a VS Code or JetBrains terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#autoinstallideextension
- [definition] `diffTool` — Choose where Claude Code shows the diff of an `Edit` or `Write` change it proposes when a [VS Code](/docs/en/vs-code) or [JetBrains](/docs/en/jetbrains#features) IDE is connected: `"auto"` opens it in the IDE's diff viewer, `"terminal"` keeps it in the terminal. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#difftool
- [definition] `externalEditorContext` — When you press `Ctrl+G`, Claude Code opens the prompt you're typing in your [external editor](/docs/en/interactive-mode#general-controls). — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#externaleditorcontext
- [definition] `permissionExplainerEnabled` — When Claude asks permission to run a Bash or PowerShell command, you can press `Ctrl+E` on the prompt to get a model-generated [explanation of the command](/docs/en/permissions#permission-system): what it does, why Claude is running it, and what could go wrong, labeled **Low risk**, **Med risk**… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#permissionexplainerenabled
- [definition] `teammateDefaultModel` — Removed in v2.1.234, together with its `/config` row **Default teammate model**. Setting it has no effect on current versions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#teammatedefaultmodel

- [parameter] `model.id`, `model.display_name`: Current model identifier and display name — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `cwd`, `workspace.current_dir`: Current working directory. Both fields contain the same value; `workspace.current_dir` is preferred for consistency with `workspace.project_dir`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `workspace.project_dir`: Directory where Claude Code was launched, which may differ from `cwd` if the working directory changes during a session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `workspace.added_dirs`: Additional directories added via `/add-dir` or `--add-dir`. Empty array if none have been added — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `workspace.git_worktree`: Git worktree name when the current directory is inside a linked worktree created with `git worktree add`. Absent in the main working tree. Populated for any git worktree, unlike `worktree.*`, which is present only while the session is in a [worktree session](/docs/en/worktrees) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `workspace.repo.host`, `workspace.repo.owner`, `workspace.repo.name`: Repository identity parsed from the `origin` remote, for example `"github.com"`, `"anthropics"`, `"claude-code"`. Absent outside a git repository or when no `origin` remote is configured — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `cost.total_cost_usd`: Estimated session cost in USD, computed client-side at list price unless a [`modelPricing`](/docs/en/settings-reference#modelpricing) table is in effect. May differ from your actual bill. Resets to \$0 when `/clear` starts a new session. Before v2.1.211, the total carried over after `/clear` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `cost.total_duration_ms`: Total wall-clock time since the session started, in milliseconds — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `cost.total_api_duration_ms`: Total time spent waiting for API responses in milliseconds — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `cost.total_lines_added`, `cost.total_lines_removed`: Lines of code changed — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `context_window.total_input_tokens`, `context_window.total_output_tokens`: Token counts currently in the context window, from the most recent API response. Input includes cache reads and writes — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `context_window.context_window_size`: Maximum context window size in tokens. 200000 by default, or 1000000 for models with extended context. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `context_window.used_percentage`: Pre-calculated percentage of context window used — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `context_window.remaining_percentage`: Pre-calculated percentage of context window remaining — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `context_window.current_usage`: Token counts from the last API call, described in [context window fields](#context-window-fields) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `exceeds_200k_tokens`: Whether the total token count (input, cache, and output tokens combined) from the most recent API response exceeds 200k. This is a fixed threshold regardless of actual context window size. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `fast_mode`: Whether [fast mode](/docs/en/fast-mode) is enabled for the session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `effort.level`: Current reasoning effort (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`). Reflects the live session value, including mid-session `/effort` changes. Ultracode is not a distinct level and reports as `xhigh`. Absent when the current model does not support the effort parameter — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `thinking.enabled`: Whether extended thinking is enabled for the session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage`, `rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage`: Percentage of the 5-hour or 7-day rate limit consumed, from 0 to 100 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `rate_limits.five_hour.resets_at`, `rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at`: Unix epoch seconds when the 5-hour or 7-day rate limit window resets — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `rate_limits.spend_limit.used_percentage`, `rate_limits.spend_limit.resets_at`: Behind a [Claude apps gateway](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-spend-limits#usage-warnings-in-claude-code), the percentage used of the spend limit that applies to you, and the Unix epoch seconds when its period resets. The percentage runs from 0 to 100, or above 100 once you exceed the limit. Requires Claude Code… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `prompt_cache`: The session's [prompt cache](/docs/en/prompt-caching) statistics for the main conversation: hit ratio, misses, and whether the cache is warm. See [prompt cache fields](#prompt-cache-fields) for every field. Absent until the main conversation's first API response. Requires Claude Code v2.1.251 or later — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `session_id`: Unique session identifier — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `session_name`: Session name. Uses the custom name set with the `--name` flag or `/rename` when one exists, otherwise the AI-generated session title. The [default display name](/docs/en/sessions#name-your-sessions), such as `my-app-3f`, doesn't populate this field. Absent when the session has neither a custom name nor an AI-generated title — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `prompt_id`: UUID identifying the user prompt currently being processed. Matches the [`prompt.id` attribute on OpenTelemetry events](/docs/en/monitoring-usage#event-correlation-attributes). Absent until the first user input. Requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `transcript_path`: Path to conversation transcript file — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `version`: Claude Code version — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `output_style.name`: Name of the current output style — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `vim.mode`: Current vim mode (`NORMAL`, `INSERT`, `VISUAL`, or `VISUAL LINE`) when [vim mode](/docs/en/interactive-mode#vim-editor-mode) is enabled — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `agent.name`: Agent name when running with the `--agent` flag or agent settings configured — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `pr.number`, `pr.url`: Open pull request for the current branch. Mirrors the PR badge in the footer. In a repository with a GitLab remote, Claude Code fills these fields from the branch's open [merge request](/docs/en/interactive-mode#gitlab-merge-requests) instead, so `pr.number` is the merge request number. Merge request data requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later. Absent when not in a git… — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `pr.review_state`: Review status of the open PR: `approved`, `pending`, `changes_requested`, or `draft`. May be independently absent even when `pr` is present — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `pr.kind`: `mr` when `pr` describes a [GitLab merge request](/docs/en/interactive-mode#gitlab-merge-requests). Absent for GitHub pull requests, so scripts written before this field keep working. For a merge request, Claude Code sets `review_state` to `approved` when GitLab reports it mergeable, `pending` for any other open state, and `draft` for a draft. Requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `worktree.name`: Name of the active worktree. Present only while the session is in a [worktree session](/docs/en/worktrees) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `worktree.path`: Absolute path to the worktree directory — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `worktree.branch`: Git branch name for the worktree (for example, `"worktree-my-feature"`). Absent for hook-based worktrees — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `worktree.original_cwd`: The directory Claude was in before entering the worktree — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `worktree.original_branch`: Git branch checked out before entering the worktree. Absent for hook-based worktrees — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#available-data
- [parameter] `warm`: Whether the cached prefix is still within its TTL. `false` when the last response reported no cache tokens, even while `caching_observed` is `true` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `caching_observed`: Whether any response this session reported cache tokens. `false` means prompt caching is off, or your provider or gateway doesn't report it — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `ttl`: [Cache lifetime](/docs/en/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime) of the current cached prefix: `"5m"` or `"1h"` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `expires_at`: When the cached prefix leaves its TTL and goes cold, in epoch seconds. `null` when the last response reported no cache tokens — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `requests`: API requests recorded for the main conversation this session — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `misses`: Requests that re-processed content the cache already held: more than 5% and at least 2,000 tokens of what the request could have read from cache, with no compaction or tool-result clearing to explain the shortfall in cache reads — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `expected_rebuilds`: Cache rebuilds that followed a compaction or a clearing of old tool results — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `hit_ratio`: Cache read tokens as a fraction of all input tokens this session, from 0 to 1. The denominator counts cache reads, cache writes, and uncached input. `null` while those counts are all zero — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `cache_write_tokens`: All tokens written to the cache this session, the first request's initial write included — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `miss_recache_tokens`: Tokens written to the cache by the requests counted as misses — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `last_miss_at`: When the last miss happened, in epoch seconds. `null` while the session has no misses — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields
- [parameter] `recache_tokens_if_cold`: Tokens the next request re-caches if the cache has gone cold by then. `null` right after a compaction or a clearing of old tool results, until the next request records the rewritten conversation's size — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#prompt-cache-fields

- [definition] Create a script that reads JSON and prints output — Claude Code sends JSON data to your script via stdin. This script uses [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/), a command-line JSON parser you may need to install, to extract the model name, directory, and context percentage, then prints a formatted line. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#build-a-status-line-step-by-step

- [definition] Context window usage — Display the current model and context window usage with a visual progress bar. - [definition] Git status with colors — Show git branch with color-coded indicators for staged and modified files. - [definition] Cost and duration tracking — Track your session's API costs and elapsed time. The `cost.total_cost_usd` field accumulates the estimated cost of all API calls in the current session. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#cost-and-duration-tracking

- [definition] Rate limit usage — Display Claude.ai subscription rate limit usage in the status line. The `rate_limits` object contains a rolling `five_hour` window and a weekly `seven_day` window. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#rate-limit-usage
- [definition] Cache expensive operations — Your status line script runs frequently during active sessions. Commands like `git status` or `git diff` can be slow, especially in large repositories. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#cache-expensive-operations
- [definition] Windows configuration — On Windows, Claude Code runs status line commands through Git Bash when Git Bash is installed, or through PowerShell when Git Bash is absent. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#windows-configuration
- [definition] Subagent status lines — The `subagentStatusLine` setting renders a custom row body for each [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) shown in the agent panel below the prompt. - [definition] Tools reference — Complete reference for the tools Claude Code can use, including permission requirements and per-tool behavior. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#tools-reference
- [definition] Configure tools with permission rules and hooks — For the most part, Claude decides when to use these tools and you don't need to name them yourself when interacting with Claude. You reference tool names directly when defining permissions and other configuration: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#configure-tools-with-permission-rules-and-hooks
- [definition] Agent tool behavior — The Agent tool spawns a subagent in a separate context window. The subagent works through its task autonomously, then returns a single text result to the parent conversation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#agent-tool-behavior
- [definition] AskUserQuestion tool behavior — Claude uses `AskUserQuestion` to ask you multiple-choice questions when it needs a decision or a clarification. Answer by picking an option, or type your own text through the `Other` row or the notes field. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#askuserquestion-tool-behavior
- [definition] Question auto-continue timeout — Questions stay open until you answer them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#question-auto-continue-timeout
- [definition] Bash tool behavior — The Bash tool runs each command in a separate process. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#bash-tool-behavior
- [definition] Timeout and output limits — Each command runs under a timeout, and Claude manages it: when it wants longer than the default for a command, it passes the `timeout` parameter with that call — you never set a per-command timeout. Two [environment variables](/docs/en/env-vars) bound what Claude gets: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#timeout-and-output-limits
- [definition] Background commands — For long-running processes such as dev servers or watch builds, Claude can set `run_in_background: true` to start the command as a background task and continue working while it runs. List and stop background tasks with `/tasks`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#background-commands
- [definition] Memory limit on Linux and WSL — On Linux and WSL, set [`CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT`](/docs/en/env-vars#variables) to a size such as `4G` to cap the memory that Bash, PowerShell, and [Monitor](#monitor-tool) tool commands can use, so one runaway build can't take the memory the rest of the session needs. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#memory-limit-on-linux-and-wsl
- [definition] Edit tool behavior — The Edit tool performs exact string replacement. It takes an `old_string` and a `new_string` and replaces the first with the second. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#edit-tool-behavior
- [definition] EndConversation tool behavior — The EndConversation tool ends the current session. Claude uses it only in two situations: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#endconversation-tool-behavior
- [definition] Glob tool behavior — The Glob tool finds files by name pattern. It supports standard glob syntax including `**` for recursive directory matching: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#glob-tool-behavior
- [definition] Grep tool behavior — The Grep tool searches file contents for patterns. Where [Glob](#glob-tool-behavior) finds files by name, Grep finds lines inside them. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#grep-tool-behavior
- [definition] LSP tool behavior — The LSP tool gives Claude code intelligence from a running language server. After each file edit, it automatically reports type errors and warnings so Claude can fix issues without a separate build step. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#lsp-tool-behavior
- [definition] Monitor tool — The Monitor tool lets Claude watch something in the background and react when it changes, without pausing the conversation. Ask Claude to: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#monitor-tool
- [definition] WebSocket source — The WebSocket source requires Claude Code v2.1.195 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#websocket-source
- [definition] NotebookEdit tool behavior — NotebookEdit modifies a Jupyter notebook one cell at a time, targeting cells by their `cell_id`. It doesn't perform string replacement across the notebook the way [Edit](#edit-tool-behavior) does on plain files. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#notebookedit-tool-behavior
- [definition] PowerShell tool — The PowerShell tool lets Claude run PowerShell commands natively. On Windows, this means commands run in PowerShell instead of routing through Git Bash. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#powershell-tool
- [definition] Enable the PowerShell tool — Set `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1` in your environment or in `settings.json`: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#enable-the-powershell-tool
- [definition] Shell selection in settings, hooks, and skills — Three additional settings control where PowerShell is used: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#shell-selection-in-settings-hooks-and-skills
- [definition] Windows encoding and exit codes — On Windows, the following PowerShell encoding and exit-code behaviors require Claude Code v2.1.214 or later: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#windows-encoding-and-exit-codes
- [definition] Preview limitations — The PowerShell tool has the following known limitations during the preview: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#preview-limitations
- [definition] Read tool behavior — The Read tool takes a file path and returns the contents with line numbers. Claude is instructed to always pass absolute paths. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#read-tool-behavior
- [definition] SendFeedback tool behavior — Claude-drafted feedback is a feedback report about Claude Code that Claude writes for you. It requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#sendfeedback-tool-behavior
- [definition] What you see when Claude drafts — After Claude queues a draft, you see a card above your prompt with the draft's title. Press `1` to review the draft, press `2` twice to send it as written, or press `0` to dismiss it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#what-you-see-when-claude-drafts
- [definition] Review and edit a draft — Run `/feedback` with no argument to open your queue. It lists every queued draft from all your sessions, including drafts whose cards you dismissed or never saw. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#review-and-edit-a-draft
- [definition] Send a draft — When you send a draft, Claude Code submits it the same way as a `/feedback` report, with the same [retention](/docs/en/data-usage#feedback-using-the-%2Ffeedback-command), and deletes the draft from your machine. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#send-a-draft
- [definition] Discard or keep a draft — When you discard a draft, Claude Code deletes it from your machine. A draft you leave in the queue expires after 30 days, or after [`cleanupPeriodDays`](/docs/en/settings-reference#cleanupperioddays) when that's shorter. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#discard-or-keep-a-draft
- [definition] Turn Claude-drafted feedback off — Set **Claude-drafted feedback** to `off` in `/config`, which writes the [`feedbackDrafts`](/docs/en/settings-reference#feedbackdrafts) setting, or set [`CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK=0`](/docs/en/env-vars) for one session. With either, Claude can't queue drafts. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#turn-claude-drafted-feedback-off
- [definition] Sessions without Claude-drafted feedback — Claude Code includes the tool in interactive terminal sessions on your own machine that use the Claude API rather than a cloud provider. It leaves the tool out of: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#sessions-without-claude-drafted-feedback
- [definition] Task tool availability — In Claude Code v2.1.233 and later, the following tools aren't available on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, or later versions of those families unless you opt in: `TodoWrite`, `TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskUpdate`, and `TaskList`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability
- [definition] WebFetch tool behavior — WebFetch takes a URL and a prompt describing what to extract. It fetches the page, converts the response to Markdown when the server returns HTML, and runs the prompt against the content using a small, fast model. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#webfetch-tool-behavior
- [definition] WebSearch tool behavior — WebSearch runs a query against Anthropic's [web search](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool) backend and returns result titles and URLs. It doesn't fetch the result pages. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#websearch-tool-behavior
- [definition] Session search limit — A session can make at most 200 WebSearch calls, counted across the main conversation and every [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) it spawns, so searches made by parallel research fan-outs count against the same limit. The limit requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#session-search-limit
- [definition] Write tool behavior — The Write tool creates a new file or overwrites an existing one with the full content provided. It doesn't append or merge. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#write-tool-behavior
- [definition] Check which tools are available — Your exact tool set depends on your provider, platform, and settings. To check what's loaded in a running session, ask Claude directly: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#check-which-tools-are-available

- [parameter] Swedish: `sv` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#change-the-dictation-language
- [parameter] Turkish: `tr` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#change-the-dictation-language
- [parameter] Ukrainian: `uk` — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#change-the-dictation-language
- [definition] Voice dictation — Speak your prompts in the Claude Code CLI with hold-to-record or tap-to-record voice dictation. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#voice-dictation
- [definition] Requirements — Voice dictation streams your recorded audio to Anthropic's servers for transcription. Audio is not processed locally. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#requirements
- [definition] Enable voice dictation — Run `/voice` to enable dictation. The first time you enable it, Claude Code runs a microphone check. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#enable-voice-dictation
- [definition] Hold to record — Hold mode is push-to-talk: recording runs while you hold the key and stops when you release it. This is the default mode. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#hold-to-record
- [definition] Tap to record and send — Tap mode toggles recording with a single keypress: tap once to start, speak, then tap again to send the prompt. There is no warmup, and you don't need to keep the key held. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#tap-to-record-and-send
- [definition] Change the dictation language — Voice dictation uses the same [`language` setting](/docs/en/settings-reference#language) that controls Claude's response language. If that setting is empty, dictation defaults to English. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#change-the-dictation-language
- [definition] Rebind the dictation key — The dictation key is bound to `voice:pushToTalk` in the `Chat` context and defaults to `Space`. The same binding controls both hold and tap modes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#rebind-the-dictation-key
- [definition] Troubleshooting — Common issues when voice dictation does not activate or record: — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#troubleshooting
- [definition] Terminal not listed in macOS Microphone settings — If your terminal app does not appear under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, there is no toggle you can enable. Reset the permission state for your terminal so the next `/voice` run triggers a fresh macOS permission prompt. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#terminal-not-listed-in-macos-microphone-settings
- [definition] Reset the microphone permission for your terminal — Run `tccutil reset Microphone <bundle-id>`, replacing `<bundle-id>` with your terminal's identifier: `com.apple.Terminal` for the built-in Terminal, or `com.googlecode.iterm2` for iTerm2. For other terminals, look up the identifier with `osascript -e 'id of app "AppName"'`. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#terminal-not-listed-in-macos-microphone-settings
- [definition] Quit and relaunch your terminal — macOS won't re-prompt a process that is already running. Quit the terminal app with Cmd+Q, not just close its windows, then open it again. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#terminal-not-listed-in-macos-microphone-settings
- [definition] Trigger a fresh prompt — Start Claude Code and run `/voice`. macOS prompts for microphone access; allow it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation#terminal-not-listed-in-macos-microphone-settings
